details.aesthetic: This is a regional journal directory, not a single journal with its own aesthetic. It lists outlets spanning haiku, experimental poetry, flash fiction, African American literary themes, Asian American literature, Southern literature, and more — all connected to the DC/MD/VA/DE corridor.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown

100 word story.index_line: Not a journal — Beltway Poetry Quarterly's directory of DC/Baltimore/Mid-Atlantic journals; submit to the listed outlets, not this page
100 word story.name: 100 Word Story
100 word story.summary: Beltway Poetry Quarterly is a directory/resource page listing literary journals with ties to the DC/Baltimore/Mid-Atlantic region, not a journal that accepts direct submissions itself. The page catalogs dozens of journals ranging from poetry and flash fiction outlets to regional and identity-focused publications. A writer should visit the individual journals listed rather than submitting here.

details.aesthetic: Science fiction in all its forms—hard sci-fi, cyberpunk, and beyond—told as tightly self-contained flash fiction under 600 words; no sequels, prequels, or stories dependent on previously published pieces.
details.multiple_submissions: allowed, up to a maximum of 6 submissions pending at once; must wait for one to be published or rejected before submitting another
details.red_flags: Strict word limit enforced by rejection (no editing for overage); stories with spelling/grammar errors will be rejected outright rather than edited; acquires first electronic rights plus non-exclusive subsequent (e.g. print anthology) rights.
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed (work must not have been published or sold elsewhere, in print or online)
details.word_limit: under 600 words

365 tomorrows.index_line: 365 Tomorrows: daily sci-fi flash under 600 words, any subgenre, no sequels or series entries, no fee, no simultaneous subs
365 tomorrows.name: 365 Tomorrows
365 tomorrows.summary: 365tomorrows is a daily flash fiction site publishing science fiction exclusively, in every subgenre from hard sci-fi to cyberpunk, in stories under 600 words. It was founded on the premise that flash fiction is the ideal form for internet-era reading, and it runs on a high-volume, quick-turnaround model publishing one story per day.

details.aesthetic: Not a journal — this is a journal-matching consultancy. The operator also runs a journal called Coastal Shelf and curates Notebooking Daily, but no editorial aesthetic for those outlets is described here.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This is not a literary journal and does not accept creative writing submissions. A writer looking to submit fiction, poetry, or nonfiction for publication will find no outlet here.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

3am magazine.index_line: 3:AM Magazine — not a journal; a paid service matching writers to journals ($3–$25). Doesn't publish work; submit elsewhere.
3am magazine.name: 3:AM Magazine
3am magazine.summary: This is not a literary journal but a paid literary magazine recommendation service run by Zebulon Huset, a widely published writer and MFA graduate who matches writers to suitable journals based on survey responses. It operates in tiers ($3 for 3 recommendations, $5 for 8, $25 for a two-round 13-journal consultation). Writers seeking a journal to submit to should look elsewhere; this service helps find journals, it does not publish work itself.

details.aesthetic: Seeks work that is 'overlooked and unclassifiable,' publishing beyond established literary confines. Track record suggests an affinity for debut literary fiction and story collections with moral and emotional weight (Jamel Brinkley, Ada Zhang, Mahreen Sohail); strong interest in international and translated literature (Dorthe Nors, Motoyuki Shibata's Japanese literature focus); poetry editor on staff. Serious, literary, with a nonprofit mission and award-winning institutional prestige.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This is an about/masthead page with no submission guidelines. Writer must find a separate submissions page before attempting to submit.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

a public space.index_line: A Public Space: overlooked, unclassifiable fiction/poetry with moral weight; strong translation focus; check separate page for submission guidelines
a public space.name: A Public Space
a public space.summary: A Public Space is a prestigious independent nonprofit literary magazine founded in 2006 by Brigid Hughes, dedicated to overlooked, unclassifiable, and boundary-crossing writing in fiction, poetry, and arts/culture. Its track record includes launching debut collections that went on to win PEN/Faulkner, Dylan Thomas Prize, and National Book Award finalist status, with a strong international and translation focus. No submission guidelines are present on this page.

details.aesthetic: unknown
details.multiple_submissions: unknown

able muse.name: Able Muse
able muse.summary: The page returned a human verification/bot check gate and no journal content was accessible. Nothing about the journal's aesthetic, policies, or submission guidelines can be determined from this text.

details.aesthetic: Work connecting art to spirit, earth, social justice, and cultural change; this issue focuses on how art challenges, responds to, and critiques shifts in culture—both protest art and personal/inner work. Accepts poetry, prose, music (video/recorded), visual art, and performance art.
details.multiple_submissions: Poetry allows up to 3 pieces; limits for other genres unknown due to truncated page.
details.red_flags: Submission guidelines are cut off mid-sentence; prose word limits and other key details are missing from the page. Writer should find the full guidelines on Submittable before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Poetry: up to 3 pieces, max 50 lines each. Prose and other genres: unknown (guidelines cut off).

about place.index_line: About Place: art meets spirituality, ecology, social justice; theme issue on art in a changing world; opens Aug 15 2026; guidelines page cuts off mid-sentence
about place.name: *About Place
about place.summary: About Place Journal seeks work linking art, spirituality, social justice, and ecology; this issue's theme is 'The Power of Art in a Changing World,' welcoming poetry, prose, music, visual and performance art. Submissions open August 15, 2026 and are due October 1, 2026 via Submittable. The page cuts off mid-sentence in the guidelines, so full format/word-limit details for prose and other genres are not visible.

details.aesthetic: Character-driven speculative fiction (hard/soft SF, fantasy, slipstream, cyberpunk, steampunk, urban fantasy, magical realism, space opera, YA, hypertext, ghost stories, etc.) with strong world-building and emotional depth; no horror, zombies, vampires, werewolves, elves, retold fairy tales, AI-generated text, gratuitous sex/violence/gore, or political content.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — one submission per reading period
details.reading_period: Fiction: Feb 1–7 and Aug 1–7 only (next: 2027); poetry has a separate schedule
details.red_flags: Extremely narrow reading windows (one week, twice a year); submissions outside those windows are deleted unread; wrong email subject line may also result in work never being read; no reprints, no serials, no AI-generated work; flat $80 payment for stories over 1,000 words caps earnings for longer pieces
details.response_time: ~3 months; query if no response after 6 months
details.simultaneous_submissions: Not allowed — stated explicitly for both fiction and poetry
details.word_limit: Up to 10,000 words (query first above that); flash = under 1,000 words

abyss an apex.index_line: Abyss & Apex: character-driven spec fic/poetry, no horror/vampires/elves/AI; reads only Feb 1-7 & Aug 1-7, one sub per window
abyss an apex.name: Abyss an Apex
abyss an apex.summary: Abyss & Apex publishes character-driven speculative fiction and poetry across a wide range of subgenres, strongly favoring emotional resonance and world-building while explicitly rejecting horror, zombies, vampires, elves, werewolves, AI-generated work, and political stories. Fiction reads only two one-week windows per year (Feb 1–7 and Aug 1–7, 2027 next up); stories up to 10,000 words, paying $0.08/word up to 1,000 words then flat $80. No simultaneous submissions and no multiple submissions per period — missing the narrow reading window or using the wrong email subject line will get work deleted unread.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry, and an 'Enlightenment' category; no specific voice or theme preferences stated beyond these genre categories.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Reading period and response time are not listed on this page — writer must check Submittable to confirm the journal is currently open before preparing a submission.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, provided the writer flags them as simultaneous and promptly withdraws if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

adroit journal.index_line: Adroit Journal — fiction, nonfiction, poetry, plus 'Enlightenment' category; pays $50-100; Submittable only, check site for open dates
adroit journal.name: Adroit Journal
adroit journal.summary: The Adroit Journal publishes fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry, and an 'Enlightenment' category, paying $100 for prose and $50 for poetry/Enlightenment contributors. Submissions are via Submittable only (no email except for writers with disabilities, no postal mail); simultaneous submissions are allowed with prompt notification. Reading period and response time are not stated on this page, so writers should check Submittable directly for current open/closed status.

details.aesthetic: Scholarly essays on African American literature, theatre, film, visual arts, and culture; 'Forgotten Manuscript' features (1,500–3,500 word essays contextualizing neglected texts); fiction; poetry; interviews. Renowned contributors include Toni Morrison, Rita Dove, and Amiri Baraka. Official MLA LLC African American publication.
details.multiple_submissions: One essay at a time; one fiction piece at a time; up to six poems at a time; submitting an essay blocks any concurrent creative submission
details.reading_period: Closed May 1, 2026 – Sep 15, 2026 for first-time submissions; open otherwise (year-round outside closure)
details.red_flags: Mandatory MLA 3rd edition style — non-compliant or unpaginated manuscripts are immediately rejected; authors must strip all identifying info; image permissions and fees are the author's responsibility; unsolicited book reviews not accepted; simultaneous submission penalties are unusually severe including a permanent ban
details.simultaneous_submissions: Not allowed; first violation = 3-year ban; if a signed contract is revoked due to simultaneous submission = permanent ban
details.word_limit: Critical essays: 6,000–8,500 words (excluding endnotes and Works Cited); fiction: up to 3,500 words; Forgotten Manuscripts essays: 1,500–3,500 words (plus 3,000–5,000 word excerpts); poetry: no word limit stated

african american review.index_line: African American Review — scholarly essays, fiction, poetry on Black literature/culture; strict MLA style; simultaneous subs risk a 3-year ban
african american review.name: African American Review
african american review.summary: African American Review publishes scholarly essays, fiction, poetry, interviews, and 'Forgotten Manuscript' features focused on African American literature, theatre, film, visual arts, and culture, with strict MLA 3rd edition formatting required. Critical essays run 6,000–8,500 words; fiction up to 3,500 words; up to six poems per submission; one submission type at a time per author. Simultaneous submissions are strictly prohibited with severe penalties: a three-year ban for a first infraction and a permanent ban if a signed contract must be revoked.

details.aesthetic: Ethical-dilemma short fiction in any genre (sci-fi, fantasy, romance, historical, etc.) where the moral question has no clear right answer; must spark philosophical discussion. Children's and YA also accepted. No poems, novels, or artwork. Avoids overtly religious/proselytizing stories, modern political or pop-culture names, and overused tropes (brain uploads, plant sentience, right-to-die).
details.fee: Fast Pass fee available (amount not specified); standard submission is free
details.multiple_submissions: No more than three submissions per six months
details.red_flags: Extremely narrow thematic focus with ~3% acceptance rate; editors stop reading at the third typo; Fast Pass fee amount not disclosed on this page; publication rights include podcast, audiobook, and anthology consideration—review their author agreement before submitting
details.response_time: 2–3 months standard; 3–5 days via paid Fast Pass
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Children's: under 1,500 words; Young Adult: under 3,500 words; Adult: 1,500–7,000 words (2,500–4,000 sweet spot)

after dinner conversation.index_line: Any-genre stories built on unresolvable ethical dilemmas, 2,500–4,000 words ideal; ~3% acceptance, skip overused tropes like brain uploads
after dinner conversation.name: After Dinner Conversation
after dinner conversation.summary: After Dinner Conversation publishes short fiction (any genre) built around genuine ethical dilemmas—stories where the 'right answer' is unknowable, not merely difficult; adult stories run 1,500–7,000 words, with the 2,500–4,000 range performing best. Response time is 2–3 months standard, or 3–5 days via paid Fast Pass; no more than three submissions per six-month period. Watch out for their narrow thematic focus (3% acceptance rate, 90% rejections are aesthetic misfits), a hard stop at the third typo, and a list of overused topics (brain uploads, plant sentience, right-to-die) plus blanket bans on overtly religious content, modern political/pop-culture names, and AI-generated conversation transcripts.

details.aesthetic: Writing that 'catches experience before the crusts of habit form'—personal essays, think-pieces, memoir, free verse, prose poems, visual/concrete/formal poetry, short stories, flash fiction, hybrid forms. No genre romance, horror, mystery, or sci-fi (though elements from those are okay); no academic essays or purely journalistic writing.
details.fee: $3 via online portal (Subfolio); free for paper mail submissions
details.multiple_submissions: One story or essay, or up to five poems per submission; one submission per reading period only
details.reading_period: Sep 1 – Dec 15 and Jan 15 – May 31 (no submissions June, July, August)
details.red_flags: Must disclose any AI, found-material, or collaborative elements in cover letter; previously published work in English (including online/social media) not eligible; do not email work; do not resubmit revised work already considered
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must withdraw immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: No hard limit, though length can affect decisions

agni.index_line: AGNI: literary essays, memoir, poetry, hybrid forms resisting convention; no genre romance/horror/mystery/sci-fi; $3 online fee
agni.name: AGNI
agni.summary: AGNI seeks poetry and prose (personal essays, memoir, short fiction, prose poems, hybrid) that resist convention and feel irreducibly individual, with no genre romance/horror/mystery/sci-fi and no purely academic or journalistic writing. Two reading windows per year (Sep 1–Dec 15, Jan 15–May 31); online submissions cost $3, paper is free but slower. Writers must disclose AI or found-material use upfront, must not submit more than once per reading period, and should not query before four months have passed.

details.aesthetic: Innovative literary and multimedia work across all genres—personal essays, criticism, memoir, fiction of all styles, poetry (traditional or experimental/cross-genre), collaborative pieces, music, video, and multimedia. Centered on a Southern California perspective but open to all writers globally; especially interested in work from women, BIPOC, and LGBTQ creators.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed — only one piece per reading period; submitting more than one disqualifies all submissions
details.reading_period: unknown (currently closed at time of page capture)
details.red_flags: Submissions capped at 200 per reading period; currently closed; payment only through USC's system (no Zelle, PayPal, Venmo, check, or wire transfer); journal retains First North American Serial Rights
details.response_time: unknown; writers asked to wait at least one month before inquiring
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but writer must immediately notify via withdrawal form if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 4000 words for prose, fiction, and collaborations; up to 5 pages for poetry

airlight.index_line: Air/Light — SoCal-rooted innovative lit/multimedia, all genres; one submission per period, others disqualified; currently closed
airlight.name: Air/Light
airlight.summary: Air/Light publishes innovative literary work across all genres and mediums with particular interest in women, BIPOC, and LGBTQ creators, approaching arts from a Southern California perspective. Prose and fiction cap at 4000 words, poetry at 5 pages, submissions are free but capped at 200 per reading period, and only one piece may be submitted per reading period. Submitting more than one piece disqualifies all of them, and payment is exclusively through USC's system—no PayPal, Venmo, or other methods.

details.aesthetic: Fiction (short stories, flash, novellas, novel excerpts), poetry (traditional and experimental, no light verse), short plays, literary nonfiction, and photo essays (query first); both traditional and experimental styles welcomed across all genres.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Narrow windows: Nonfiction Feb 14–22, Poetry Apr 10–19, Fiction May 23–31 (listed for Winter/Spring 2026 issue).
details.red_flags: Reading windows are only 8–9 days long per genre, so writers must watch the schedule carefully; photo essays require a query before submitting; hard copy submissions are not accepted.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Fiction and nonfiction up to ~90 pages/24,000 words; drama up to ~50 pages; poetry up to 6 poems per submission.

alaska quarterly review.index_line: Fiction, poetry, drama, nonfiction, traditional or experimental; brutal 8-9 day annual reading windows per genre, $3 fee
alaska quarterly review.name: Alaska Quarterly Review
alaska quarterly review.summary: Alaska Quarterly Review publishes fiction, poetry, drama, and literary nonfiction in both traditional and experimental styles, with no light verse. Submissions are accepted only during narrow windows via Submittable with a $3 fee; response time is 4–12 weeks. The reading windows are very tight (often just 8–9 days each), and photo essays require a query before submitting.

details.aesthetic: SF, fantasy, and horror; also considers humor or general interest with a quirky, original slant. Wants strong characters, good plotting, clever but logical twists, and experimental ideas. Avoids clichés, contrivance, and fiction based on existing movies, TV, or others' printed media.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — only one story per submission
details.red_flags: Submissions not in Word (.doc/.docx) or RTF attachment will not be read; stories pasted into email body are rejected; a physical mailing address is required (contracts and payment sent by post); reprints must include prior publication name and date; short-shorts, flash fiction, and stories over 5000 words face extra scrutiny.
details.response_time: Up to 6 weeks for initial review; final decisions made at end of 2-month submission cycle
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but must disclose at time of submission
details.word_limit: No stated minimum or maximum, but stories over 5000 words are a hard sell; flash under 100 words and short-shorts under 500 words also difficult. Non-fiction capped at 2000 words.

allegory.index_line: Allegory: SF/fantasy/horror under 5000 words, no tie-ins; $15 flat pay; Word/RTF only, snail mail address required or rejected
allegory.name: Allegory
allegory.summary: Allegory is a biannual online magazine publishing SF, fantasy, and horror fiction, seeking strong characters, logical twists, and experimental ideas while avoiding clichés and media tie-ins. Submission windows are fixed two-month periods (e.g. May 1–June 30, 2026), with a soft preference for stories under 5000 words and a flat $15 payment per piece. Writers must use strict email/attachment formatting (Word or RTF only, standard manuscript format) and include a snail mail address, or their submission will not be read.

details.aesthetic: California and the West regional focus; short fiction with lively writing, strong sense of place, and moving narratives; poetry with strong sense of place and emotion.
details.multiple_submissions: Poetry: up to 4 poems in a single file; Fiction: not stated
details.red_flags: No reply sent on rejections — writers must track the 90-day window themselves; simultaneous submissions will not be considered, which is a hard rule stated twice.
details.response_time: 90 days; no reply within 90 days means rejection
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 4,000 words preferred; Poetry: up to 90 lines, max 4 poems per submission

alta journal.index_line: Alta Journal: California/West-focused fiction (<4000 words) and poetry with strong sense of place; no simultaneous subs, silence = rejection
alta journal.name: Alta Journal
alta journal.summary: Alta Journal publishes California- and West-focused short fiction and poetry with a strong sense of place, preferring stories under 4,000 words and poems under 90 lines (max 4 per submission). Response time is 90 days, with no reply meaning a pass. Simultaneous submissions are strictly prohibited, and writers should read the magazine before submitting.

details.aesthetic: Character-driven fiction; poetry of any form or subject chosen by eclectic editors; creative nonfiction including traditional personal essays and genre-pushing forms; also a Flash Flood showcase for prose and prose poetry up to 1000 words.
details.fee: $3 for general submissions; fee waiver available by emailing americanliteraryreview@gmail.com; no fee for art submissions.
details.multiple_submissions: Fiction: one story at a time. Poetry: up to five poems at a time. Essays: one work at a time.
details.reading_period: General: Oct 1–Dec 1 and Jan 1–May 1; Flash Flood: first two weeks of each month during the academic year; Contest (ALR Awards): Jun 1–Sep 1.
details.red_flags: Current UNT students and graduates within the past 3 years are ineligible. No AI-generated or LLM-assisted work accepted. 300-submission cap per genre (portal closes when reached). No refunds on withdrawn submissions. No feedback provided. No edits accepted after submission.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but notify immediately via Submittable if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: under 8000 words advised, no hard cap. Essays: under 8000 words advised, no hard cap. Poetry: no word or page limit. Flash Flood: 1000 words or less.

american literary review.index_line: Character-driven fiction, eclectic poetry, essays (incl. experimental); online only; monthly Flash Flood ≤1000 words; $3 fee; no AI
american literary review.name: American Literary Review
american literary review.summary: ALR publishes character-driven fiction, eclectic poetry (any form/subject), and creative nonfiction essays including experimental work, all for online publication only. General submissions run Oct 1–Dec 1 and Jan 1–May 1 with a $3 fee and a 300-submission cap per genre; a Flash Flood showcase (prose/prose poetry ≤1000 words) opens the first two weeks of each month during the academic year. Watch out for the UNT student/recent-grad ineligibility rule, the no-AI policy, and the no-refund policy on withdrawn submissions.

details.aesthetic: unknown
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Wrong page entirely — this is a Writer's Digest how-to article, not a journal's submission guidelines or about page. No submittable journal is described.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

american reader.index_line: American Reader — mislabeled source: this is a Writer's Digest cover-letter how-to, not a journal; skip
american reader.name: American Reader
american reader.summary: This page is not a literary journal. It is a Writer's Digest instructional article about how to write cover letters for literary journal submissions. No specific journal is described or catalogued here.

details.aesthetic: Contemporary literary short fiction across a wide range of voices, established and emerging; no set content restrictions but extremely high standards; publishes in print (triannual) and online.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed — one story at a time only
details.red_flags: Work posted online anywhere (blogs, Facebook, etc.) is considered previously published and ineligible; paper submissions are recycled unread; reading period is only 4 months per year.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, on condition author immediately withdraws via Submittable if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

american short fiction.index_line: Fiction only, extremely high bar; Sept–Dec reading window, $3 fee, one story at a time; any online posting counts as published
american short fiction.name: American Short Fiction
american short fiction.summary: American Short Fiction publishes high-quality literary short fiction only (no poetry, nonfiction, plays, or reviews), accepting unsolicited submissions September through December with a $3 fee and one story at a time. No word limit is stated, but standards are described as 'extremely high' and familiarity with the magazine is expected. Writers should note the 8-month minimum wait before querying and that any online appearance—including blogs and social media—counts as previously published.

details.aesthetic: Hard SF where a scientific or technological element (physical, sociological, psychological, or engineering-based) is so central that removing it collapses the story; strong plots with believable characters; fact articles on frontier research topics written in an accessible, informal style; poetry also accepted.
details.multiple_submissions: Poetry: up to 6 poems per submission, wait for response before sending more; fiction policy not explicitly stated beyond standard one-at-a-time implied
details.red_flags: AI-assisted submissions (ChatGPT etc.) result in a ban from future submissions; no email or fax submissions accepted; submission system scheduled down March 11–13; hardcopy strongly discouraged and requires SASE for any response
details.response_time: 2–3 months average; follow up after 4 months
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed
details.word_limit: Short fiction up to ~20,000 words; serials 40,000–80,000 words; fact articles ~4,000 words

analog science fiction and fact.index_line: Analog: Hard SF where science/tech is load-bearing, up to 20k words (serials to 80k); fact articles & poetry too; no AI-assisted work, no simultaneous subs
analog science fiction and fact.name: Analog: Science Fiction and Fact
analog science fiction and fact.summary: Analog publishes hard science fiction where science or technology is integral to the plot, with believable characters; they also take fact articles (~4,000 words) and poetry. Fiction runs up to ~20,000 words; serials 40,000–80,000 words; fee-free online submission only via their portal. AI-assisted writing results in an immediate ban, and simultaneous submissions are explicitly prohibited.

details.aesthetic: Speculative fiction (science fiction, fantasy, horror and sub-genres); engaging stories with a strong opening; poetry must be speculative; non-fiction covers speculative genres, weird/real science, history, con reports, geekdom — how-to-write articles are discouraged. M-rated maximum: no gratuitous sex or violence.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — one submission per author at a time across all categories; a single file with multiple poems is explicitly rejected
details.red_flags: Submissions are currently closed. Payment is in AUD and capped at AUD$100 for fiction regardless of word count; payment is based on final edited word count, not submitted count. RTF is the only accepted file format. All personal info must be removed from the manuscript or it will likely be rejected. Non-AU/NZ non-subscribers are limited to half the word count of subscribers.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Not allowed — do not submit elsewhere until a hold/reject decision is received
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 20,000 words for subscribers or AU/NZ authors; up to 10,000 words for all others. Flash fiction under 1,000 words. Non-fiction: under 5,000 words (3,000 preferred). Poetry: under two pages.

andromeda spaceways.index_line: Andromeda Spaceways: SF/fantasy/horror + speculative poetry/nonfiction, M-rated; AUD$100 cap; closed to submissions
andromeda spaceways.name: Andromeda Spaceways
andromeda spaceways.summary: Andromeda Spaceways publishes speculative fiction (SF, fantasy, horror), poetry, and non-fiction in those genres, with an anonymous submissions system and an M-rated content ceiling. Word limits vary by category and author status (up to 20,000 words for subscribers/AU/NZ, 10,000 for others; poetry under 2 pages; non-fiction under 5,000 words). Submissions are currently closed, no simultaneous or multiple submissions are allowed, and manuscripts must be RTF with all personal information stripped out.

details.aesthetic: International in scope (at least one themed issue focused entirely on the Indian subcontinent), blending literary fiction with immersive nonfiction and strong visual art programs. Fiction tends toward social and familial complexity; nonfiction is grounded, sensory, and reportorial. The magazine has a curatorial, issue-by-issue thematic structure and champions writers from the regions it covers alongside Western contributors.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No submission guidelines found; the site appears to be a blog/promotional page. The magazine may be on hiatus or defunct—the blog post explicitly mentions 'coming out of a hiatus' and the content appears dated. Writers should verify current activity before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

annalemma.index_line: Global, issue-themed fiction/nonfiction/art with reportorial depth (Issue Nine: India, caste, corruption); no submission guidelines found—verify it's still active
annalemma.name: annalemma
annalemma.summary: Annalemma is a literary magazine publishing fiction, nonfiction, and art with a global, humanist sensibility—Issue Nine centers on India, with gritty on-the-ground nonfiction, socially layered fiction about caste and corruption, and interviews with human-rights figures. The work is atmospheric and reportorial in nonfiction, character-driven and morally textured in fiction, paired with substantial visual art. No submission guidelines are present in this text.

details.aesthetic: New fiction, poetry, and nonfiction translated from Arabic to English; reviews of books translated from Arabic or relevant to the field; interviews with translators, authors, and publishers; essays on Arabic literature and translation. Original English fiction or poetry is not accepted.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No original English writing accepted; AI-assisted translations explicitly rejected; translators must submit both the Arabic original and English translation; volunteer-run team may be slow to respond.
details.response_time: approximately 1 month before writer is encouraged to follow up
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

anomaly.index_line: ArabLit: Arabic literature in English translation only—fiction, poetry, essays, interviews; no original English work, no AI translations, submit Arabic + English together
anomaly.name: *Anomaly
anomaly.summary: ArabLit publishes fiction, poetry, nonfiction, reviews, interviews, and essays focused exclusively on Arabic literature in English translation (no original English writing). No word limits or reading-period restrictions are stated; response time is roughly one month before you should follow up. AI-assisted translations are explicitly rejected, and both the Arabic original and English translation must be submitted together.

details.aesthetic: Personal and political work that 'had to be written'; poetry that is experimental and/or sonically driven; nonfiction on pressing topics (immigration, DEI, affordability) in forms like memoir, braided essay, oral history, literary journalism; fiction preferably under 5,000 words; small-press book reviews with a political/analytical lens; Palestinian creative work (all genres, immediate and concrete); Ukrainian nonfiction (any form, invasion foregrounded or backgrounded); translations with original text included.
details.fee: Fee charged for some genres (amount unspecified); waived for BIPOC writers via separate no-fee Submittable form
details.multiple_submissions: Fiction: no more than one story at a time; poetry: 3–5 poems per submission; other genres not specified
details.reading_period: Open now through June 30, 2026 (fiction currently closed)
details.red_flags: Fiction is currently closed; no contributor payment; fee amount not disclosed on page; BIPOC writers must use the specific no-fee form or they may be charged
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Nonfiction up to 6,000 words; fiction preferably under 5,000 words; poetry 3–5 poems, no more than 7 pages; other genres unknown

another chicago magazine.index_line: Another Chicago Magazine — politically urgent, personally driven poetry/nonfiction; fiction closed; unpaid; fee unless BIPOC (separate form)
another chicago magazine.name: *Another Chicago Magazine
another chicago magazine.summary: ACM publishes politically engaged, personally driven work across poetry (experimental/sonic), nonfiction (memoir, essays, journalism up to 6,000 words), fiction (under 5,000 words), translations, art, reviews of small-press books, and special calls for Palestinian and Ukrainian voices. Open now through June 30, 2026; simultaneous submissions allowed with prompt notification if accepted elsewhere; no payment to contributors. A fee applies to some genres (waived for BIPOC writers via a separate no-fee form), and fiction is currently closed.

details.aesthetic: Quality-first; favors Atlantic Canadian and Canadian writers but open to all; welcomes new and young writers; publishes fiction and poetry (implied by references to stories and pieces); longer work held to a higher standard.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Closed at time of page capture; no open calls for submissions
details.red_flags: Submissions currently closed. No previously published work accepted in any format. Revised submissions invited after feedback are not guaranteed publication and must compete against new submissions.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

antigonish review.index_line: Antigonish Review: quality-first fiction/poetry, Canadian/Atlantic focus but open to all; no reprints; currently closed
antigonish review.name: *Antigonish Review
antigonish review.summary: The Antigonish Review prioritizes quality writing with a mandate to encourage Atlantic Canadian and Canadian writers, though they welcome submissions from anywhere including new and young writers. No submission length is specified, but longer pieces face a higher quality bar; response time is 2–3 months. Submissions are currently closed, and previously published work in any format is strictly rejected.

details.aesthetic: Serious, intellectually engaged nonfiction essays bridging scholarly substance and broader readerly concern (social science and humanities topics); fiction chosen for distinction and compelling craft rather than genre or trend, publishing only 2-3 stories per issue; poetry judged on inseparable form/content with no light or inspirational verse; occasional short book evaluations, no unsolicited reviews.
details.multiple_submissions: submit manuscripts one at a time except poetry (3-6 poems at once); do not mix genres in one envelope
details.reading_period: currently closed/on hiatus, not accepting submissions
details.red_flags: Currently on hiatus and not accepting any submissions; no electronic submissions accepted; requires SASE or submission is discarded unread; no free sample copies; mail-only postal submissions required.
details.simultaneous_submissions: discouraged; if accepted elsewhere, must notify immediately
details.word_limit: up to 5,000 words typically, 8,000 words at outside limit

antioch review.index_line: Antioch Review: intellectual essays for general readers, 2-3 distinguished stories, serious poetry — CURRENTLY ON HIATUS, not accepting submissions
antioch review.name: Antioch Review
antioch review.summary: The Antioch Review is a venerable literary and intellectual quarterly publishing interpretive nonfiction essays for educated general readers, literary journalism, a small handful of distinguished short stories per issue, and competitive poetry, all held to high literary standards; it is currently on hiatus and not accepting submissions.

details.aesthetic: Unknown from this text; genres accepted are poetry, fiction, nonfiction, flash fiction, and visual art.
details.multiple_submissions: The form allows submitting multiple works in one submission (separate titles with commas), but no explicit policy on concurrent separate submissions is stated.
details.red_flags: No aesthetic information available from this page; writer should visit the journal's main site before submitting to assess fit.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

apalachee review.index_line: Apalachee Review: poetry, fiction, nonfiction, flash, visual art; no fee; no stated aesthetic—check site before submitting
apalachee review.name: Apalachee Review
apalachee review.summary: Apalachee Review accepts poetry, fiction, nonfiction, flash fiction, and visual art via its own submission manager. The text is purely a submission portal interface and reveals nothing about editorial aesthetic, themes, or the character of published work. No submission fee is charged (price shown as $0.00).

details.aesthetic: Dark, weird, and beautiful speculative fiction — horror, science fiction, fantasy, slipstream. Prioritizes distinct voices from marginalized and under-represented writers. Stories should feel twisted, strange, and leave readers changed; gratuitous gore for shock value alone is explicitly unwanted.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed
details.reading_period: Odd months only: January, March, May, July, September, November
details.red_flags: Flash fiction contest theme is announced on Patreon only — off-theme stories are auto-rejected. Recent flash fiction winners must wait one issue cycle before resubmitting. AI-generated or AI-assisted writing is explicitly banned. Submissions go through Moksha; full detailed guidelines are there, not fully on this page.
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed
details.word_limit: Up to 9,000 words (flash fiction contest is separate with its own track)

apex magazine.index_line: Apex Magazine: dark, weird speculative fiction prioritizing marginalized voices; 8¢/word; odd months only; no AI-assisted work
apex magazine.name: Apex Magazine
apex magazine.summary: Apex publishes dark, weird, beautiful speculative fiction (horror, SF, fantasy, slipstream) with a strong preference for marginalized voices and stories that leave readers changed. Main fiction up to 9,000 words at 8¢/word; submissions open odd months only (Jan, Mar, May, Jul, Sep, Nov). No reprints, no multiple submissions, no AI-assisted writing, and flash fiction requires matching a monthly Patreon-announced theme or it's auto-rejected.

details.aesthetic: Literature and art exploring intersectional identity—race, gender, sexuality, class, disability, migration, diaspora, oppression—from marginalized perspectives; values linguistic diversity and work that interrogates political and aesthetic status quos; prioritizes writers of color and oppressed identities, including an explicit invitation to Palestinian, Lebanese, Congolese, and Sudanese writers.
details.multiple_submissions: One piece per reading period for the main journal; up to two flash pieces submitted separately for Perigee
details.reading_period: Main journal portal closed; check back spring 2027. Perigee (digital platform) rolling but currently closed.
details.red_flags: Portal is closed until spring 2027—no point submitting now. Work from over-represented perspectives that primarily interrogates the writer's own privilege is explicitly discouraged. Work must be previously unpublished.
details.response_time: 6 weeks for flash; unknown for main journal and book reviews
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 5,000 words for prose; up to 5 poems per submission; flash (Perigee) defined as under 1,000 words, up to 2 pieces

apogee.index_line: Apogee: intersectional identity-politics lit/art by marginalized writers, not privilege-interrogation pieces; closed until spring 2027
apogee.name: Apogee
apogee.summary: Apogee publishes fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and visual art centered on intersectional identity politics, prioritizing writers of oppressed and marginalized identities who interrogate aesthetic and political status quos. Prose is capped at 5,000 words; poetry at five poems per submission; one piece per reading period; no fee; simultaneous submissions allowed with notification. The main portal is currently closed until spring 2027, and writers from over-represented perspectives whose work primarily interrogates their own privilege are explicitly not what the journal seeks.

details.aesthetic: Original, unpublished work connected to Appalachia and its people—expanding, not stereotyping, regional identity. Fiction: literary only, no genre (fantasy, mystery, crime, sci-fi). CNF: personal, lyric, meditative, literary journalism, experimental—no sentimental local-color writing. Poetry: nearly any aesthetic, truly original. YA: intelligent, creative slices of adolescent/human experience. Craft essays: mechanics of writing and the writing life.
details.multiple_submissions: Limited: one story or essay OR up to five poems per submission; submitting more than one piece in the same prose genre at once will be discarded
details.red_flags: Submissions outside Sep 1–Dec 1 are discarded without consideration; exceeding per-genre submission limits triggers discard; submitting to the editor-solicitation portal without a personal invitation causes automatic rejection; book reviews require a prior query and are not open to unsolicited full submissions
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify promptly if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction, CNF, YA: up to 7,500 words; craft essays: up to 3,500 words; poetry: 1–5 poems at a time

appalachian review.index_line: Appalachian Review: literary fiction/CNF/poetry/YA rooted in Appalachia, no stereotypes; reads Sep 1–Dec 1 only, strict per-genre limits
appalachian review.name: Appalachian Review
appalachian review.summary: Appalachian Review publishes fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry, YA, and craft essays rooted in or capturing the spirit of Appalachia—no genre fiction, no stereotypes, no local-color sentimentality. Submissions are accepted September 1–December 1 only, with a ~10-month response time; fiction/CNF/YA cap at 7,500 words, craft essays at 3,500. Work received outside the reading window is discarded, multiple submissions beyond the stated per-genre limits are discarded, and submitting to the editor-solicitation portal without an invitation results in automatic rejection.

details.aesthetic: Themed speculative fiction — fantasy, sci-fi, horror, and literary; sought emotionally resonant stories with clear prose, proactive characters, and lived-in settings; also published spec-fic poetry; no AI-generated content, erotica, fan fiction, gratuitous violence, or nonfiction.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed; one poem and one short story per theme maximum; withdrawing and resubmitting within the same theme period counted as a multiple submission.
details.red_flags: Magazine is permanently closed to all submissions — submitting is pointless. Historically, submissions sent outside reading windows or not following formatting guidelines were deleted unread.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Not allowed generally; exception was made for writers identifying as Disabled, BIPOC, or LGBTQIA+ who noted their identity and the simultaneous submission in their cover letter.
details.word_limit: Short fiction: 1,000–5,000 words; flash fiction: under 1,000 words; poetry: not specified beyond being a separate category.

apparition.index_line: Apparition — themed spec-fic (fantasy/sci-fi/horror) stories and poetry — PERMANENTLY CLOSED, do not submit
apparition.name: Apparition
apparition.summary: Apparition Lit was a themed speculative fiction magazine (fantasy, sci-fi, horror, literary) publishing poems and short stories (1k–5k words) plus monthly flash fiction (<1000 words) four times a year. It is now permanently closed to all submissions after seven years of operation. Writers should not submit anything, as the magazine is no longer accepting work.

details.aesthetic: Literary poetry (short, non-rhyming preferred), short fiction (fabulism and magical realism welcome; no horror, sci-fi, or mysteries), flash fiction, personal essays/creative nonfiction (no scholarly, critical, inspirational, or journalistic work), and prose poetry. Emphasis on beautifully crafted, original work in English.
details.multiple_submissions: Poetry: up to 6 poems per submission; flash fiction: up to 3 pieces (or up to 6 microfiction); short fiction: 1 story per submission; essays: 1 longer essay or multiple flash essays up to 4,000 words total
details.red_flags: No attachments accepted (work must be pasted into email body); no genre fiction (horror, sci-fi, mysteries); no scholarly, critical, inspirational, or journalistic essays; simultaneous submission policy not stated anywhere on the page
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Short fiction: up to ~4,000 words; flash fiction: up to ~1,000 words each (up to 3 pieces, or up to 6 microfiction/linked pieces totalling 4,000 words); essays: up to 4,000 words; poetry: no set limit but preference for under two pages

apple valley review.index_line: Apple Valley Review: literary poetry, fiction, fabulism, and essays; no genre fiction; email body only, no attachments
apple valley review.name: *Apple Valley Review
apple valley review.summary: Apple Valley Review seeks beautifully crafted poetry, short fiction (including flash and fabulism/magical realism), and creative nonfiction/essays with a literary aesthetic—no genre fiction, scholarly essays, or inspirational writing. Word limits vary by genre: up to 4,000 words for short fiction and essays, 1,000 words per flash piece, no hard limit for poetry (but short and non-rhyming preferred); submissions are free and read year-round via email only, with work pasted into the message body. Writers must not send attachments, must not submit previously published work (in English), and should note that simultaneous submission policy is not stated.

details.aesthetic: Imaginative, genre-spanning writing emphasizing interconnection and formal or linguistic invention; strong focus on literary translation and international perspectives (from Egypt to Brazil to South Korea to Russia), plus U.S. writers from regions outside the mainstream literary marketplace; includes graphic storytelling/comics alongside fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed; only one submission per writer per year
details.reading_period: opens twice a year (specific dates not given; check social media/Submittable)
details.red_flags: Very restrictive frequency—writers may submit only once per year, and windows are limited to twice yearly; translated work requires a formal letter of rights from the source author or estate.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with notification required if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: prose under 8,000 words; poetry up to 5 pages; comics up to 5 pages

arkansas international.index_line: Arkansas International: translation-forward fiction, poetry, nonfiction, comics; international/invention-driven; one submission per writer per year
arkansas international.name: Arkansas International
arkansas international.summary: The Arkansas International publishes literary translation alongside fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, and graphic storytelling, with an explicit commitment to international voices and work from over 70 countries plus U.S. regions outside the literary mainstream. The aesthetic favors imaginative, boundary-crossing writing that builds interconnection through invention, and translated pieces require the source text and a rights letter from the author or estate. Submission windows open only twice a year, and writers may send new work just once annually.

details.aesthetic: Multiple journals covered: ranges from design-forward independent lit mags (Firewords) to long-established prestige journals (Boulevard, Louisville Review) to anonymous-submission equity-focused outlets (Armchair/Shotgun); common thread is openness to unpublished or early-career writers across fiction, poetry, and nonfiction.
details.multiple_submissions: Brittle Star allows 1–4 poems at a time; others unknown
details.red_flags: This is a roundup article from a dormant aggregator site (Aerogramme is no longer updated), not a journal's own guidelines page. Details may be outdated; writer should verify each journal's current guidelines directly before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Brittle Star: up to 2000 words; Litro: up to 3000 words; others unknown

armchairshotgun.index_line: Armchair/Shotgun: details unverified — sourced from a dormant roundup, not the journal's own guidelines; confirm directly before submitting
armchairshotgun.name: Armchair/Shotgun
armchairshotgun.summary: This is not a single journal but an article from Aerogramme Writers' Studio listing 9 literary magazines that welcome new and unpublished writers, including Brittle Star, The Louisville Review, Phoebe, Boulevard, Litro, and others. The site itself is no longer being updated. No submission guidelines for any individual journal are provided in sufficient detail to act on.

details.aesthetic: Not a journal; this is a how-to guide for writers navigating the submission process generally.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Wrong site entirely — no journal to evaluate here.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

arrowsmith.index_line: Arrowsmith — not a journal; this is Purdue OWL's general guide to submitting to literary magazines, skip
arrowsmith.name: Arrowsmith
arrowsmith.summary: This is not a literary journal — it is the Purdue OWL's general educational resource on how to submit to literary magazines. It contains no information about any specific journal's aesthetic, submission mechanics, or editorial identity.

details.aesthetic: Not a single journal — a aggregated reference list spanning the full range of literary publishing: mainstream prestige journals, experimental venues (Fence), genre-adjacent (Bear Deluxe), diaspora-focused (Callaloo), CNF-only (River Teeth), and open-form community magazines (Four Chambers).
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Varies by journal; examples: One Story Sept. 1–May 31; TriQuarterly Oct. 1–March 31; Kenyon Review contest Feb 1–28.
details.red_flags: This is a third-party aggregator page, not an official journal site — details may be outdated (e.g., Black Clock noted as reopening 'Fall 2012'). Verify all specifics directly with each journal before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Varies; One Story explicitly allows simultaneous submissions; others not specified in this text.
details.word_limit: Varies by journal; One Story listed as 3,000–8,000 words; Five Points prefers ~7,500 words; Kenyon Review Short Fiction Contest listed as 1,200 words or fewer.

artful dodge.index_line: Not a journal — Tankersley's aggregator listing dozens of journals/contests; outdated in places, verify directly before submitting
artful dodge.name: Artful Dodge
artful dodge.summary: This is a curated third-party directory of literary journals and contests compiled by Ed Tankersley, not a single journal's own site. It lists submission details and brief descriptions for dozens of well-known literary magazines (Tin House, Kenyon Review, One Story, etc.) and contests. Writers should visit individual journal sites for current, authoritative guidelines.

details.aesthetic: Poetry (4-6 poems suggested), fiction, creative nonfiction (both up to 25 pages), and flash (1-3 pieces, up to 1,000 words each); no stated thematic or stylistic preference beyond standard literary journal fare.
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per genre at a time allowed; must wait for a response before submitting another piece in the same genre
details.red_flags: Fee is nonrefundable even on withdrawal; Spring 2025 issue is online-only, not print; foreign nationals subject to 30% tax withholding on payment unless a treaty applies
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Prose up to 25 pages; flash up to 1,000 words each piece

arts and letters.index_line: Arts & Letters: general literary poetry/fiction/CNF/flash, no stated aesthetic; $3 fee, nonrefundable; closed now
arts and letters.name: Arts & Letters
arts and letters.summary: Arts & Letters publishes poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and flash in a traditional literary journal format twice yearly (Spring and Fall). Submissions are currently closed; when open, prose is capped at 25 pages and flash at 1,000 words each, with a $3 submission fee. Writers should note the fee is nonrefundable even if they withdraw, and Spring 2025 will be online-only rather than in print.

details.aesthetic: Literary Hub publishes craft essays, criticism, interviews, and cultural commentary about literature; it is not a venue for fiction, poetry, or personal essay submissions from writers seeking publication of creative work.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This is not a submittable literary journal — it is a literary news and culture site. A writer sending fiction here would be wasting their time.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

as you were.index_line: As You Were: not a journal — a Lit Hub article on vetting journals; no submissions accepted here
as you were.name: As You Were
as you were.summary: This is Literary Hub, a major online literary culture publication, not a journal that accepts fiction submissions. The page is an article by Erika Dreifus about how writers should evaluate journals before submitting — it describes no journal of its own.

details.aesthetic: Character-driven science fiction where people, not gadgetry, are the focus; serious and thoughtful but accessible, with occasional humor; open to borderline fantasy, slipstream, and surreal work; explicitly excludes sword & sorcery, explicit sex, and explicit violence; fiction should illuminate human existence against a cosmic-scale backdrop.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown (poetry requires a separate form per poem)
details.red_flags: No reprints accepted; no simultaneous submissions; explicitly bans AI-assisted or AI-written submissions and may ban repeat offenders; does not accept email submissions (online form or paper mail only); rights grant includes non-exclusive archive, translation, anthology, and paper-goods/merchandise rights beyond first publication.
details.response_time: about five weeks (query if no response after 45 days)
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed
details.word_limit: Fiction 1,000-20,000 words (seldom outside this range; pays full rate up to 7,500 words, reduced rate beyond); poetry up to 40 lines

asimovs science fiction.index_line: Asimov's: character-driven SF (1k-20k words), open to slipstream/surreal; no sword & sorcery, no AI-assisted work, 8-10¢/word
asimovs science fiction.name: Asimov's Science Fiction
asimovs science fiction.summary: Asimov's Science Fiction is a long-running, professional-paying SF magazine favoring character-oriented stories set against speculative backdrops, with room for borderline fantasy, slipstream, and surreal fiction but no sword & sorcery or explicit sex/violence. It pays 8-10 cents/word for fiction and $1/line for poetry, does not accept simultaneous submissions, reprints, or AI-assisted writing, and submits via an online system with roughly five-week response times.

details.aesthetic: Long-form work: single long poems, poetic sequences, long short stories, novellas, novel excerpts, long essays, narrative nonfiction, personal essays, belletristic literary criticism (no scholarship), and translations of long works. Also open to music criticism, photography, visual art, comics, and interviews via query. No genre fiction, no YA.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — one submission per reading period only
details.reading_period: Currently closed; unknown when next window opens
details.red_flags: Journal is currently closed with no announced reopening date; no payment to contributors; response times are running beyond the 6-month target; AI-assisted work is strictly rejected and the policy is ideologically firm; previously published work (including on personal websites) is not considered
details.response_time: Up to 6 months, but currently slower than that
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Poetry: ~5–15 pages (no strict limit); Fiction and Essays: 7,500–20,000 words (some flexibility); Translations: follow relevant genre guidelines

at length.index_line: At Length: long-form only (5–15pp poetry, 7.5–20k prose), one sub per period, no pay; currently closed
at length.name: At Length
at length.summary: At Length publishes long-form work across poetry, fiction, essays, and translations, with a strong emphasis on extended, self-contained pieces (roughly 5–15 pages for poetry; 7,500–20,000 words for prose). Submissions are via email with genre noted in the subject line; one submission per reading period is allowed, no previously published work, and no AI-assisted writing. The journal is currently closed, pays no contributors, and response times have been running slower than the stated six-month target.

details.aesthetic: Fiction and poetry that aligns with The Atlantic's published work; writers are directed to familiarize themselves with past issues as the primary guide to fit.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No response policy — silence means rejection, so writers get no confirmation their submission was received or reviewed.
details.response_time: unknown; no response indicates no interest
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

atlanticthe atlantic online.index_line: The Atlantic: top-tier fiction/poetry matching their published pages; year-round, no fee, silence = rejection, no confirmation of receipt
atlanticthe atlantic online.name: The Atlantic/*The Atlantic Online
atlanticthe atlantic online.summary: The Atlantic seeks strong fiction and poetry aligned with their published work, with no stated word limits or formal submission window. Manuscripts must be submitted as Word or PDF via dedicated email addresses. Writers should note that no response means no interest — they only reply if considering a piece.

details.aesthetic: Work that defies pigeonholing and refuses the formulaic; short and flash fiction that is 'haunting' or 'inventive,' smile-inducing poetry, and multimedia electric lit (videos, soundscapes). The sensibility is countercultural and Beat-adjacent—Algonquin Round Table swagger meets digital-age experimentation—with tolerance for banal humor alongside serious craft. Actively anti-mainstream, anti-apathy, anti-censorship.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This text is a 2011 launch announcement; the journal may have changed significantly or gone inactive. No submission guidelines are present. The submishmash link and email listed are likely outdated. Verify current status before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

atticus review.index_line: Atticus Review: genre-busting flash/short fiction, poetry, and multimedia lit—inventive, darkly funny, anti-formulaic (2011 launch; verify active status)
atticus review.name: Atticus Review
atticus review.summary: Atticus Review is a weekly online journal from indie press Atticus Books publishing short fiction, flash fiction, poetry, and multimedia/electric literature with a sensibility tagged 'Six Degrees Left of Literature'—anti-formulaic, genre-busting, darkly humorous, and activist-inflected. It prizes writers who 'eschew the mainstream for the inventive' and favors work with chutzpah, warped humor, and formal experimentation including audio and interactive video. This is a launch announcement from 2011 with no concrete submission mechanics stated.

details.aesthetic: Speculative fiction that defies categorization—too literary for genre mags, too weird for CanLit—including fantasy, soft sci-fi, slipstream, fabulism, magical realism, myth, folklore, dystopia, and dreamy realism; also poetry. Equity-centered, character-driven work preferred. Tales & Feathers (closed 2026) focuses on cozy/slice-of-life fantasy.
details.multiple_submissions: One short story AND up to five poems per call for Augur; priority-call submitters may submit a second time in each category during the July worldwide call
details.reading_period: July 1–15, 2026 (Augur Magazine); Tales & Feathers closed in 2026
details.red_flags: Extremely short reading window (July 1–15 only); AI-generated work results in breach of contract if accepted; no reprints; no previously submitted pieces unless significantly rewritten; detailed 'do not send' content list that could catch writers off guard (punching-down, trauma as plot device, marginalization-swap speculative premise)
details.response_time: By end of October 2026 (query if no response by then)
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must email immediately to withdraw if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 5,000 words for Augur Magazine fiction; up to 2,500 words for Tales & Feathers fiction

augur.index_line: Augur: equity-focused speculative/slipstream fiction & poetry; July 1–15 only, strict no-AI, no trauma-as-plot-device
augur.name: Augur
augur.summary: Augur publishes speculative and literary-boundary-defying fiction (fantasy, sci-fi, slipstream, fabulism, dreamy realism) plus poetry, with a strong equity focus; Augur accepts one short story and up to five poems per submitter, capped at 5,000 words for fiction, during a narrow July 1–15 window only. Writers should note the strict no-AI policy (breach of contract if violated), the 'please don't send' list covering punching-down comedy, trauma-as-plot-device, and stories where non-marginalized characters experience marginalization as a speculative conceit.

details.aesthetic: Speculative science fiction, fantasy, and horror; no derivative stories; horror must have a supernatural element; no reprints, poetry, novel extracts, serials, or AI-generated work.
details.multiple_submissions: One story at a time only
details.reading_period: Feb 1–Sep 30 (Australian writers and subscribers); Mar 1–14 (open to all)
details.red_flags: Previously rejected stories must not be resubmitted; stories must not be publicly available anywhere (personal websites, forums, self-published collections) before or after acceptance until 12 months post-publication; RTF format strictly required; non-subscriber open window is only 14 days per year (Mar 1–14).
details.response_time: Up to 2 months for subscribers; up to 4 months for non-subscribers
details.simultaneous_submissions: Not allowed
details.word_limit: 2000–8000 words (fiction); 500–2000 words (non-fiction)

aurealis.index_line: Aurealis: SF/fantasy/horror (supernatural required), 2000-8000 words; non-subscribers get one 14-day window (Mar 1-14) yearly
aurealis.name: Aurealis
aurealis.summary: Aurealis publishes science fiction, fantasy, and horror short fiction (2000–8000 words) with a speculative bent, rejecting derivative work and horror without a supernatural element; submissions are open to Australian writers and subscribers Feb–Sep, and to everyone Mar 1–14 only. No simultaneous submissions, one story at a time, RTF files only, strict formatting requirements. Non-subscribers face up to 4-month waits, previously rejected stories must not be resubmitted, and stories must not appear publicly anywhere (including personal websites) before acceptance.

details.aesthetic: Nonfiction, fiction, and poetry; writers should read recent issues to understand the magazine's voice before submitting.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Nonfiction requires a two-paragraph pitch only — do not send a complete manuscript.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: 2,200–5,000 words (prose preferred); poetry unspecified

baffler.index_line: Baffler — sharp political/cultural nonfiction plus fiction and poetry; nonfiction by pitch only, no full drafts; pays all contributors
baffler.name: Baffler
baffler.summary: The Baffler publishes nonfiction (pitch only, 2 paragraphs), fiction, and poetry, with prose preferred at 2,200–5,000 words; all contributions are paid. Nonfiction must be pitched rather than submitted as a complete manuscript. No reading period, response time, fee, or simultaneous submission policy is stated.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, short fiction, and creative nonfiction across a wide range of voices and themes; editors want to be 'pleasantly surprised' and select based on merit and the needs of the journal; also runs flash fiction, flash CNF, and prose poem contests.
details.fee: None for non-contest submissions; $8 for contest submissions
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per category per reading period only; submissions in more than one category are permitted
details.red_flags: No AI-generated work accepted; writers must be 18+; do not withdraw and resubmit to make revisions; submissions exceeding word/poem limits or outside accepted genres are declined without review
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; withdraw promptly via Submittable if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 5,000 words for prose; up to 3 poems per submission; additional per-category limits visible on Submittable

baltimore review.index_line: Baltimore Review: poetry/fiction/CNF, no AI-generated work, human-only; closed until Aug 1, 2026
baltimore review.name: Baltimore Review
baltimore review.summary: The Baltimore Review publishes poetry, short fiction, and creative nonfiction selected on merit and fit, with a clear preference for fully human-authored work and no AI-generated content. Non-contest prose is capped at 5,000 words; poets may submit up to three poems per period; no submission fee for general work, $8 for contests. The journal is currently closed (reopens August 1, 2026), enforces a strict one-submission-per-category-per-period rule, and rejects work that exceeds limits or falls outside its genres without review.

details.aesthetic: Thought-provoking poetry and prose by, for, or about the people of Hawaiʻi; work that inspires and connects; no hate speech, stereotypes, exoticization, or discriminatory content.
details.multiple_submissions: Up to 5 poems per author for poetry; no explicit limit stated for prose beyond the word/page cap
details.red_flags: Hard copy mail only—no online submissions accepted; no previously published work; no AI-generated writing; rejection letters only mailed if SASE is included; copyright permissions required for any quoted/lyric material not in the public domain
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify editors immediately by email if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 5,000 words (prose); up to 10 pages / 5 poems (poetry)

bamboo ridge.index_line: Bamboo Ridge — Hawaiʻi-rooted poetry/prose by, for, or about its people; mail-only submissions, no online, postmarked by July 15, 2026
bamboo ridge.name: Bamboo Ridge
bamboo ridge.summary: Bamboo Ridge publishes poetry and prose rooted in Hawaiʻi—by, for, or about its people—with a strong regional and community identity; prose is capped at 5,000 words and poetry at 10 pages/5 poems, with a hard-copy-only postmark deadline of July 15, 2026. Simultaneous submissions are allowed with prompt withdrawal notice, but no online submissions, no previously published work, and no AI-generated writing are accepted. Writers should note that rejection letters are only sent if an SASE is included, and acceptances are notified by email only.

details.aesthetic: unknown
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Wrong site entirely — this is a Writer's Digest craft article, not a journal's submission page. No journal to evaluate.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

bangalore review.index_line: *Bangalore Review — mislabeled: this is a Writer's Digest cover-letter guide, not a journal; skip
bangalore review.name: *Bangalore Review
bangalore review.summary: This is not a literary journal — it is a Writer's Digest article offering advice on writing cover letters for literary journal submissions. No specific journal is described.

details.aesthetic: Original, potent, literarily sound fiction and creative non-fiction with a contemporary feel and strong imaginative distinction; favors gritty realism but open to fantasy, magic realism, slipstream. No tales, fables, reworked fairy tales, vignettes, poetry, literary criticism, or academic pieces.
details.multiple_submissions: one piece at a time; must receive a response before submitting a second
details.red_flags: No payment offered; writers expected to have read 2–3 archive stories before submitting; novel extracts only considered if fully self-contained; do not put story title in email subject line (spam filter risk)
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 5,500 words; CNF: best under 3,000 words, up to 5,000 words considered

barcelona review.index_line: Barcelona Review: gritty realism plus fantasy/slipstream fiction & CNF to 5,500 words; unpaid, one submission at a time
barcelona review.name: *Barcelona Review
barcelona review.summary: The Barcelona Review seeks original, potent short fiction and creative non-fiction with a contemporary literary feel, favoring gritty realism but open to most genres; fiction tops out at 5,500 words and CNF at 5,000, with a 12-week response time year-round. Writers must submit one piece at a time and wait for a response before sending another, and should have read 2–3 stories from the archives before submitting. No payment is offered, novel extracts must be fully self-contained, and poetry is not accepted.

details.aesthetic: Pop-culture-obsessed personal essays, fiction, and poetry with a sharp, humorous sensibility; currently open only for newsletter personal essays (under 1K words on pop-culture obsessions) and book reviews that fit 'Our Whole Thing'.
details.multiple_submissions: One piece at a time; exception: up to five poems may be submitted together as a single document
details.reading_period: Newsletter essays and book reviews: open, ongoing. Print issue, online issues, Writer Camp, conference proposals, book pitches: currently closed.
details.red_flags: Print and online issues are closed, so $50 contributor payment does not apply to currently open categories; book reviews are unpaid; AI-written submissions explicitly rejected; only Word or .rtf files accepted — other formats reduce chances of publication
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; writer must notify promptly if work is accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Under 1,000 words for newsletter essays; up to ~8,000 words general guideline for other work

barrelhouse.index_line: Barrelhouse: witty, pop-culture-obsessed essays/fiction/poetry; print/online closed—only open for sub-1K newsletter essays and book reviews
barrelhouse.name: Barrelhouse
barrelhouse.summary: Barrelhouse publishes pop-culture-inflected personal essays, fiction, and poetry with a witty, irreverent voice; print and online issues are currently closed, but newsletter essays (under 1K words) and book reviews are open. General prose runs up to ~8,000 words; one piece at a time (up to five poems); simultaneous submissions allowed with prompt withdrawal notice; response time around six months. AI-written work is explicitly rejected, and writers should note that only Word/.rtf files are accepted via Submittable.

details.aesthetic: Experimental work across poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, visual art, and cross-genre pieces; values play with language, form, and unconventional subject matter; also welcomes traditional styles and translations (with permission documentation required).
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per genre per reading period
details.red_flags: Current UT Austin students are ineligible; alumni must have graduated at least 3 years before the current open call; previously published contributors must wait 2 years before resubmitting; identifying information must be removed from the document itself.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must email the relevant editor immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction up to 6,000 words; nonfiction up to 5,000 words; poetry: 3–5 poems; visual art: unspecified

bat city review.index_line: Bat City Review: language-forward, form-bending poetry/fiction/CNF/hybrid work; UT Austin students ineligible; opens Aug 15 2025
bat city review.name: Bat City Review
bat city review.summary: Bat City Review publishes poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, art, and cross-genre/hybrid work that experiments with language, form, and unconventional subject matter, alongside traditional styles and translations. Open August 15–September 15 2025; fiction capped at 6,000 words, nonfiction at 5,000; one submission per genre per reading period via Submittable only. UT Austin current students cannot submit, and alumni must wait three years post-graduation; previously published contributors must wait two years before resubmitting.

details.aesthetic: Original literary fiction (flash to short story, up to 7,500 words) and poetry (up to 5 poems); all work must be entirely human-produced, previously unpublished in print or online, and in English.
details.multiple_submissions: fiction: 1 story per submission; poetry: 1 submission of up to 5 poems; must wait for decision before submitting again
details.red_flags: UNO students, faculty, and alumni are ineligible. Must wait 3 months after a rejection before resubmitting—more frequent submissions are automatically declined. AI-composed, revised, or edited work is prohibited and may trigger withdrawal of acceptance even after the fact.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; must notify immediately via Submittable note if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: up to 7,500 words for fiction; up to 5 poems for poetry

bayou magazine.index_line: Bayou Magazine: fiction (flash–7,500 words) and poetry, human-written only, no AI-assisted work; reads Sep 15–Dec 15; UNO affiliates ineligible
bayou magazine.name: Bayou Magazine
bayou magazine.summary: Bayou Magazine publishes poetry and fiction in English, welcoming flash to short-shorts up to 7,500 words, with a strong stance against AI-generated or AI-assisted content. Submissions are open September 15–December 15 via Submittable only; expect up to 5 months for a response. UNO students, faculty, and alumni are ineligible, and resubmitting within 3 months of a rejection will get you declined automatically.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction and nonfiction broadly related to health, healing, illness, mind, and body. Fiction: character-driven, original voices, strong settings; no genre fiction (romance, sci-fi, horror), rarely flash. Nonfiction: essays that go beyond standard illness narrative with creative analysis; no academic discourse or footnotes. Poetry: accessible, vivid, strong narrative; up to three poems.
details.fee: $5 per general submission; waived for current subscribers (subscribing at time of submission also waives fee); hardship waiver available on request
details.multiple_submissions: one submission at a time (up to 3 poems count as one submission); no explicit policy on multiple prose submissions stated
details.red_flags: Submissions closed until September 1, 2026; no genre fiction; no academic essays with footnotes; AI-generated or AI-shaped work prohibited and authorship affirmation required; previously published work (including online) ineligible with strict definition of 'published'
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: up to 5,000 words for fiction/nonfiction (sweet spot 2,500–4,000); poems any length

bellevue literary review.index_line: Bellevue Literary Review: character-driven fiction, essays, and narrative poetry on health/illness/body; no genre fiction; closed until Sept 2026
bellevue literary review.name: Bellevue Literary Review
bellevue literary review.summary: BLR publishes literary work centered on health, healing, illness, mind, and body—favoring character-driven fiction, essays that transcend illness narrative, and accessible poetry with vivid narrative. Prose is capped at 5,000 words; up to three poems per submission; $5 fee (waived for current subscribers). Submissions are closed until September 1, 2026, and the AI-authorship prohibition is strictly stated.

details.aesthetic: Poetry (single poem or group), fiction (short story or flash), and creative nonfiction (essay or flash nonfiction); no stated thematic or stylistic restrictions beyond genre.
details.multiple_submissions: Up to 3 poems, or up to 3 flash pieces, or 1 story/essay per entry fee
details.red_flags: Online submission system only; $15 fee applies; this is a contest, not a standard open submission window; full guidelines only on external site (bhreview.org).
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Up to 1,500 words for flash fiction/nonfiction; up to 4,000 words for stories or essays; poems any length (up to 3 submitted)
