bellingham review.index_line: Bellingham Review contest: poetry, fiction, CNF, no aesthetic stated; $15/entry, March 15 deadline, $1,000 prizes
bellingham review.name: Bellingham Review
bellingham review.summary: Bellingham Review's annual contest awards $1,000 prizes in poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction, with all entries considered for publication. Submit up to 3 poems (any length), flash pieces up to 1,500 words each, or a story/essay up to 4,000 words via online system only, with a $15 entry fee by March 15. This is a contest listing on Poets & Writers, not the journal's own submissions page—visit bhreview.org for complete guidelines.

details.aesthetic: Fiction only—contemporary short stories, both traditional and experimental, on any subject or theme; occasional excerpts; welcomes new and established writers alike.
details.fee: none for standard submissions; contest fee applies for their short story contest
details.multiple_submissions: one story at a time only
details.red_flags: SASE required, implying postal submissions may be primary or required; longer stories explicitly disadvantaged; contest fee is separate and unspecified in amount.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed
details.word_limit: 1 to 60 pages; longer pieces less likely to be accepted

beloit fiction journal.index_line: Fiction only, flash to 60pp (longer disadvantaged); Aug 1–Dec 1; free, SASE suggests postal preferred
beloit fiction journal.name: Beloit Fiction Journal
beloit fiction journal.summary: Beloit Fiction Journal publishes literary short fiction only—traditional and experimental—ranging from flash to sixty pages, with longer pieces at a disadvantage. Reading period is August 1–December 1; one story at a time; simultaneous submissions allowed; response time 3–6 months. Writers should note the SASE requirement (suggesting postal submissions) and that a separate contest fee exists, distinct from the free standard submission.

details.aesthetic: Literary adventure fantasy in secondary-world settings (different zoology, ecology, physical laws, or pre-1930s/alternate Earth history); character-driven stories centered on yearning, with close/limited POV and prose that is lush yet clear; open to steampunk, Weird West, and 'sixguns & sorcery' but not urban fantasy, contemporary settings, science fiction, or traditional fairy-tale/fable narrative voice; dry wit and wry satire welcome, slapstick not; extreme sex/violence capped at R-rated intensity and never involving children.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Does not accept novel excerpts, serials, or reprints (including self-published/Patreon/Kickstarter-released work); no poetry; strict genre boundaries (no urban fantasy, no sci-fi, no modern settings past ~1930s).
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: strongly prefers under 15,000 words; longer considered if exceptional

beneath ceaseless skies.index_line: Beneath Ceaseless Skies — literary adventure fantasy in secondary worlds, close-POV lush prose, no urban fantasy/sci-fi/modern settings, no reprints, <15k words
beneath ceaseless skies.name: Beneath Ceaseless Skies
beneath ceaseless skies.summary: Beneath Ceaseless Skies publishes 'literary adventure fantasy': character-focused stories set in richly imagined secondary worlds (pre-modern, alternate-history, steampunk, or otherwise non-modern), written in lush but clear close-POV prose. It explicitly avoids urban/contemporary fantasy, science fiction, poetry, traditional fairy-tale narration, novel excerpts, and reprints, and favors fresh takes over familiar tropes like elves or tavern openings. Stories also air as an audio fiction podcast alongside the biweekly online issues.

details.aesthetic: Innovative, intelligent, and moving fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry, film writing (submitted via nonfiction category), and cross-genre work; favors writing that is 'simultaneously graceful and reckless'; writers should have familiarity with contemporary literature in their genre.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Current/recent Bennington College students, faculty, and staff are ineligible; alumni and past employees must wait 3 years before submitting. Work must be previously unpublished in print or online, including personal blogs. No unsolicited reviews or interviews accepted.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Prose: up to 30 pages (double-spaced, paginated); poetry: 3–5 poems per submission

bennington review.index_line: Bennington Review: graceful-and-reckless fiction, nonfiction, poetry, cross-genre; no fee; Bennington College affiliates ineligible/wait 3 yrs
bennington review.name: Bennington Review
bennington review.summary: Bennington Review seeks innovative, intelligent, and 'simultaneously graceful and reckless' fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry, and cross-genre work, published twice yearly in print. Reading period is January 5–March 15, 2026; poetry submissions are 3–5 poems, prose up to 30 pages, with a 5–8 month response time. Watch out for the blanket ban on current and recent Bennington College students, faculty, and staff, plus a 3-year waiting period for alumni and past employees.

details.aesthetic: Innovative and reflective short fiction across all genres that plays with form and content, OR traditionally constructed stories with fresh voices and original ideas; strong emphasis on visceral emotional impact and representing LGBTQIA+, BIPOC, disabled, and noncitizen voices. Will not publish work promoting racism, misogyny, homophobia, transphobia, or ableism.
details.multiple_submissions: Allowed up to 2 within any 3-month period; each submission must be a separate email
details.red_flags: Extremely long response time (8–12+ months); student-run journal causes additional delays over summer and between semesters; strict blind-submission formatting required (no author info on document); specific email subject line and file format (.doc or .pdf) required or submission may be mishandled
details.response_time: 8 months to a year (8–12+ months stated in two places)
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: No minimum; no more than 30 pages (double-spaced, 12pt Times New Roman)

berkeley fiction review.index_line: Visceral, form-flexible short fiction (30pp max) prioritizing marginalized voices; free but expect 8-12+ month wait
berkeley fiction review.name: Berkeley Fiction Review
berkeley fiction review.summary: BFR seeks innovative, visceral short fiction across all genres, with particular commitment to minority and marginalized voices; submissions are free, blind, and capped at 30 pages with an 8–12+ month response time. Writers may send up to two submissions per three-month period via email only, in a specific format with blind documents. The multi-tier democratic review process (requiring approval from 30–40+ staff) means a very long wait, and student-run scheduling causes further delays between semesters.

details.aesthetic: Poetry exclusively, any form or length (sonnets, villanelles, free verse, etc.), with the editorial criterion being whether the work makes the reader 'forget they are reading a poem'—i.e., emotionally true and technically accomplished. Current issues lean toward Kentucky and surrounding-region voices, though all strong work is considered. The journal is connected to a working-writers community (Workhorse of Lexington) and prizes honest, well-crafted truth-telling over any single style.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Year-round, but volume closes when 40 poets are selected—can close as early as April; publishes in December
details.red_flags: Volume closes at 40 poets and can fill by April despite year-round reading—submit early in the year to avoid missing the window.
details.response_time: As promptly as possible; no specific timeframe given
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: 1–6 poems per submission; no word/line limit specified

big wing review.index_line: Yearling: Poetry only, Kentucky/Appalachian sensibility, personalized feedback for all—caps at 40 poets/year, can close by April
big wing review.name: Big Wing Review
big wing review.summary: Yearling: A Poetry Journal for Working Writers is an annual Kentucky-based poetry-only journal that distinguishes itself by providing personalized editorial feedback to every submitter. It welcomes any form, style, or length, accepts 1–6 poems per submission, and caps each annual volume at 40 poets—meaning it can fill as early as April for its December publication. Writers seeking a regional Appalachian/Kentucky sensibility alongside a genuinely supportive editorial process will find it worth investigating.

details.aesthetic: Not a journal — this is a CLMP directory page listing calls for submissions from many member literary magazines and presses, ranging from flash horror to poetry in translation to chapbook contests.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This is not a single journal. The writer should follow the individual links to each publisher's own site before drawing any conclusions about guidelines, fees, or aesthetics.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

bigbridgeorg.index_line: Not a journal — CLMP's aggregated calls-for-submissions page; follow links to individual publishers before submitting
bigbridgeorg.name: *Bigbridge.org
bigbridgeorg.summary: This is the CLMP (Community of Literary Magazines and Presses) aggregated calls-for-submissions page, not a single journal — it lists dozens of different member publications seeking work. No single journal's aesthetic, guidelines, or policies can be attributed here; each listing links to a separate publisher with its own requirements.

details.aesthetic: Publishes work addressing the full range of contemporary Black concerns across multiple forms: essays, poetry, fiction, photography, art, and reviews. Emphasizes intellectual rigor ('uncompromised thought'), accessibility ('generous and readable analysis'), and the application of Black genius to twenty-first-century realities. Affiliated with NYU's African American Affairs and Black Visual Culture centers, suggesting an academic but culturally engaged sensibility.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No submission guidelines found in this text; writer should seek the journal's dedicated submissions page before attempting to submit.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

black renaissance noire.index_line: Black Renaissance Noire: essays, poetry, fiction, photography, and art on contemporary Black intellectual and cultural life; rigorous, readable, visually driven
black renaissance noire.name: Black Renaissance Noire
black renaissance noire.summary: Black Renaissance/Renaissance Noire is an NYU-affiliated journal publishing essays, poetry, fiction, photography, art, and reviews centered on contemporary Black intellectual and cultural life, inviting uncompromised thought and generous analysis. The journal is sponsored by the Institute of African American Affairs and the Center for Black Visual Culture, signaling an academic-yet-engaged sensibility with strong visual arts integration. No submission guidelines are present in this text.

details.aesthetic: Fiction: surreal, magical, absurdist, oneiric — work that rejects realism entirely. Poetry: historically and politically grounded, exploring place, colonial/postcolonial bodies, and linguistic change. Comics/Art: visually engaged work that 'witnesses and radically reimagines,' including non-page-based forms (textiles, sculptures, collages); greyscale print only. Strong editorial priority given to writers of color, queer/trans, disabled, immigrant, fat writers, and femmes.
details.fee: $5 per submission; $10 for expedited response; fee waivers available on request for financial hardship; free for incarcerated writers
details.multiple_submissions: do not mix genres in the same submission; may submit to both print and online journals separately
details.reading_period: unknown (active submissions listed but no open/close dates beyond issue-specific deadlines)
details.red_flags: University of Alabama affiliates (current or within past 4 years) are ineligible; past print contributors must wait 3 years to resubmit to print (1 year for online); previously published work not considered
details.response_time: 1–6 months (expedited option available for $10, response within 2 weeks)
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; must disclose at submission and notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 6,000 words; Art/Comics: up to 6 pages total

black warrior review.index_line: Black Warrior Review: surreal/absurdist fiction, politically grounded poetry, boundary-pushing comics/art; priority to marginalized writers; $5 fee
black warrior review.name: Black Warrior Review
black warrior review.summary: Black Warrior Review seeks surreal/speculative fiction, historically and politically grounded poetry, and visually engaged comics/art, with a strong editorial commitment to marginalized voices. Submissions are $5 (fee waivers available), capped at 6,000 words for fiction and 6 pages for art, with a 1–6 month response window. Writers affiliated with the University of Alabama within the past four years are ineligible, and past contributors must wait 1–3 years before resubmitting.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction, poetry, personal essays and self-contained memoir excerpts, translations (with permissions), book reviews of debut/second books published within a year, craft essays, interviews, video essays blending language/image/sound, and sound-based literature pairing voiceover with music or sound design. Prioritizes craft and collective vision; no unsolicited criticism or book reviews in CNF channel.
details.fee: $3 for most categories; currently-enrolled students can email for a waived-fee form
details.multiple_submissions: One prose piece at a time for CNF; up to 5 at a time for video essays and sound-based literature; poetry limit not explicitly stated
details.red_flags: $3 fee applies broadly; no querying before 6 months have passed; strict no-generative-AI policy for video/sound work; book reviews only for first or second books published within the past year
details.response_time: 6 months minimum; longer if submitted just before summer break
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must be indicated as such and Blackbird notified immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Prose up to 8,000 words (query beyond that); poems up to 10 pages (query beyond that); book reviews up to 500 words; craft essays and interviews up to 2,000 words; video/sound submissions up to 12 minutes

blackbird.index_line: Blackbird — polished literary fiction, poetry, CNF, translations, video/sound art; $3 fee, 6-month wait, no querying early
blackbird.name: *Blackbird
blackbird.summary: Blackbird publishes literary fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction (personal essays), translations, book reviews, craft essays, interviews, video essays, and sound-based literature with a strong emphasis on craft and quality across all genres. Submission fees are $3 for most categories; prose over 8,000 words or poems over 10 pages require a query first; response time is six months or longer. Writers should note the $3 fee (students can request a waiver), the strict no-AI policy for video/sound work, and that querying before six months have passed is explicitly discouraged.

details.aesthetic: Fiction of any genre, no genre restrictions; open to authors of all backgrounds and experience levels.
details.fee: none (optional paid feedback at $10 per 1,000 words)
details.multiple_submissions: One at a time; must wait at least one month before submitting a new story after rejection (3 months for a revised version of a rejected piece)
details.reading_period: Open until filled; closes without notice when they have enough stories
details.red_flags: Submission window closes without warning; no Submittable—must submit via email with specific subject line format; AI-written or AI-assisted work not accepted; unsolicited social media submissions ignored
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; notify immediately if accepted elsewhere

blackbriar review.index_line: Blackbriar Review — any-genre fiction, 1,000–6,000 words, email only; closes without notice; no AI-assisted work
blackbriar review.name: *Blackbriar Review
blackbriar review.summary: Blackbriar Review publishes genre fiction of any kind, welcoming all experience levels, with a focus on story over category. Accepts 1,000–6,000 words, no fee, via email only. The submission window closes without notice, and AI-assisted work is explicitly banned.

details.aesthetic: Innovative, experimental, avant-garde poetry and fiction plus literary criticism (companions, studies, histories); rooted in the small-press/Language-poetry lineage with contributors like Anne Waldman, Ron Silliman, Steve McCaffery, Clayton Eschleman, Bill Berkson, Kazim Ali, and Amy King; values formal risk and 'definition-defying' work over commercial appeal.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No paper submissions accepted for poetry; no materials are returned so don't send irreplaceable originals; authors expected to actively market/tour/podcast their own work; no advances paid and royalties only 10% of net receipts, possibly split among contributors.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, explicitly stated as acceptable
details.word_limit: unknown

blazevox.index_line: *BlazeVOX — Avant-garde poetry, fiction, and criticism in the Language-poetry vein; email submissions, no advances, authors expected to self-promote
blazevox.name: *BlazeVOX
blazevox.summary: BlazeVOX is a long-running (est. 2000) online journal and affiliated small press publishing innovative, experimental poetry, fiction, and literary criticism, with a roster of avant-garde and language-adjacent poets like Anne Waldman, Ron Silliman, and Steve McCaffery. Its ethos is unapologetically anti-commercial and formally adventurous—work must, in the editor's words, 'not suck'—and it is currently building out a series championing 'courageous, innovative, definition-defying' women writers. Submissions go straight to the editor by email; the press pays modest royalties on books but no advances, and expects authors to actively self-promote and tour/read their work.

details.aesthetic: Previously unpublished flash fiction, short fiction, creative nonfiction, and poetry; no specific thematic or stylistic focus stated beyond rejecting AI-generated content.
details.multiple_submissions: one fiction or CNF piece per email; 1-3 poems may be submitted together in one email
details.reading_period: year-round for general submissions; themed calls announced periodically
details.red_flags: No payment to contributors; name must not appear anywhere on attachments; AI-generated work is rejected outright.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must be noted in the submission email and editor notified immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

bloom.index_line: BLOOM — Flash, short fiction, CNF, poetry; no stated aesthetic beyond rejecting AI-generated work; free, no payment, year-round
bloom.name: BLOOM
bloom.summary: Bloom publishes flash fiction, short fiction, creative nonfiction, and poetry with no stated aesthetic restrictions beyond a hard rejection of AI-generated work. Submissions are free, sent by email, with a two-week response target and no word limit specified. Writers must strip their name from attachments and notify immediately if a simultaneous submission is accepted elsewhere.

details.aesthetic: Ambitious, exuberant flash fiction, flash creative nonfiction, memoir, essay, and short poetry that offer insight, complicate existing conversations, and enrich understanding of human experience in a diverse world.
details.multiple_submissions: one submission per participant only
details.red_flags: Submissions currently closed; strict eligibility: must self-identify as BIPOC, reside in Minnesota for 6+ months prior, be a US resident or valid taxpayer, and must not have published a first book; MSU Mankato alumni ineligible within 5 years of graduation; split winnings not allowed
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: 750 words max for flash fiction and flash CNF; poetry up to 3 poems in one file, max 5 pages

blue earth review.index_line: Blue Earth Review — MN BIPOC Emerging Writer Award: flash fiction/CNF & short poetry, 750 words; MN residents only, no first book; 2025 closed
blue earth review.name: Blue Earth Review
blue earth review.summary: The MN BIPOC Emerging Writer Award from Blue Earth Review seeks ambitious flash fiction, flash CNF, and short poetry that complicate conversations and illuminate human experience, with strict Minnesota residency and BIPOC identity eligibility requirements. Submissions are capped at 750 words for prose and 5 pages/3 poems for poetry, with one submission per participant and no fee. Writers should note submissions are currently closed for 2025, MSU Mankato alumni must wait 5 years post-graduation, and unpublished-book status is required.

details.aesthetic: Literary, mainstream, and experimental fiction; non-rhyming poetry of all types and topics. Seeks authentic, emotionally moving work; rejects cleverness for its own sake, sentimentality, genre fiction, and novel excerpts.
details.multiple_submissions: Fiction over 3000 words: one story at a time. Fiction under 3000 words: multiple stories allowed, totaling up to 3000 words. Poetry: unknown.
details.red_flags: No payment. Previously published work considered only if published at least one year prior. Must wait one month after a fiction rejection before resubmitting fiction. Writers who violate conduct expectations may be banned.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but writer must promptly notify BLR upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: 100–6000 words. Poetry: unknown.

blue lake review.index_line: Blue Lake Review: literary/mainstream/experimental fiction (100-6000 wds) and non-rhyming poetry; wants authentic, not clever or sentimental; no genre fiction
blue lake review.name: *Blue Lake Review
blue lake review.summary: Blue Lake Review publishes literary, mainstream, and experimental fiction (100–6000 words) and non-rhyming poetry of all types, prioritizing authentic, emotionally genuine work over cleverness or sentimentality—no genre fiction, novel excerpts, or rhyming verse. Simultaneous submissions are allowed with prompt notification; multiple submissions depend on word count (one story at a time over 3000 words; under 3000 words, multiple stories up to 3000 words total). No payment is offered, and writers should wait at least a month after a fiction rejection before resubmitting.

café irreal.summary:
**Aesthetic Focus:** The Cafe Irreal publishes "irreal" fiction — a form of the fantastic that deliberately avoids realistic characterization, resolved plots, and recognizable settings, instead evoking a reality that is constantly undermined; think Kafka, Borges, Lispector, and Kobo Abe, where absurdity functions as normalcy rather than punchline.

**Practical Limits:** Stories must be under 2,000 words with no stated minimum; the journal is a quarterly webzine, though no specific reading periods or response times are mentioned in the available text; submissions are accepted via email only (editors@cafeirreal.com), pasted directly into the body of the message — no attachments accepted.

**Notable Restrictions and Red Flags:** Writers must include name, address, email, and a short bio in the email body, with "submission" in the subject line; translations are welcome; and critically, the journal explicitly does *not* want realistic portrayals, emotional investment in characters, or tidy resolutions — submitting conventional literary fiction or genre fantasy would almost certainly be a mismatch.

details.aesthetic: Regional focus on Appalachia across disciplines; welcomes scholarly articles, critical think pieces, poetry, book/film/music/exhibit reviews, creative nonfiction, photo essays, artwork with artist statements, and interviews with regional figures. Scholarly work should be accessible to interdisciplinary audiences and primary-source-based.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown

details.red_flags: No payment (one contributor copy only); reviews are not accepted unsolicited and self-published works are never reviewed; scholarly articles require a query/abstract first before full submission; AI-generated work is explicitly prohibited; print photo essays are black-and-white only (color accepted for digital outlet only).
details.simultaneous_submissions: Discouraged but considered for poetry; writers must notify if accepted elsewhere. Policy for other genres not stated.
details.word_limit: Scholarly articles: 5,000–12,000 words; book reviews: 700–1,000 words; review essays: 1,000–1,800 words; creative nonfiction: 800–2,500 words; interviews: 4,000–8,000 words; poetry: 3–5 poems

center for appalachian studies.index_line: Appalachian-focused scholarship, CNF, interviews, photo essays; poetry only Jan & Jul; no pay, no AI work
center for appalachian studies.name: Center for Appalachian Studies
center for appalachian studies.summary: Appalachian Journal is a peer-reviewed regional studies journal publishing scholarly articles, poetry, creative nonfiction, reviews, interviews, and photo essays focused on the Appalachian region. It accepts most genres year-round with no fee, but poetry has narrow annual windows (January and July only); word limits vary widely by genre (poetry: 3–5 poems; articles: 5,000–12,000 words; CNF: 800–2,500 words; interviews: 4,000–8,000 words). AI-generated work is explicitly rejected, reviews are by invitation/suggestion only (no unsolicited reviews), and the journal offers no payment—only one contributor copy.

details.aesthetic: Deeply rooted in Indigenous literary and artistic traditions; publishes poetry, fiction, nonfiction, visual art, interviews, and book reviews. Contributors are predominantly Indigenous writers and artists (Cherokee, Diné, Mohawk, Lakota, Kanaka ʻŌiwi, Blackfeet, Mvskoke, and others), with work that centers healing, kinship, land, language, ancestral memory, and decolonial thought. Each issue is organized around a thematic framework — the Winter 2026 issue themes 'release, reimagine, re(cycle)' — giving work a cohesive, curated feel. Tone is reflective and graced rather than experimental or edgy.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown

chapter house formerly mud city.index_line: Chapter House (IAIA): Indigenous-centered fiction, poetry, nonfiction, art on kinship, land, memory, healing; themed issues, community-rooted, not for outsider takes
chapter house formerly mud city.name: *Chapter House (formerly Mud City)
chapter house formerly mud city.summary: Chapter House Journal is the literary publication of the Institute of American Indian Arts (IAIA) in Santa Fe, publishing fiction, poetry, nonfiction, and art with a strong centering of Indigenous voices, nations, and storytelling traditions — contributors are largely Native American, Native Hawaiian, and Indigenous writers from across Turtle Island and the Pacific. The work engages themes of cyclical time, memory, kinship, healing, land, and identity with a reflective, community-oriented sensibility. No submission guidelines were found in this text.

details.aesthetic: Literary poetry, fiction (short story), and essays showcasing strong craft, familiarity with contemporary innovations, and mindfulness of literary traditions; open to broad audiences, genres, styles, and topics.

chariton review.index_line: Chariton Review: craft-focused literary fiction, essays, poetry — likely defunct since 2020; charges submission fees, pays nothing. Avoid.

chautauqua.name: Chautauqua
chautauqua.summary: Chautauqua is a literary journal now based independently at UNCW (formerly tied to the Chautauqua Institution), publishing fiction, essays, and poetry alongside interviews with writers about their personal writing practices, all shaped by an editorial ethos of reflection, dialogue, and community drawn from the Chautauqua philosophy of Arts, Learning, Spirituality, and Leisure. Editorial decisions are made collaboratively by graduate and undergraduate students working with professional editors. The journal is transitioning to a fully online publication and seeks diverse voices, both emerging and established, with a hopeful, welcoming tone.

details.aesthetic: Clear, unique writer's voice; work that reflects an appreciation for the rhythm and music of language; passion and commitment to the art of writing; explores what it means to be human. chicago quarterly review.index_line: Chicago Quarterly Review: voice-driven fiction, essays, poetry, translation prizing language's rhythm; copies only, no cash payment
chicago quarterly review.name: Chicago Quarterly Review
chicago quarterly review.summary: CQR seeks work with a clear, unique voice that illuminates human experience through attention to the rhythm and music of language, across fiction, nonfiction, poetry, translations, and visual art. Prose is capped at 5,000 words; poetry at 3–5 poems per submission; artwork must be black-and-white JPEG only. Previously published work is not accepted, and only one story may be submitted at a time.

details.aesthetic: Experimental and non-traditional work across poetry, fiction, and literary criticism; fiction favors non-traditional narrative; nonfiction focuses on analytical book reviews, commentary essays, interviews, and unconventional prose forms around modern/contemporary literature, poetics, and critical theory — not personal essays or memoir.
details.fee: Small fee for poetry and fiction via Submittable; fee waiver available on request for financial hardship; nonfiction (pitch by email) not mentioned as having a fee
details.multiple_submissions: Fiction: one story or excerpt, or up to five short-shorts in one file; poetry: no explicit cap but 5–20 pages suggested; nonfiction: pitch-based, not specified

details.red_flags: No payment to contributors; personal essays and memoir explicitly unwelcome; nonfiction requires a pitch, not a full submission; previously published work (anywhere, including online) not accepted; do not submit by mail
details.response_time: At least 6 months (do not query before then)
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must note in cover letter and notify promptly if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 5,000 words (one story/excerpt) or up to five short-shorts; poetry: roughly 5–20 pages; nonfiction: 1,500–2,500 words (reviews), 2,500–5,000 words (commentary)

chicago review.index_line: Chicago Review: experimental poetry/fiction/criticism; no memoir or personal essays; nonfiction by pitch only; no pay; 6-month wait
chicago review.name: Chicago Review
chicago review.summary: Chicago Review publishes poetry, fiction, and criticism-focused nonfiction with a preference for experimental, non-traditional work; poetry runs 5–20 pages, fiction up to 5,000 words, nonfiction 1,500–5,000 words via pitch only. Poetry and fiction are open Oct 1–Jun 1 (nonfiction year-round) with a small Submittable fee and a six-month wait before querying. Writers should note they cannot pay contributors, personal essays and memoir are explicitly unwanted, and nonfiction requires a pitch rather than a full submission.

details.aesthetic: Chicago-centric literary journalism and essays; contributors write on identity (race, gender, sexuality), pop culture, and place, often in hybrid or lyric essay forms. The contributor roster skews toward MFA-credentialed Chicago-area writers working in creative nonfiction, essays, and criticism, often engaging race, identity, pop culture, and place. No submission guidelines were found in this text.

details.aesthetic: Jungian psychology nonfiction — completed, well-edited book-length manuscripts only; no essays, dissertations, or works-in-progress. Published under Chiron, innerQuest, and Koa Books imprints.

details.multiple_submissions: unknown

chiron review.summary: Chiron Publications is a Jungian-focused book publisher seeking completed, professionally edited nonfiction manuscripts (no essays, dissertations, or proposals). Manuscripts should be 35,000–90,000 words, double-spaced, Times New Roman 12pt, in Word format, submitted by email with a description and author résumé. Writers should be aware that accepted authors are charged production fees (editing, design, indexing, etc.), making this a hybrid/subsidy publisher rather than a traditional one.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction and poetry with a distinctive voice (lyric, narrative, etc.); nonfiction including memoir, lyric essay, personal essay, nature writing, and literary journalism with emotional depth, crisp language, engaging voice, and strong structure; no theme issues; quality is the guiding criterion.
details.multiple_submissions: One genre at a time; do not resubmit until a response is received
details.red_flags: No AI-generated or AI-assisted work (contract terminated if discovered); no revisions or alterations after submission; no postal mail, email, or student (OSU) submissions; multiple submissions returned with no response if policy violated
details.response_time: 6-9 months; up to 1 year before querying
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately by email if accepted elsewhere and withdraw via online system (fiction/nonfiction) or email (individual poems/flash fictions)
details.word_limit: Flash fiction up to 1,000 words each; other genres rarely exceed 25 pages but no strict cap

cimarron review.index_line: Cimarron Review — literary fiction, poetry, nonfiction favoring distinctive voice over theme; strict no-AI policy, year-round, 6-9 month response
cimarron review.name: Cimarron Review
cimarron review.summary: Cimarron Review seeks literary fiction, poetry, and nonfiction with distinctive voice and emotional depth, favoring work that surprises rather than conforms to theme. Submit 3-6 poems, one story (any length), up to three flash fictions (≤1,000 words each), or one nonfiction piece; no length cap but rarely exceeds 25 pages; year-round via online system only. Watch out for the strict no-AI policy (contract terminated if violated), the ban on resubmitting before hearing back, no revisions after submission, and a 6-9 month response time with a one-year wait before querying.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction, nonfiction, poetry, drama, and translations across print and online (miCRo flash) formats; editors publish specific genre statements; translation from less-translated languages especially welcome; no AI-generated work unless it constitutes a dual creative-critical computational poetics project.
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per calendar year per print genre (unless they have encouraged a previous submission); up to 3 pieces in one file for miCRo; up to 5 poems in one file for poetry
details.reading_period: Print: September 1, December 1, and May 1 (closes when cap is reached); miCRo: nearly year-round except during Schiff Awards entry period (early summer) or if backlog occurs
details.red_flags: Strict one-submission-per-genre-per-calendar-year limit for print; UC affiliates (current/former students, faculty, staff, family) ineligible unless 2+ years removed; 1-year wait required after publication before resubmitting in the same medium; they prefer to publish the piece as submitted and will not consider later author revisions before copyediting; reading periods close at a cap with no advance notice of when that will happen
details.response_time: Typically 6 months; do not query until after 1 year
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; withdraw prose immediately if accepted elsewhere; notify them if individual poems are accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 10,000 words; literary nonfiction: under 5,000 words preferred (longer considered); miCRo prose/nonfiction/hybrid: 500 words max; miCRo poetry: 32 lines or less; poetry: up to 5 poems / 10 manuscript pages; miCRo drama: ~3 minutes in performance

cincinnati review.index_line: Cincinnati Review: fiction/nonfiction/poetry/drama/translation plus miCRo flash; 1 submission/genre/year; opens Sep/Dec/May, caps fast
cincinnati review.name: Cincinnati Review
cincinnati review.summary: The Cincinnati Review publishes literary fiction, nonfiction (preferring under 5,000 words), poetry, drama, translations, and flash work (miCRo), with a strong editorial voice and genre-specific standards; print submissions open only in September, December, and May (capped), while miCRo is nearly year-round; writers should note the strict one-submission-per-genre-per-calendar-year rule, the one-year cooldown after publication, UC affiliation restrictions, and a firm stance against AI-generated work.

details.aesthetic: Science fiction and fantasy in any subgenre (hard SF, folkloric/contemporary/surreal fantasy, translations welcome); strong emphasis on prose quality with no separation of style and substance; stories must work equally well in text and audio formats. Extensive list of hard-sell tropes including zombies, sexy vampires, pun-based humor, RPG adventures, and trunk stories.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed within seven days of a rejection; no resubmission of rejected stories
details.red_flags: Strict AI-writing ban with permanent ban as penalty; no simultaneous submissions; no horror; extensive hard-sell trope list that will trip up many genre writers; online submission system only, no email or mail.
details.response_time: Typically under two days; queries only after two weeks
details.simultaneous_submissions: Not allowed
details.word_limit: 1000–22,000 words, no exceptions

clarkesworld.index_line: Clarkesworld: SF/F, prose-forward and audio-ready; no horror, extensive hard-sell trope list, strict no-AI policy, 14¢/word
clarkesworld.name: Clarkesworld
clarkesworld.summary: Clarkesworld publishes science fiction and fantasy short fiction (no horror, but dark SF/F okay) with a strong emphasis on prose quality, audio suitability, and rigor; stories must be 1000–22,000 words, pay is 14¢/word, and response time is typically under two days. Simultaneous submissions are not allowed, and there is a detailed and extensive list of hard-sell tropes to avoid. Writers should note the strict ban on AI-assisted writing, which can result in a permanent submission ban.

details.aesthetic: Quarterly lit mag publishing fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, craft essays (quirky, personal, non-academic, 800–2000 words), and book reviews of recent small/indie press titles including chapbooks and novellas. Welcomes translations (with author permission or public domain). Values diverse human voices and specific, personal perspectives.
details.fee: $5 (waivable on request via email, no explanation required)
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: AI-generated or AI-assisted work is rejected outright; no email or postal submissions accepted—Subfolio portal only; previously published work not considered (personal blog posts may be an exception); book review pitches require direct email to a named editor, not a submission form
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with immediate notification if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown (craft essays: 800–2000 words; no word limit stated for other genres)

cleaver.index_line: Cleaver — fiction/poetry/CNF/craft essays/indie-press reviews; wants quirky, specific human voices, not academic; AI writing rejected outright; $5 fee waivable
cleaver.name: *Cleaver
cleaver.summary: Cleaver is a quarterly literary magazine publishing fiction, poetry, essays, craft essays, and book reviews (focusing on small/indie presses), with a strong preference for distinct human voices and specific, quirky perspectives over academic work. Submissions are year-round via Subfolio only, with a $5 fee (waivable on request), and craft essays should run 800–2000 words. AI-generated or AI-assisted work is categorically rejected, and previously published work is not considered (with a narrow exception for personal blogs).

details.aesthetic: Voice-driven poetry and prose with purpose and point; genre writing welcome if it transcends plot/world-building. Hard sells: hard end rhyme, heavy abstraction, archaic syntax inversions, and bland or eventless prose. Admired writers include Amy Hempel, Denis Johnson, Lydia Davis, Barry Hannah, Flannery O'Connor, Richard Siken, and similar.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Currently closed; will reopen first to past submitters with delayed responses, then more broadly (timing unspecified)
details.red_flags: Submissions are closed with no firm reopening date; backlog is explicitly noted as large; reopening will be tiered, prioritizing past submitters first—new submitters may wait significantly longer
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, with timely notification via Submittable note if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

coastal shelf.index_line: Voice-driven poetry/prose like Hempel, Denis Johnson, Lydia Davis; no rhyme or abstraction—closed, large backlog, past submitters prioritized on reopening
coastal shelf.name: Coastal Shelf
coastal shelf.summary: Coastal Shelf publishes poetry and prose with a strong voice and clear purpose, favoring writers in the vein of Amy Hempel, Denis Johnson, and Lydia Davis—avoiding hard end rhyme, abstraction, and plotless genre writing. Submissions are currently closed, with reopening planned first for past submitters, then more broadly once their backlog clears. Simultaneous submissions are allowed with timely notification, and blind reading means no author name in the file.

details.aesthetic: Poetry and fiction; published work ranges from surreal humor and pop-culture nostalgia to quiet domestic realism and lyric compression — voice-driven, specific, often surprising in register.
details.fee: Free from Sept 15; $3 from Oct 15; waived for BIPOC Writers project in November
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — one submission per reading period only
details.reading_period: Opens September 15 (free) and October 15 (paid $3); November is exclusive to BIPOC Writers project (fee waived); closes end of academic year — check Twitter/Instagram for current status
details.red_flags: Do not withdraw a submission partially — only full withdrawal is permitted; no email or postal submissions (exception: incarcerated writers); Submittable only.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately via Submittable if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 5000 words total (1 story or up to 3 flash); Poetry: 3–5 poems per submission

cola formerly yemassee.index_line: Cola (ex-Yemassee): eclectic poetry/fiction, surreal humor to lyric grief; one submission per period; free Sept 15, $3 Oct 15, BIPOC window Nov
cola formerly yemassee.name: *Cola (formerly Yemassee)
cola formerly yemassee.summary: Cola publishes poetry and fiction with a lively, eclectic voice spanning humor, grief, and the everyday bizarre. Free submissions open September 15, paid ($3) October 15, with a BIPOC-exclusive window in November; fiction is capped at 5000 words and poets submit 3–5 poems per period. Writers may only submit once per reading period and must not withdraw partial submissions if a piece is accepted elsewhere.

details.aesthetic: War and military service impacts beyond combat: reintegration, homecoming, exile, injury, loss, home front, discharge, military/civilian divide — across poetry, fiction, CNF, and visual art. Seeks work that translates these experiences in new or unexpected ways.
details.multiple_submissions: May submit in multiple genres simultaneously, but must wait for a response in one genre before sending another submission in the same genre; authors must wait one year after publication before submitting new work
details.reading_period: Year-round; deadlines March 1 (spring issue) and September 1 (fall issue)
details.red_flags: No previously published poetry, fiction, or CNF accepted; previously published visual art is fine. Authors published by Collateral must wait one year before submitting again. Volunteer-run on academic timelines, so response times may vary.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately if work is accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 5000 words for fiction and CNF; poetry in batches of 1–5 poems totaling no more than 10 pages

collateral journal.index_line: Collateral: poetry/fiction/CNF/art on war's aftermath — reintegration, homecoming, military/civilian divide, not combat itself
collateral journal.name: *Collateral Journal
collateral journal.summary: Collateral publishes poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and visual art exploring the impact of war and military service beyond combat — reintegration, homecoming, loss, the military/civilian divide, and related themes, with a push toward fresh perspectives. Fiction and CNF cap at 5000 words; poetry goes in batches of 1–5 poems (max 10 pages); deadlines are March 1 (spring) and September 1 (fall), with year-round reading and a 4–6 month response window. No previously published prose or poetry; simultaneous submissions are fine but notify immediately if taken, and authors must wait one year after publication before submitting again.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction and personal essays with contemporary themes; original, idiosyncratic characters and distinctive language. Poetry (no further style restrictions stated). No flash fiction or flash nonfiction. Translations accepted with permission proof.
details.multiple_submissions: Only one story or essay at a time; must wait for a response before submitting again
details.reading_period: Fiction & poetry: Aug 1 – Mar 31; Nonfiction: year-round; Book reviews: Aug 1 – Apr 30
details.red_flags: CSU faculty (current or emeritus), staff, and students are ineligible; CSU alumni must wait 3 years post-graduation. Writers published in CR within the last 2 years must refrain from submitting. Foreign nationals on B1/WB, B2/WT, H-1B, or F-1 visas cannot receive payment. Submissions near winter break or end of reading period may face significantly longer response times.
details.response_time: ~4 months (sometimes quicker); slower during winter break and near end of reading period
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but writer must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction and nonfiction: generally 15–25 manuscript pages; no flash accepted. Poetry: unknown.

colorado review.index_line: Colorado Review: literary fiction/essays with idiosyncratic voice, 15-25pp, no flash; CSU affiliates ineligible
colorado review.name: Colorado Review
colorado review.summary: Colorado Review publishes literary fiction, personal essays, and poetry with contemporary themes, favoring original voice and idiosyncratic characters; fiction/poetry is accepted August 1–March 31, nonfiction year-round, with a ~4-month response time. Submissions are online only via Submittable; no flash fiction or flash nonfiction; one piece at a time. Watch out for the two-year embargo if previously published there, and strict CSU affiliation restrictions (faculty, staff, students, and recent alumni ineligible).

details.aesthetic: All varieties of speculative fiction (alternate history, high fantasy, hard SF, dark fantasy) with solid characters and plot; the speculative element must comment on the world/society, not merely entertain. Flash welcome if fully plotted. Present tense accepted but lower acceptance rate.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed (no more than 5 stories within any 30-day period)
details.red_flags: No simultaneous submissions and no reprints are strict rules. Yahoo email addresses routinely fail to receive their replies — use an alternative. AI-authored stories rejected outright. Payment via PayPal only, which may be a problem for writers in unsupported countries.
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed
details.word_limit: Up to 10,000 words (preferred 500–5,000); novellas up to 20,000 words serialized

colored lens.index_line: Speculative fiction (SF/fantasy/alt-history) where the premise must comment on society, not just entertain; no reprints/sims; fast 1-week replies
colored lens.name: The Colored Lens
colored lens.summary: The Colored Lens publishes speculative fiction (alternate history, fantasy, hard SF, dark fantasy) that comments on the real world, with strong plot fundamentals required and present tense a harder sell. Stories up to 10,000 words (preferred 500–5,000), novellas to 20,000 serialized; response within a week via Google Form. No simultaneous submissions, no reprints, no AI-authored work, and Yahoo email addresses cause delivery problems.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, flash fiction, short fiction, essays, op-eds, translations (any language; especially strong in Spanish, Italian, French, Korean, Russian, Polish, Japanese, Mandarin, Hebrew, Arabic), and cover art/visual work. No stated thematic or stylistic preference beyond broad literary scope.
details.multiple_submissions: One genre at a time; must wait for a decision before submitting again
details.reading_period: Closed now (Spring 2026); reopens August 2026 for Fall 2026 issue
details.red_flags: Submissions not adhering to guidelines are deleted unread with no response; no payment to contributors; name must not appear anywhere in the document
details.response_time: Within 5 months; query permitted after 3 months
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify in the same email chain if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Flash fiction: under 1,000 words each (up to 3 pieces); short fiction: under 3,000 words; prose total not to exceed 3,000 words

columbia review.index_line: Columbia Review: poetry, flash/short fiction, essays, translations, no theme; strict format-or-deleted; closed until Aug 2026
columbia review.name: Columbia Review
columbia review.summary: The Columbia Review publishes poetry, prose (flash and short fiction), translations, cover art, and essays/reviews/op-eds, with no Columbia affiliation required and blind judging. Limits are 5 poems, up to 3 flash pieces under 1,000 words each, or one short fiction piece under 3,000 words; one genre per submission. Submissions not following guidelines are deleted unread without response, and writers must wait for a decision before resubmitting.

details.aesthetic: Strong sense of place across stories, essays, poems, translations, and dispatches; setting must be crucial to character, narrative, mood, and language. Discourages conventional travelogues that report on foreign experiences without engaging larger themes. Actively seeks writers from Black, Indigenous, LGBTQIA+, disabled, immigrant, and other underrepresented communities.
details.fee: none (subscribers submit free year-round; no fee mentioned for general submissions)
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Stories, essays, poetry, translations: March 1–June 1 and September 1–December 1; dispatches: year-round; subscribers: year-round for free
details.red_flags: Email and paper submissions are not read and not returned—Submittable only. Images/art not currently accepted. Longer response times explicitly acknowledged due to multi-read process.
details.response_time: unknown (notes longer wait times due to 3-read process)
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

common the.index_line: The Common: place-driven fiction, essays, poetry, translations, dispatches—setting shapes character; no travelogues; Submittable only, no email/paper
common the.name: Common, The
common the.summary: The Common publishes place-driven fiction, essays, poetry, translations, and dispatches where setting is integral to character and narrative, actively welcoming underrepresented writers. General submissions are open March 1–June 1 and September 1–December 1, with subscribers able to submit year-round for free. Writers should avoid conventional travelogues and note that all submissions must go through Submittable—email and paper submissions are explicitly rejected and ignored.

details.aesthetic: Catholic lay intellectual tradition — essays on religion, politics, and culture; original fiction and poetry; book reviews. The sensibility is serious, humanistic, and ecumenical within a broadly Christian framework. Staff backgrounds include philosophy, history, theology, and MFA programs, suggesting openness to literary and academic writing alike. Published pieces visible here include personal essays and cultural criticism.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No submission guidelines found in this text; writer should seek a dedicated submissions page before querying.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

commonweal.index_line: Commonweal: Catholic lay intellectual essays, criticism, fiction, and poetry on religion, politics, and culture; serious, ecumenical, humanistic tone
commonweal.name: Commonweal
commonweal.summary: Commonweal is a long-running (founded 1924) Catholic lay intellectual magazine publishing essays, fiction, poetry, and cultural criticism from a perspective rooted in Catholic Christian tradition but editorially independent of the Church hierarchy. It is serious, scholarly in tone, and oriented toward public affairs, theology, and culture; contributors include academics, journalists, and literary writers. No submission guidelines were found in this text.

details.aesthetic: Science fiction only (no fantasy); stories should illustrate an interesting concept, be engaging, and explain the science/technology clearly; preference for technologically optimistic or advancement-focused narratives over post-apocalyptic/dystopian; scientifically plausible, self-consistent, and technically detailed when appropriate.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Submissions are currently closed — no open window is given, so the writer must check back later before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown

compelling science fiction.index_line: Hard SF with clear science and optimistic, progress-minded futures over dystopia; 1k-10k words; CLOSED to submissions
compelling science fiction.name: Compelling Science Fiction
compelling science fiction.summary: Compelling Science Fiction wants hard SF that balances an interesting concept, narrative engagement, and clear scientific explanation, with a stated preference for optimistic/progress-oriented futures over dystopian or post-apocalyptic ones. Stories must be 1,000–10,000 words; reprints accepted at 1 cent/word vs. 8 cents/word for originals. Submissions are currently closed, so there is no point submitting now.

details.aesthetic: Poetry-focused, valuing originality, intelligence, courage, irreverence, and humanity; playful, self-aware editorial voice (issue titles chosen 'for our own amusement'); selection based on merit and taste rather than theme; no interest in AI-assisted writing of any kind.
details.fee: none noted for magazine submissions; unknown for book prizes
details.multiple_submissions: send 3-5 poems per submission
details.reading_period: unknown for general submissions; book prizes: Minds on Fire Open Book Prize Aug 1-Nov 3, 2026, Marystina Santiestevan First Book Poetry Prize Apr 1-Jul 7, 2026
details.red_flags: Not currently accepting fiction; postal submissions require SASE or manuscripts are recycled; all correspondence may be published in whole or in part; strict no-AI policy.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown, but explicitly asks to be notified immediately to withdraw if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown (submit 3-5 poems)

conduit.index_line: Conduit: poetry only (fiction closed), wants originality/irreverence over theme fit; pays in copies, no AI-assisted work
conduit.name: Conduit
conduit.summary: Conduit seeks previously unpublished poetry with originality, intelligence, courage, irreverence, and humanity, favoring merit and idiosyncratic taste over any thematic fit; fiction submissions are currently closed. It pays only in contributor copies, and its sister press runs two $1,500 book prizes judged respectively by Bob Hicok and the Conduit editorial board.

details.aesthetic: Short fiction in any style or genre; poetry; visual art and photography — international work, print-focused, no stated thematic restrictions.
details.multiple_submissions: poetry allows up to 3 poems per submission; fiction limit not explicitly stated beyond word count
details.red_flags: No response means rejection — writers will not hear back if their work is declined, so there is no way to follow up or know definitively after 3 months without reaching out.
details.response_time: within 3 months, but only if accepting the work
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: up to 5,000 words (fiction); up to 50 lines per poem, max 3 poems

confingo.index_line: Confingo: print-only fiction/poetry/art, any style, high production values; silence at 3 months means rejection
confingo.name: Confingo
confingo.summary: Confingo is a print-only biannual publishing short fiction (any style/genre), poetry, and art from around the world with an emphasis on quality production. Stories up to 5,000 words, max three poems up to 50 lines each; artwork must be high-res A5-ready. They only respond if accepting work (within three months), so no reply means a rejection.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction (genre fiction accepted if it has literary merit or transcends/challenges genre), poetry, personal essays, cultural/political essays, and self-contained memoir sections. Quality of writing, thought, and imagination are the stated criteria.
details.multiple_submissions: One story or nonfiction piece per submission; up to five flash fiction pieces; up to five poems per submission
details.red_flags: U.S. writers must mail non-poetry submissions with SASE — e-mail from U.S. writers is deleted; submissions received outside the Sep 15–Apr 15 reading period are returned or deleted unread; no responses to queries; double spaces after periods explicitly flagged as a problem
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must be noted in cover letter; notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 7,200 words (one piece) or flash fiction up to 500 words per piece (up to five pieces); nonfiction: 1,500–5,000 words; poetry: up to five poems

confrontation.index_line: Confrontation: literary fiction/essays/poetry, genre-with-merit ok; US writers must mail, no e-mail; reads Sep 15–Apr 15 only
confrontation.name: Confrontation
confrontation.summary: Confrontation publishes literary fiction (including genre fiction with literary merit), poetry, and personal/cultural/political essays and memoir excerpts. Stories up to 7,200 words; nonfiction 1,500–5,000 words; up to five poems per submission; reading period September 15–April 15 only. U.S. writers must submit non-poetry by postal mail with SASE; e-mail submissions from U.S. writers are deleted without response, and submissions outside the reading period are also discarded unread.

details.aesthetic: Innovative poetry, fiction, essays, hybrid and other experimental writings; issue 86 themed around rites of passage (ceremonies, milestones, rituals, religious and secular transitions across a lifetime).
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Partial submission withdrawals are strongly discouraged; do not query before 8 months have passed; previously unpublished work only.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but writer must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

conjunctions.index_line: Conjunctions: innovative/experimental fiction, poetry, essays, hybrid work; issue 86 on rites of passage, June 5–July 5 window, $4 fee, 6–8mo response
conjunctions.name: Conjunctions
conjunctions.summary: Conjunctions publishes innovative poetry, fiction, essays, and hybrid writing; issue 86 is themed around rites of passage with a one-month Submittable window (June 5–July 5). Fee is $4 per submission; response time is 6–8 months. Partial withdrawals are strongly discouraged, and writers must notify immediately if work is accepted elsewhere.

details.aesthetic: Literary work centered on war, geopolitical violence, and their human consequences; includes personal and critical essays, narrative nonfiction, interviews, all forms of poetry, short fiction, flash fiction, excerpts, translations, reviews, and visual art/graphic narratives; contributor list includes veterans, war writers, and literary translators (Phil Klay, Brian Turner, Elliot Ackerman, Peter Balakian).
details.multiple_submissions: Up to three poems per submission; other genres not specified beyond one submission per period implied
details.reading_period: Spring (Jan 15 - Apr 15) and Fall (Jul 15 - Oct 15); translations open year-round
details.red_flags: Zero-tolerance AI policy—suspected AI-generated work triggers review via AI-detection software and may result in permanent ban; reviews are primarily solicited, with only pitches open to outside writers.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Fiction shorts/excerpts under 5,000 words, flash under 1,000 words; nonfiction under 4,000 words; reviews 1,500-3,000 words; poetry up to three poems per submission

consequence.index_line: Consequence: war and geopolitical violence across all genres, pays writers; zero-tolerance AI policy, reviews mostly solicited
consequence.name: Consequence
consequence.summary: Consequence Forum publishes poetry, fiction, nonfiction, translation, reviews, and visual art that address the consequences of war and geopolitical violence, appearing in its print journal, website, or Substack. It pays contributors across all genres, runs biannual reading periods, and has published writers like Phil Klay, Brian Turner, and Peter Balakian, reflecting a literary war-and-conflict-focused sensibility.

details.aesthetic: Cross-genre work that defies traditional forms; fiction that reads like poetry and resists conventional story structure (preferred 1,500 words or less, short-shorts encouraged); poetry with plurality of meaning and dual reverberation of beauty and concern, including prose poems; lyrical, narrative commentary (creative nonfiction/essay) that delivers meaning through art rather than exposition.
details.multiple_submissions: No more than three poems per submission; no limit stated for fiction or commentary
details.red_flags: Payment for book reviews is not guaranteed (depends on fundraising); poetry is highly competitive with only a very small percentage accepted; no explicit simultaneous submission policy stated.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: 1,500 words or less preferred for fiction; no word limit stated for other genres

contrary.index_line: Contrary: cross-genre, category-defying work—lyrical fiction under 1,500 words, plural-meaning poetry, art-driven commentary; no exposition-heavy prose
contrary.name: *Contrary
contrary.summary: Contrary is a quarterly online journal seeking cross-genre work that defies category—lyrical, poetic fiction (preferably under 1,500 words), contrary poetry with plural meaning, and art-driven commentary akin to creative nonfiction. Submit up to three poems per issue; fiction skews short. Note that payment for book reviews is not guaranteed and depends on fundraising.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, essays, and translation folios; values unique individual creative expression; longer prose must earn its length; no AI-generated work.
details.multiple_submissions: 4–6 poems, OR one story, OR three flash pieces, OR one essay at a time; wait at least 6 months after a response before resubmitting.
details.red_flags: International writers have 30% tax withheld upfront from all payments, beyond the journal's control. Submitting triggers addition to their mailing list.
details.response_time: Within 12 weeks, though can be longer especially in spring; do not query until at least 3 months have passed.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere.
details.word_limit: No length restrictions for prose, but longer pieces must justify their length; translation intro essay 800–1200 words.

copper nickel.index_line: Copper Nickel: poetry/fiction/essays/translation valuing distinct individual voice; pays $30/page; no AI work; reads Aug–Dec, Jan–Mar
copper nickel.name: Copper Nickel
copper nickel.summary: Copper Nickel publishes poetry, fiction, essays, and translation folios rooted in individual creative expression, paying $30/printed page with per-piece minimums and maximums. Reading periods run August 15–December 15 and January 15–March 1; submit 4–6 poems, one story, three flash pieces, or one essay at a time. Generative AI work is explicitly rejected, and international writers face a 30% upfront tax withholding on payments.

details.aesthetic: Speculative fiction (science fiction, fantasy, horror), poetry, and art with a literary-genre sensibility. Contributor profiles reference mythic, psychological, and eldritch themes consistent with the journal's name; published authors also appear in Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Lady Churchill's Rosebud Wristlet, PodCastle, and Interzone, suggesting work that values craft and imaginative depth over purely commercial genre fare.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Submission portal requires creating an account before submitting; guidelines page exists but its content was not captured here—verify all mechanics before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown

cosmic roots and elderich stories.index_line: Cosmic Roots & Eldritch Shores: literary-leaning SF/F/horror, poetry & art; contributors also in Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Interzone, PodCastle; account required to submit
cosmic roots and elderich stories.name: Cosmic Roots and Elderich Stories
cosmic roots and elderich stories.summary: Cosmic Roots & Eldritch Shores publishes speculative fiction, poetry, and art—its contributor bios signal a community of genre-serious writers appearing in venues like Beneath Ceaseless Skies, PodCastle, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Galaxy's Edge, and Interzone, suggesting a taste for literary-leaning SF/F and horror. Contributors span academic and workshop backgrounds (Odyssey, MFA programs) alongside working short-fiction professionals. Submission mechanics are not detailed in the available text; writers should check the full guidelines before submitting.

details.aesthetic: Original, unpublished poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction; work that shifts between deep meditation and startling crystallization, tackling both large themes (climate change, the sublime) and the intensely personal.

crab creek review.index_line: Crab Creek Review: poetry/fiction/CNF spanning meditative to crystalline, personal to sublime; free; tiny Sep 15–Oct 15 window, caps at 300 subs
crab creek review.name: Crab Creek Review
crab creek review.summary: Seattle-based woman-run journal publishing original poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction with a broad aesthetic range (personal to expansive, meditative to crystalline). Reading period is brief—Sep 15 to Oct 15—or until a 300-submission Submittable cap is hit, so early submission is critical. No fee; payment is contributor copies only.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction, poetry, essay, and memoir; sometimes theme-based issues — specific aesthetic preferences not described on this page
details.multiple_submissions: unknown

crab orchard review.summary: Crab Orchard Review is a literary magazine affiliated with the MFA program at Southern Illinois University Carbondale, publishing fiction, essay, memoir, and poetry, sometimes with themed calls for submissions. The reading period listed is Feb. 15 – Apr. 1. Most submission details are not available on this page and writers must check the magazine's own website for current guidelines.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction and creative nonfiction where craft elements are central; craft/critical essays examining fiction or CNF technique; interviews with fiction and CNF writers focused on craft. No poetry criticism, no personal essays submitted to the craft category.
details.multiple_submissions: one piece per genre at a time only; you may have one fiction piece, one CNF piece, and one craft piece under consideration simultaneously

details.word_limit: Flash fiction/CNF up to 1,000 words; short fiction/CNF up to 6,000 words; craft and critical essays 1,500–2,500 words

craft.index_line: *CRAFT — Craft-forward fiction/CNF (flash to 6,000 words) plus craft essays and process interviews; no fee, year-round; strict no-AI policy
craft.name: *CRAFT
craft.summary: CRAFT publishes literary fiction and creative nonfiction with a strong emphasis on craft elements, plus craft/critical essays and interviews about the writing process. Flash up to 1,000 words, short fiction/CNF up to 6,000 words, craft essays 1,500–2,500 words; no submission fee; open year-round. Writers should note the strict no-AI policy (auto-declined), a 3-month resubmission wait after a decline in creative categories, and a 3-month exclusivity window post-publication.

details.aesthetic: Memorable and energetic fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and artwork from creators with diverse, unique backgrounds.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Aug 1 – Oct 31; Jan 2 – Apr 1; BIPOC free period Jul 1–31

cream city review.name: Cream City Review
cream city review.summary: Cream City Review publishes fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and artwork from diverse, broad-ranging creators with an emphasis on memorable and energetic work. General submissions open August 1–October 31 and January 2–April 1, with a free BIPOC-specific window in July; response time is about 8 months. Writers should note that summer processing is explicitly slower, so expect delays beyond the already long 8-month window if submitting near that period.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and visual art for a print literary journal; specific aesthetic preferences not detailed on this page.

cut the.index_line: CutBank: poetry/fiction/CNF/art, free general window Sep 15–Feb 1; contests $20, no open calls now
cut the.name: Cut, The
cut the.summary: CutBank publishes poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and visual art for a print journal, with a general reading window of September 15–February 1; contests (poetry, fiction, CNF, chapbook) run December 1–February 1 or January 1–May 31 with $20 entry fees and $500–$1000 prizes. No simultaneous submission policy, word limits, or response times are stated on this page. Writers should note there are currently no open calls, and CutBank strongly recommends reading past issues before submitting.

details.aesthetic: Serious literary work across poetry, fiction, and CNF with a Northwestern/regional flavor grounded in place and landscape, but not provincially so. The editorial staff's own work trends toward personal essay, experimental nonfiction, nature writing, and character-driven fiction. The magazine's legacy names (Kittredge, Hugo, Erdrich, Welch, Heaney, Bender) suggest work that is both formally accomplished and emotionally resonant, comfortable with both lyric and narrative modes.

cutbank.name: Cutbank
cutbank.summary: CutBank is a University of Montana literary magazine founded in 1973, publishing poetry, fiction, and literary nonfiction twice yearly in print, with a global scope but regional (Montana/Western) bias and a strong history of featuring both established and emerging writers. Contributors and editors reflect an MFA program sensibility; published alumni include Louise Erdrich, Seamus Heaney, Aimee Bender, and Chris Offutt. Submission mechanics are not detailed on this page.

details.aesthetic: Socially and politically engaged work addressing racism, sexism, homophobia, xenophobia, climate change, immigration, and environmental justice; poetry (Joy Harjo Poetry Contest), nonfiction (Barry Lopez Nonfiction Contest), and short fiction (Rick DeMarinis Short Story Contest); resistance writing, Indigenous language, and wilderness themes valued.

cutthroat.index_line: Cutthroat: socially/politically engaged poetry, fiction, nonfiction on justice, race, climate; reopened Aug 2026 but badly backlogged, expect slow replies
cutthroat.name: *Cutthroat
cutthroat.summary: Cutthroat publishes socially engaged poetry, fiction, and nonfiction with a focus on equity, justice, environmental issues, and voices of POC, LGBTQ+, women, and immigrants. Reading period reopened August 1, 2026; submissions go through Submittable, with named contests for poetry, nonfiction, and short fiction. Writers should note the journal is recovering from staff health issues and explicitly asks for patience with delayed responses.

details.aesthetic: Death and everything surrounding it—afterlives, psychopomps, mourning, underworlds, death personified, cultural funeral rites—across all genres (horror, litfic, slipstream, fantasy, sf, hist-fic, etc.); worldwide and multicultural perspectives strongly encouraged; hard nos include zombies, vampires, demons, Lovecraft, murder-as-plot-end, weird West, steampunk, military fiction, and stories opening with a character waking up.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — one submission at a time; must wait 7 days after a rejection before resubmitting
details.reading_period: Varies by category and month; poetry open July 1–21 and Sept 1–21; fiction open Oct 1–31 (2026 schedule); other windows TBD or closed—subscribe to author newsletter for announcements.

details.response_time: ~2 weeks; longer may indicate second-round hold
details.simultaneous_submissions: Not allowed — must wait until a story is withdrawn or rejected elsewhere before submitting
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 5,000 words (hard limit); novelettes 7,500–17,500 words in a special October window. Nonfiction: 1,000–4,000 words. Poetry: up to 3 poems per submission.

deadlands.index_line: The Deadlands: death-themed fiction/nonfiction/poetry, any genre; no zombies/vampires/Lovecraft; narrow seasonal windows, 10¢/word
deadlands.name: The deadlands
deadlands.summary: The Deadlands publishes death-themed fiction, nonfiction essays, and poetry from a worldwide, multicultural perspective across all genres (litfic, fantasy, horror, sf, etc.), with strong interest in marginalized voices. Fiction runs up to 5,000 words at 10¢/word; nonfiction essays $100 flat (1–4k words); poetry $50/poem (up to 3 poems); response time is roughly two weeks. No simultaneous or multiple submissions; no AI-generated work; no zombies/vampires/Lovecraft/murder-as-ending/weird West/steampunk/military; stories must be unpublished originals (blogs and Patreon count as prior publication).

details.aesthetic: L'art pour l'art focus on poetry (all/most forms, experimental and literary styles) and nonfiction (criticism, essays, articles) covering literature/books, music, and visual arts — theory, analysis, and general coverage; open to experimental and literary styles.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown

decadent review.index_line: Decadent Review: l'art pour l'art poetry and criticism/essays on lit, music, art — DEFUNCT as of Feb 2025, site down, skip

decadent review.summary: The Decadent Review was a German l'art pour l'art publication covering experimental and literary poetry, criticism, essays, and visual/music arts writing with no monetary payment. No word or line limits were specified, and simultaneous submission policies were unknown. Critically, this project is believed defunct as of February 2025 and its website was not functioning on Duotrope's last visit — submitting here would likely be a waste of time.

details.aesthetic: Work that does not 'dull the edges' of art; unflinching, politically aware writing. Fiction, poetry, nonfiction, and multimedia. Actively centres Queer, Trans*, Two Spirit, Black, Indigenous, writers of colour, and Global South voices.
details.multiple_submissions: Up to 3 poems at once; up to 2 prose pieces if each is under 1,000 words
details.red_flags: Submissions are currently closed. No payment offered. Blogs, websites, and YouTube count as prior publication, making work ineligible. Acceptance grants First North American Serial Rights and Archival Rights, and accepted work is subject to minor editing.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify decomp promptly if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: 8,000 words maximum for prose; up to 3 poems at a time; two prose pieces allowed if each is under 1,000 words

decomp.index_line: *Decomp: unflinching, politically charged fiction/poetry/nonfiction centering Queer, BIPOC, Global South voices — currently closed
decomp.name: *Decomp
decomp.summary: decomp publishes fiction, poetry, nonfiction, and multimedia work with an unflinching, politically engaged aesthetic, especially welcoming marginalized and BIPOC/Queer voices. Prose is capped at 8,000 words (two pieces allowed if under 1,000 words each), up to 3 poems per submission, with a 90-day response target. Submissions are currently closed, and the journal counts blogs, websites, and YouTube as prior publication.

details.aesthetic: Experimental poetry and prose — 'experiments, derivations, plunges, incisions, compressions, investigations, dilations'; writing that pushes narrative expectations. Welcomes writers from marginalized communities and non-traditional literary backgrounds. Also publishes Translations, Conversations, Critiques, Performance, Reviews, and FIVES multimedia critical-creative work.
details.fee: $5 per submission (fee waivers available on request, no questions asked)
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per genre at a time; must wait for a decision before submitting again in that genre
details.reading_period: Poetry and prose: seasonal windows announced via social media; Conversations, Critiques, Performance, Reviews, Translations, and FIVES: year-round (subject to monthly 800-submission cap). Next window opens March 1, 2026.
details.red_flags: Strict 2-year embargo after publication before resubmitting to any genre; 6–9 month wait required between submissions; submitting to wrong genre risks work being returned unread; no edits accepted after submission unless work is already accepted
details.response_time: 6–9 months (inferred from required wait between submissions; explicit response time not stated)
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Prose generally no more than 4,000 words (single work) or 3–5 flash/micro pieces; poetry 3–5 poems per submission

denver quarterly.index_line: Denver Quarterly: experimental poetry/prose that bends narrative, marginalized voices centered; $5 fee, seasonal windows, 2-yr embargo after publication
denver quarterly.name: Denver Quarterly
denver quarterly.summary: Denver Quarterly publishes experimentally-minded poetry and prose (plus translations, criticism, and multimedia) that pushes narrative expectations and centers marginalized voices.
