Prose is capped around 4,000 words; poetry windows are seasonal with an 800-submission cap, while some categories (Conversations, Critiques, Reviews, Translations, FIVES) are year-round. Writers should note the new $5 fee per submission (fee waivers available on request), a strict one-submission-per-genre-at-a-time rule, a 6–9 month wait between submissions, and a 2-year embargo after publication before resubmitting.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction — no further stylistic or thematic detail provided
details.multiple_submissions: Up to 5 poems in one attachment, or one fiction/CNF piece per submission
details.red_flags: Very limited guidelines visible; no information on simultaneous submissions, fees, or response time — writer should check the full website before submitting
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Up to 5000 words (fiction/CNF); up to 5 poems (poetry)

descant.index_line: Descant: poetry, fiction, CNF; no stated aesthetic; open through Apr 1, 2026; guidelines thin—check site first
descant.name: Descant
descant.summary: Descant publishes poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction, with a current open call running through April 1, 2026. Poets may submit up to 5 poems; prose submissions cap at 5000 words. No further aesthetic, fee, or response-time details are provided on this page.

details.aesthetic: Hybrid, experimental forms: poems masquerading as stories, indices, obituaries, sentence diagrams, schematics, annotations, definitions. Values vivisection, urgency, risk, elegance, iteration, ruins, mechanical processes. Enjoys and also eschews traditional forms. Open to AI-assisted work if it 'rules.' No work previously published online or in print (personal websites excepted).
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Sound section closed for unsolicited submissions. Avoid '13 ways of looking at X' titles. Do not mention awards (e.g. Hopwoods) in cover letters. If submitting a multi-poem batch, the submissions manager does not allow withdrawal of a single poem from the set—a practical complication for simultaneous submissions.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere and withdraw via submissions manager
details.word_limit: unknown

diagram.index_line: DIAGRAM: hybrid/structural work—poems as indices, obituaries, schematics, diagrams; free; no "13 ways of looking at X" titles; sound closed to unsolicited work
diagram.name: *DIAGRAM
diagram.summary: DIAGRAM is an experimental electronic journal prizing work that is structural, taxonomic, or hybrid in form—poems as indices, stories as obituaries, schematics, annotations—with a strong bias toward urgency, risk, and language doing something new. They accept text, images, and new media via a submissions manager (hardcopy accepted but slower); simultaneous submissions are allowed with immediate notification of acceptance elsewhere. Writers should avoid '13 ways of looking at X'-style titles, omit award credentials in cover letters, and note that the sound section is closed for unsolicited submissions.

details.aesthetic: Global in scope and explicitly non-Anglosphere in focus; publishes a mix of literary essays, translated fiction and poetry, and investigative reporting on politics and society. Contributors include writers from Kenya, Lebanon, Hungary, Russia, and Italy. The sensibility is serious, internationally minded, and socially engaged — work that 'sparks conversation and causes controversy.' Translation is a core feature, not an afterthought.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No submission guidelines found on this page. Writer should locate a dedicated submissions page before querying. The journal's strong non-Anglosphere focus may mean it prioritizes writers from outside the English-speaking world or work in translation.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

dial the.index_line: Dial, The — Global essays, investigative journalism, and translated fiction/poetry, non-Anglosphere focus; find submissions page before querying
dial the.name: * Dial, The
dial the.summary: The Dial publishes investigative journalism, essays, and literature primarily from writers outside the Anglosphere, with a strong emphasis on translation and international political-literary perspectives. Work ranges from reported pieces on policy and disaster preparedness to translated poetry and fiction from Hungary, Lebanon, and beyond. No submission guidelines were found on this page.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction across all styles; blind-reviewed, prize-oriented journal produced with graduate and undergraduate students at Fairfield University. No stated thematic or stylistic restrictions.
details.fee: $10 (contest entry); $3 (non-contest entry); free for incarcerated writers
details.multiple_submissions: Poetry allows up to 3 poems in one submission; separate contest categories require separate submissions; no explicit statement on submitting to multiple genres simultaneously
details.red_flags: Non-contest submitters receive NO rejection notice—silence by early 2026 means decline; journal does not pay for accepted work unless the piece wins one of the three $1,000 prizes; previously published work is ineligible
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, with notification to Dogwood upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Prose (fiction/nonfiction): up to 22 pages; Poetry: 1–3 poems, max 10 pages (contest) or max 15 pages (non-contest)

dogwood.index_line: Dogwood: open-aesthetic poetry/fiction/nonfiction contest ($1,000/genre); $10 fee, or $3 non-contest with no rejection notice—silence means no
dogwood.name: Dogwood
dogwood.summary: Dogwood publishes poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction via a blind-review contest model with $1,000 prizes per genre, plus a non-contest track for publication only. Contest submissions close September 5, 2025; prose up to 22 pages, poetry 1–3 poems/max 10 pages; fees are $10 (contest) or $3 (non-contest). Non-contest submitters receive no rejection notice—silence by early 2026 means a pass—and the journal does not pay for accepted non-prize work.

details.aesthetic: Broad arts and culture scope — literary and mainstream fiction (short stories) and poetry (open forms); no themes imposed; inspired by the French concept of a 'file,' suggesting eclectic, curated content across fashion, photography, music, and culinary pursuits alongside creative writing.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Publication is believed defunct as of May 2014 — submitting here would almost certainly be a waste of time. Reprints not allowed. No payment information available.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: No specific word count limits known

dossier journal.index_line: Dossier Journal — arts/culture fiction and poetry alongside fashion and photography — DEFUNCT since 2014, do not submit
dossier journal.name: Dossier Journal
dossier journal.summary: Dossier is a defunct bi-annual print arts and culture journal (fashion, photography, creative writing, art) with no stated themes or specific guidelines, publishing literary and mainstream fiction and poetry. No word count or line limits are specified, and no fee, response time, or simultaneous submission policy is recorded. The publication is believed defunct as of May 2014, making submission pointless.

details.aesthetic: Polished literary fiction (especially short-shorts ~500 words and works under 2,000 words); poetry of all forms; creative nonfiction/essays preferring pieces under 1,500 words with an arts and culture focus—cultural critique, feminist and intersectional critique, science, medical, nature writing, literary journalism, experimental nonfiction; visual and intermedia gallery work. Seeks diverse voices on diverse subjects.
details.fee: unknown (Gertrude Stein Award has a separate per-story payment, but the amount is not stated on this page)
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed for general submissions; multiple submissions are allowed for the Gertrude Stein Award only
details.red_flags: Work posted on public blogs, online magazines, or public forums is treated as previously published and will almost never be accepted. AI-generated writing (whole or partial) is categorically rejected. Poetry must be submitted as separate files in separate submissions—bundling poems in one document will likely disqualify them. Payment for online publication is no cash; only print contributors receive anything (a free copy).
details.response_time: 3–6 months (sometimes same day; contact them if no response after 6 months)
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must withdraw via Submittable immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction and creative nonfiction: up to 8,000 words; poetry: 1–5 poems per submission

dr tj eckleburg review.index_line: Dr. T.J. Eckleburg Review: polished short fiction/CNF (arts-culture focus) & poetry; no-cash online pay; AI writing flatly rejected
dr tj eckleburg review.name: Dr. T.J. Eckleburg Review
dr tj eckleburg review.summary: Eckleburg publishes polished literary fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, and visual art with a preference for shorter, tightly woven works and a broad, culturally engaged range of voices and subjects. Fiction and essays run up to 8,000 words year-round; poetry is 1–5 poems submitted as separate files in separate submissions. No multiple submissions for general slots; AI-generated writing is flatly refused; and work appearing in public blogs or online forums is considered previously published.

details.aesthetic: Weird Fiction broadly covering SF, Fantasy, and Horror; prizes the absurd with human truth, outlandish premises with character arcs, humor, body horror, folklore, cult bureaucracy, eldritch comedy, alien cultures, augmented sentience — must work well read aloud with full-cast audio production.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Submissions are currently CLOSED. Emails sent directly to submissions@drabblecast.org are deleted unread — do not submit via email.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: 500–4,000 words for short fiction; drabbles exactly 100 words; twabbles exactly 100 characters

drabblecast.index_line: Drabblecast: audio-first Weird Fiction — absurd, humorous, disturbing SF/F/Horror, 500-4,000 words or 100-word drabbles; CLOSED, no email subs
drabblecast.name: Drabblecast
drabblecast.summary: The Drabblecast publishes Weird Fiction — strange, humorous, absurd, or disturbing speculative short fiction (SF/F/Horror) that works well as audio; they explicitly seek underrepresented voices. Short fiction runs 500–4,000 words, drabbles exactly 100 words, twabbles exactly 100 characters; pays $0.06/word (originals) capped at $300. Submissions are currently CLOSED, and stories sent directly to the email are deleted unread — use only their official submission system.

details.aesthetic: Dark futuristic fiction, cyberpunk, literary sci-fi, magical realism, slipstream, and speculative fiction; wants diverse protagonists, unique dystopias/utopias, unconventional societies; welcomes dark stories with happy endings; hard sells include vignettes, folktales, myths, Lovecraft pastiche, sword-and-sorcery fantasy, and pandemic stories.
details.multiple_submissions: Up to 1 original story and 1 reprint story at the same time; up to 3 poetry submissions at once, each submitted separately; no multiple submissions in the same category
details.red_flags: Submissions are currently closed. Blind review is strictly enforced — any identifying info in the file causes automatic rejection. Rejected stories cannot be resubmitted under any circumstances, even after revision. Hard-pass content violations result in a permanent ban. Very few reprint slots available.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must withdraw via Moksha immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Original fiction up to 4,000 words; reprints up to 7,000 words; poetry up to 50 lines

dread machine.index_line: Dark cyberpunk/lit-sci-fi, diverse protagonists, unconventional societies; no vignettes/folktales/Lovecraft/pandemic; closed; strict blind review, no resubmissions
dread machine.name: The dread machine
dread machine.summary: The Dread Machine publishes dark, futuristic speculative fiction and cyberpunk with an emphasis on literary quality, diverse protagonists, and unconventional societies; original fiction is capped at 4,000 words and poetry at 50 lines, with response time around two months. Submissions are currently closed, and the blind review process strictly requires all personal identifying information be removed from the file itself or the submission is automatically rejected. Writers should note that rejected stories cannot be resubmitted in any form, hard-pass violations result in a ban, and the wishlist explicitly discourages vignettes, folktales, Lovecraft pastiche, and pandemic stories.

details.aesthetic: Hopeful speculative fiction (hopepunk, solarpunk) emphasizing connection, empathy, forgiveness, and positive futures; settings include space colonization, near-future Earth, and fantasy; speculative poetry also welcome. Current theme: 'Open Channel: The Art of Connection.'
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed; may resubmit if a piece is returned and the reading period is still open
details.reading_period: Currently closed; check back September 2026 for reopening notice
details.red_flags: Submissions are closed as of 03/26/26 through at least September 2026; AI-generated stories are not accepted; no multiple submissions permitted.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: up to 7,000 words

dream forge.index_line: DreamForge: hopepunk/solarpunk fiction & poetry of connection and utopian futures, $0.08/word; closed until Sept 2026, no AI
dream forge.name: dream forge
dream forge.summary: DreamForge publishes hopeful, humanist speculative fiction (hopepunk/solarpunk) and poetry with themes of connection, empathy, and utopian possibility; pays $0.08/word for original fiction up to 7,000 words. Submissions are currently closed as of March 2026, with a possible reopening in September 2026. No multiple submissions are allowed, and AI-generated stories appear to be explicitly unwelcome.

details.aesthetic: Socially engaged cultural criticism, class-sensitive analysis, longform essays, short fiction, poetry, interviews, dispatches, and 150-word Mentions reviews; favors sharp/surprising interventions, upbeat cynicism, generous takedowns; rejects personal essays, party-line thinking, theory-bro references, AI writing, and trauma narratives.
details.multiple_submissions: One pitch/submission at a time per category
details.red_flags: Nonfiction drafts are not accepted—essays must start as a 2–4 paragraph pitch only; the 'We don't want' and 'We're bored by' lists are extensive and should be read carefully before submitting; response time is unspecified.
details.response_time: unknown (promises a response to every pitch but notes it may take some time)
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Fiction: no word limit stated; poetry: up to six poems; Mentions: 1–4 sentences (approx. 150 words); essays: pitch only (2–4 paragraphs), no draft submissions accepted

drift the.index_line: Drift, The — Class-conscious criticism, essays, fiction, poetry; upbeat cynicism over party-line takes; essays need pitch only, no drafts
drift the.name: Drift, The
drift the.summary: The Drift publishes sharp, class-conscious cultural criticism, socially engaged essays, fiction, poetry, and 150-word 'Mentions' reviews—favoring upbeat cynicism and surprising angles over party-line takes or personal essays. Essays require a 2–4 paragraph pitch (no drafts); fiction has no word limit; poetry allows up to six poems; one submission at a time per category. Writers should avoid personal essays, AI-generated work, theory-bro references, trauma narratives, and anything resembling a term paper—the 'We don't want' and 'We're bored by' lists are unusually long and specific.

details.aesthetic: Fiction and non-fiction, previously unpublished in English; actively encourages submissions from writers underrepresented in literary magazines; no poetry.
details.fee: none (pays contributors; fee scale starts at €300 for pieces up to 2,500 words, increases with word count)
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No confirmation email is sent after submission — writers must note the date themselves. No postal submissions accepted.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

dublin review.index_line: Dublin Review: fiction/nonfiction only, no poetry; prioritizes underrepresented voices; pays from €300; no submission confirmation sent, so track your own date
dublin review.name: Dublin Review
dublin review.summary: The Dublin Review publishes fiction and non-fiction (no poetry) previously unpublished in English, with a stated commitment to underrepresented writers. Submissions are online-only with a 16 MB file size cap; no word limit or reading period is specified. Writers should note there is no confirmation email sent, so they must record their submission date manually.

details.aesthetic: Lyrically charged, emotionally raw work across poetry, flash fiction, hybrid, and nonfiction; strong use of cultural specificity (diaspora, race, class, queerness, carceral experience); imagery grounded in the body and domestic life; writing that resists sanitization in favor of mess and immediacy. The Lorca epigraph signals a preference for work with visceral, instinctive force over technical polish.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No submission guidelines found on these pages; writer should seek a dedicated submissions page before attempting to submit.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

duende.index_line: Duende: raw, embodied poetry/prose/hybrid work steeped in Lorca's duende—diaspora, queerness, incarceration, the body; no polish, no sanitizing; submission info not found
duende.name: *Duende
duende.summary: Duende is the national literary journal of Goddard College's BFA program, publishing poetry, prose, hybrid work, and art with a strong emphasis on embodied, emotionally urgent voices—work that is raw, culturally specific, and formally alive, drawing its name from Lorca's concept of deep song. The journal has featured themed issues (food, incarcerated writers) and spotlights marginalized voices including writers of color, LGBTQ+ writers, and incarcerated contributors; no submission mechanics were found on these pages.

details.aesthetic: Broadly eclectic: short fiction, poetry, nonfiction, travel writing, humor (satire/artwork), reviews, interviews, and miscellany (academic essays, experimental work, etc.). Values varied perspectives, international voices, and work that surprises; quality is the sole criterion regardless of author background.
details.multiple_submissions: One piece (or up to 5 poems) per category submission; multiple category submissions not explicitly addressed.
details.red_flags: Submission fee of $2 applies to every category. Former contributors and Spotlight Authors have special conditions that must be reviewed before submitting. Hyperlinks in the body of reviews/interviews are removed.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must immediately withdraw via Submittable and/or email editors@eclectica.org if accepted elsewhere.
details.word_limit: Up to 20,000 words for prose (fiction, nonfiction, travel, humor, miscellany); pieces over 20,000 words submitted under a separate 'Novella-length and longer' category. Up to 5 poems per submission.

eclectica.index_line: Eclectica: all-genre and eclectic—fiction, poetry, nonfiction, travel, humor, reviews; $2/category fee, prose to 20k words
eclectica.name: *Eclectica
eclectica.summary: Eclectica publishes a wide range of forms and genres—fiction, poetry, nonfiction, travel, humor, reviews, and miscellany—with a stated preference for varied, eclectic perspectives and international or underrepresented voices. Submissions are $2 per category, with prose up to 20,000 words (longer pieces have their own category) and poetry up to five poems. Simultaneous submissions are allowed but require immediate withdrawal notification, and former contributors have special conditions to check before submitting.

details.aesthetic: Original English-language work across poetry, short fiction, creative nonfiction, drama, and visual art; no book reviews; publishes well-known, emerging, and debut writers; no stated thematic restrictions.
details.multiple_submissions: One piece per year per genre (drama, fiction, CNF); up to 5 poems per year (poetry)
details.reading_period: Aug 1 – Dec 15 (poetry, fiction, CNF, drama); Aug 1 – Jan 31 (art)
details.red_flags: No reprints, including previously published online work; no email submissions accepted; international contributors cannot receive payment
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but must withdraw immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 8,000 words (fiction, creative nonfiction, drama); up to 5 poems per submission (poetry)

eclipse lit.index_line: ellipsis…: All genres, no reviews; pays $10/poem, $3/page prose, but no reprints or email subs; Aug 1–Dec 15
eclipse lit.name: Eclipse Lit
eclipse lit.summary: ellipsis… is a student-run annual journal (Westminster University, since 1965) publishing poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, drama, and art with a prize culture and modest payment ($10/poem, $3/page prose). Submission window is August 1–December 15 for text genres (August 1–January 31 for art), with an 8,000-word cap on prose/drama and up to 5 poems per year. Watch out for the no-reprints rule (including work published online), the no-email-submissions rule, and the fact that international contributors cannot be paid.

details.aesthetic: Place-based and climate-crisis-engaged work across all genres; nonfiction that engages seriously but not overly solemnly with ecology and natural history; deeply place-rooted fiction; poetry using form/meter innovatively (French repeating forms, golden shovels, etc.) and engaging with social/natural sciences, identity, and ecology. Prioritizes historically underrepresented voices.
details.fee: none (postal submissions and general Submittable window are fee-free; subscriber-only fee-free online window noted for September 2026)
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per reading period per genre window; additional submissions deleted or recycled unread
details.reading_period: Two general windows per year (January/February and August/September); plus a Valentine's Day window; fall 2026 general window is closed
details.red_flags: Fall 2026 general window already closed—only current subscribers can submit online in September 2026. Windows may close early without notice. Submittable sometimes fails to deliver decline messages. Postal submissions outside the US are not accepted; SASE required for domestic mail submissions.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Prose: up to ~10,000 words (30 double-spaced pages); minimum 2,000 words. Poetry: 3–5 poems per submission.

ecotone.index_line: Ecotone: place-rooted, climate-engaged fiction/nonfiction/poetry, one submission per window—fall 2026 closed except to subscribers
ecotone.name: Ecotone
ecotone.summary: Ecotone publishes place-based and climate-engaged fiction, nonfiction, and poetry, prioritizing underrepresented voices; prose up to ~10,000 words, poetry 3–5 poems per submission, with two general reading periods per year plus a Valentine's Day window. Writers may submit once per reading period only—additional submissions are deleted unread regardless of genre. The fall 2026 general window is already closed (subscriber-only fee-free window opens September 2026), and Submittable may silently decline without delivering the rejection message.

details.aesthetic: Scholarly yet polemical art theory and cultural criticism; engages Marxist, post-colonial, and technopolitical frameworks; contributors are internationally recognized academics, artists, and critics; essays blend theory with contemporary political and aesthetic analysis
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No submission guidelines found; journal appears to be editorially commissioned rather than open to unsolicited submissions — a writer should research how to approach the editors before attempting to submit
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

eflux journal.index_line: E-Flux Journal: dense theory-essays on art, politics, tech, radical history for academic contributors; likely commissioned, not open submission
eflux journal.name: E-Flux Journal
eflux journal.summary: e-flux Journal is a prestigious international art theory and criticism journal publishing long-form essays at the intersection of politics, technology, architecture, and contemporary art — contributors include prominent theorists, artists, and curators. Its sensibility is rigorous, politically engaged, and conceptually ambitious, with titles addressing carceral politics, AI, political theology, and radical history. No submission guidelines are visible; this appears to be an invitation-only or editorially commissioned publication.

details.aesthetic: Dynamic literary fiction and novel excerpts; strange and diverting flash prose, poetry, and graphic narratives; personal narrative essays that 'essay as a verb' (interrogate, investigate, introspect); cultural criticism that uses art/media as a lens into broader cultural trends or personal experience — braided personal/analytical essays welcome, no reviews or strictly academic work.
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per category per submission period; may submit across multiple categories simultaneously
details.reading_period: Two to four one-week windows per year (typically Spring and Fall for fiction); cultural criticism pitches via email year-round (currently closed); year-round for paying members ($5/month or $50/year)
details.red_flags: Cultural criticism is currently closed; no generative AI content (any AI use must be disclosed or work will be rejected); do not send full drafts for cultural criticism — pitch only; short one-week submission windows announced only 1–2 weeks in advance, requiring close monitoring
details.response_time: Fiction: 6–8 months; The Commuter (flash/poetry): 3–6 months; Personal narrative essays: 6–8 months; Cultural criticism pitches: follow up after 2 weeks if no response
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: 2,000–10,000 words; Flash/poetry/graphic narratives: under 1,500 words; Personal narrative essays: 2,000–6,500 words; Cultural criticism: 3,500 words or less

electric literature.index_line: Electric Literature: dynamic fiction, flash, essays that interrogate; brief announced-only windows; cultural criticism closed; no AI
electric literature.name: *Electric Literature
electric literature.summary: Electric Literature publishes literary fiction, flash prose, poetry, graphic narratives, personal narrative essays, and cultural criticism with a focus on dynamic, interrogative, and culturally engaged writing. Fiction runs 2,000–10,000 words; flash/poetry under 1,500 words; personal essays 2,000–6,500 words; cultural criticism 3,500 words or less; submission windows open two to four times a year for one week at a time, with year-round access for $5/month members. Writers should note the strict no-AI policy (disclosure required for any use), that cultural criticism is currently closed, and that full drafts should not be sent for cultural criticism pitches.

details.aesthetic: Speculative fiction — science fiction, fantasy, and the macabre — with willingness to push traditional genre limits; no poetry, fan fiction, serials, novels, non-fiction, or over-the-top sex/violence.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — one story at a time; wait for response before submitting another
details.reading_period: Year-round; quarterly deadlines: Jan 15 (Feb issue), Apr 15 (May issue), Jul 15 (Aug issue), Oct 15 (Nov issue)
details.red_flags: No AI-generated or partially AI-generated work; no reprints including anything posted online; no receipt confirmation sent and no status queries answered; RTF attachment with cover letter required or attachment may not be opened
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but must disclose upfront and notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere

electric spec.index_line: Electric Spec: SF/fantasy/macabre pushing genre limits, 250–7000 words, $20/story, no AI-generated work, RTF submissions only
electric spec.name: Electric Spec
electric spec.summary: Electric Spec publishes science fiction, fantasy, and the macabre (250–7000 words), favoring stories that push genre limits while excluding AI-generated work, reprints, poetry, fan fiction, and extreme sex or violence. They pay $20 per story, read year-round with quarterly deadlines, and respond within 3.5 months. Writers should note no receipt acknowledgment is sent, no status queries are entertained, and RTF attachment format with a cover letter is required.

details.aesthetic: All genres welcome; fiction must respond to a monthly themed prompt. Editors prize surprising concepts, original twists, strong character, and tight structure. Heavily penalizes clichéd prose (e.g., 'heart thudded,' 'orbs' for eyes), backstory dumps, tense shifts, and common tired story shapes (waking-up openings, dream sequences, writer-protagonist stories, animal-reveal endings).
details.multiple_submissions: Allowed, provided they are distinct stories (not the same story with minor alterations or different endings)
details.reading_period: Monthly window: opens on the first, closes at midnight on the final day of each month
details.red_flags: Writer must be new or unpublished — established writers are ineligible. Submission must include the monthly prompt word or it will be rejected regardless of quality. Online submission system only; no email, mail, or social media submissions accepted.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed
details.word_limit: 500–2000 words (excluding title), no exceptions

elegant literature.index_line: Elegant Literature: monthly-prompt flash/short fiction (500–2000w), new/unpublished writers only, no fee; strict anti-cliché standards
elegant literature.name: *Elegant Literature
elegant literature.summary: Elegant Literature publishes themed short fiction (all genres) from new or unpublished writers only, judged on creativity, character, structure, and prose quality. Stories must be 500–2000 words, follow the current monthly prompt, and be submitted via their online form during a monthly window. Writers should note the strict 'new/unpublished' eligibility requirement and a long list of hard-sell tropes and discouraged phrases that will hurt acceptance chances.

details.aesthetic: Short, sentence-level literary fiction with an experimental and internet-native sensibility; published work by Gordon Lish, Diane Williams, Brian Evenson, Gary Lutz, Blake Butler, Elizabeth Ellen, and similar writers in the Lish lineage.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Journal is permanently closed as of November 2010 — do not submit.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

elimae.index_line: Elimae — sentence-driven, Lish-lineage minimalist fiction (Lutz, Evenson, Diane Williams); CLOSED since 2010, do not submit
elimae.name: *Elimae
elimae.summary: Elimae was a pioneering online literary journal (1996–2010) publishing short, sentence-oriented fiction in a minimal, text-focused design; it championed writers like Gordon Lish, Diane Williams, Brian Evenson, and Gary Lutz. It is now closed, having published its final issue in November 2010.

details.aesthetic: Narrative prose and free verse poetry exploring human emotions, experiences, dreams, and revelations; leans surreal with strong imagery and language; edgy, experimental, humble and personal rather than credential-driven, favors authentic voice over resume-building cover letters.
details.multiple_submissions: allowed, strongly encouraged
details.red_flags: none noted
details.response_time: expedited for non-fits; updates roughly every 14 days if under heavy consideration
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, strongly encouraged
details.word_limit: unknown

elj.index_line: ELJ: surreal, emotionally raw prose and free verse steeped in dreams and imagery; wants authentic voice, not polish or pedigree
elj.name: ELJ
elj.summary: ELJ Editions publishes narrative prose and free verse poetry drawn to the surreal, emotional extremity, dreams, and powerful imagery, favoring edgy and experimental work over conventional craft polish.

details.aesthetic: Free verse poetry and flash fiction only; most literary genres considered except horror and erotica; work must have literary undertones. Themed contest section per issue (2016 theme: Un/Civil Disobedience).
details.fee: None for general submissions; $10 for themed contest entries
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed; may resubmit only after receiving a declination
details.red_flags: Poetry submissions require a minimum of 5 poems—sending fewer will likely disqualify the entry. Name must not appear anywhere in the submitted document (blind reading). Contest prohibits multiple submissions and limits entries to one piece.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but must notify in cover letter and notify promptly if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Flash fiction up to 750 words; poetry: 5–8 poems per submission (no fewer than 5)

emerge magazine.index_line: eMerge Magazine: free verse (5-8 poems) and flash fiction to 750 words; no horror/erotica; blind reading July 1-Aug 15 only
emerge magazine.name: eMerge Magazine
emerge magazine.summary: Emerge publishes free verse poetry and flash fiction (up to 750 words) across most literary genres, excluding horror and erotica, with a blind submission process. Reading period is July 1–August 15 only, with poetry requiring exactly 5–8 pieces per submission and prose up to 3 stories; simultaneous submissions allowed with notification, but multiple submissions are not. The themed contest carries a $10 entry fee, and writers must not include their name in the manuscript itself—only in the Submittable cover letter.

details.aesthetic: Print: poetry, short fiction, creative nonfiction with a focus on emerging and underrepresented voices. Online: flash fiction/nonfiction, poetry, humor, lists, genre-defying miscellany, comics, and visual art.
details.fee: $2 reading fee for print (waivable—email submission instead to avoid it); online is free.
details.multiple_submissions: Print: allowed, but wait for a response in the same genre before sending another. Online: one piece at a time only.
details.reading_period: Print: Aug 1 – Nov 1 annually. Online: unknown (email-based, no stated window).
details.red_flags: Submission manager currently shows no open calls, so the print window may be closed. The $2 fee can be sidestepped via email, which adds a workaround step writers should note.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere.
details.word_limit: Online prose: under 1000 words; online poems: under one page. Print word limit: unknown.

emrys journal.index_line: Emrys Journal: emerging/underrepresented voices in poetry, fiction, nonfiction; online flash/humor/comics; $2 print fee; currently no open calls
emrys journal.name: Emrys Journal
emrys journal.summary: Emrys Journal champions emerging and underrepresented voices across poetry, short fiction, and creative nonfiction for its annual print issue, plus flash prose (under 1000 words), poetry, humor, lists, and visual miscellany for its online companion. The print window runs August 1–November 1 with a $2 reading fee (waivable by email), while online submissions are free and open via email only. Multiple submissions are allowed but must be staggered by genre for print, and only one piece at a time for online; the submission manager currently shows no open calls.

details.aesthetic: Wide variety of stories, poems, essays, and genre-bending work; recurring themes not specified but discoverable via the journal's archives and website.
details.fee: unknown (fee waiver available for financial hardship)
details.multiple_submissions: Art: up to five images at a time; prose: unknown
details.reading_period: Print issues: May 1–Jun 15 (Fall/Winter) and Nov 1–Dec 15 (Spring/Summer); art submissions year-round; Breakout Prize: Mar 1–Apr 15; Fresh Voices Fellowship: Sep 15–Nov 1.
details.red_flags: No AI-generated work accepted; writers expected to read the journal before submitting; art-specific page so prose submission details are limited here.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

epiphany.index_line: Epiphany: fiction, poetry, essays, genre-bending work; windows May 1–Jun 15 & Nov 1–Dec 15; no AI-generated work
epiphany.name: Epiphany
epiphany.summary: Epiphany publishes a wide variety of fiction, poetry, essays, and genre-bending work with recurring themes, valuing community and voice; print issues have two submission windows per year (May 1–Jun 15 and Nov 1–Dec 15), with response times of 5–6 months. This page is focused on art submissions, so prose/poetry guidelines are sparse here. Writers should note the no-AI policy, the need to familiarize themselves with the journal before submitting, and that a fee waiver is available for those facing financial hardship.

details.aesthetic: Poetry (up to 5 poems per batch), short fiction, flash fiction suites, essays, comics, and cover art (PDF via Submittable). Favors adventurous, shorter work over conventional long pieces. No literary criticism, book reviews, or children's/YA writing.
details.fee: $3 per electronic submission via Submittable (with occasional free-submission weekends); no fee for mail submissions
details.multiple_submissions: Poetry: up to 5 poems per batch; prose/essay: one piece or a suite of flash pieces per submission. Implicit one-submission-at-a-time per genre.
details.reading_period: Electronic: Aug 1–Aug 31 and Jan 1–Jan 31 (or until cap). Mail: accepted anytime but only read in September, October, February, and March.
details.red_flags: Strict no-AI policy—any AI-assisted work is rejected as fraudulent. Mail submissions without a SASE will not receive a response. Electronic submissions close quickly (end of month or when cap is met). Magazine is print-only; nothing published online.
details.response_time: Faster for mail submissions sent during reading months (Sep, Oct, Feb, Mar); slower outside those months. No specific timeframe stated for electronic.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, no conditions stated
details.word_limit: No stated word limit; editors note preference for shorter, adventurous work over longer conventional pieces.

epoch.index_line: Epoch: adventurous poetry/fiction/comics, favors short over conventional long work; $3 fee, strict no-AI policy, print-only
epoch.name: Epoch
epoch.summary: EPOCH (Cornell) publishes poetry, fiction, essays, comics, and cover art with a preference for adventurous short work over competent-but-conventional long pieces, and explicitly rejects AI-generated writing, literary criticism, book reviews, and children's/YA content. Electronic submissions open August 1 and January 1 (open until month's end or cap is reached) at $3 per submission, while mail submissions are free but only read in September, October, February, and March. Writers should note the strict no-AI policy (called 'fraudulent'), the required SASE for mail submissions, and that the $3 Submittable fee applies even though free-submission weekends are occasionally offered.

details.aesthetic: Science fiction broadly construed (superheroes, steampunk, space opera, time travel, alternate history); must center science, technology, future projections, and/or their impact on people; leans hopepunk, escapism, and optimism; welcomes dark humor and satire but not grimdark; no horror, erotica, or content punching down at marginalized groups; audio-first format means preference for clarity, tight pacing, and simple structure.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Closed to general submissions; open only for Democratic Futures special window (end date unknown)
details.red_flags: General submissions are CLOSED; only a special window is open. AI-generated content results in a permanent ban. No horror, sexual assault, gore, child abuse, animal cruelty, or stories treating marginalized hardships as thought experiments—writers in adjacent genres should note the sister podcasts (PseudoPod, PodCastle, Cast of Wonders) instead.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Original short fiction: 1,500–6,000 words; reprint short fiction: 1,500–7,500 words; reprint novelettes: 7,500–18,000 words; limits are firm

escape pod.index_line: Escape Pod: hopepunk/optimistic SF audio+text, 1.5-6k words; CLOSED except Democratic Futures window; no horror/grimdark
escape pod.name: Escape Pod
escape pod.summary: Escape Pod publishes optimistic, hopepunk-leaning science fiction (broadly defined) in text and audio, favoring clarity and tight pacing for a listening audience; original fiction runs 1,500–6,000 words, reprints up to 18,000 words. General submissions are currently closed—only the Democratic Futures special window is open. Writers should note strict prohibitions on AI-generated content, sexual assault/gore/horror/child abuse, and stories that treat marginalized hardships as thought experiments.

details.aesthetic: Fantasy and science fiction short stories; not interested in horror or grimdark except flash fiction (which may include horror if it has a supernatural element); no fan fiction; open to serials if complete at submission; welcomes reprints with proof exclusivity has lapsed.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed
details.reading_period: Open (submissions open at time of page)
details.red_flags: Stories with spelling mistakes are discarded outright; writers must be 18+; no responses to questions about rejections; Australian-content selections require proof of residency; reprints require proof exclusivity has lapsed.
details.response_time: Up to 2 months (contact them if no response after 2 months)
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; no withdrawal condition stated
details.word_limit: Flash: 500–1000 words; Standard: 2000–5000 words (longer accepted); Novelette/novella: 15,000+ words

etherea.index_line: Etherea: SFF short fiction/flash, no horror or grimdark (except flash); A$25–200; strict no-typos policy, one sub at a time
etherea.name: Etherea
etherea.summary: Etherea publishes fantasy and sci-fi short fiction (and flash) in Australian dollars, with no horror/grimdark except in the flash category; stories run 500–1000 words (flash), 2000–5000 words (standard), or 15,000+ words (novelette/novella), paying A$25–A$200 flat. Submissions are open, simultaneous submissions are allowed, but multiple submissions are not, and writers must be 18+. Watch out for the strict proofreading requirement (spelling errors get discarded), the 21-day cooldown after rejection, and the need to prove Australian residency if selected as Australian content.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction with compelling characters, voice, and fresh plots; poetry with arresting imagery, polished language, emotional impact, and lyricism without pretension; creative non-fiction as riveting real-life narrative with distinct voice (mainly via contest).
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per writer at a time, in one genre only; may submit again after a response is received
details.reading_period: January, July, August, and December (opens 1st, closes last day of month or when unpaid cap is reached); Non-Fiction Contest open until October 15
details.red_flags: Submission windows close early when unpaid cap is reached—submit early in the month; writers may only appear in EVENT once every two years (wait at least 1.5 years after publication before resubmitting); no PDFs accepted; no AI-assisted work accepted; Douglas College staff/faculty and family excluded from most categories
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; writer must notify EVENT immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 5,000 words for fiction; up to six poems per submission

event magazine.index_line: Event Magazine: literary fiction/poetry with fresh voice; Jan/Jul/Aug/Dec only, no AI work, one pub per 2 years
event magazine.name: Event Magazine
event magazine.summary: EVENT publishes literary fiction (compelling voice, fresh plots), poetry (arresting imagery, lyricism), and creative non-fiction (primarily via annual contest); fiction and poetry submissions are capped at four months per year (January, July, August, December) and close early once unpaid limits are reached. One submission per writer at a time, up to six poems or one story (max 5,000 words), no fee, simultaneous submissions allowed with immediate notification. Writers should note the strict two-year recurrence cap, the AI-prohibition, the no-PDF rule, and that submission windows can close before month-end.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and video art; especially excited by work that blurs genres and forms. Previously unpublished only; excerpts from forthcoming books considered if published in Evergreen first.
details.fee: $5, with hardship fee waiver available on request
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed until hearing back on current submission
details.red_flags: Fee waiver is explicitly restricted to severe financial hardship; poetry submissions go to a separate email address (jeeleong@evergreenreview.com), not the main submission portal
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must withdraw promptly if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 7,500 words for fiction and nonfiction; up to 10 poems (in one file) for poetry

evergreen.index_line: Evergreen: genre-blurring fiction/nonfiction/poetry/video art; unpublished only; $5 fee; poetry submits via separate email
evergreen.name: *Evergreen
evergreen.summary: Evergreen Review publishes fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and video art with a strong interest in genre-blurring and hybrid forms. Fiction/nonfiction cap at 7,500 words; poetry up to 10 poems per submission; $5 fee with hardship waiver available. Only previously unpublished work is accepted, book excerpts must appear before the book's release, and writers must wait for a response before resubmitting.

details.aesthetic: unknown
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: All guidelines are offsite on Ola submission manager; submissions sent by email are explicitly ignored. This page contains no usable submission details.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

exacting clam.index_line: Exacting Clam: fiction, poetry, essays, reviews, art; no guidelines here—all details on Ola manager; email submissions ignored
exacting clam.name: Exacting Clam
exacting clam.summary: Exacting Clam publishes fiction, poetry, essays, reviews, and art, but all submission guidelines live exclusively on their external Ola submission manager—none are reproduced here. No word limits, reading periods, fees, or aesthetic details are stated on this page. Writers must visit Ola for actual guidelines; emails are explicitly ignored.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction, nonfiction, and poetry dealing with health, disease, healing, the human body, medical encounters, and the broader human condition; work that engages ambiguity and the intersection of science, medicine, policy, and literary arts.
details.fee: $5 per fiction or nonfiction submission; $2 per poem, up to 3 poems
details.multiple_submissions: Poetry: up to 3 poems per submission; prose: unknown if multiple pieces allowed
details.red_flags: Fees apply to all submissions; word limits and response times not disclosed; journal strongly encourages purchasing a back issue before submitting, implying familiarity with the publication is expected.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

examined life.index_line: Examined Life: fiction/nonfiction/poetry on illness, medicine, the body; $5 prose/$2 poem fee; reads Feb 1–Apr 12
examined life.name: Examined Life
examined life.summary: The Examined Life Journal (U of Iowa Carver College of Medicine) publishes literary fiction, nonfiction, and poetry exploring healthcare, illness, healing, and the human condition at the intersection of medicine and the literary arts. Submissions are open 2/1/2026–4/12/2026 with a $5 fee per prose submission and $2 per poem (up to three poems). Word limits and response times are not stated on the page, and writers are nudged to buy a back issue before submitting.

details.aesthetic: Poetry in any form or style; flash fiction and flash nonfiction targeting 300–500 words (microfiction, sudden fiction, etc.); original photography and 2D digital art. Triannual print and digital publication.
details.fee: Modest fee charged (exact amount not stated)
details.multiple_submissions: Poetry: up to 3 poems per submission. Flash fiction/nonfiction: up to 2 pieces per submission. Visual art: up to 3 images per submission.
details.reading_period: Jan issue: Oct 1 – Dec 10; Apr issue: Jan 1 – Mar 10; Oct double issue: Apr 1 – Sep 10
details.red_flags: Double-anonymous review requires removing all author identifying information from files before upload — failure risks disqualification. Post-publication changes to byline or bio are not possible. Fee waivers cannot be granted without breaking anonymity.
details.response_time: Rolling basis (explicitly noted for the October double issue); otherwise unknown
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must withdraw immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Poetry: up to 3 poems, fewer than 6 pages. Flash fiction/nonfiction: 300–500 words or less per piece, fewer than 5 pages. Visual art: up to 3 JPG files, max 7MB each at 1,850px on longest side.

exile.index_line: Exile (Burningword): poetry, 300–500-word flash, photography/digital art; strict double-anonymous review, fee, three seasonal windows
exile.name: Exile
exile.summary: Burningword publishes poetry (any form), flash fiction and nonfiction (300–500 words), photography, and 2D digital art in a triannual print/digital journal. Submissions are seasonal with three distinct windows per year, all routed through Submittable, and a modest fee is charged. Writers must strip their name from submitted files for double-anonymous review, and post-publication edits to byline or bio are impossible.

details.aesthetic: Theme-driven work with strong voice and sense of place; values risk-taking, genre-blurring, cathartic conflict, and experimental forms across fiction, nonfiction, poetry, stage/screen, visual art, comics, and film.
details.multiple_submissions: Only one piece per genre at a time; must wait for a response before submitting another
details.red_flags: Submissions are currently closed; previously published work (including online) is not considered; pieces exceeding word limits will not be read
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must note in cover letter and notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction/nonfiction: up to 5,000 words; flash fiction: up to 1,000 words per piece (up to 3 pieces); poetry: up to 3 poems; stage/screen: up to 15 pages; film: up to 15 minutes; comics: up to 3 pages per piece (up to 3 pieces)

exposition review.index_line: Exposition Review: seasonal-theme journal for genre-blurring, voice-driven work across all forms; reads Sep 15–Dec 15 only
exposition review.name: *Exposition Review
exposition review.summary: Exposition Review seeks risk-taking, voice-driven work that blurs genre boundaries, organized around a seasonal theme; fiction and nonfiction cap at 5,000 words, poetry and flash fiction allow up to three pieces, and the submission window runs September 15–December 15 only. Simultaneous submissions are allowed with immediate notification required, but only one piece per genre may be submitted at a time, and previously published or over-limit work is flatly rejected.

details.aesthetic: Speculative flash fiction only: science fiction, fantasy, supernatural, superhero, or hybrids. Engaging stories within a very tight word count; foul language and non-explicit sexual content acceptable if narratively justified; no erotica.
details.multiple_submissions: one story at a time; may submit another after hearing back, no cool-down period
details.red_flags: Currently closed to both fiction and art. Zero-tolerance AI policy (ChatGPT etc.) can result in a permanent submission ban. Self-publishing on a blog, website, or Patreon counts as prior publication and makes a story ineligible. PayPal business accounts may incur fees the magazine cannot cover.
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed — story must not be submitted elsewhere until a response is received
details.word_limit: up to 1,000 words

factor four.index_line: Factor Four: speculative flash (SF/fantasy/supernatural/superhero) to 1,000 words, $0.11/word; CLOSED; zero-tolerance AI ban; no simultaneous subs
factor four.name: Factor Four
factor four.summary: Factor Four publishes speculative flash fiction (sci-fi, fantasy, supernatural, superhero) up to 1,000 words at $0.11/word, with a 30–60 day response time and no simultaneous submissions permitted. Submissions are currently closed as of 01/01/2026. Writers should note the strict no-AI policy with a zero-tolerance ban, and that any prior self-publication—including on a personal blog, website, or Patreon—disqualifies a story as a reprint.

details.aesthetic: Original fiction (short stories, self-contained novel excerpts, novellas), poetry, and visual art; prioritizes work that is personal and singular to the author's voice.
details.multiple_submissions: Fiction: one piece at a time, wait for response before sending another. Poetry: 4–6 poems per submission, wait for response before sending more.
details.red_flags: No pay for contributors; they do not respond to status inquiries; no previously published work (print or web) considered; postal submissions must be re-sent electronically if accepted; visual artists must query first before submitting work.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; no specific withdrawal condition mentioned
details.word_limit: unknown

failbettercom.index_line: failbetter.com — Fiction, poetry, art valuing a singular, unmistakably personal voice; no pay, no reprints, archives online permanently
failbettercom.name: *failbetter.com
failbettercom.summary: failbetter publishes original fiction, poetry, and visual art with a strong emphasis on work that is distinctly personal and could only have come from that writer. Online submissions get a response in 8–12 weeks; postal submissions take 3–6 months, and they do not respond to status inquiries. They acquire exclusive first-time internet rights and archive all work online, and they do not pay contributors.

details.aesthetic: Character-driven fantasy, science fiction, horror, and humor with at least a slight speculative element; no formula, values surprise via character insight, ideas, plot, or prose style; explicitly encourages diverse voices and international writers; long publication history with recurring reviewers (Charles de Lint, Elizabeth Hand, Michelle West, James Sallis, Chris Moriarty) and columnists covering film, TV, and science.
details.multiple_submissions: prefer not to see more than one submission from a writer at a time
details.red_flags: No querying allowed for fiction (must submit full manuscript); does not accept freelance submissions for columns/nonfiction, only fiction via the online submission form.
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed
details.word_limit: up to 25,000 words

fantasy and science fiction.index_line: Character-driven SF/fantasy/horror, no house formula, wants voice/idea surprise; pro rates; full mss only, up to 25k words, no simultaneous subs
fantasy and science fiction.name: Fantasy & Science Fiction
fantasy and science fiction.summary: The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction is a long-running genre magazine publishing character-oriented fantasy, science fiction, horror, and humor with at least some speculative element, with no house formula beyond wanting to be surprised by voice, ideas, or prose. It pays professional rates (8-12 cents/word) on publication, is edited by Sheree Renée Thomas, and draws on a stable of veteran genre columnists and reviewers. Submissions must be complete manuscripts up to 25,000 words, sent one at a time, with no simultaneous submissions allowed.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, literary journalism, fiction in translation, and visual art; no explicit thematic mandate but directs writers to their archive to gauge taste.
details.multiple_submissions: Once per genre per year only
details.red_flags: Submission caps (250 poetry, 150 fiction) can close the window before Dec 15 — submit early; previously published contributors must wait 2 years before resubmitting; submissions outside the Oct 1–Dec 15 window will not be read.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Poetry: up to 5 poems, max 10 pages; Fiction: one short story, up to 20 pages (double-spaced); Art: up to 5 pieces

faultline.index_line: Faultline: general lit-journal aesthetic, all forms; Oct 1–Dec 15 only, caps often close it early—submit fast
faultline.name: Faultline
faultline.summary: Faultline publishes poetry, fiction (including CNF, literary journalism, and translation), and art, favoring work that fits the lit-journal aesthetic browsable in their archive. Submissions open October 1–December 15 only, with hard caps (250 poetry, 150 fiction slots) that may close the window early. Previously published contributors must wait two years before resubmitting, and missing the narrow window means work goes unread.

details.aesthetic: Cross-genre, idiosyncratic, and intelligent writing that resists mainstream and recognizable experimentalism; committed to queer writers and writers of color; publishes poetry, fiction, translation, and hybrid/Other work including poets theater.
details.fee: A reading fee is required; exact amount not stated on this page — see Submittable portal
details.multiple_submissions: Poetry: unlimited submissions per period. Fiction: limited to one submission per submission period. Other/Translation: unknown.
details.red_flags: Window is closed until summer 2026; no AI-assisted work accepted; repeat contributors in the same genre must wait four issues or two years — no exceptions; fiction submitters limited to one submission per period; fiction submissions with more than one story or more than three flash fictions will not be read.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown — not addressed for magazine submissions
details.word_limit: Fiction: one story up to 8,000 words, or three flash fictions up to 1,000 words each. Poetry: up to 3 poems, no more than 10 pages. Other: up to 12 pages. Translation follows the same genre-specific limits.

fence.index_line: Fence: idiosyncratic, boundary-crossing poetry/fiction/hybrid; queer writers & writers of color; closed until summer 2026, fee required
fence.name: Fence
fence.summary: Fence publishes idiosyncratic, boundary-crossing poetry, fiction, translation, and hybrid work with a stated commitment to queer writers and writers of color; submissions are capped at 8,000 words for fiction and 10 pages for poetry, with a reading fee required. The magazine window is currently closed and will reopen by summer 2026, with a response time of 3–9 months. Writers should note the strict no-AI policy, a repeat-contributor embargo of four issues or two years within the same genre, and that fiction submitters are limited to one submission per period.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, nonfiction, poetry, interviews, and English translation; also accepts website pieces and critique opportunities. No stated thematic or stylistic preferences.
details.fee: Fee implied (fee waiver available on request for financial hardship), but exact amount unknown
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No open calls at this time — submissions are currently closed. Reading window is only one month per year (January), so timing is critical. Fee amount is unspecified.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

festival review.index_line: Festival Review: fiction, nonfiction, poetry, interviews, translation; no stated aesthetic; opens January only, closed now; fee (waivable)
festival review.name: *Festival Review
festival review.summary: The Festival Review publishes fiction, nonfiction, poetry, interviews, and English translation across quarterly print issues and a website, with reading open only each January. No word limits, response times, or simultaneous submission policies are stated. There are presently no open calls, so submissions cannot be made right now.

details.aesthetic: Short fiction only (no novel excerpts, non-fiction, poetry, or illustrated work); general literary short stories plus themed calls and an annual ghost story call; sister imprint Uncertain Stories takes stories with a light supernatural or speculative edge. Strongly recommends reading an anthology before submitting.
details.multiple_submissions: Up to 3 stories allowed; each submitted separately via the form; they prefer 2–3 to understand the writer's range
details.reading_period: Current spring call open; deadline midnight UK time 30 September 2026
details.red_flags: No-AI policy explicitly includes grammar/punctuation correction tools; first serial rights plus ~6-month exclusivity required; anthologies currently sold out so reading samples is harder; PDF and Microsoft Works files not accepted
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must notify if accepted elsewhere

fiction desk.index_line: The Fiction Desk — literary short fiction (1k–15k words), themed anthologies plus ghost-story/speculative sister line; £5/story fee, strict no-AI policy (even grammar tools)
fiction desk.name: The Fiction Desk
fiction desk.summary: The Fiction Desk publishes literary short fiction in themed and general anthology calls, including a sister imprint (Uncertain Stories) for supernatural/speculative work; stories must be 1,000–15,000 words and submitted via online form by 30 September 2026 for the current spring call. There is a £5 per-story submission fee, and up to three stories may be submitted simultaneously. Writers should note a strict no-AI policy that extends even to grammar-correction tools, and first serial rights plus a ~six-month exclusivity period are required.

details.aesthetic: Literary and experimental fiction; translations of works unpublished in English; unconventional stories; emerging and established voices. No genre fiction (sci-fi, romance, erotica, detective, YA), no novel excerpts, no plays, poetry, non-fiction, or heavy hybrid work.
details.multiple_submissions: One story at a time; system blocks a second submission until the first is decided
details.red_flags: Reading window is only one month per year (October); payment amount is unspecified and varies by year; no email or postal submissions accepted
details.response_time: 3–6 months (no office hours in January or summer months)
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must withdraw immediately via Submissions Manager if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: 1,000–20,000 words; preference for under 7,500 words

fiction international.index_line: Fiction International: experimental/literary fiction and translations, no genre or verse; opens submissions only in October
fiction international.name: Fiction International
fiction international.summary: FICTION publishes literary and experimental fiction (including translations), favoring unconventional voices across a wide word-count range of 1,000–20,000 words, with a strong preference for pieces under 7,500 words. Submissions are accepted only via their online manager during the single month of October 1–31. Writers should note the extremely narrow reading window, the hard exclusion of genre fiction and all non-prose forms, and that payment is unspecified/variable.

details.aesthetic: Literary and experimental fiction, including translations of works unpublished in English; favors unconventional stories; publishes emerging and established voices; no genre fiction (sci-fi, romance, erotica, detective, YA), no novel excerpts, no graphic stories, no interviews.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed; one story at a time; system blocks second submission until first is decided
details.red_flags: Extremely narrow reading window (one month per year); payment amount is unspecified and varies by year; no email or postal submissions accepted — electronic only
details.response_time: 3–6 months (no office hours in January or summer months)
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; must withdraw immediately via Submissions Manager if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: 1,000–20,000 words; preference for under 7,500 words

fiction magazine.index_line: Fiction Magazine — literary/experimental fiction, no genre; reads Oct 1–31 only, one story at a time
fiction magazine.name: Fiction Magazine
fiction magazine.summary: FICTION publishes literary and experimental fiction (including translations), favoring unconventional work between 1,000–20,000 words, with a strong preference for stories under 7,500 words. Submissions are electronic only via their Submissions Manager, with a narrow reading window of October 1–31 exclusively. Writers should note the very short annual reading period and that genre fiction, novel excerpts, poetry, plays, and hybrid work are explicitly rejected.

details.aesthetic: Multi-genre (fiction, poetry, CNF, drama/monologues, art, photography); character-driven, concise, human sensibility; themed issue ('The Truth Will Set You Free' — moments of potential release from dire circumstances, literal or not); no porn, excessive gore, gratuitous violence, or children's fiction; welcomes international contributors and written-plus-image pairings.
details.multiple_submissions: One piece at a time per genre (fiction, nonfiction, poetry, drama each limited to one submission at a time)
details.red_flags: Identifying information anywhere outside the cover-letter field results in disqualification with no fee refund; payment for regular submissions is contributors' copies only (no cash); journal reserves the right to edit or separate paired written/image submissions.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed — notify them as soon as accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction and nonfiction: aim for 2500 words or fewer; poetry: no strict limit but no epics or multi-part sequences; drama: aim for 5 min (monologue) or 7–9 min (dramatic work)

fiction writers review.index_line: American Writers Review: multi-genre, themed ('Truth Will Set You Free'), character-driven concise work; strict anonymity rule, $5 fee, disqualifies if broken
fiction writers review.name: *Fiction Writers Review
fiction writers review.summary: American Writers Review is a multi-genre journal seeking previously unpublished fiction, poetry, CNF, drama, art, and photography around a yearly theme ('The Truth Will Set You Free' for 2026), with a preference for character-driven, concise work with human sensibility. Regular submissions run Feb 2–Aug 1, 2026 with a $5 reading fee; contest submissions close July 1, 2026 with a $15 fee and a $250 prize. Writers should watch out for the strict no-identifying-information rule (violations mean disqualification with no refund) and the one-piece-at-a-time limit per genre.

details.aesthetic: Not a journal — this is a third-party aggregator/directory of literary magazines, featuring brief blurbs about many different publications.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This is a directory site, not a journal. There is no publication to submit to here.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

fictionweek literary review.index_line: Not a journal — a directory site listing other literary magazines; nothing here to submit to
fictionweek literary review.name: *FictionWeek Literary Review
fictionweek literary review.summary: This is not a literary journal but a directory site ('Literary Magazines') that catalogues and lists literary magazines to help writers find submission opportunities. It contains no content belonging to a single journal. There is nothing here a writer would submit to.

details.aesthetic: Short fiction only (including translations) across three length tiers; must be previously unpublished anywhere, including the writer's own blog or social media. No stated theme or form restrictions beyond prose fiction.
details.multiple_submissions: one story at a time; must await response before sending another
details.red_flags: No payment offered. Submission goes unread if writer fails to wait two months after a decline or withdrawal before resubmitting. No PDFs; do not paste story in email body. Work must not appear in another publication for three months post-publication; Fictive Dream retains non-exclusive electronic archival rights indefinitely and can remove stories without notice.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but writer must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: up to 2,500 words (microfiction up to 400; flash up to 1,000; short stories up to 2,500)

fictive dream.index_line: Fictive Dream: unpaid short fiction to 2,500 words, no theme restrictions; one at a time, two-month wait after decline
fictive dream.name: Fictive Dream
fictive dream.summary: Fictive Dream publishes short fiction (including translations) in three tiers—microfiction up to 400 words, flash up to 1,000, and short stories up to 2,500—with no stated thematic restrictions, prioritising unpublished work. Submit one story at a time via Word attachment to their Gmail; response within three weeks; no payment. Writers must wait two months after a decline or withdrawal before resubmitting, and violating this rule means the submission goes unread.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction, nonfiction, and poetry from established and emerging writers; values surprise and delight; publishes essays and book reviews; has featured BIPOC-focused special issues; each summer issue is devoted to a single genre.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Jan 1–Mar 31 (online, Canadian residents only); Sep 15–Nov 30 (online, open); year-round (postal only)
details.red_flags: Online submissions in the Jan–Mar window are restricted to Canadian writers only; no email submissions accepted; the long response window (6–9 months) combined with limited online reading periods may slow turnaround significantly for international writers.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with notice
details.word_limit: unknown

fiddlehead.index_line: Fiddlehead — literary fiction, nonfiction, poetry valuing surprise and delight; Jan–Mar online window Canadian-only, free, no email subs
fiddlehead.name: Fiddlehead
fiddlehead.summary: The Fiddlehead is a prestigious Canadian literary journal (est. 1945) publishing fiction, nonfiction, and poetry from both established and emerging writers, with a special annual single-genre summer issue. Online submissions have split reading windows (Canadian-only Jan–Mar, open Sept–Nov), while postal submissions are accepted year-round; response time is 6–9 months. No email submissions are accepted, and the Canadian-only restriction on the January window will block many international writers.

details.aesthetic: Not applicable — this is a multi-journal directory, not a single journal.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This is a Reedsy directory page, not a journal's own site. No submission guidelines for any specific journal are present here; the writer should visit each journal's own site directly.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

firmament.index_line: Firmament: not a journal — Reedsy directory listing 100+ magazines; visit each journal's own site for guidelines
firmament.name: Firmament
firmament.summary: This page is a third-party directory listing 100+ literary magazines, not the site of any single journal. It contains brief blurbs and metadata for many publications but no submission guidelines for any one journal in particular.

details.aesthetic: Literary and eclectic — short fiction, essays, poetry, interviews, letters, and international reporting, paired with contemporary illustration. The founding ethos celebrated 'canny and irrepressible' literary voices, suggesting a preference for distinctive, unconventional writing over mainstream or safe work.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Journal is no longer active; ceased publication in 2023. Do not submit.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

five dials.index_line: Five Dials — eclectic fiction, essays, poetry, illustrated international voices — DEFUNCT since 2023, do not submit
five dials.name: *Five Dials
five dials.summary: Five Dials was a Hamish Hamilton literary magazine (2008–2023) publishing short fiction, essays, poetry, interviews, letters, and reportage with an international scope and a characterful, misfit-celebrating sensibility. It is now defunct after 66 issues, so submissions are no longer possible.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, poetry, flash fiction, literary nonfiction, and translations; no specific themes stated—journal recommends ordering sample copies to understand tastes.
details.multiple_submissions: One prose piece per submission; up to three poems per poetry submission
details.red_flags: Response time can exceed four months and writers cannot query until five months have elapsed, making this a slow process; postal submissions are not accepted and will not be returned.
details.response_time: 4 weeks to 4+ months; do not query until 5 months have passed
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; no specific withdrawal condition stated
details.word_limit: Up to 7500 words for prose; up to 50 lines per poem

five points.index_line: Five Points: fiction/poetry/nonfiction, no stated aesthetic; reads Sept–Dec only; slow response, 5-month query wait
five points.name: Five Points
five points.summary: Five Points publishes fiction, poetry, flash fiction, literary nonfiction, and translations, favoring work best understood by reading sample issues. Prose is capped at 7500 words with one piece per submission; up to three poems (max 50 lines each) per submission; reading period is September 1–December 1. Response time can exceed four months and writers must wait five full months before querying—and submissions are Submittable-only, no postal mail.

details.aesthetic: Character- and place-centered literary fiction, non-fiction, and poetry with an emphasis on 'the meat of it'—real people, mistakes, day drinkers, fighters, hope and despair rendered with grit and honesty rather than message-driven writing; stylistically varied from spare lyric flash to grounded narrative prose, inclusive of emerging and established writers globally.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: unknown (currently closed, reopening soon per page)
details.red_flags: Submissions are currently closed, so guidelines/mechanics are not stated on this page; writer must check back later for specifics.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

five south.index_line: Five South: gritty, character-driven fiction/non-fiction/poetry—working-class lives, hospital bills, family relics; no soapboxing. Closed, reopening soon
five south.name: *Five South
five south.summary: Five South is an online, biannual literary journal publishing fiction, non-fiction, and poetry (plus a weekly poetry/flash fiction feature) grounded in grounded, character-driven storytelling—grit, honesty, working-class and everyday lives, memory, and place, with room for despair and hope but no soapboxing. Its published work ranges from lyrical flash and prose poems to narrative fiction about laborers, hospital bills, and family relics, favoring nuance and voice over polemic. Submissions are currently closed as of the page's timestamp, with reopening promised 'soon.'

details.aesthetic: Complete flash fiction, 500–1000 words, across speculative (sci-fi, fantasy, slipstream, horror) and literary fiction; crisp prose, well-developed characters, compelling plots, satisfying resolutions; no hatred/prejudice/violence toward any social group.
details.multiple_submissions: One story per call; may submit to separate concurrent calls (e.g., general + themed) but only one story per each call
details.reading_period: Closed as of August 2026; schedule posted on Patreon and Bluesky
details.red_flags: Strict AI policy: suspected AI-generated or AI-polished work is rejected and the account may be banned. No resubmissions of previously declined work unless editorially requested. No PDF, images, or graphics. Manuscript must be fully anonymized. Submissions emailed to the editor address are deleted unread.
details.response_time: Up to 10 weeks (query permitted if still in-progress after 10 weeks)
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify and withdraw immediately upon acceptance elsewhere

flash fiction online.index_line: Flash Fiction Online — 500–1000-word speculative/literary flash, crisp prose, strict no-AI policy; closed as of Aug 2026
flash fiction online.name: *Flash Fiction Online
flash fiction online.summary: Flash Fiction Online publishes complete 500–1000-word stories across speculative and literary genres, seeking crisp prose, well-developed characters, and satisfying resolutions. One story per call; simultaneous submissions allowed with prompt withdrawal notice; queries permitted after 10 weeks. Currently closed for submissions as of August 2026, and AI-generated or AI-polished work is strictly prohibited with potential account bans.

details.aesthetic: Short speculative fiction only (100–1,000 words): all subgenres of fantasy and science fiction, slipstream, seasonal/holiday stories. Wants work that provokes emotion or thought. No horror as primary appeal, no literary fiction without SF/F element, no gratuitous sex or violence, no fanfic, no previously published translations.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed; one story at a time
details.red_flags: No email submissions (deleted unread); poorly formatted submissions may be rejected unread; no reprints including anything publicly posted online; no AI-generated work; previously accepted authors limited to one story per calendar year; seasonal submissions must arrive at least 3 months before the occasion.
details.response_time: 30 days normal; contact after 60 days if no response
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed
details.word_limit: 100–1,000 words (November window: drabbles only, implying 100 words)

flash point science fiction.index_line: Flash SF/fantasy/slipstream, 100–1,000 words; strict Shunn format, no reprints/AI, one submission at a time, narrow windows
