flash point science fiction.name: Flash Point Science Fiction
flash point science fiction.summary: Flash Point Science Fiction publishes speculative flash fiction (SF, fantasy, slipstream) strictly between 100–1,000 words, with multiple short reading windows per year and a 30-day normal response time. No simultaneous or multiple submissions are allowed, and the format must follow Shunn manuscript style as a .doc/.docx or the story may be rejected unread. Watch out for the no-reprints rule (including anything publicly posted online), the no-AI policy, and the requirement to submit seasonal stories at least 3 months before the relevant occasion.

details.aesthetic: A general-interest literary journal open across genres—poetry, flash and traditional-length fiction, short ten-minute plays, flash and traditional creative nonfiction, and visual art/photography—without a stated thematic niche; university-affiliated (Emporia State) and modest in production (greyscale interior printing).
details.multiple_submissions: allowed to submit more than one genre/type at once, following per-genre limits; only one short story or one essay per submission
details.reading_period: November 1 - February 1 annually (submissions outside this window are logged and read next cycle)
details.red_flags: No longer accepts postal submissions; email submission only accepted in rare cases, otherwise Submittable required.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with a request to notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Short stories: one story 7-25 pages or up to three flash pieces (1-3 pages) each; essays: 5-25 pages traditional or 1-3 pages flash; plays: 10 minutes or shorter; poems: up to six poems

flint hills review.index_line: Flint Hills Review: general-interest annual—poetry, fiction, flash, ten-minute plays, CNF, art; no niche; reads Nov 1-Feb 1
flint hills review.name: Flint Hills Review
flint hills review.summary: Flint Hills Review is an annual literary journal (published through Emporia State University) accepting poetry, short stories, flash fiction, short plays, creative nonfiction, and artwork/photography, printed with greyscale interior images and a color cover. It reads once a year and welcomes simultaneous and multi-genre submissions within stated per-genre limits.

details.aesthetic: Innovative, voice-driven prose and poetry across realism, fabulism, minimalism, maximalism, lyric/braided/hermit crab/flash essays, literary journalism (with personal element), experimental and traditional poetry, and graphic narratives. Values surprise, risk, lush or spare language, emotional and intellectual depth.
details.fee: Small fee via Submittable (exact amount not stated)
details.multiple_submissions: One story or essay at a time (or up to 3 flash pieces under 15 pages total); no more than 5 poems at a time
details.red_flags: UCF faculty, staff, and current students cannot submit poetry, fiction, or nonfiction; alumni must wait 5 years after graduation. Submissions outside length guidelines will not be considered. Simultaneous submission policy not stated.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Up to 9,000 words (30 manuscript pages) for fiction/nonfiction; up to 5 poems at a time; up to 3 flash pieces if total is under 15 pages

florida review.index_line: Florida Review: voice-driven fiction/nonfiction (fabulism, hybrid/lyric essays) and risk-taking poetry; UCF affiliates barred from submitting
florida review.name: Florida Review
florida review.summary: The Florida Review seeks innovative, voice-driven fiction, nonfiction (realism, fabulism, lyric and hybrid essays), and poetry with emotional depth and formal risk, up to 9,000 words for prose and 5 poems per submission. A small Submittable fee applies; simultaneous submission policy is unstated. UCF faculty, staff, and students are excluded from poetry/fiction/nonfiction submissions, and alumni must wait five years post-graduation.

details.aesthetic: Queer and trans literary writing in all forms; especially cross-genre, intersectional, marginal, and transgressive work; both daring/risky pieces and tender/intimate ones; centers LGBTQ+ writers of color, youth, elders, and those outside traditional cultural centers.
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per genre per reading period only.
details.reading_period: Print: Feb 1–Apr 1 (Fall edition) and Aug 1–Oct 1 (Spring edition); Online: Aug 15–Oct 15 (Winter) and Feb 15–Apr 15 (Summer).
details.red_flags: Genre caps (poetry 500, fiction 250) may close early; withdrawing a submission does not free up your cap slot, so do not withdraw and resubmit with minor edits; previously published work not accepted; if work was recently accepted, must wait two reading periods (1 year) before submitting again; no AI-generated art for online issue.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must withdraw immediately if accepted elsewhere.
details.word_limit: Up to 7,500 words (fiction/nonfiction); 3–5 poems (max 5 pages); up to 20 pages (cross-genre/drama); online issue: up to 5 pieces, video/audio max 5 minutes.

foglifter.index_line: Foglifter: urgent, cross-genre queer/trans writing, centering QTPOC, youth, and elders; one submission per genre per window
foglifter.name: Foglifter
foglifter.summary: Foglifter publishes urgent, daring queer and trans writing in all forms, with particular interest in cross-genre, intersectional, and transgressive work by LGBTQ+ writers of color, youth, and elders. The print journal accepts 3–5 poems, up to 7,500 words of fiction/nonfiction, or up to 20 pages of cross-genre work during two annual windows (Feb 1–Apr 1 and Aug 1–Oct 1), with a $100 honorarium and no submission fee. Watch out for genre submission caps (500 for poetry, 250 for fiction), the one-submission-per-genre-per-period rule, and the policy that withdrawing and resubmitting counts against the cap.

details.aesthetic: Original creative work across forms (poetry, fiction, nonfiction, translations); past contributors suggest literary/experimental range; no harmful stereotypes or bigoted content accepted.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Currently closed; open period dates unknown
details.red_flags: No AI-generated work at any stage; no previously published work; current and former American University students and faculty are ineligible; submissions currently closed with no reopening date given.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must notify FOLIO and withdraw immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

folio.index_line: Folio: cross-genre literary work, no AI or reprints; closed to submissions; American University affiliates ineligible
folio.name: Folio
folio.summary: FOLIO is a nationally recognized literary journal (est. 1984) publishing original creative work across forms by new and established authors, with a strong anti-discrimination editorial stance. No word limits or response times are stated; submissions are currently closed. Writers should note the hard bans on AI-generated work, previously published work, and submissions from current or former American University students and faculty.

details.aesthetic: Craft-conscious literary work across poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and translation; editors emphasize 'fine attention to craft' paired with 'powerful and compelling voice,' finished but surprising stories, nonfiction that 'pushes at the corners of the form,' and poetry open to all styles and forms; actively encourages diverse voices; publishes interviews and artwork alongside genre work.
details.fee: $3 most months; free in January, April, August, and November
details.multiple_submissions: limited: poetry 3-5 poems per submission, up to 3 times/year; fiction/nonfiction one piece at a time, up to 3 times/year (flash allows up to 3 pieces per submission); translation same caps as respective genre
details.reading_period: year-round, but fee-free only in January, April, August, and November; may close specific genres early if submission caps are reached
details.red_flags: Unsolicited email submissions are discarded unread (must use online submissions manager); no individual responses to withdrawal requests; will not respond to manuscript (book) submissions; work must be previously unpublished.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must be noted in cover letter and journal must be informed immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: up to 6,000 words for fiction/nonfiction/translation prose; flash pieces under 1,000 words

four way review.index_line: Four Way Review: craft-forward poetry/fiction/nonfiction/translation, strong distinctive voice; $3 fee waived Jan/Apr/Aug/Nov; capped 3x/year
four way review.name: Four Way Review
four way review.summary: Four Way Review, the online triannual affiliated with independent press Four Way Books, publishes poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and translation that combines careful craft with a strong, distinctive voice, drawing from both established and emerging writers. It runs frequent open reading periods with a small $3 fee most months (waived in January, April, August, and November) and caps how often writers may submit per year, so it favors patient, guideline-attentive submitters over frequent ones.

details.aesthetic: Literary journal publishing poetry (up to 3 poems/7 pages), short fiction or novel excerpts, flash fiction, creative nonfiction, visual art, and experimental/hybrid work; unpublished and unsolicited only; annual Special Feature with its own theme each cycle; strong interest in BIPoC and LGBTQ+ voices.
details.fee: $3; waived for current subscribers and for financial hardship (email hills@sfsu.edu); free tier on Submittable for BIPoC/LGBTQ+ writers
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per period, in a single genre only
details.reading_period: General: open now through June 15; Special Feature: July 15 – September 30 annually
details.red_flags: AI-generated or AI-assisted work rejected on sight; submissions limited to one genre per period (easy to disqualify yourself); artwork must be 300 dpi at 8.5×11 inches with labeled ZIP files or may be mishandled; incarcerated authors must submit hard copy only
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must notify immediately via Submittable if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction/CNF: 6000 words or 20 pages; flash fiction: 1000 words per piece (up to 3); poetry/experimental: 7 pages (up to 3 pieces); visual art: up to 10 pieces

fourteen hills.index_line: Fourteen Hills: poetry/fiction/CNF/hybrid work welcoming BIPoC & LGBTQ+ voices; one genre per period, $3 fee, AI writing rejected
fourteen hills.name: Fourteen Hills
fourteen hills.summary: Fourteen Hills publishes poetry, fiction, flash fiction, creative nonfiction, visual art, and experimental/hybrid work, with a stated interest in BIPoC and LGBTQ+ writers. General submissions are open until June 15th; Special Feature submissions run July 15–September 30 annually; response time is 4–8 months; fee is $3 (waived for subscribers and fee-hardship requests). Writers should note the strict one-submission-per-period-per-genre rule, the AI-generated content rejection policy, and that the fee is not waived by default for marginalized communities (a separate free tier exists on Submittable).

details.aesthetic: Environmentally focused literary journal publishing poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and visual art (photography, painting, sculpture, paper art) organized around themed issues. Work engages nature, landscape, place, and ecological stewardship; contributors frequently hold MFAs and have publication credits in respected literary journals. The 'For the Birds' issue signals attentiveness to the nonhuman world, biodiversity, and habitat. Pittsburgh-connected but with national and international reach.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No submission guidelines present in this text; writer should locate the submissions page before proceeding.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

fourth river.index_line: Fourth River: Pittsburgh journal of place-based writing—poetry, fiction, nonfiction, art on nature, ecology, and human/nonhuman relations; themed issues (e.g. birds)
fourth river.name: Fourth River
fourth river.summary: The Fourth River is a Pittsburgh-based literary journal with a strong environmental and place-based sensibility, publishing poetry, fiction, nonfiction, and visual art; its themed issues (e.g., 'For the Birds,' Fall 2025) draw work exploring nature, habitat, stewardship, and human relationships to the nonhuman world. Contributors tend to be writers and artists with backgrounds in ecology, environmental journalism, and conservation. No submission mechanics were found in this text.

details.aesthetic: Flash and microfiction with emotional resonance; characters revealed through action; themes of human connection, sorrow, joy, and diversity. No experimental form requirements stated—voice and emotional impact are primary.
details.multiple_submissions: up to 2 stories per submission (in one document); must wait 1 month after initial reply before submitting again
details.red_flags: AI-generated or AI-assisted work is auto-declined. Submittable only—no email or postal submissions. 3-month post-publication exclusivity clause; no payment for reprints. Do not describe your stories in the cover letter.
details.response_time: up to 2 months (usually sooner); BIPOC fast-response track: 3 weeks or fewer
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify immediately and withdraw if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Micro: up to 400 words; Flash: 401–1,000 words

fractured lit.index_line: Fractured Lit — micro/flash (≤1,000 words), emotionally resonant human-condition stories; $50–75, no fee; AI-generated work auto-declined
fractured lit.name: *Fractured Lit
fractured lit.summary: Fractured Lit publishes emotionally resonant micro (≤400 words) and flash fiction (401–1,000 words) exploring the human condition, paying $50–$75 for originals with no submission fee. Year-round open via Submittable only; up to two stories per document, resubmit only after 1 month from initial reply. AI-generated work is automatically declined, and a 3-month post-publication exclusivity window applies.

details.aesthetic: Unknown — no published work, themes, or editorial sensibility discernible from the available text; the name 'Kingdom Writers' may suggest a faith-based or Christian literary orientation, but this is unconfirmed.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Extremely limited information available; informal presentation ('my next magazine issue') suggests a small personal project rather than an established literary venue — writer should research further before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

freight what are you carrying.index_line: Freight: no aesthetic or samples available; small Kingdom Writers Association project soliciting an issue — vet before submitting
freight what are you carrying.name: *Freight: What are You Carrying?
freight what are you carrying.summary: This appears to be a small, informal magazine operated by the Kingdom Writers Association Group, currently soliciting submissions for an upcoming issue. No published work, editorial aesthetic, or submission specifics are visible from this text. The absence of any concrete guidelines makes it impossible to assess fit or logistics.

details.aesthetic: All genres welcome, with strong preference for weird, formally risky, voice-driven work; accepts short fiction, flash fiction, creative nonfiction, and poetry for the print magazine.
details.multiple_submissions: allowed — 'submit as many pieces as you'd like'
details.red_flags: No refunds for incorrect submissions; 'previously unpublished' includes personal blogs, websites, and social media — stricter than many journals; no AI-generated work accepted; reading fees are non-negotiable as they fund contributor payments.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but withdraw immediately via Submittable if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Short fiction: 1,001–7,500 words; CNF: up to 6,500 words; flash: up to 1,000 words; poetry: up to 3 pages per poem, up to 5 poems per submission

friction.index_line: F(r)iction: weird, formally risky, voice-driven fiction/CNF/poetry; $2.50 fee, year-round, strict unpublished rule (no blogs/social media)
friction.name: F(r)iction
friction.summary: F(r)iction favors weird, risk-taking work with strong unique voice across fiction, flash, CNF, and poetry in all genres for its print magazine. Short fiction runs 1,001–7,500 words, CNF up to 6,500, flash up to 1,000, poetry up to 3 pages/5 poems, with a $2.50 submission fee and year-round reading. Writers should note that previously unpublished means no personal blogs or social media either, no AI-generated work is accepted, and refunds are not given for incorrect submissions.

details.aesthetic: Themed special issue: 'insanity' interpreted broadly—personal mental experience, family, community, nature, inanimate objects, animals, politics, the cosmic. Accepts poetry, flash fiction, short fiction, and creative nonfiction. Tone is informal and experimental; the editor's framing suggests range and irreverence are welcome.
details.multiple_submissions: Discouraged but not forbidden; editor prefers one poem, one flash, one story, or one CNF piece
details.reading_period: Closed as of June 6, 2026; reopening in 'a few weeks'
details.red_flags: Submissions currently closed. No work published or forthcoming in any active online venue. If declined without invitation to resubmit, must wait at least one month before sending more work.
details.response_time: Aiming for a few weeks or less after reopening
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: 500–3,000 words for prose and longer pieces; poetry may be under 500 words but not trivially short (e.g., a single haiku), unless exceptional

frigg.index_line: *Frigg*: 'Insanity Issue'—fiction, flash, poetry, CNF on insanity broadly construed; irreverent tone welcome. Closed now, reopens in weeks.
frigg.name: *Frigg
frigg.summary: Frigg is running a themed special issue ('The Insanity Issue') open to fiction, flash, poetry, and creative nonfiction loosely connected to 'insanity' in any sense—personal, political, natural, cosmic. Word count is 500–3,000 (poetry may be shorter); one piece per genre per writer is preferred. Submissions are currently closed as of June 6, 2026, reopening in a few weeks; work previously published in active online venues is not eligible.

details.aesthetic: Fiction that haunts and defies fixed shape; literary nonfiction that is structurally playful, hybrid, or essayistic; poetry curious about form and language with a distinct POV; art and genre-bending hybrid work; experimental reviews and interviews that push criticism into personal narrative, fabulism, or cross-medium conversation. Strong commitment to underrepresented voices across race, gender, sexuality, disability, and socioeconomic background.
details.fee: $3 per submission; fee waiver available for financial hardship via email
details.multiple_submissions: Multiple pieces allowed within genre limits (up to 5 poems, 2 short-shorts, 1 story, or 1 essay per submission), but submissions in more than one genre must be submitted separately
details.reading_period: Sep 1 – Nov 15 (general submissions); spring contests run separately
details.red_flags: Submissions close November 15—window is only ~10 weeks; each genre requires a separate Submittable submission and separate $3 fee; pieces over 15 pages are unlikely to be accepted; do not query status before 6 months
details.response_time: 4 months target; do not query until 6 months have elapsed
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must note in cover letter and notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: ~15 pages strongly preferred for fiction and nonfiction; poetry capped at 10 pages/3–5 poems; no explicit word count stated for reviews (long-form preferred); 'unknown' in strict word-count terms

fugue.index_line: Fugue: form-daring fiction/nonfiction/poetry/hybrid, ~15pp max; Sep 1–Nov 15 only, $3/genre, separate submissions each
fugue.name: Fugue
fugue.summary: Fugue publishes poetry, fiction, literary nonfiction, hybrid/art forms, and experimental reviews that prize formal daring, underrepresented voices, and work that lingers emotionally. General submissions run September 1–November 15 only, with a $3 fee per submission (fee waivers available on request) and a 4-month target response time. Writers should note the strict genre-by-genre piece limits, the requirement to submit each genre separately with a separate fee, and that pieces over roughly 15 pages face steep odds.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction and poetry that shocks, surprises, moves, or tickles — sometimes all at once. Canadian voices prioritized but international writers welcome. No genre fiction. Flash, short fiction, and poetry all accepted. Poetry selection is instinct-driven ('we'll know it when we see it').
details.multiple_submissions: allowed — 1 short fiction piece per entry; up to 3 flash pieces per entry; up to 3 poems per entry
details.reading_period: unknown (no open calls at time of page capture)
details.red_flags: No submissions currently open — writer must check back later. No pay for online-only publication (only print publication is paid). Name must not appear anywhere in the document or filename.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with condition: withdraw immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Short fiction: ~3000 words (a little over is fine); Flash fiction: under 1000 words; Poetry: unknown

funicular magazine.index_line: Funicular Magazine — lit fiction/poetry/flash that shocks or moves you, no genre; blind subs only; no pay online; CLOSED, no open calls
funicular magazine.name: Funicular Magazine
funicular magazine.summary: Funicular Magazine publishes literary fiction and poetry (including flash) that shocks, surprises, moves, or amuses — no genre fiction, no previously published work, and blind submissions only (no name on document). Short fiction is capped at ~3000 words, flash at ~1000 words, with up to 3 pieces allowed per entry for flash and poetry. There are currently no open calls for submissions, so the writer must wait for a reading period to open.

details.aesthetic: Character-driven, quiet, reflective science fiction or SF-tinged literary fiction; favors slipstream, cyberpunk, post-apocalypse, and the bizarre; high-adventure and humor pieces are discouraged. No reprints, no AI-written work.
details.multiple_submissions: One story at a time; may submit another immediately after rejection
details.reading_period: Odd-numbered months only (one month windows): next periods are Nov 1–30 2026, Jan 1–31 2027, Mar 1–31 2027
details.red_flags: Submissions currently closed with infrequent, short windows (one month every two months); pays in CAD; feedback on rejections is rare and only a 1–2 sentence summary when offered at all
details.response_time: Aim of 30 days; query if no response within 45 days
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but must withdraw immediately if accepted elsewhere

fusion fragment.index_line: Fusion Fragment: quiet, character-driven SF/slipstream, no humor or high-adventure; closed until Nov 1, odd-month windows only
fusion fragment.name: Fusion Fragment
fusion fragment.summary: Fusion Fragment publishes character-driven, quiet SF and SF-tinged literary fiction (slipstream, cyberpunk, post-apocalypse, bizarre) in the 2,000–15,000 word range, explicitly disfavoring high-adventure or humorous tones and rejecting AI-written work and reprints. Submissions are currently closed, opening November 1st, with one-month reading windows on odd-numbered months only. Writers should note the strict no-AI and no-reprint policies, and that simultaneous submissions require prompt withdrawal if accepted elsewhere.

details.aesthetic: Scholarly essays and criticism aimed at a wide public readership; sections span literary fiction, poetry, literature in translation, higher education, technology, politics, urbanism, TV, music, sports, and more. Tone is serious and idea-driven but not jargon-heavy—think long-form intellectual journalism grounded in academic expertise. Contributors are typically academics, critics, and researchers.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No submission guidelines found anywhere on the site; the journal appears to operate via solicited contributions from academics and established critics rather than open submissions. A writer should contact section editors directly before attempting to submit.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

galaxy brain.index_line: Galaxy Brain (Public Books): academic essays/criticism for general readers, culture-to-politics; solicited only, no open submissions
galaxy brain.name: Galaxy Brain
galaxy brain.summary: Public Books is an academic-public crossover magazine publishing essays, reviews, and criticism across literature, politics, culture, technology, and the arts—written by scholars and academics for a broad, educated audience. Its work is intellectually serious but accessible, blending university expertise with public-interest writing on topics from syllabus data and Weber to literary fiction and global Black history. No submission guidelines were found; this appears to be an invitation-only or editor-solicited publication.

details.aesthetic: Themed anthologies of SF and fantasy short fiction; current theme is ocean myths and creatures (mermaids, selkies, etc.) with a preference for fantasy and urban fantasy, accepting hints of darkness or SF as long as the core is fantastical; diverse world mythologies strongly encouraged; no horror even with supernatural elements; no unoriginal trend-chasing without a distinct twist.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed — one story per anthology call only
details.reading_period: September 1 – October 1 (next opening; current anthology closed to open submissions)
details.red_flags: Trunk stories (previously rejected by this editor at any publication) are banned even with revisions; manuscript format deviations result in deletion with no warning; italics must be rendered as underlines due to editor's visual impairment; open submissions for the current anthology (A Call of the Ocean) are already closed as of the page date.
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed — explicitly prohibited with a strong warning
details.word_limit: up to 4,000 words

galaxys edge.index_line: Galaxy's Edge — themed fantasy/SF anthologies (next: ocean myths, no horror); closed now, reopens Sept 1–Oct 1, no trunk stories or sims
galaxys edge.name: Galaxy's Edge
galaxys edge.summary: Galaxy's Edge publishes themed SF/fantasy anthologies (current theme: ocean creatures and myths, skewing fantasy/urban fantasy, no horror); stories must be original, unpublished, and under 4,000 words, submitted via Moksha portal only during the open window (next opening September 1–October 1). Open submissions for the current anthology are closed; no simultaneous or multiple submissions are tolerated, and trunk stories (previously rejected by this editor) are explicitly banned.

details.aesthetic: Eclectic literary mix: fiction (flash to ~20 pages max in recent years), poetry, essays, reviews, interviews, graphics. Covers social issues (homelessness, war, economy) alongside timeless themes (love, loss, sex, family). Edgy material and genre-adjacent literary work welcomed. Strong Washington DC literary identity.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Approximately June 1 through mid-to-late June (historically until July 1 or until full); does not read outside of June
details.red_flags: Reading window is extremely narrow (as short as 17 days) and closes early if they fill up. Acceptance rates are very low: ~1 in 60 for poetry, ~1 in 40 for fiction. This page is a 2013 blog interview, not an official submissions page—key details like fees, simultaneous submission policy, and current reading dates are absent.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

gargoyle.index_line: Gargoyle: edgy eclectic lit (fiction/poetry/essays/graphics), literary not genre despite name; tiny June-only window, very low odds
gargoyle.name: Gargoyle
gargoyle.summary: Gargoyle publishes eclectic literary work—fiction, poetry, essays, reviews, interviews, and graphics—with an edgy, contemporary voice covering both timely social themes and timeless human ones. Their reading period is extremely short (historically around June 1–17 or until full), so timing is critical. Writers who haven't read the magazine frequently misjudge its aesthetic; it is literary, not sci-fi or horror despite the name.

details.aesthetic: Serious, wide-ranging literary journal with strong presence in all major genres: lyric and narrative poetry, literary fiction, long-form essays (including cultural criticism and adapted nonfiction), translations from multiple languages (Uyghur, Chinese, French), and in-depth book reviews of poetry collections, criticism, and nonfiction. Visual art folios with critical apparatus are a recurring feature. Work tends toward the intellectually ambitious and culturally engaged—topics include race, history, medicine, grief, and identity.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No submission guidelines visible on this page; writer must locate a dedicated submissions page before attempting to submit.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

georgia review the.index_line: Georgia Review, The — Intellectually ambitious fiction, poetry, essays, translation, and art folios; culturally engaged work on race, history, grief, identity
georgia review the.name: Georgia Review, The
georgia review the.summary: The Georgia Review is a prestigious literary quarterly publishing fiction, poetry, essays, translations, visual art, and book reviews, with a notably wide-ranging and serious sensibility—recent work spans Uyghur poetry in translation, Tulsa reparations journalism, elegies, and experimental fiction. Contributors include established names (Reginald McKnight) alongside emerging voices, and the journal integrates substantial art folios. No submission mechanics were visible on this page.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and art/comics; journal directs writers to purchase an issue to understand specific tastes. Occasional special categories and contests (poetry, flash fiction, poetry comics, flash nonfiction).
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per genre per submission period; art/comics limited to twice per year
details.reading_period: Nov 1 – Jan 15 (subject to change); art/comics open year-round
details.red_flags: Compensation is one contributor copy only, no payment; response time for art/comics can stretch to 10 months across two submission periods; reading period dates are subject to change so writers should verify before submitting.
details.response_time: Up to 4 months for writing; up to 10 months for art/comics
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must notify via Submittable form ASAP upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

gigantic sequins.index_line: Gigantic Sequins: poetry, fiction, CNF, art/comics; read an issue first; Nov 1–Jan 15; copy-only payment, no fee
gigantic sequins.name: Gigantic Sequins
gigantic sequins.summary: Gigantic Sequins publishes poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and art/comics, and recommends reading an issue before submitting to understand their aesthetic. Open reading period typically runs November 1–January 15 (subject to change), with a 4-month response window for writing and up to 10 months for art/comics. Writers should note the one-submission-per-genre-per-period rule and that compensation is a single contributor copy only.

details.aesthetic: Recovery-themed work interpreted broadly (grief, war, addiction, illness, loss, etc.); fiction should show character development, psychological penetration, and lyricism without sentimentality or purple prose; essays exploratory rather than journalistic or academic; poetry need not be first-person or autobiographical.
details.multiple_submissions: Up to 3 poems allowed in one submission (in one document); no explicit statement on multiple prose submissions
details.reading_period: Closed during summer months; open January, April, July, and October publication cycle
details.red_flags: Closed to submissions during summer months — timing could trip up writers; all poems must be in a single document or submission will likely be rejected.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Prose up to 3,000 words; flash (S.O.S.) under 1,000 words; up to 3 poems per submission

glossolalia.index_line: Rkvry Quarterly: recovery-themed poetry/fiction/essays (grief, addiction, illness); lyrical, unsentimental; closed summers; $10 pay
glossolalia.name: *Glossolalia
glossolalia.summary: Rkvry Quarterly publishes poetry, fiction, flash, and essays unified by a broad 'recovery' theme (grief, addiction, exile, illness, etc.), valuing lyricism and psychological depth without sentimentality. Prose runs under 3,000 words, flash under 1,000, and up to three poems per submission; pays $10 on publication. Submissions close during summer months, so writers should check timing before submitting.

details.aesthetic: Lifts strange, daring, underrepresented voices from the heartland and beyond; publishes poetry, short fiction, flash fiction, micro fiction, CNF (all lengths), and Spanish-to-English translations; nominates for Pushcart, Best of the Net, Best Small Fictions, Best Microfictions, and Pen/Dau.
details.fee: $4 for poetry and short fiction/CNF; $2.50 for flash fiction and flash CNF
details.multiple_submissions: Allowed, but the submission fee applies to each
details.reading_period: Year-round, with seasonal issue cycles: Jan 21–Apr 20 (Summer), Apr 21–Jul 20 (Autumn), Jul 21–Oct 20 (Winter), Oct 21–Jan 20 (Spring)
details.red_flags: Per-submission fee even for multiple submissions; poetry portal closes after 100 submissions received (hard cap); work must be 'previously uncurated' (not just unpublished — personal blogs/social media are fine, but formally curated prior appearances are not); blind review required (name must be removed from document)
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; withdraw via Submittable if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Poetry: up to 5 poems / 10 pages per submission; flash prose: 400–1000 words; micro prose: under 400 words; short fiction/CNF upper limit cut off in page content but appears to start above 1000 words

good life review.index_line: Good Life Review: strange, daring, heartland-adjacent voices; poetry/fiction/flash/CNF; $4 fee each, blind review, 100-sub poetry cap
good life review.name: *Good Life Review
good life review.summary: The Good Life Review publishes poetry, fiction, flash, micro, and CNF with a mission to lift underrepresented and heartland-adjacent voices; fees are $4 for standard submissions and $2.50 for flash/CNF, with a 4-month response time and a 100-submission cap per poetry portal. Multiple submissions are allowed but each incurs a fee, and the journal is always open with rolling seasonal reading periods. Writers should note the blind-review requirement (remove name from document), the 'previously uncurated' standard (not just unpublished), and that submission caps can close portals at any time.

details.aesthetic: Eclectic, engaging, and challenging literary writing and art; genres include poetry, fiction, literary nonfiction, short plays, comics, translations, and experimental/hybrid work; actively seeks and prioritizes submissions from Black, Indigenous, POC, 2SLGBTQ+, and disabled writers during a dedicated window; visual art largely by invitation, Canada-based artists only.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed - one genre only, one submission per author per volume year; subsequent submissions will not be read or returned
details.reading_period: Regular submissions Sept 15 - June 15 (closed until reopening Sept 15, 2026); additional window June 16 - Sept 14 for under-represented/marginalized writers
details.red_flags: Manuscripts received outside the reading window are automatically rejected; no emailed submissions accepted; mailed submissions require SASE or reply-only email or they will not be read or returned; only one submission per author published per volume year; visual work mostly by invitation only.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction and nonfiction up to 3500 words; poetry up to 6 pages; other/hybrid work up to 3500 words or 5 pages; book reviews 450 words; interviews and craft essays 900 words

grain magazine.index_line: Grain: eclectic/experimental poetry, fiction, nonfiction, hybrid work; pays per page; one submission per genre per year, strict windows
grain magazine.name: Grain Magazine
grain magazine.summary: Grain is a long-running, internationally acclaimed Canadian literary quarterly publishing eclectic, surprising poetry, fiction, literary nonfiction, and hybrid/experimental work from Canadian and international writers. It pays $50 per printed page (up to $250, or $500 for cover art) and enforces strict, narrow submission windows and one-submission-per-genre-per-year limits.

details.aesthetic: Diverse, globally minded work across fiction, nonfiction (essays, reportage, criticism, memoir), and poetry; interested in engaged citizenship and stories from outside major metropolitan centers; welcomes translations (with original text attached); all work must be in English and previously unpublished.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Journal explicitly disclaims responsibility for lost submissions and will not correspond about them; fiction and other genres use different email addresses, so misdirected submissions are a real risk.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 5,000 words; essays and reportage: 2,500–4,000 words; poetry: unknown

grand journal.index_line: Grand Journal: global, civically engaged fiction/nonfiction/poetry, non-metro voices, translations welcome; separate emails per genre, no-fee, year-round
grand journal.name: Grand Journal
grand journal.summary: Grand Journal publishes fiction, nonfiction (essays, reportage, memoir, criticism), and poetry with a global, civically engaged outlook that resists metropolitan bias and welcomes translations; fiction tops out at 5,000 words and essays at 4,000, with year-round submissions for a biannual print edition and an online outlet. Response time is up to three months and simultaneous submissions are allowed with immediate notification upon acceptance elsewhere. Writers should note that the journal accepts no responsibility for lost submissions and will not engage in correspondence about them.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction and non-fiction (essays, memoir); champions new, underrepresented, and international voices; publishes original English-language work and original translations never before published in English; no academic essays, reviews, or poetry currently (poetry submissions paused).
details.fee: £3.50 per submission (waivable for low-income writers via application; 200 free slots per window)
details.multiple_submissions: One piece per genre per window; submitting multiple pieces in the same genre is not allowed
details.reading_period: Four windows in 2026: 1–31 March, 1–30 June, 1–30 September, 1–31 December
details.red_flags: Work previously published anywhere online or in print is ineligible; no feedback provided on submissions; poetry submissions currently closed; book manuscripts and proposals not accepted
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: No set limit; typical submissions are 3,000–6,000 words

granta.index_line: Granta: literary fiction/nonfiction, international and underrepresented voices; first-English-publication only, no poetry; £3.50 fee, four windows/year
granta.name: Granta
granta.summary: Granta publishes literary fiction and non-fiction (3,000–6,000 words typical) with a strong international, translated, and underrepresented-voices focus; submissions open four one-month windows per year with a £3.50 fee (waivable for low-income writers). Only first-ever English publication is accepted, no previously web-published work, and one piece per genre per window—no feedback given.

details.aesthetic: Great Plains and rural Nebraska literature — poetry and prose rooted in place, pioneer heritage, ecological and political concerns, and contemporary Midwestern life. Past readers include William Kloefkorn, Twyla Hansen, Traci Brimhall, Debra Marquart, and Josip Novakovich, suggesting a range from accessible regionalist work to more formally ambitious literary writing.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This is a college reading series and public event program, not a literary magazine that accepts manuscript submissions. A writer cannot submit work here; they might seek an invitation to read.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

great plains quarterly.index_line: Not a journal — Wayne State College's public reading series for Great Plains/Nebraska writers; no submissions accepted
great plains quarterly.name: Great Plains Quarterly
great plains quarterly.summary: WSC Press hosts the Plains Writers Series, a long-running (since 1977) reading and event series at Wayne State College in Wayne, Nebraska, focused on Great Plains and rural Nebraska prose and poetry. This is a public reading/event series, not a literary journal that accepts submissions. No submission guidelines exist here.

details.aesthetic: Poetry (3–6 poems, visual poetry welcome), fiction that is 'fully embodied' and reveals something new, and nonfiction that bends genre through structural risk-taking, multiple voices, research, and chronological deviation; memoir must engage larger ideas beyond personal story.
details.multiple_submissions: Poetry: one submission of 3–6 poems; Fiction: one story only; Nonfiction: one piece only
details.reading_period: Open now for Issue 73 (specific dates not stated)
details.red_flags: Nonfiction is fact-checked; poetry for Issue 72 is not being read; the $2 fee is new due to Submittable free-submission cap being reached; review essays require direct email contact rather than Submittable
details.response_time: Up to 6 months (query after 6 months if no response)
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately by withdrawing prose via Submittable or noting withdrawn poems for poetry submissions if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Poetry: up to 10 pages for 3–6 poems; Fiction: up to 9,000 words (one story); Nonfiction: up to 9,000 words (one piece)

great river review.index_line: Great River Review: fiction/nonfiction to 9,000 words, genre-bending nonfiction favored; poetry closed for Issue 72; $2 fee
great river review.name: Great River Review
great river review.summary: Great River Review publishes poetry (3–6 poems), fiction, and nonfiction (both up to 9,000 words) with a preference for fully realized, risk-taking work that deepens on re-reading. Submissions are open for Issue 73 with a $2 USD fee due to Submittable limits. Writers should note that poetry for Issue 72 is closed, nonfiction will be fact-checked, and the response window can stretch to six months before a query is appropriate.

details.aesthetic: No fixed theme, subject, or style; editors chase surprising, risk-taking work across fiction and poetry; welcomes previously unpublished writers and underrepresented voices; diverse editorial staff each year.
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per genre per submission period only
details.reading_period: Nov 1 – Jan 1 (general); Jun 1 – Aug 1 for Robert Watson Literary Prizes contest only
details.red_flags: Very narrow reading window (Nov 1–Jan 1); $3 fee applies to non-subscribers; no email submissions accepted—Submittable only; summer submissions route only through their contest, not general submissions.
details.response_time: By May 31 (acceptances in May; non-acceptances released by May 31)
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately via Submittable if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction up to 7,500 words (or 25 double-spaced pages); flash fiction up to 500 words; one story per submission. Poetry up to 10 pages, recommended 5–7 poems; individual poems rarely exceed 2 pages.

greensboro review.index_line: Greensboro Review: no-theme fiction/poetry seeking "bolt of lightning" voice; Nov 1–Jan 1 only, one submission per genre, $3 fee unless subscriber
greensboro review.name: Greensboro Review
greensboro review.summary: The Greensboro Review seeks surprising, non-thematic short fiction and poetry that reads as a 'bolt of lightning'—no house style, strong emphasis on voice and freshness. Submissions open November 1–January 1 only (Fall issue); there is a $3 reading fee waived for subscribers. Writers should note the narrow window, the per-genre once-only rule, and that the fee applies unless they verify subscriber status.

details.aesthetic: Themed non-fiction and fiction responding to 'Bodies of Work': the human body in digital/modern life, looksmaxxing, biohacking, disability, gender identity, and historic/present perceptions of bodily states. No pitches; full submissions only.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: July 13 – August 23 (closes 11:59 pm AEST, Sunday 23 August 2026)
details.red_flags: Poetry excluded from this call (separate poetry call-out opens September 7). No pitches accepted — full manuscripts only. Themed issue, so off-theme work will not fit.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: up to 4,000 words

griffith review.index_line: Griffith Review 95: fiction/nonfiction on 'Bodies of Work' (embodiment, disability, gender, tech); 4,000 words, full MS only, no poetry, closes Aug 23
griffith review.name: Griffith Review
griffith review.summary: Griffith Review 95 seeks themed non-fiction and fiction responding to 'Bodies of Work' — embodiment, digital life, disability, gender, and bodily identity. Submissions are capped at 4,000 words and open July 13 to August 23 (poetry submissions open separately on September 7). Writers should note that pitches are not accepted — full manuscripts only — and poetry is excluded from this call.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, craft essays, interviews, book reviews, and visual art; no restrictions on form, style, or subject matter; emphasis on high quality from both emerging and established writers; reviews focus on small, independent, and university press books only.
details.fee: $4 (waived for subscribers); covers 3–5 poems or one prose piece up to 7,000 words; first 100 submissions on Aug 1 are fee-free
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed; must wait for a response to current submission before submitting again in the same genre
details.reading_period: Aug 1 – Oct 31 (genres may close early if submission caps are reached)
details.red_flags: No submissions from anyone currently or recently affiliated with UT Knoxville; no back-to-back issue acceptances; caps on genre slots mean late submitters may be locked out; conduct clause allows disqualification for public or private behavior contradicting journal's stated values
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 7,000 words for fiction, nonfiction, and craft essays; 3–5 poems; reviews approximately 700 words

grist.index_line: Grist: open-aesthetic fiction/poetry/CNF up to 7K words; Aug 1–Oct 31, $4 fee, capped genre slots fill fast
grist.name: Grist
grist.summary: Grist publishes high-quality fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, craft essays, reviews, and visual art with no restrictions on form, style, or subject matter, drawing from both emerging and established writers. Submissions open August 1–October 31 with a $4 fee (waived for subscribers), caps on genre slots (100 fee-free on Aug 1, then 500 fiction, 500 poetry, 150 CNF), and a 7,000-word prose limit. Writers should note: no submissions from those currently or recently affiliated with UT Knoxville, no back-to-back issue acceptances, and one submission per genre at a time until a response is received.

details.aesthetic: unknown
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: All actual guidelines are hosted on Submittable, not this page; no pitches accepted, only completed manuscripts. Writer must check Submittable for all current details before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

guernica.index_line: Guernica — no stated aesthetic here; guidelines live on Submittable, completed manuscripts only, no pitches
guernica.name: *Guernica
guernica.summary: Guernica's submissions page defers all editorial guidelines to their Submittable profile, so no aesthetic, word limit, or reading period details are available here. Only completed manuscripts are accepted—no pitches—and submissions must go through Submittable. Writers must visit Submittable directly to get current guidelines before submitting.

details.aesthetic: Open to all aesthetic affiliations; publishes poetry, fiction, nonfiction, translations, interviews, single/first-book reviews, critical art writing, and online exclusives including prose and poetry.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed — multiple submissions in the same genre are rejected unread; must wait for a response before submitting again
details.reading_period: Sep 1 – Mar 1 (print); online exclusives reading period not stated
details.red_flags: Multiple submissions in the same genre are not read or responded to; accepted authors must wait two years from publication date before resubmitting; no email or postal submissions accepted.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify promptly if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Print prose: up to 7,000 words; online prose: soft cap at 3,000 words; interviews: up to 12 pages; single-book reviews: up to 4 pages; translation prose: up to 20 double-spaced pages.

gulf coast.index_line: Gulf Coast: all-aesthetic poetry/fiction/nonfiction/translation/criticism; Sep 1–Mar 1; $3 fee; no multiple subs, one genre at a time
gulf coast.name: Gulf Coast
gulf coast.summary: Gulf Coast publishes poetry, fiction, nonfiction, translations, interviews, and critical art writing across all aesthetic affiliations, for both a print edition and online exclusives. Print submissions open September 1–March 1; prose capped at 7,000 words, poetry up to five poems, with a $3 reading fee. Multiple submissions in the same genre are rejected unread, and accepted authors must wait two years before resubmitting.

details.aesthetic: Scottish and international writing that challenges, re-imagines, or undermines the status quo; pushes boundaries of form and function; rejects literary/genre distinctions. Accepts poetry, fiction, and essays.
details.multiple_submissions: One prose submission per issue; poetry up to 3 poems in one document
details.reading_period: Two annual windows: Spring and Autumn (currently closed)
details.red_flags: Strict file-naming convention required (firstname_surname_form); misnamed files may not be read. Work must be previously unpublished in print and online. Submissions currently closed.
details.response_time: Within 10 weeks of the submissions window closing
details.simultaneous_submissions: Not allowed
details.word_limit: Fiction and essays: up to 2500 words; Poetry: up to 3 poems totalling no more than 100 lines

gutter.index_line: Gutter — Scottish/international fiction, poetry, essays blurring literary-genre lines; strict file-naming; closed except two annual windows
gutter.name: Gutter
gutter.summary: Gutter publishes new Scottish and international fiction, poetry, and essays that challenge form and the status quo, rejecting distinctions between literary and genre writing. Submissions open twice yearly (Spring and Autumn); prose capped at 2500 words, poetry up to 3 poems/100 lines; response within 10 weeks of window closing. No simultaneous submissions and strict file-naming rules—misnamed files may not be read.

details.aesthetic: Minimalist, informal, irreverent fiction inspired by early web journals (elimae, McSweeney's, eyeshot, Surgery of Modern Warfare); no specific theme stated.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Sporadic, announced in real-time via Twitter/email/SMS; open for only a few hours at a time
details.red_flags: Submissions open unpredictably for only a few hours; writer must follow Twitter or subscribe to SMS/email alerts or will almost certainly miss the window entirely.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

had magazine.index_line: HAD: minimalist, irreverent flash fiction, early-web sensibility; no fee; opens for hours only, follow Twitter or miss it
had magazine.name: *HAD Magazine
had magazine.summary: HAD publishes flash/short fiction in a minimalist, informal aesthetic nodding to early web lit journals like elimae and eyeshot. Submissions open sporadically for only a few hours at a time, announced via Twitter, email, or text—with a 24-hour max response time. Writers must monitor social media or sign up for notifications to catch the window, as there is no predictable reading period.

details.aesthetic: Long-form narrative journalism, essays, and literary fiction; fine writing and original thought on politics, society, environment, and culture; also publishes experimental/short-form pieces in sections like Readings and the Harper's Index.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Submissions must be sent by physical mail only — no email for fiction or nonfiction queries. Unsolicited nonfiction manuscripts and poetry will not be considered or returned. No individual acknowledgment due to volume, so writers get no confirmation their work arrived.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

harpers.index_line: Harper's: elite long-form journalism, essays, fiction on politics/culture; fiction by mail only, no poetry, no email, no confirmation
harpers.name: Harper’s
harpers.summary: Harper's publishes long-form narrative journalism, essays, and fiction from both emerging and established voices, with a focus on politics, society, environment, and culture. Fiction submissions are accepted unsolicited by mail only; nonfiction requires a query with SASE, and poetry is flatly rejected. Writers must use postal mail for all submissions, and volume means no individual acknowledgment, so don't expect a confirmation.

details.aesthetic: Fiction: strange, off-kilter, scene-driven; literary and experimental; flash to short story. Nonfiction: narrative and hybrid forms, diverse voices. Poetry: strong lyric voice, urgency, hybridity, raw emotion, disjunction with intention, edgy work.
details.fee: none (note: related prizes listed separately do charge fees)
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per reading period only; flash categories allow up to 3 pieces in one submission
details.reading_period: Poetry & nonfiction: open through Oct 15, 2026; fiction: opens Jan 1, 2027 through Mar 15, 2027
details.red_flags: Fiction is closed until January 2027; submission caps may close periods early; no payment offered; prize contests charge fees (separate from regular submissions)
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed
details.word_limit: Flash fiction up to 1,000 words (up to 3 pieces); short story 1,000–4,500 words; essays/narrative nonfiction up to 5,500 words (flash up to 1,000, up to 3 pieces); poetry: no line limits stated, up to 3 pieces.

harpur palate.index_line: Strange, scene-driven fiction; urgent hybrid nonfiction; raw lyric poetry—no pay; fiction closed until Jan 2027
harpur palate.name: Harpur Palate
harpur palate.summary: Harpur Palate seeks strange, scene-driven fiction (up to 4,500 words), urgent lyric poetry, and narrative/hybrid nonfiction (up to 5,500 words) with diverse voices and experimental edges. Fiction is closed until January 2027; poetry and nonfiction close October 15, 2026; submit only once per reading period via Submittable. No payment, no reprints, and the journal may close early if submission caps are hit.

details.aesthetic: Art, fiction, and poetry of any form or length; fiction typically 700–7000 words; poetry includes traditional written styles plus illustrated/nontraditional forms like poetry comics.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Outside contributors accepted only 'at discretion' — the journal is primarily for the Harvard community; name must not appear anywhere in the submitted document or submission will likely be disqualified from anonymous review.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: No minimum or maximum; fiction typically 700–7000 words

harvard advocate.index_line: Harvard Advocate: art, fiction, poetry any form; outside writers accepted only at discretion, mostly Harvard-affiliated; anonymous review, no fee
harvard advocate.name: Harvard Advocate
harvard advocate.summary: The Harvard Advocate publishes art, fiction, and poetry of any form, primarily from the Harvard community but with outside contributors considered at their discretion; fiction tends toward 700–7000 words with no hard limits, and all submissions are reviewed anonymously. They are currently accepting rolling digital submissions for their Summer 2026 issue with no stated response time or fee. Outside contributors should note they are only accepted 'at discretion,' and writers must ensure their name appears nowhere in submitted documents.

details.aesthetic: Short fiction, poetry, and essays across all career stages; no specific themes or forms stated beyond general literary publishing.
details.fee: Yes, via Submittable (amount not stated; waivable for financial hardship by emailing info@harvardreview.org)
details.multiple_submissions: No more than twice per year
details.red_flags: No status inquiries accepted; book reviews are solicited only; no paper submissions; do not email editors to withdraw a Submittable submission.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify via Submittable withdrawal (not email) if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 7,000 words prose; up to 5 poems

harvard review.index_line: Harvard Review: general literary fiction, poetry, essays, no stated aesthetic slant; fee via Submittable, max 2 submissions/year, 6mo response
harvard review.name: Harvard Review
harvard review.summary: Harvard Review publishes short fiction, poetry, and essays with no stated thematic or formal restrictions beyond general literary quality. Prose is capped at 7,000 words and poetry at 5 poems; submissions are limited to twice per year and go through Submittable, which charges a reading fee (waivable for hardship). Book reviews are solicited only, no paper submissions are accepted, and the journal cannot respond to status inquiries.

details.aesthetic: Literary poetry (left-margin preferred, no unorthodox spacing), literary short fiction (not genre), creative nonfiction (narrative essays, memoir — no journalism or academic work), and flash fiction/nonfiction in the same mold; work about Hawai'i and the Pacific welcomed but not required.
details.multiple_submissions: Poetry: up to 3 poems (each as a separate submission); Flash fiction/nonfiction: up to 3 pieces (each separate); Fiction and CNF: one submission at a time
details.reading_period: August through February (or until backlog is full)
details.red_flags: Window may close before February if backlog grows too large — no advance notice given. HPR faculty and students are categorically ineligible. Poems with unorthodox or non-left-margin spacing are strongly discouraged. All files must be submitted as Word documents.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify and withdraw via Submittable immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction and CNF: up to 4,000 words; Flash fiction and flash nonfiction: up to 750 words; Poetry: no word limit stated

hawaii review.index_line: Hawai'i Review: literary poetry, fiction, CNF, and flash; strict left-margin poetry only; closes early if backlog fills, so submit by August
hawaii review.name: Hawai’i Review
hawaii review.summary: HPR is an award-winning online literary journal publishing poetry, literary fiction, and creative nonfiction (including flash) from all regions, with a preference for literary over genre work and left-margin-aligned poetry. Fiction and CNF cap at 4,000 words; flash caps at 750; up to 3 poems or flash pieces at a time, but only one fiction or CNF submission at a time. The reading window closes in February or earlier if the backlog grows too large, so submit early; HPR faculty and students are ineligible.

details.aesthetic: International literary journal publishing poetry, fiction, essays, visual art, and translations into English; strongly committed to amplifying Black, Indigenous, BIPOC, LGBTQIA+, and disability community voices alongside diverse global perspectives.
details.fee: $3 per submission; free tier available for underrepresented writers (at least 50 free slots per genre)
details.multiple_submissions: one submission per genre at a time (print); one submission at a time (web); second submission will not be read
details.reading_period: unknown (translations open year-round; other genres open during unspecified submission periods)
details.red_flags: No AI-generated work (whole or partial); no previously published work including social media and Substack; ASU-affiliated writers must wait 3 years after disaffiliation; prior HFR contributors must wait 2 years before resubmitting; submitting in wrong genre results in automatic decline; submitters auto-enrolled in newsletter
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; must notify and withdraw via Submittable immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Poetry: up to 3 poems totaling 8 pages; prose: under 20 pages (hard stop at 25 for translations); translations: up to 6 poems/micro-fictions or one essay/story, preferred under 17 pages

haydens ferry.index_line: Hayden's Ferry: fiction/poetry/essays/translations centering BIPOC & LGBTQIA+ voices; $3 fee; no AI; 6mo response
haydens ferry.name: Hayden’s Ferry
haydens ferry.summary: Hayden's Ferry Review (ASU) publishes fiction, poetry, essays, visual art, and translations with a commitment to diverse and underrepresented voices on a national and global scale. Poetry is capped at 3 poems/8 pages; prose under 20 pages double-spaced; translations up to 6 poems/micro-fictions or one essay/story, favoring under 17 pages. Watch out for the $3 fee (free tier for underrepresented writers), a strict no-AI and no-previously-published policy (including social media and Substack), a 2-year resubmission wait after prior publication in HFR, and a 3-year embargo for anyone affiliated with ASU.

details.aesthetic: Libertarian-perspective reviews and commentary on SF/fantasy (and other genres secondarily); themes of liberty, individualism, free markets, resistance to tyranny; balanced rather than purely scathing criticism preferred; also accepts movie, TV, comics, poetry, and music coverage.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No payment offered. All accepted work must be licensed Creative Commons Attribution 3.0—non-negotiable. Original fiction is not accepted at this time. Contributors must register a user account and provide a bio.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

hazlitt.index_line: Prometheus Unbound: libertarian SF/fantasy reviews and commentary, no fiction, unpaid, mandatory CC-BY 3.0 license
hazlitt.name: *Hazlitt
hazlitt.summary: Prometheus Unbound is a libertarian-perspective review site focused on science fiction and fantasy, accepting reviews, articles, news, and commentary (not original fiction) from contributors who share that outlook. No word limit or reading period is stated, there is no pay, and all accepted work must be licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 3.0—non-negotiably. Writers should note the site does not accept original fiction at this time and cannot guarantee any review or publication.

details.aesthetic: Literary and visual art centered on medicine, illness, disability, and healing; accepts fiction, poetry, narrative, memoir, and visual art (color or B&W, 300dpi).
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — submit only once per period; prose limited to one narrative; poetry up to five poems in one submission
details.reading_period: Sep 1 - Mar 31 (visual art not reviewed until after Jul 1)
details.red_flags: No open calls at time of page capture. Work must be unpublished in any format including the internet — blog posts or online publications disqualify a piece. Prose exceeding 2,500 words or multiple narratives will not be reviewed. Clinicians must alter patient identifying details.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed
details.word_limit: Prose: 2,500 words max (one narrative); Poetry: up to 5 poems, no more than 10 pages total

healing muse.index_line: Healing Muse: fiction, poetry, memoir & art on illness, medicine, disability; 2,500-word prose cap; no reprints, even online; no open calls now
healing muse.name: Healing Muse
healing muse.summary: The Healing Muse is an annual journal focused on medicine, illness, disability, and healing, publishing fiction, poetry, memoir, and visual art. Prose is capped at 2,500 words (one piece per submission); poetry up to five poems/10 pages; reading period is September 1–March 31. There are no open calls right now, work must be previously unpublished in any format including online, and submissions are screened for plagiarism.

details.aesthetic: Arthropod-themed short fiction (as indicated by 'Year's Best Arthropod Short Fiction' anthologies and zine history).
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Closed — indefinite hiatus, no longer accepting submissions.
details.red_flags: Submissions are permanently closed with no indication of reopening. Submitting here would be a waste of time.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

hexagon.index_line: Hexagon — arthropod-themed short fiction; CLOSED indefinitely, do not submit, try Duotrope/Chill Subs instead
hexagon.name: Hexagon
hexagon.summary: Hexagon published arthropod-themed short fiction across 20 issues and 10 guest-edited zines. Submissions are permanently closed; the journal is on indefinite hiatus. Do not submit — the page explicitly redirects writers to Duotrope, Chill Subs, or The Submission Grinder instead.

details.aesthetic: Indie literary fiction, nonfiction, essays (especially 'Rejected/Fucked Up Modern Love' style), sports-related fiction and nonfiction, book reviews, and poetry; associated with edgy, cult-literary voices (Garielle Lutz, Elizabeth Ellen). Work has appeared in Best American Short Stories, Best American Essays, O. Henry Prize anthologies.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No response unless accepted. Writers with agents are explicitly told to check with their agent before submitting. SF/LD Book submissions are currently closed.
details.response_time: Only notified if accepted; no timeframe given
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

hobart.index_line: Hobart: indie/cult-lit fiction, essays, sports writing, poetry; Lutz/Ellen sensibility; silence means no; SF/LD Book closed
hobart.name: *Hobart
hobart.summary: Hobart publishes literary fiction, nonfiction (including 'Rejected/Fucked Up Modern Love' essays and sports writing), poetry, and book reviews with a cult, indie sensibility associated with names like Garielle Lutz and Elizabeth Ellen. Submissions are emailed directly to specific editors (found on the About page) or to hobartsubmissions@gmail.com with title and genre in the subject line; no word limit or fee is stated. Writers should note they will only hear back if accepted, and SF/LD Book submissions are currently closed.

details.aesthetic: Ultra-short fiction and poetry curated to fit a postcard, paired with matching visual art — work that is complete and resonant in minimal space. The journal emphasizes beauty and physical object-hood, suggesting a preference for lyrical, image-driven pieces with strong endings.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This page is a subscription/store page, not a guidelines page. Writers should visit hootreview.com directly for submission mechanics. The postcard format implies an extremely tight word limit — likely under 150 words — which would disqualify most standard short fiction.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

hoot.index_line: HOOT: postcard-length flash fiction/poetry with art, under ~150 words; check hootreview.com for submission details
hoot.name: HOOT
hoot.summary: HOOT is a literary journal that publishes flash fiction and poetry on physical postcards — each piece paired with original art and mailed monthly to subscribers. The format is extremely constrained by design (postcard-length work). Submission mechanics are not detailed on this page.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, literary translation, personal essay, creative nonfiction; critical writing including book reviews, arts criticism (film, dance, theater, visual art), public-facing scholarship, and literary essays; also accepts work with visual components (comics, visual poetry, photo essays). Welcomes work in translation and books from smaller/university presses.
details.fee: $3 per submission; waived for subscribers and for the fMRI Writing Prize contest.
details.multiple_submissions: Submit one work at a time (explicitly stated for critical writing; implied for other genres).
details.reading_period: Creative work (poetry, fiction, translation, personal essay, creative nonfiction): September–October only. Critical writing: year-round. Subscribers may submit any genre year-round.
details.red_flags: Creative submissions are only accepted in September–October, making this irrelevant most of the year for fiction/poetry writers; the $3 fee applies per submission and adds up; subscribers get year-round access and fee waivers, creating a two-tier system.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must withdraw promptly if accepted elsewhere; for flash fiction or poems, notify them so they know what remains available.
details.word_limit: unknown

hopkins review.index_line: Hopkins Review: poetry, fiction, essays, translation, criticism; favors under-the-radar work; creative window Sept-Oct only; $3/submission fee
hopkins review.name: Hopkins Review
hopkins review.summary: The Hopkins Review publishes poetry, fiction, literary translation, personal essay, creative nonfiction, and critical writing (reviews, arts criticism, public-facing scholarship) with a clear preference for work that has received less mainstream attention; creative work is accepted only in September–October while critical writing is year-round, both with a $3 fee. Payment is $50 for poetry and $100 for prose; subscribers have fees waived and can submit year-round. Watch out for the narrow creative submission window, the per-submission fee, and the requirement to withdraw or notify promptly on simultaneous acceptance.

details.aesthetic: Literary quality is the sole criterion; publishes fiction, poetry, personal and critical essays, book reviews, and criticism of literature, art, theatre, dance, film, and music. No specific style or theme preferred—encourages reading a current issue to gauge range.
details.multiple_submissions: Up to 7 poems at once; prose limited to one manuscript (excerpt if novel); no explicit limit stated for nonfiction beyond word count
details.reading_period: Poetry: Apr 1–Jun 30; Fiction: Sep 1–Nov 30; Nonfiction: Jan 1–Mar 31 (subscribers may submit year-round)
details.red_flags: Poetry and nonfiction must be submitted by postal mail with SASE—electronic submission accepted for fiction only. Decisions communicated by postal mail only; no email or phone inquiries answered. Manuscripts submitted outside the genre-specific reading windows are returned unread. Previously published work or work forthcoming in book form is not considered. Book reviews are considered on-spec only for first-time reviewers.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Not allowed
details.word_limit: Under 10,000 words for prose; up to 7 poems per submission

hudson review no simultaneous subs.index_line: Hudson Review: elite general-lit fiction/poetry/criticism; postal-only for poetry/nonfiction, strict genre-specific reading windows, no simultaneous subs
hudson review no simultaneous subs.name: Hudson Review (*no simultaneous subs)
hudson review no simultaneous subs.summary: The Hudson Review publishes literary fiction, poetry, essays, and criticism across arts and culture with a sole criterion of literary quality and no genre specialty. Prose must be under 10,000 words; poetry up to 7 poems; reading periods are strictly genre-specific windows (poetry Apr–Jun, fiction Sep–Nov, nonfiction Jan–Mar). Writers should note that simultaneous submissions are not allowed, poetry and nonfiction must be submitted by postal mail (not electronically), and decisions are communicated only by postal mail—no email or phone inquiries answered.

details.aesthetic: Original, unpublished work across short fiction (Howard Frank Mosher Prize), poetry (Ruth Stone Prize), creative nonfiction, and translation (fiction, CNF, or poetry); no song lyrics or copyrighted material embedded in manuscripts.
details.multiple_submissions: Allowed — writer may enter more than one piece per category or across categories, each requiring its own fee
details.red_flags: VCFA current and former faculty, staff, and students are ineligible and will be disqualified if selected; entry fees non-refundable; manuscripts must be fully anonymous or risk disqualification; these appear to be 2022 contest guidelines and may be outdated
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must notify within 24 hours if accepted elsewhere; entry fees are non-refundable
details.word_limit: Prose and translation prose: under 6,000 words; poetry: up to 3 poems per entry

hunger mountain.index_line: Hunger Mountain — contest-only fiction/poetry/CNF/translation, $20/entry, VCFA-affiliated writers ineligible (2022 dates, may be outdated)
hunger mountain.name: Hunger Mountain
hunger mountain.summary: Hunger Mountain runs contest-only submissions (short fiction, poetry, CNF, translation) with cash prizes and publication; all contests open April 1 and close June 15, 2022, with a $20 entry fee per submission. Word limits are under 6,000 words for prose/translation prose, up to three poems per entry. Current and former VCFA faculty, staff, and students are disqualified, and entry fees are non-refundable even if a simultaneous submission is accepted elsewhere.

details.aesthetic: Work by women, femmes, and non-binary writers writing against patriarchal expectations; open to experimental, humorous, and literary styles across fiction (including flash and novel excerpts), nonfiction (essays, narrative nonfiction, articles), and poetry (including prose poetry).
details.multiple_submissions: Poetry requires 3–5 pieces per submission; no multiple-submission policy stated for prose.
details.red_flags: Project is believed defunct as of May 2021; submitting is almost certainly pointless.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed
details.word_limit: Flash fiction up to 1,000 words; short stories and novel excerpts up to 5,000 words; nonfiction up to 5,000 words; poetry 3–5 poems with no line limit stated.

hysterical rag.index_line: Experimental/humorous fiction, nonfiction, poetry by women/femmes/non-binary writers — DEFUNCT as of 2021, do not submit
hysterical rag.name: *Hysterical Rag
hysterical rag.summary: Hysterical Rag published experimental, humorous, and literary fiction, nonfiction, and poetry by women, femmes, and non-binary writers, with pieces up to 5,000 words and poetry in batches of 3–5. Simultaneous submissions were allowed; no reprints. This project is believed defunct as of May 2021, so submitting here would almost certainly be a waste of time.

details.aesthetic: Polished short stories, creative nonfiction (all kinds welcome), and exceptional poetry; standalone novel excerpts accepted but rarely over 25 pages; no chapbooks or novellas.
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per category per reading period unless editor requests more; multiple categories allowed simultaneously
details.reading_period: Sep 8 – Nov 15 (may close early or reopen in winter/spring depending on volume and staffing)
details.red_flags: Reading period may close early without notice; very small poetry quota per issue means poetry is especially competitive.
details.response_time: 6 months or less; inquiries allowed after 9 months
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; withdraw immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: no hard limit but most published stories are under 25 double-spaced pages; poetry: up to five poems per submission.

idaho review.index_line: Idaho Review: polished literary fiction, CNF, and poetry, novel excerpts welcome; poetry slots very limited, reads Sep 8–Nov 15
idaho review.name: Idaho Review
idaho review.summary: The Idaho Review publishes polished short fiction, creative nonfiction, and poetry (including standalone novel excerpts), with a premium on exceptional quality and a small poetry quota per issue. Reading period runs September 8–November 15 with possible early closure or additional winter/spring periods; one submission per category per period, responses within six months. Writers should note the journal may close early due to volume, and mailed submissions are not accepted except for incarcerated writers or those with accessibility needs.

details.aesthetic: Work with a sustained engagement with Judaism, Christianity, or Islam—orthodoxy, unease, grappling, or ambivalence all welcome, but some faith connection is required; publishes poetry, fiction, essays, interviews, translation, and artist profiles.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No email or postal submissions; no previously published work including anything web-published or self-published; faith connection is a hard requirement and must be discernible even if indirect.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but writer must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

image journal.index_line: Image Journal: poetry, fiction, essays on faith—Judaism, Christianity, or Islam, doubt included; no prior publication anywhere, incl. web/self-pub
image journal.name: Image Journal
image journal.summary: Image Journal publishes poetry, fiction, essays, interviews, and translation with a required connection to Judaism, Christianity, or Islam—including doubt or ambivalence, but the faith link must be present.
