Submissions go through Submittable only; response time is up to six months. Previously published work (including web/self-published) is rejected outright, so writers must be careful about prior online posting.

details.aesthetic: Self-described as seeking work that is 'carefully strange' — implying literary fiction, nonfiction, and poetry that takes formal or thematic risks while remaining controlled and deliberate; publishes a mix of genres each issue plus occasional art inserts and folios, suggesting an eclectic, craft-focused sensibility rather than a narrow niche.
details.fee: $3 for general submissions (fee waivers available for hardship; free for incarcerated writers; no fee waivers for prize categories)
details.multiple_submissions: possible to submit multiple pieces in one submission (guidelines reference withdrawing a single piece from a multi-piece submission), otherwise unknown if separate submissions allowed
details.red_flags: Does not accept unsolicited email submissions, artwork, or book reviews; cannot consider work from anyone currently or recently affiliated with Indiana University (past 4 years); submission fees are non-refundable if withdrawn; acceptance rate under 0.5%.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, withdraw via Submittable if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

indiana review.index_line: Indiana Review: fiction/nonfiction/poetry seeking the "carefully strange"; craft-driven, formally risky work; acceptance under 0.5%, $3 fee
indiana review.name: Indiana Review
indiana review.summary: Indiana Review, a biannual literary journal out of Indiana University Bloomington, publishes fiction, nonfiction, and poetry with a taste for the 'carefully strange,' alongside occasional art inserts and special folios. It's highly competitive, accepting under half of one percent of submissions, and pays contributors $5/page (minimum $25) plus two copies.

details.aesthetic: Innovative and entertaining speculative/SF fiction; open to all voices globally; original unpublished work in English (translations from other languages accepted even if previously published).
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — one story at a time
details.red_flags: Any AI/LLM-generated content in a story is grounds for rejection; stories must be submitted as ODT, DOC, DOCX, or RTF in standard manuscript format or they may not be considered.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed
details.word_limit: No hard limit; preferred range 2000–6000 words

interzone.index_line: Interzone: innovative, entertaining SF/speculative fiction, 2000–6000 words; one submission at a time; no AI-generated content
interzone.name: Interzone
interzone.summary: Interzone publishes innovative, entertaining speculative fiction, welcoming diverse voices worldwide, with a sweet spot of 2000–6000 words but no hard limits. Simultaneous submissions are allowed; multiple submissions are not—one story at a time only. Writers must avoid any AI-generated content, as stories containing it will not be considered.

details.aesthetic: Voice-driven work across poetry, fiction, nonfiction, and (returning) criticism/reviews/interviews. The journal prizes literary heterodoxy and individual singularity over trend or convention. Published work in the current issue ranges from experimental collaborative poems and lyric essays to realist fiction, trans identity nonfiction, and a 'fictional draft profile of a famous photographer'—suggesting openness to formal hybridity, marginalized perspectives, and unexpected subject matter. Tone can be playful, strange, and intellectually serious simultaneously.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: upcoming (unspecified dates); reviews, interviews, and criticism will be open during the next reading period
details.red_flags: Guidelines page not reached; only an editor's note and table of contents were available. Specific submission mechanics (word limits, dates, fees, simultaneous-submission policy) must be confirmed before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

iowa review.index_line: Iowa Review: voice-driven poetry/fiction/nonfiction prizing weirdness over trend; hybrid forms, trans identity, psychosexual lyrics; reviews/criticism reopening soon
iowa review.name: Iowa Review
iowa review.summary: The Iowa Review is a prestigious, long-running journal (since 1970) publishing poetry, fiction, and nonfiction with an emphasis on distinctive individual voice over trend-following—its archive spans Language poetry to postmodernism, Stegner Fellows to Pushcarts. The current managing editor explicitly prizes 'weirdness' and heterodoxy, and the Spring 2026 issue reflects that: psychosexually charged lyrics, trans identity, experimental hybrids, and formally inventive prose sit alongside realist fiction and lyric essays. They are resuming publication of reviews, interviews, and criticism and will accept those submissions in an upcoming reading period.

details.aesthetic: Short fiction, poetry, and nonfiction; seeks strong voices, diverse perspectives, and fresh takes on the human experience; themed submission periods mean genre/topic fit is strictly enforced each cycle.
details.fee: $3 per regular submission; competitions have separate entry fees (e.g., $15 for First Book of Prose Prize); free submission days announced via social media.
details.multiple_submissions: One prose manuscript or one set of 3–5 poems per submission; maximum three manuscripts by one author per academic year.
details.reading_period: Rolling gates between mid-August and mid-April each year; specific dates and themes listed on their website.
details.red_flags: Instant rejection (no comment) for: cover letter placed inside the manuscript file; submitting outside an open gate; long manuscripts submitted outside the Trifecta Competition period; submissions exceeding the three-per-academic-year limit; manuscripts not matching the current period's theme or genre.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; writer must notify immediately via Submittable or email (ihlr.mail@gmail.com) if accepted elsewhere.
details.word_limit: Regular prose: up to 5,500 words; poetry: 3–5 poems; Trifecta Competition prose: 25–40 pages; Trifecta poetry: a single poem 10–20 pages.

iron horse.index_line: Iron Horse: fiction/poetry/nonfiction, strong voices & diverse perspectives; themed gates only, 3 subs/year max, $3 fee
iron horse.name: *Iron Horse
iron horse.summary: Iron Horse publishes short fiction, poetry, and nonfiction with themed submission periods, favoring strong voices and diverse perspectives; regular prose is capped at 5,500 words, poets send 3–5 poems, and there is a $3 fee per regular submission. Submissions open on a rolling basis between mid-August and mid-April, with free submission days announced via social media. Writers must watch out for several instant-rejection triggers: cover letters embedded in the manuscript, submissions outside open gates, long manuscripts sent outside the Trifecta Competition period, and exceeding three submissions per academic year.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction, flash fiction, creative nonfiction (first-person narrative, personal essay, memoir), and poetry centered on justice—moral rather than legal, preferably tangential to the theme; character-driven, voice-forward, original. Less interested in straightforward genre fiction.
details.multiple_submissions: Up to 3 poems or one prose piece up to 6000 words per submission implied, but policy on multiple simultaneous pieces not stated
details.red_flags: Submission details page is sparse—no reading period, response time, fee, or simultaneous submission policy listed; writers should email or check linked editorial tastes page before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Up to 3 poems or up to 6000 words for fiction/nonfiction

j journal.index_line: J Journal: literary fiction/CNF/poetry on justice as moral theme, oblique not genre crime; guidelines page sparse—email first
j journal.name: *J Journal
j journal.summary: J Journal publishes literary fiction, flash, creative nonfiction, and poetry that engages justice themes—preferably obliquely, through character and moral questions rather than genre crime writing. Submissions are by email: up to three poems or up to 6000 words of prose. Avoid straightforward genre fiction, and note that nearly all practical submission details (reading period, response time, fees, simultaneous/multiple submission policy) are absent from this page.

details.aesthetic: All forms and styles of writing, traditional to experimental; fiction, essays, and poetry. No previously published material.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — must receive a response on first submission before sending another; max 1 story or essay, or up to 5 poems per submission
details.red_flags: MSU-affiliated individuals (current or within past four years) are ineligible; one-year wait required before resubmitting; no email or paper submissions accepted; $3 fee applies.
details.response_time: 3 months target; follow up after 5 months
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: No stated word limit, but longer work must be 'truly exceptional' given the ~100-page journal.

jabberwock review.index_line: Jabberwock Review: fiction, essays, poetry, traditional to experimental; ~100pp issues, so long work must be exceptional; one submission at a time, $3 fee
jabberwock review.name: *Jabberwock Review
jabberwock review.summary: Jabberwock Review publishes all forms and styles from traditional to experimental, with no word limit but a ~100-page journal meaning long work must be exceptional. Submissions open Aug 15–Oct 1 and Jan 15–Mar 15 via Submittable only, with a $3 fee and a one-year wait before resubmitting. MSU-affiliated people (current or within four years) are ineligible, and only one submission at a time is allowed—no new submission until the first receives a response.

details.aesthetic: Science fiction (primary) and fantasy where speculative elements are central to the plot; seeks hopeful or bittersweet resolutions, character arcs, inclusive/universal themes, settings beyond Earth, and quirky or whimsical tone; horror is a hard sell; no fan fiction.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed; wait for a 4-week cool-down period before resubmitting
details.red_flags: Strict Modern Manuscript format (Shunn) required—non-compliance signals unprofessionalism and will hurt chances; no .rtf if avoidable; no emailed attachments, must use their online form; flash and horror are explicitly hard sells; stories demeaning women or marginalized groups are summarily rejected.
details.response_time: aims for 60 days; do not query until 3 months have elapsed
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed
details.word_limit: up to 7,500 words (novelette considered but harder sell; flash is a hard sell)

james gunns ad astra.index_line: SF/fantasy with hopeful or bittersweet endings, speculative core, inclusive themes; horror/flash hard sells; strict Shunn format required
james gunns ad astra.name: James Gunn’s Ad Astra
james gunns ad astra.summary: Ad Astra publishes science fiction (primarily) and fantasy with hopeful or bittersweet resolutions, inclusive themes, and central speculative elements—stories that trace a path from reality to 'what-if.' Short stories up to 7,500 words; pays $50 honorarium; aims to respond within 60 days but ask no queries until 3 months have passed. No simultaneous or multiple submissions, strict Modern Manuscript format required, and flash/horror are explicitly hard sells.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, and visual art—preference for visual art incorporating text or book arts. Strong editorial commitment to writers from/about marginalized and underrepresented communities; roughly half each issue is a themed special section guest-edited by an established writer from that community.
details.multiple_submissions: one submission per genre per reading period
details.red_flags: Current EKU students ineligible; EKU alumni must wait at least 4 years after study. Work posted publicly online (blogs, public forums) counts as previously published and will be rejected.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must withdraw via Submittable immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

jelly bucket.index_line: Jelly Bucket: fiction/poetry/CNF/visual art, ~50% each issue a guest-edited section spotlighting marginalized communities; EKU students/recent alumni ineligible
jelly bucket.name: Jelly Bucket
jelly bucket.summary: Jelly Bucket publishes fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, and visual art (especially text-integrated or book arts), with a commitment to marginalized/underrepresented communities via a guest-edited special section comprising ~50% of each issue. Reading period runs July 1–December 1; one submission per genre per period is allowed. Current EKU students and alumni within 4 years of study are ineligible, and previously published work (including public blogs) is rejected.

details.aesthetic: All genres (fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction) dealing broadly with Jewish themes and identity; no restrictions on form or function; previously published work accepted if rights are retained and piece is at least one year old.
details.multiple_submissions: one submission per reading period only (1 fiction or CNF story OR up to 5 poems); do not submit again before receiving a response; if published, wait at least 3 months before resubmitting
details.reading_period: 15th of two months before target issue through 14th of the month before (e.g., Nov 15–Dec 14 for January publication); effectively year-round on a rolling monthly basis
details.red_flags: Submitting constitutes consent to promotional email use; all submitted work is subject to editing and publication at editors' discretion without further approval; accepted pieces are also automatically considered for the podcast and a Patreon feature; no AI permitted in any part of a submission; no translations accepted.
details.response_time: unknown (editors state no exact timeframe can be specified)
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed; journal explicitly states it will no longer accept simultaneous submissions
details.word_limit: 5,000 words for fiction and creative nonfiction; up to 5 poems, each no more than 50 lines

jewish fiction.index_line: Jewish Fiction: broad Jewish-themed fiction/poetry/CNF, monthly rolling; no sim-subs, no AI, editing without approval
jewish fiction.name: *Jewish Fiction
jewish fiction.summary: The Jewish Literary Journal publishes fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction broadly defined as 'Jewish in nature,' welcoming all forms and previously published work, with a 5,000-word cap for prose and up to 5 poems (50 lines each) per submission. Submissions are accepted in a rolling monthly window (15th of two months prior through 14th of the month prior to publication), with no fee and no compensation. Key watches: no simultaneous submissions, no AI use, submitting auto-opts you into promotional emails and possible podcast use, and editors may publish with changes at their discretion.

details.aesthetic: Fiction balancing linguistic complexity with emotional simplicity; flash with strong voice, rhythm, and change; CNF grounded in specific experience that transcends the personal (no reportage or current events); poetry with riveting imagery, emotional complexity, and meaning beyond the personal (free verse preferred, experimental welcome if emotionally resonant); hybrid/genre-defying work celebrated in Blended & Beyond.
details.fee: none (paid critiques are a separate, optional paid service)
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed; one submission per author per 3-month period, in one genre category only
details.reading_period: Opens monthly by genre; genres close when monthly cap is reached or on scheduled break
details.red_flags: No AI-generated work accepted and acceptances can be revoked if AI use is discovered; previously published work rejected including personal blogs and social media; submissions must be fully blinded or may be rejected unread; do not resubmit rejected work unless invited; wait 3 months after acceptance or rejection before submitting again
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must withdraw if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction up to 4000 words; CNF up to 5000 words; flash fiction and flash nonfiction up to 1000 words; poetry up to 3 poems, max 2 pages each

jmww.index_line: JMWW: weekly fiction/flash/CNF/poetry/hybrid seeking strong voice, emotional complexity; blind submissions required, no AI work, 3-month wait between subs
jmww.name: JMWW
jmww.summary: JMWW publishes fiction, flash, CNF, poetry, hybrid/blended work, and interviews weekly, favoring strong voice, emotional complexity, and polished craft over first drafts or genre convention. Fiction caps at 4000 words, CNF at 5000, flash and flash nonfiction at 1000, poetry up to 3 poems of max 2 pages each; submissions open monthly by genre with a cap per month. Writers must blind their submissions, wait 3 months between submissions, avoid AI-generated work, and note that previously published work (including personal blogs/social media) is rejected outright.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction (experimental, gothic, feminist/weird girl horror, dark academia, environmental, speculative, intersectional); craft-driven nonfiction (lyric essays, hybrid forms, new journalism, photo essays—no academic writing or straight reportage); fresh, technically controlled poetry (traditional and experimental); dynamic reviews of books published within last 2 years; visual art as cohesive suites with clear point of view. Prioritizes marginalized voices.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed; must wait for a response before submitting again
details.red_flags: No monetary payment to contributors; 8-month minimum response time; recent contributors must wait 1 year after publication before resubmitting; AI-generated work rejected outright and publication contracts terminated if discovered post-acceptance; no previously published work; no US mail submissions
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify at time of submission and withdraw via Submittable if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction and nonfiction: up to 8,000 words (flash: up to three 1,000-word pieces); reviews: up to 1,200 words; interviews: 6–12 pages; poetry: up to 3 poems

journal the.index_line: Journal, The: experimental/gothic/feminist "weird girl" fiction, hybrid nonfiction, poetry; no pay; 8-month response; unpaid
journal the.name: Journal, The
journal the.summary: The Journal publishes literary fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, art, reviews, and interviews with a strong preference for experimental, hybrid, and marginalized voices—weird, feminist, gothic, and formally innovative work. Fiction and nonfiction run up to 8,000 words; poetry is limited to 3 poems; reviews to 1,200 words; submissions must be in double-spaced Garamond and filed via Submittable only. Allow at least 8 months for a response, no multiple submissions are accepted, recent contributors must wait a year before resubmitting, and AI-generated work is an immediate rejection.

details.aesthetic: Novellas and novella-length work that does not fit the traditional publishing landscape; works in translation accepted; two books published per year.
details.fee: $7, with free waiver available by emailing joylandeditions@joylandmagazine.com with subject 'Submittable Fee Waiver'
details.multiple_submissions: one manuscript at a time
details.red_flags: No personal response guaranteed to all submissions; a 500–1,500 word project proposal is required with every submission; outlines are not accepted.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed
details.word_limit: Submissions minimum 10,000 words; anticipated final length 20,000–60,000 words

joyland.index_line: Joyland Editions: novellas (20-60k words) outside traditional publishing; needs full/partial MS plus 500-1,500 word proposal, $7 fee
joyland.name: *Joyland
joyland.summary: Joyland Editions is a nonprofit indie press publishing two novellas per year, seeking work that doesn't fit traditional publishing — completed or partial manuscripts of 20,000–60,000 words (minimum 10,000 words submitted). The $7 fee is required via Submittable, though a fee waiver is available by email. Writers should note they cannot personally respond to all submissions, and a 500–1,500 word project proposal is mandatory.

details.aesthetic: Literary and visual arts journal publishing short fiction, essays, poetry, art, and photography; no stated thematic or stylistic preference beyond originality.
details.multiple_submissions: Up to 4 pieces per person; each piece requires its own entry form
details.reading_period: Submissions due February 19, 2027 (for 2027 issue); no open/close window stated beyond that deadline
details.red_flags: Eligibility is restricted to Spoon River College students, employees, and district residents—outside writers cannot submit. AI or AI-enhanced work is rejected outright.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but writer must notify as soon as possible if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

kaleidoscope.index_line: Kaleidoscope: prose, poetry, art, photography, no set aesthetic—restricted to Spoon River College students/staff/district residents only
kaleidoscope.name: *Kaleidoscope
kaleidoscope.summary: Kaleidoscope is a spring literary and visual arts journal at Spoon River College publishing prose, poetry, art, and photography—eligibility is restricted to SRC students, employees, and district residents. Writers may submit up to four pieces, with a deadline of February 19, 2027, and no word limit stated. AI or AI-enhanced work is explicitly rejected, and only unpublished, original work is accepted.

details.aesthetic: Undergraduate creative writing and art: flash/micro fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry, black-and-white visual art, and cover design. Folio 2026 requires all pieces to fit the theme 'Time'; Kalliope 2027 has no stated theme. Work must be original and entirely human-authored.
details.multiple_submissions: Up to 3 pieces per genre allowed; each piece must be in a separate document.
details.reading_period: Folio 2026: open now, deadline October 25, 2026. Kalliope 2027: opens October 26, 2026, deadline January 24, 2027.
details.red_flags: Eligibility is strictly limited to current Penn State University Park undergraduates during the 2026–27 academic year — no exceptions noted. AI-assisted writing is an automatic disqualification. Shape poems risk rejection if they don't fit the journal's page dimensions. File naming and formatting rules are strict; non-compliance may result in work not being considered.
details.response_time: Folio: decisions by end of November 2026. Kalliope: decisions beginning of March 2027.
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed — previously published work (including elsewhere) is explicitly rejected, implying exclusivity; simultaneous submission policy not directly stated but prior publication anywhere disqualifies work.
details.word_limit: Folio fiction: ≤500 words per piece; Folio nonfiction: 100–500 words; Folio poetry: ≤15 lines, ≤10 words per line. Kalliope fiction and nonfiction: encouraged ≤3,000 words (not a hard cap).

kalliope a journal of womens literature.index_line: Kalliope: Penn State undergrads only; fiction, nonfiction, poetry, B&W art—no AI-assisted work, no prior publication anywhere
kalliope a journal of womens literature.name: Kalliope: A Journal of Women's Literature & Art
kalliope a journal of womens literature.summary: Kalliope and its sister publication Folio are Penn State University Park undergraduate literary journals publishing fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry, and black-and-white art, with Folio themed around 'Time' and strict word/line limits (flash fiction ≤500 words, Folio poetry ≤15 lines; Kalliope encourages ≤3,000 words). Submissions are free, digital-only (.docx for writing, .jpg/.jpeg 300 DPI+ for art), with up to 3 pieces per genre allowed; Folio deadline is October 25, 2026, and Kalliope opens October 26, 2026 with a January 24, 2027 deadline. Writers must be current Penn State University Park undergraduates, no AI-generated content is permitted, and previously published work (anywhere) will not be considered.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, nonfiction, and B&W art/photography from writers and artists with a connection to Mercer County or New Jersey; regional focus is a hard eligibility requirement.
details.multiple_submissions: Only one genre category per submission cycle; one prose piece per author; poets and artists may submit up to five pieces
details.red_flags: Must have a verifiable NJ/Mercer County connection stated in cover letter — no connection, no eligibility. Art must be submitted in both color and B&W versions despite only B&W being published. Strict formatting requirements (Times New Roman 12pt, 65-char line limit for poetry, specific paragraph indentation for prose).
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 4000 words for prose; up to 5 poems for poetry; up to 5 pieces for art/photography

kelsey review.index_line: Kelsey Review: annual NJ/Mercer County regional journal, poetry/fiction/nonfiction/B&W art; requires stated local connection; reads Jan 31–May 31
kelsey review.name: Kelsey Review
kelsey review.summary: Kelsey Review publishes poetry, fiction, nonfiction, and B&W art from writers/artists connected to Mercer County or New Jersey, with prose capped at 4000 words and poetry at five poems. Reading period runs January 31–May 31 annually, with the journal published once a year in the fall. Writers must establish a NJ/Mercer County connection in their cover letter, may only submit to one genre category, and are limited to one prose piece per author.

details.aesthetic: Previously unpublished literary fiction, essays (including flash), poetry (up to 6 poems), excerpts from longer works, and translations across genres. No stated thematic constraints; historically prestigious, broadly literary.
details.multiple_submissions: Allowed across genres, but only one submission per genre; multiple submissions in the same genre will be disregarded
details.red_flags: Submissions window is only one month (Sept 1–30); multiple submissions in the same genre are silently disregarded, not returned; no revisions accepted unless editor requests; submitting adds you to their mailing list
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify immediately via Submittable message if accepted elsewhere; withdrawn work cannot be replaced
details.word_limit: Short fiction/essays up to 7,500 words; flash fiction/essays up to 1,000 words each (up to 3 pieces); poetry up to 6 poems; excerpts up to 30 double-spaced pages

kenyon review the.index_line: Kenyon Review: prestigious generalist for fiction, essays, flash, poetry, translations; reads only Sept 1-30, 2026, one piece per genre
kenyon review the.name: Kenyon Review, The
kenyon review the.summary: The Kenyon Review publishes literary fiction, essays, flash, poetry, and translations of previously unpublished work, with a strong historical prestige and no stated thematic restrictions. Submissions are only accepted September 1–30, 2026 via Submittable, with word limits varying by genre (up to 7,500 words for prose). Writers should note the extremely narrow one-month window, that multiple submissions within the same genre are disregarded entirely, and that revisions cannot be submitted unless requested.

details.aesthetic: Speculative fiction, essays, and art with a speculative element; especially interested in migration themes (immigration, colonialism, diaspora) explored explicitly, metaphorically, or obliquely. Fantasy, sci-fi, horror, and in-between genres all welcome.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Fiction: March 2026, July 2026, November 2026 (themed); Art: year-round; Audio/voice actors: ad hoc; Non-fiction: closed until further notice
details.red_flags: Submissions are intended for immigrant and diaspora creators; non-qualifying writers are explicitly asked not to submit. Reading periods can be cancelled mid-window if slots fill. No poetry accepted under any circumstances.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

khōréō.index_line: Khōréō — speculative fiction/essays/art on migration & diaspora; immigrant/diaspora creators only, no poetry; fiction opens Mar/Jul/Nov 2026
khōréō.name: *Khōréō
khōréō.summary: Khōréō publishes speculative fiction, essays, and art (fantasy, sci-fi, horror, and adjacent) with a strong focus on migration, diaspora, and immigrant experiences; submissions are open only during specific windows in 2026 (March, July, November) and are primarily intended for immigrant and diaspora creators. No poetry is accepted. Writers who do not identify as immigrants or diaspora members are asked not to submit fiction or art.

details.aesthetic: Work by and centered on writers of color from a global community; themes of cultural identity, historical truth, and community impact; literary fiction, poetry, and related forms with an emphasis on artistic rigor and voices that have been historically underrepresented. Contributors span the African diaspora, Latin American, Asian, and Indigenous traditions.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This listing is from a third-party directory (Almond Press), not Kweli's own site — no submission mechanics are provided; writer must consult kwelijournal.org directly before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

kweli.index_line: Kweli: fiction, poetry, nonfiction by writers of color worldwide; cultural identity and kinship, rigorous craft — verify submissions at kwelijournal.org
kweli.name: *Kweli
kweli.summary: Kweli Journal is an online literary magazine with a mission to nurture emerging writers of color — Black, Indigenous, and POC — publishing work that reflects diverse cultural histories and imagines future possibilities; contributors include acclaimed writers such as Victor LaValle, Camille Dungy, and Martin Espada. The journal emphasizes artistic excellence and cultural kinship across many countries and genres. Submission mechanics are not provided in this text, so specifics must be verified on their site.

details.aesthetic: Asia-connected articles, essays, reportage, personal essays, interviews, fiction (up to 3,500 words), poetry, humor, translation, and reviews; seeks lasting value, cultural depth, and intercultural understanding via specifics—not academic writing, tourist-genre first impressions, or superficial pieces.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Contributors are unpaid; submitting grants automatic web cross-posting rights (opt-out must be stated at submission); heavy backlog in fiction, poetry, and book reviews means long waits; no response to unsuccessful submissions in most sections; translations require a proposal email before submitting the work.
details.response_time: Fiction: no response after 6 weeks means rejection; other sections: unknown, editors unable to respond to all unsuccessful submissions
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Asian Encounters: ~800, max ~1,500 words; features: under 3,000 words; interviews/profiles: up to 3,000 words; translations: 2,000–3,000 words; fiction: up to 3,500 words; poetry: unknown

kyoto journal.index_line: Kyoto Journal — Asia-connected nonfiction, fiction, poetry, seeking cultural depth over tourist impressions; unpaid, no fee
kyoto journal.name: Kyoto Journal
kyoto journal.summary: Kyoto Journal publishes Asia-connected nonfiction, fiction, poetry, translation, interviews, and reportage with lasting cultural depth—not academic papers, tourist impressions, or ego-driven work. Word limits vary by section (800–1,500 for personal essays, under 3,000 for features, up to 3,500 for fiction); response time is informal and editors are all-volunteer. Contributors are unpaid, non-responses after ~6 weeks mean rejection for fiction, and submitting grants automatic permission for web cross-posting unless you opt out.

details.aesthetic: Genre science fiction and fantasy (with allowance for light horror), in the pulp-adventure tradition championed by L. Ron Hubbard; no excessive violence or sex on the page; aimed specifically at discovering new, previously unpublished writers rather than showcasing established literary styles.
details.multiple_submissions: 1 story per quarter, up to 4 per year
details.reading_period: year-round, judged in quarterly cycles (deadlines Dec 31, Mar 31, Jun 30, Sep 30)
details.red_flags: Entrants retain publication rights but the story becomes a contest entry rather than a straightforward paid submission; professionals are barred from entering; AI-assisted work is disallowed; this is a literary contest/anthology pipeline, not a traditional magazine or journal submission.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: up to but not exceeding 17,000 words

l ron hubbards writers of the future.index_line: Free contest (not a market) for unpublished SF/fantasy/light horror writers, up to 17k words; pros ineligible, no AI-assisted work
l ron hubbards writers of the future.name: L. Ron Hubbard's Writers of the Future
l ron hubbards writers of the future.summary: Writers of the Future is a quarterly short-story contest for new/amateur science fiction and fantasy writers, judged anonymously by professional genre authors, with cash prizes and an annual grand prize; it is not a paying magazine market so much as a contest feeding into an anthology of winners. Stories must be unpublished original science fiction, fantasy, or light horror, free of excessive violence or sex and free of AI-generated content, and professionals are ineligible to enter.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction driven by character and language over plot; personal or literary essays with a lived-life quality (no literary criticism standalone); poetry with original voice, multi-layered imagery, and sonic awareness. No genre fiction.
details.multiple_submissions: Poetry: up to 4 poems at once; fiction/CNF: query first if over ~15 pages; otherwise unknown if multiple separate pieces allowed simultaneously
details.red_flags: No previously published work considered; summer responses may be significantly delayed; fiction/CNF over ~15 pages requires a query before submitting
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed
details.word_limit: ~15 pages for fiction and CNF before querying required; no per-poem length limit; max 4 poems at once

lake effect.index_line: Lake Effect: character/language-driven lit fiction, lived-in essays, image-rich poetry; no genre fiction, ~15pg soft cap
lake effect.name: Lake Effect
lake effect.summary: Lake Effect publishes literary fiction, personal/creative nonfiction essays, and character/language-driven poetry with original voice and evocative imagery—no genre fiction or literary criticism. Creative nonfiction and fiction have a soft ~15-page limit before a query is required; poetry is capped at 4 poems per submission. No previously published work is accepted, and response times may stretch beyond four months in summer.

details.aesthetic: Covers fiction, poetry, nonfiction, essays, and book reviews; the name 'The Gravel Road' suggests a grounded, possibly rural or working-class sensibility, but no published work or mission statement is available to confirm tone or themes.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Opens at midnight (date unknown); currently open or recently opened
details.red_flags: Extremely sparse information; writer should visit the journal directly to confirm all submission mechanics before sending work.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

landgrant college review.index_line: Land-Grant College Review — fiction/poetry/nonfiction/reviews; name implies rural/working-class bent, unconfirmed; scant info, verify before submitting
landgrant college review.name: Land-Grant College Review
landgrant college review.summary: The Gravel Road publishes fiction, poetry, nonfiction, essays, and book reviews, suggesting a broad literary journal with a rural or vernacular aesthetic implied by its name. Very little detail is available from this text beyond the genre list and an opening announcement. Practical submission details are largely unknown.

details.aesthetic: Accessible literary fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction that can be understood without annotation and speaks to the human condition; book excerpts welcome; nonacademic style for CNF; no experimental/sculptural poetry forms; campfire-oral-tradition sensibility.
details.fee: none (for regular submissions; contests offered separately)
details.multiple_submissions: allowed with limits: up to 3 flash pieces at once (in one document), up to 5 poems at once (in one document); must wait for a response before sending another submission
details.red_flags: Journal is currently on hiatus – submission portal may be closed; no postal submissions accepted; response time unknown so follow-up timing is unclear
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed – the journal assumes all submissions are simultaneous
details.word_limit: Flash: up to 1000 words; fiction: any length (efficiency valued); poetry and CNF: no explicit word limit stated

lascaux review.index_line: Lascaux Review — accessible, unannotated fiction/poetry/CNF that "venerates the language"; no experimental forms; currently on hiatus, check before submitting
lascaux review.name: Lascaux Review
lascaux review.summary: The Lascaux Review publishes accessible (no annotation needed) literary fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction that 'venerates the language'; flash up to 1000 words, up to 3 flash or 5 poems per submission, fiction any length but efficiency valued, no experimental/sculptural poetry. Submissions are year-round with rolling publication, no fee for regular submissions (contests have $1000 prizes), and simultaneous submissions are assumed. The journal is currently on hiatus—writers should check the site for updates before submitting.

details.aesthetic: Poetry (verse, free-verse, prose poem), fiction (traditional and experimental, including flash), creative nonfiction (personal essay, travel writing, micro-essays, flash), reviews, scripts, and genre-blurring hybrid work; especially interested in underrepresented identities and translations.
details.multiple_submissions: Up to 3 flash pieces (under 1000 words) may be submitted together in one file; otherwise unknown for full-length work
details.reading_period: Year-round (with possible slower response in summer)
details.red_flags: International writers pay the same fee but receive no print copy and cannot order physical issues; summer office hours may slow responses
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but writer must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Flash fiction/nonfiction under 1000 words (up to 3 pieces per submission); no upper word limit stated for longer work

laurel review.index_line: Laurel Review: all genres plus hybrid work, underrepresented voices/translations favored; $2/genre fee; intl. writers get PDF only, no print copy
laurel review.name: Laurel Review
laurel review.summary: Laurel Review is a biannual print journal seeking poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, reviews, scripts, and hybrid work, with particular interest in historically underrepresented voices and translations. Submissions are open year-round with a $2 fee per genre category; flash writers can bundle up to three pieces under 1000 words in one file. International contributors should note they receive only a PDF/online publication—no print copy—and cannot order physical issues.

details.aesthetic: Original science fiction and fantasy: near-future soft SF, far-future hard SF, epic fantasy, sword-and-sorcery, urban fantasy, magical realism, science-fantasy, folktales. No subject off-limits; experimental work encouraged. Not a market for erotica, fan fiction, media tie-ins, or poetry.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed; one story per open submission period
details.red_flags: Currently closed with no stated reopening date; do not query about reopening. AI-assisted or AI-written work is rejected. If a story was previously rejected by editor John Joseph Adams, the guidelines imply restrictions on resubmission (sentence cut off in source).
details.simultaneous_submissions: Not allowed
details.word_limit: 1,500–10,000 words (under 5,000 preferred); flash fiction up to 1,500 words also considered

lightspeed.index_line: Lightspeed: SF/fantasy, any subject, under 5,000 words preferred, 8¢/word — currently closed, no simultaneous/multiple subs
lightspeed.name: Lightspeed
lightspeed.summary: Lightspeed publishes original science fiction and fantasy across a wide spectrum—hard SF to folktales, magical realism to epic fantasy—with no subject off-limits and an explicit diversity welcome; stories of 1,500–10,000 words are considered, with under 5,000 preferred, at 8 cents/word. The magazine is currently closed to submissions, accepts one story per open period, and prohibits simultaneous and multiple submissions. No AI-assisted work is accepted, reprints and nonfiction are solicited/assigned only, and writers should not query about reopening dates.

details.aesthetic: Feminist literary writing with a Jewish-women focus: fiction with 'heart, soul and chutzpah'; reporting, analysis, opinion, memoir, poetry. Must have a feminist angle — not just women's interest but gender broadly. Literary, political, and satirical voices all welcome.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Closed until end of calendar year; reopens January (nonfiction and poetry by email, fiction via form)
details.red_flags: Submissions currently closed until January; no previously published work; omitting your name may mean no response; manuscripts sent by mail are not returned
details.response_time: Follow up after 2 weeks if no response; consider no response after 6 weeks a rejection
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must notify Lilith immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: under 3,000 words; features: ~2,000 words; news briefs: under 500 words; back-page pieces: 800 words; blog posts: 500–800 words (longer possible); poetry: no more than 5 poems

lilith.index_line: Lilith: feminist Jewish-women's writing with chutzpah — fiction, memoir, poetry, satire; closed until January
lilith.name: Lilith
lilith.summary: Lilith publishes feminist, Jewish-women-focused literary writing across nonfiction, fiction, poetry, and memoir — lively, political, satirical work with a clear feminist angle. Fiction under 3,000 words; features ~2,000 words; blog posts 500–800 words; no more than 5 poems. Submissions are currently closed until end of calendar year; response time is informal (follow up at 2 weeks, assume rejection at 6 weeks); simultaneous submissions allowed only with immediate notification if accepted elsewhere.

details.aesthetic: Strange, unsettling, sharp-edged, emotionally evocative fiction and poetry; favors weird fiction, magical realism, soft science fiction, and genre-straddling work; poetry should have strong imagery and precise language with fantastical elements encouraged but not required.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed; may submit a new story only after receiving a rejection
details.red_flags: Currently closed to both fiction and poetry with no reopening date; no reprints or non-fiction accepted.
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed
details.word_limit: up to 10,000 words (fiction); any length (poetry)

liminal.index_line: liminal — weird fiction, magical realism, soft sci-fi; unsettling, emotionally sharp; fiction 6¢/word, poetry $50/poem; CLOSED, no simultaneous subs
liminal.name: liminal
liminal.summary: Liminal publishes strange, unsettling, emotionally resonant fiction and poetry across genres, with a soft spot for weird fiction, magical realism, and soft sci-fi. Fiction runs up to 10,000 words at 6¢/word; poetry is 1–3 poems at $50 each, any length. The market is currently CLOSED to both fiction and poetry, and does not accept simultaneous or multiple submissions.

details.aesthetic: Innovative, urgent writing across fiction, nonfiction, poetry, hybrid, translation, and visual art; for translation specifically, seeks global voices responding to life experience independent of trends, spanning all languages and cultures.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed until a response is received on the current submission
details.reading_period: Prose and poetry portals open twice a year (specific dates on site); art and translation year-round
details.red_flags: No monetary compensation; submissions from professional coordinating services rejected outright; previously rejected work will not be reconsidered; translators must independently secure publication rights
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Prose up to 25 pages; poetry up to 5 poems or 10 pages

lit magazine.index_line: LIT Magazine: innovative, trend-resistant fiction/nonfiction/poetry/hybrid/translation/art; no pay; prose/poetry portals open twice yearly
lit magazine.name: *LIT Magazine
lit magazine.summary: LIT (New School MFA) publishes innovative fiction, nonfiction, poetry, hybrid, translation, and art with a broad, urgent, trend-resistant aesthetic. Prose capped at 25 pages, poetry at 5 poems/10 pages; prose/poetry portals open twice yearly, art and translation year-round. No pay, no resubmitting until a response is received, and previously rejected or agency-filed work will not be considered.

details.aesthetic: Work that reads as lived-in and urgent: personal essays about racial tension, immigrant experience, and college-era recklessness; fiction with strong sense of place (Miami, Queens, NYC); poetry that refuses easy titling or categorization. The journal's own tagline — 'No Poem Is the Only Poem. No Story Is the Only Story.' — signals pluralism. Published pieces include creative nonfiction essays on writing process, a review piece referencing Natasha Brown, and titles like 'Church for Sale,' 'Wicked Games,' and 'The Boy and the Vagrant,' suggesting emotionally charged, character-driven work with a literary but not academic tone.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: The About page strongly urges writers to read the Submissions page before submitting; specific mechanics (word limits, fees, response time, simultaneous submission policy) are not stated here and must be checked there.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

litbreak.index_line: Litbreak (NYC, year-round): raw, urban, personal-narrative fiction/CNF/poetry — check Submissions page for mechanics, none stated on-site
litbreak.name: Litbreak
litbreak.summary: Litbreak is a New York City-based online literary journal publishing short fiction, novel excerpts, poetry, and creative nonfiction, with a sensibility that favors raw, compulsive, experiential writing — personal narrative with urban grit, formal experimentation, and emotional directness. The archive goes back to 2015, all posts remain permanently online, and the journal accepts submissions year-round. No submission mechanics (word limits, fees, response times) were visible on these pages, so the writer should consult the dedicated Submissions page before sending.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, personal essays, short plays, and visual art (cover art, literary cartoons, photography, paintings, drawings in B&W or color); styles range from classical to experimental; publishes both established names and first-time authors.
details.fee: $3 via Submittable; none for snail-mail submissions
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Stated as year-round, but currently closed until further notice (Fiction Awards contest was open until Jan 2020)
details.red_flags: Journal has posted a prominent notice that it is NO LONGER TAKING SUBMISSIONS until further notice; the only listed exception (Fiction Awards, open until Jan 2020) appears to have already closed, suggesting the journal may be on indefinite hiatus.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but notify them immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Prose/essays up to 10,000 words; poetry and short plays up to 4,000 words

literal latte.index_line: Literal Latte: classical-to-experimental poetry, fiction, essays, plays, art; CLOSED to submissions until further notice
literal latte.name: *Literal Latte
literal latte.summary: Literal Latte publishes poetry, fiction, essays, short plays, and art ranging from classical to experimental, drawing heavily from unsolicited submissions. Prose up to 10,000 words, poetry/plays up to 4,000 words; Submittable carries a $3 fee while snail mail is free. Critical caveat: the journal has posted a prominent notice that it is NO LONGER TAKING SUBMISSIONS until further notice, making this page largely moot for writers right now.

details.aesthetic: unknown — page directs to separate About webpage
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No payment to contributors. Currently closed. Aesthetic guidance is on a separate page not provided here.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

literary orphans.index_line: Literary Orphans: no stated aesthetic (see About page); unpaid; closed, reopens Fall 2020
literary orphans.name: *Literary Orphans
literary orphans.summary: Literary Orphans provides no aesthetic details on this page, directing visitors to their About webpage instead. Submissions are currently closed (Summer 2020, reopening Fall 2020) and previously published work is not accepted except from personal blogs or workshopping sites. The journal does not pay contributors.

details.aesthetic: Favors courageous, boundary-pushing fiction, bold nonfiction/essays, poetry that 'compels and challenges,' work in translation, and hybrid/in-between-y forms; committed to short form (stories, poems, essays, flash) and only accepts excerpts if they stand alone as self-contained pieces.
details.fee: none, but submitters are required to be subscribers ($25 print or $10 electronic) or submissions will not be considered
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: capped/variable open periods rather than fixed dates; closed indefinitely as of the Covid-19 note in this text, though guidelines describe reopening periodically until submission volume exceeds capacity
details.red_flags: Submissions without an accompanying subscription will not be considered; as of the page's Covid-19 note, the journal was closed with no timeline to reopen, so current status should be verified.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but notify them promptly if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

literary review.index_line: Literary Review: bold, boundary-pushing short fiction/nonfiction/poetry/hybrids; subscription required to submit; status uncertain post-Covid, verify before sending
literary review.name: Literary Review
literary review.summary: The Literary Review (TLR) publishes courageous fiction, bold nonfiction, translated work, and challenging poetry, along with hybrid/in-between forms, favoring short, self-contained pieces over novel excerpts; it comes out twice a year and pays contributors an honorarium. Submissions require the writer to be a subscriber, and as of this text the journal's submissions status is uncertain (was closed indefinitely due to Covid-19 impacts, though separate guidelines describe an open, capped reading period).

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction (short stories to novellas), creative nonfiction (essays on literature, art, culture, music; biography, memoir), and poetry with no restrictions on style or form. Seeks work that 'moves and amazes'—big minds, large hearts, sharp pens.
details.fee: unknown (contest fees not stated on this page; Submittable used)
details.multiple_submissions: One story or essay at a time, up to three poems per submission; must wait for a response before submitting again; each contest counts as its own category
details.reading_period: Regular submissions currently closed indefinitely (as of 3/3/26); three contests are open with results posted August 2026
details.red_flags: All regular submissions are closed indefinitely as of March 2026—only contest submissions are currently accepted; previously published work (including personal blogs) is not considered; no email or postal submissions accepted
details.response_time: Up to 9 months (may be longer for work under serious consideration)
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must withdraw immediately via Submittable if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Print: up to 15,000 words; Online: up to 4,000 words

litmag.index_line: LitMag: fiction/nonfiction/poetry, any style, up to novella length—REGULAR SUBS CLOSED, contests only through Aug 2026
litmag.name: LitMag
litmag.summary: LitMag publishes literary fiction (up to novellas), creative nonfiction, and poetry in any style, seeking work that 'moves and amazes'—big minds, large hearts, sharp pens. Print limit is 15,000 words; online is 4,000; one story/essay at a time, up to three poems; pays on acceptance. Critical watch-out: all regular submissions (fiction, poetry, nonfiction, online) are currently CLOSED indefinitely—only the three named contests are open as of the page date.

details.aesthetic: Chapbooks: poetry in any style (lyric, narrative, formal, prose, hybrid including haibun), 18–36 pages, thematically coherent, with rich imagery, sonics, associative leaps, and clarity. Litmosphere journal: poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and art; specific aesthetic criteria not detailed on this page.
details.fee: Chapbooks: $10 via Submittable (fee waivers available for those who cannot afford it). Litmosphere: unknown.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Chapbooks: April 1–30, 2026 (or until cap reached). Litmosphere: January (Spring issue) and July (Fall issue), closes at 300 submissions.
details.red_flags: Litmosphere caps at 300 submissions and 'usually reach that well before the end of the month' — submit early in January or July. Full Litmosphere guidelines are on a separate site not included here, so the writer must visit that site before submitting. Charlotte Lit reserves the right to publish fewer or no chapbook manuscripts if submissions are not a good fit.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Chapbooks: allowed; must withdraw immediately via Submittable if accepted elsewhere. Litmosphere: unknown.
details.word_limit: Chapbook manuscripts: 18–36 pages of poems. Litmosphere word/page limits: unknown (full guidelines on separate site).

litmosphere journal of charlotte lit.index_line: Litmosphere: poetry/fiction/CNF/art, semi-annual; caps at 300 subs, closes fast—submit early Jan or Jul
litmosphere journal of charlotte lit.name: Litmosphere: Journal of Charlotte Lit
litmosphere journal of charlotte lit.summary: Charlotte Lit Press publishes poetry chapbooks (lyric, narrative, formal, prose, hybrid) valuing thematic cohesion, rich imagery, and sonic precision, plus a separate semi-annual journal (Litmosphere) covering poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction. Chapbook submissions run April 1–30, 2026 only, capped before month-end, with a $10 fee (waivers available); Litmosphere opens in January (Spring) and July (Fall), also capped at 300. Writers should note Litmosphere closes well before month-end and full Litmosphere guidelines live on a separate site not reproduced here.

details.aesthetic: Distinct voice, pressure, and movement; work that stays with the reader. Publishes fiction, essays/non-fiction, flash, poetry, audio-led storytelling (Litro Lab), and visual art/photography.
details.multiple_submissions: One piece per theme; multiple themes may be submitted simultaneously
details.red_flags: General submissions are closed until September 2026; previously published work (print or online) is not accepted; FastTrack editorial feedback service is paid and explicitly does not influence publication decisions
details.response_time: unknown (estimates to be published when submissions reopen)
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with prompt withdrawal if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: ~3,000w, up to 5,000 exceptional; Essays/non-fiction: up to 2,000w; Flash: up to 1,000w; Poetry: up to 3 poems ~40 lines each; Audio: 3–10 minutes

litro magazine.index_line: Litro Magazine: fiction, essays, flash, poetry, audio/visual seeking distinct voice and pressure — CLOSED until September 2026
litro magazine.name: Litro Magazine
litro magazine.summary: Litro seeks distinct voice, pressure, and movement across fiction (≈3,000w, up to 5,000), essays (up to 2,000w), flash (up to 1,000w), poetry (up to 3 poems), and audio/visual work. Simultaneous submissions are allowed with prompt withdrawal; one piece per theme, though multiple themes may be submitted simultaneously. Critical watch-out: general submissions are currently closed and do not reopen until September 2026.

details.aesthetic: unknown
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This page describes no journal; it is a Writer's Digest craft article about submission cover letters. No submission target exists here.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

little fiction.index_line: *Little Fiction — not a journal; a Writer's Digest article on cover letters. No submission target here.
little fiction.name: *Little Fiction
little fiction.summary: This is not a literary journal — it is an article on Writer's Digest offering advice on how to write cover letters for literary journal submissions. No actual journal is described or catalogued here.

details.aesthetic: Favors bold, voice-driven fiction and nonfiction ('fearless essays and killer short stories'); casual, contemporary sensibility based on the informal tone of their own guidelines; also runs a separate annual flash fiction issue.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed - only one submission at a time, except possibly one fiction and one nonfiction piece together
details.reading_period: currently closed (submissions temporarily closed; flash issue also closed, opens once annually)
details.red_flags: Submissions are currently closed with no stated reopening date; response time is vaguely described as requiring 'very patient' waiting.
details.response_time: unknown, described only as requiring patience
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but notify them if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: no strict limit, but typically 2,000-5,000 words for regular submissions

little fiction big truths.index_line: Bold, voice-driven essays and stories, 2-5k words, plus an annual flash issue; currently closed, response times slow
little fiction big truths.name: *Little Fiction, Big Truths
little fiction big truths.summary: A journal publishing 'fearless essays and killer short stories,' generally in the 2,000-5,000 word range though they resist hard limits, plus one annual flash fiction issue; the tone of the guidelines is casual and writer-friendly. Submissions are currently closed, with updates posted via Twitter and Instagram.

details.aesthetic: Annual journal of poetry and prose in the 'little magazine' tradition; international, literary, and high-register; has published Lydia Davis, Joy Williams, Marilyn Hacker, Padgett Powell, Mark Strand, Jamaica Kincaid — editor has NYRB and FSG background.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Closed at time of this page; no reopening date given
details.red_flags: Submissions currently closed with no stated reopening date; response time explicitly acknowledged as potentially 'months or years'; strong editorial aversion to simultaneous submissions makes this a slow, exclusive-only queue with no guaranteed reply window
details.response_time: Months to years by the editor's own admission
details.simultaneous_submissions: Not allowed — editor explicitly states mass or simultaneous submissions are given lowest priority and are considered offensive
details.word_limit: unknown

little star.index_line: Little Star: high-literary poetry/prose (Davis, Joy Williams, Strand) — closed; exclusive submissions only, no simultaneous, reply may take years
little star.name: Little Star
little star.summary: Little Star publishes poetry and prose in the minimalist 'little magazine' tradition, with a literary, international sensibility (Brodsky, Lydia Davis, Joy Williams, Marilyn Hacker). The journal is not currently accepting submissions, and when open it strongly prefers exclusive, targeted submissions over simultaneous or mass submissions. Response times can run months to years, and the editor is openly hostile to work that appears mass-submitted.

details.aesthetic: Poetry: ultra-specific use of language, up to 50 lines. Non-fiction: lyric essays, memoir, personal essays, reportage, criticism, features — no academic essays or reviews, prefers pitches for non-fiction. Fiction: literary short stories with new/emerging voices. Also accepts art, illustration, and photography.
details.fee: Free during submission windows; £3.50 outside windows; Short Story Prize: £12 per entry (£6 subsequent/student/low-income)
details.multiple_submissions: Allowed — multiple pieces must be combined into a single document; poetry allows up to 5 poems per submission
details.reading_period: Jan 1–31, Mar 1–31, May 1–31, Jul 1–31, Sep 1–30, Nov 1–30 (free); outside these windows a fee applies; prize periods close that category
details.red_flags: Work will not be read if submitted in wrong category, submitted as multiple documents instead of one, or if previously published anywhere online or in print. Quota fills up during free windows — submit early in the month. Prize periods close open submissions for that genre category.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Poetry: 50 lines max, up to 5 poems per submission. Non-fiction: no set limit but typically under 4,000 words. Short story (open submissions): not stated for regular window; prize entries: up to 4,000 words.

london magazine.index_line: The London Magazine — precise, unflashy poetry, essays/fiction/reportage; must be wholly unpublished; free windows odd months only, else £3.50
london magazine.name: The London Magazine
london magazine.summary: The London Magazine publishes poetry committed to precise language, essays across lyric/memoir/criticism/reportage, short fiction, and art/illustration, all requiring first-ever publication (no prior online or print appearances). Free submissions are open only during six specific one-month windows per year (odd months); outside those windows a £3.50 fee applies, and category prize periods close that genre to open submissions. Writers must submit in the correct Submittable category or their work won't be read, and multiple pieces must be combined into one document.

details.aesthetic: Lively, vivid literary fiction and flash fiction (1,000–4,000 words and under 1,000 words respectively); compelling, distinctive-voice nonfiction essays/memoir/flash (1,000–4,000 words); poetry in any form (free verse, formal, prose, experimental) that surprises and impresses; translations of poetry or prose with original text and rights permission; book reviews of underseen titles up to 1,200 words.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed unless invited by an editor; flash fiction explicitly requires one story per submission
details.red_flags: Previously published work is not considered; song lyrics cannot be quoted without copyright permission; translations require a signed letter from the rights holder or will be rejected; multiple submissions are prohibited without editor invitation
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, must be noted in the cover letter
details.word_limit: Fiction: 1,000–4,000 words; Flash Fiction: under 1,000 words; Nonfiction: 1,000–4,000 words (flash also welcome); Poetry: 3–5 poems; Translation: up to 5 poems or 5 pages of prose; Book Reviews: up to 1,200 words

los angeles review.index_line: Los Angeles Review: lively, vivid fiction/flash/poetry/essays/translations; $3 fee; no previously published work, no multiple submissions
los angeles review.name: Los Angeles Review
los angeles review.summary: LAR publishes lively, vivid literary fiction, flash fiction, essays, poetry (all forms welcome), translations, and book reviews with a strong emphasis on quality and distinctive voice. General submissions are open year-round via Submittable with a $3 reading fee; award submissions run April 1–July 31, 2026 with a $20 fee. Watch out for the no-previously-published-work rule, the song-lyrics copyright restriction, the one-story-per-submission limit for flash fiction, and the mandatory rights-holder permission letter required for translations.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction and poetry; short/flash fiction and experimental or lyrical hybrid prose under 1,500 words also accepted; K-12 poetry for Cornerstone section; no creative nonfiction; no color or images; quality of writing is primary criterion.
details.multiple_submissions: One submission, in one genre, per issue
details.reading_period: General call (Poetry & Fiction): Sept 14–19, 2026; Cornerstone: Sept 1–Nov 1, 2026
details.red_flags: Submission windows for general calls are extremely narrow (5-6 days); fiction categories capped at 100 submissions each; returning contributors must wait 4 issues after acceptance in a genre before resubmitting in that genre; no unsolicited creative nonfiction accepted; no color printing or images.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must withdraw immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: 1,500+ words (no hard cap, but longer pieces less likely to be chosen); Short Fiction/Hybrid Prose: under 1,500 words; Poetry: up to 5 poems per submission

louisville review.index_line: Literary fiction and poetry, no CNF; free, no fee; brutal 5-6 day windows (Sept 2026); fiction capped at 100 subs
louisville review.name: Louisville Review
louisville review.summary: The Louisville Review publishes literary fiction and poetry (including K-12 Cornerstone poetry), prioritizing quality above all else, with no color/image printing and a cap of 100 submissions per fiction category. Submission windows are narrow and brief—typically 5-6 days for general calls—so writers must watch the schedule carefully. Returning contributors in Poetry or Fiction must wait four issues after acceptance before resubmitting in that genre.

details.aesthetic: Wide-ranging literary journal: fiction, creative nonfiction, flash prose, poetry, visual art, YA literature, and literary translation; multilingual submissions welcomed in all genres; also curates a monthly content series (Amuse-Bouche) across all genres.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — one submission per reading period regardless of genre
details.reading_period: Most genres (Fiction, CNF, Flash, Poetry): August 1–31; Amuse-Bouche: August 1–September 30; Visual Art, Translation, YA: open year-round, reviewed August 1–September 30
details.red_flags: All identifying information must be removed from the document title, submission title, and the work itself — submissions with identifying info in files will not be read. Antioch MFA faculty and staff are ineligible. Antioch alumni must wait at least two years post-graduation. A per-genre submission cap of 300 applies, so windows may close before the listed date.
details.response_time: By end of November (for most genres); rolling basis for Amuse-Bouche
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Up to 3,500 words for all prose genres; up to three poems for poetry genres

lunch ticket.index_line: Lunch Ticket — all genres incl. YA, translation, multilingual work; free, 3,500-word cap; strip all identifying info or it's rejected unread
lunch ticket.name: *Lunch Ticket
lunch ticket.summary: Lunch Ticket publishes fiction, creative nonfiction, flash prose, poetry, visual art, YA literature, and literary translation across all genres, with a strong welcome for multilingual work and two named prizes. Submissions are free, capped at 3,500 words (or three poems), and limited to one submission per reading period; most genres close August 1–31, 2026. Writers must strip all identifying information from files and titles or their work will not be read—and Antioch MFA faculty/staff are categorically ineligible.

details.aesthetic: Triannually-published print lit mag; genre-specific aesthetic criteria are detailed within each individual submission form, not on this general page.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Closed until September (exact reopen date not specified); general open period unknown
details.red_flags: Submissions are currently closed (on vacation until September); no previously published work accepted (print or online); no translations considered; files must be .docx or submission will not be considered; genre-specific guidelines only found inside each submission form, not on this page.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must notify promptly if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

macguffin.index_line: The MacGuffin: genre-specific criteria per submission form; no reprints or translations; closed until September
macguffin.name: The MacGuffin
macguffin.summary: The MacGuffin is a triannual print literary magazine from Schoolcraft College with genre-specific guidelines housed in each submission form; submissions are currently closed until September. No word limits are stated on this page, but no previously published work (print or online) is accepted, no translations, and files must be .docx in Times New Roman 12pt. Writers should note the office is on vacation and submissions are closed, so nothing can be sent until September.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, and visual art (covers, inside sleeves); art must be submitted as a cohesive set capable of framing an entire issue (front/back cover plus possible inside sleeves).
details.multiple_submissions: One per genre per reading cycle for poetry/fiction; unlimited submissions for art, provided each submission's pieces are unique and cohesive
details.reading_period: Fall: Aug 1 – Nov 1; Contest: Nov 1 – Feb 1; Spring: Jan 1 – Mar 15; Zine (The People's Farm x TMR): Feb 17 – Apr 18
details.red_flags: Separate contest window (Nov–Feb) may confuse writers expecting standard fall or spring slots; previously published work not accepted; art not declined may be held for consideration in future issues without an explicit expiration.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with notification required upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

madison review.index_line: Madison Review: poetry, fiction, art (cohesive cover sets); $2/submission; separate Nov-Feb contest window vs. fall/spring reading periods
madison review.name: Madison Review
madison review.summary: The Madison Review publishes poetry, fiction, and art across two annual issues (digital fall, print spring). Standard submissions cost $2 per submission, limited to one per genre per reading cycle; art submissions are unlimited but must be conceptually cohesive enough to frame an entire issue. Writers should note the distinct submission windows and that contest submissions occupy a separate November–February slot.

details.aesthetic: Literary poetry, short fiction, creative nonfiction, and translations; values style as much as substance; CNF must be literary (personal essay, memoir, travel, etc.) not argumentative or review-based; welcomes under-represented voices; not interested in AI-generated work.
details.fee: None for Canadian writers; CAD$7 (approx. USD$5) per submission for international writers
details.multiple_submissions: Once per genre (poetry, fiction, CNF, translations) per calendar year for regular submissions; contest submissions are unlimited (with fees)
details.reading_period: Canadian writers: Jan 1 – Jun 30; International writers: Feb 14 – Feb 28 (or until cap reached)
details.red_flags: International reading window is only ~2 weeks (Feb 14–28) and capped; no previously published work accepted, including excerpts or work revised after publication; unsolicited reviews not accepted; contest pieces must not be simultaneously submitted elsewhere.
details.response_time: 1–6 months for poetry; up to 9 months for fiction and CNF
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed for regular submissions with notification and prompt updates if accepted elsewhere; not allowed for contest submissions
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 8,000 words (Canadian), up to 4,000 words (international), or 1–3 flash pieces up to 750 words each; CNF: up to 5,000 words, or 1–2 pieces up to 1,000 words each; Poetry: 3–5 poems, up to 10 pages.

malahat review.index_line: Malahat Review: literary poetry/fiction/CNF/translation; Canadians read Jan-Jun, international window just Feb 14-28 with fee
malahat review.name: Malahat Review
malahat review.summary: The Malahat Review publishes poetry, short fiction, creative nonfiction, and translations, with a strong welcome for historically under-represented writers; fiction runs up to 8,000 words (Canadians) or 4,000 words (international), CNF up to 5,000 words, and poetry 3–5 poems up to 10 pages. Canadian writers submit January 1–June 30; international writers have a narrow window of February 14–28 with a CAD$7 fee and a submission cap. Writers should note the once-per-genre-per-calendar-year limit, the strict no-previously-published rule (including excerpts and revised work), and that contest submissions cannot be simultaneously submitted elsewhere.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction, poetry, creative non-fiction/essays, and visual art; currently themed around 'Displacement' — including diaspora, climate migration, home and identity, sociopolitical displacement, and gender/body displacement. Draws on international and experimental voices.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — one submission per issue maximum
details.reading_period: 1–28 February (current special issue window); generally two submission periods per year aligned with Summer and Winter issues
details.red_flags: Word documents only — no PDFs or other formats accepted. Response time is explicitly unpredictable. Postal submissions accepted but online strongly encouraged.
details.response_time: Allow 3 months before following up; no firm deadline stated
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, no conditions stated
details.word_limit: Up to 6,000 words for prose (stated as a rarity to exceed); up to 3 poems for poetry

manchester review.index_line: Manchester Review: fiction/poetry/essays on 'Displacement' (diaspora, migration, identity); Feb 1-28 window, Word docs only, one sub/issue
manchester review.name: Manchester Review
manchester review.summary: The Manchester Review publishes literary fiction, poetry, essays, and art, currently seeking work on the theme of 'Displacement' for a special issue; prose is capped at 6,000 words and poets may send up to 3 poems, with submissions open 1–28 February. One submission per issue is the rule, simultaneous submissions are allowed, and only Word documents are accepted. Writers should note the vague response-time warning ('may not always respond in a timely manner') and are advised to follow up if no reply within three months.

details.aesthetic: Creative nonfiction/personal essay, poetry, short fiction, and visual art (photography, drawing, painting, short comics, mixed media, printmaking) from teen writers and artists aged 13-19; encourages voices from all backgrounds.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Next deadline April 30, 2026 (Summer 2026 issue); publishes two editions per year
details.red_flags: Strictly limited to writers/artists aged 13-19 — adults cannot submit. AI-generated work and fan art are explicitly rejected. Accepted contributors must sign a release form granting publication and social media/marketing rights.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: up to 1,200 words

margins.index_line: Margins: teen writers/artists 13-19 only, all genres under 1,200 words, free, no AI-generated work, deadline April 30 2026
margins.name: Margins
margins.summary: Margins is a student literary magazine (ages 13-19) publishing poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and visual art across multiple mediums. Writing submissions must be 1,200 words or less; next deadline is April 30, 2026 for the Summer 2026 issue. Writers should note the strict age restriction (13-19 only) and that AI-generated work is explicitly rejected.

details.aesthetic: Broad, socially and politically engaged literary quarterly balancing established and emerging writers; fiction spans flash, experimental, historical, and realist modes but favors outward-facing over self-focused narratives; nonfiction includes essays on literature, art, science, philosophy, and public affairs; poetry and hybrid/cross-genre work welcomed; public affairs section seeks internationalist, freedom-oriented, culturally-political writing; one visual artist featured per issue (mostly solicited); no illustration of prose.
details.fee: none for regular submissions; unsolicited blog submissions carry a $50 honorarium (payment to author, not a fee)
details.multiple_submissions: No mixed submissions - essays, fiction, hybrid, poetry, and translation manuscripts must be submitted separately; one piece (or one poetry set of up to 6 poems) per submission per genre
details.reading_period: Oct 1 - Apr 30 (closed May 1 - Sept 30); BIPOC authors and translations accepted year-round via mail/email outside this window
details.red_flags: Online submission manager shuts down outside reading period (Oct-Apr); art submissions mostly solicited so unsolicited chances are limited; book reviews published online only, not in print.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Fiction/nonfiction/hybrid/translation: 7500 words or 20-30 pages depending on genre; poetry: generally under 100 lines; blog pieces: 1000 words max; Working Titles e-book series: 7,000–25,000 words

massachusetts review.index_line: Massachusetts Review: outward-looking fiction/nonfiction/poetry engaging politics and world affairs; BIPOC/translation submissions open year-round, otherwise Oct-Apr only
massachusetts review.name: Massachusetts Review
massachusetts review.summary: The Massachusetts Review is a long-running (since 1959), politically and socially engaged literary quarterly publishing fiction, nonfiction, poetry, hybrid work, translation, performance, and visual art, favoring work that looks outward at 'the world' over the purely personal, with a stated commitment to under-represented and internationalist voices. It also runs a public affairs section and blog, plus a digital e-book series (Working Titles) for longer prose. Reading period is closed May 1–Sept 30, with a BIPOC and translations exception allowing year-round submission via email/mail.
