details.aesthetic: Fiction or narrative nonfiction with an unmistakable individual voice; judge Weike Wang prizes clean sentences, surprising storytelling, humor, and substance—'write to your smartest friend.'
details.fee: $20 per submission; free for writers from historically marginalized/underrepresented groups (cap of 50 already met per page)
details.multiple_submissions: allowed; each submission requires a separate $20 entry fee
details.red_flags: Previously published work—including personal blogs and social media—is automatically disqualified. AI-generated or AI-assisted work (including LLM-assisted translation) is automatically disqualified. Writers with a major-press novel or memoir published or under contract are ineligible. The free-submission cap for underrepresented writers has already been met.
details.response_time: by end of December 2026; winners announced by end of January 2027
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; must withdraw via Submittable or contact the journal if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: under 6,000 words

masters review new voices.index_line: Masters Review Summer Award: voice-driven fiction/nonfiction to 6,000 words; $20 fee; no prior pub, no AI, no major-press contract
masters review new voices.name: *Masters Review: New Voices
masters review new voices.summary: The Masters Review's Summer Short Story Award seeks fiction or narrative nonfiction with a distinctive voice, clean sentences, and surprising storytelling, judged this cycle by Weike Wang. The contest runs July 1–August 30, 2026, with a $20 entry fee, a 6,000-word cap, and responses by end of December 2026. Writers should note that AI-assisted work, previously published work (including blogs/social media), and submissions from writers with major-press book contracts are automatically disqualified.

details.aesthetic: Mostly fiction, some nonfiction; no explicit rules on voice or theme—reading back issues is the only guidance given. Poetry is rarely published in the Quarterly. No previously published work considered. No AI-assisted writing accepted.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Postal submissions only (849 Valencia St., San Francisco CA 94110); no manuscripts returned; response requires a self-addressed stamped postcard or writer gets no reply; website submissions follow completely separate guidelines at a different link; AI-assistance of any kind results in rejection and requires a future attestation at publication.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

mcsweeneys.index_line: McSweeney's: eclectic fiction, taste defined by back issues; postal-only, no AI, SASP required for reply, slow response
mcsweeneys.name: McSweeney’s
mcsweeneys.summary: McSweeney's Quarterly publishes mostly fiction and some nonfiction with no stated stylistic rules, strongly recommending reading past issues to understand taste; submissions are postal only with no length limit and an AI-prohibition policy requiring a signed attestation. Writers should note there is no email option for Quarterly submissions, no manuscript return, and response requires including a self-addressed stamped postcard.

details.aesthetic: Meanjin was a long-running Australian literary journal founded in 1940, known as a mainstay of Australia's cultural landscape. No further aesthetic detail is available from this text.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Meanjin closed in September 2025 and is no longer operating; submitting to it would be impossible.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

meanjin.index_line: Meanjin: 85-year Australian literary institution — CLOSED September 2025, not accepting submissions
meanjin.name: Meanjin
meanjin.summary: This page is a news article from Crikey (an Australian political/media news outlet) reporting that Meanjin, Australia's second-oldest literary journal, closed in September 2025 after Melbourne University Publishing withdrew financial support. Meanjin was an 85-year-old Australian literary institution; it is no longer accepting submissions as it has shuttered.

details.aesthetic: unknown
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This page contains no journal to evaluate — it is a Writer's Digest craft/advice article, not a journal's submission guidelines or about page.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

memorious.index_line: Memorious: NOT A JOURNAL — Writer's Digest article on cover letters for lit-mag submissions; no journal to evaluate
memorious.name: *Memorious
memorious.summary: This is not a literary journal — it is a Writer's Digest instructional article about how to write cover letters for literary journal submissions. No specific journal is described or catalogued here.

details.aesthetic: Motherhood-focused literary journal publishing a broad range across genres: poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, essays, craft, interviews, book reviews, and hybrid/experimental forms. Themed folios suggest attention to curated, conceptual issues. The 'Mom Egg' identity signals work about caregiving, family, gender, and the female experience broadly construed.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No submission guidelines visible on this page; writer must locate the Submit section of the site before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

mer vox online quarterly mom egg review.index_line: MER VOX Online Quarterly: motherhood-centered poetry, fiction, essays, hybrid work; themed folios; check site for submission guidelines
mer vox online quarterly mom egg review.name: *MER VOX Online Quarterly (Mom Egg Review online)
mer vox online quarterly mom egg review.summary: Mom Egg Review (MER) is a literary journal centered on motherhood and related experiences, publishing poetry, fiction, creative prose, essays, craft pieces, interviews, book reviews, and hybrid work across a print annual and an online quarterly. The work skews toward literary voices exploring family, identity, and womanhood, with themed folios (e.g., 'Summer / Girl'). No submission mechanics are visible on this page.

details.aesthetic: A literary journal blending established, award-winning authors (Pulitzer, National Book Award winners) with debut and early-career writers; publishes fiction, poetry, nonfiction, author interviews, and book reviews; edited by MFA students, giving it a contemporary, craft-focused, workshop-adjacent sensibility.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No open submission calls at the time of this text, so timing must be checked before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

meridian.index_line: Meridian (UVA): fiction, poetry, nonfiction, interviews, reviews mixing big names with debut writers; MFA-run, craft-focused; currently closed
meridian.name: Meridian
meridian.summary: Meridian is an annual literary magazine run by MFA students at the University of Virginia, publishing fiction, poetry, nonfiction, interviews, and book reviews alongside notable established writers like Seamus Heaney and Rita Dove, while prioritizing early-career and debut authors. Work from the magazine has appeared in Best American anthologies, the Pushcart Prize anthology, and New Stories from the South, and its stories have been O. Henry Prize short-listed. Submissions are currently closed with no open calls listed.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, poetry, translations, and nonfiction including personal essays, essays on writing, and short reviews; no specific voice or theme restrictions stated.
details.fee: None for regular submissions; contests require an entry fee (amount unspecified).
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Year-round (but currently closed at time of page capture).
details.red_flags: Currently not open for submissions. No AI-generated content accepted (whole or in part). Previously published work (print or online) is ineligible. Postal submissions without an SASE receive no response.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, with immediate notification required upon acceptance elsewhere.
details.word_limit: unknown

midamerican review.index_line: Mid-American Review: fiction, poetry, translations, nonfiction, no stated aesthetic bent—but currently closed and bans AI-assisted work outright
midamerican review.name: Mid-American Review
midamerican review.summary: Mid-American Review publishes fiction, poetry, translations, and nonfiction (personal essays, essays on writing, short reviews) with no stated stylistic restrictions beyond a strict ban on AI-generated content and previously published work. Submissions are free year-round via online manager or postal mail (SASE required); contests carry an entry fee. The journal is currently closed to submissions, and any AI-assisted work—even partially—will be rejected.

details.aesthetic: Regionally rooted literary journal centered on Midwest identity and place, open to poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and visual art/photography; actively seeks new and underrepresented voices rather than an established house style.
details.fee: fee-based via Submittable, but waived on request for financial need; free for incarcerated writers submitting by mail
details.multiple_submissions: unknown (poetry allows 1-5 poems per submission; not stated for prose)
details.red_flags: Only pays in one free contributor copy; online publication delayed six months after print release; must wait a year to resubmit if previously published in the journal.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with request to notify if work is accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: up to 6,000 words for prose; poetry 1-5 poems or 10 pages

midwest review.index_line: Midwest Review: poetry, fiction, CNF & art rooted in Midwest place/identity, favors new & underrepresented voices; pays one copy only
midwest review.name: Midwest Review
midwest review.summary: Midwest Review is an annual print-and-online journal, edited by University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point English faculty and a regional editorial team, publishing poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and visual art by writers and artists with ties to the Midwest (broadly defined, with room for crossing borders). It emphasizes new voices and underrepresented perspectives, nominates contributors for major prizes (Pushcart, Best of Small Fictions, PEN/Dau), and pays only in a contributor copy.

details.aesthetic: Creative and critical writing; all types of poetry considered; short fiction and flash fiction. No specific thematic or stylistic preference stated.
details.multiple_submissions: Limited: one story or up to four flash pieces per period for fiction; 3–5 poems per period for poetry. New submissions blocked for three months after your last submission, regardless of decision status.
details.reading_period: Aug 15 – Oct 15 and Jan 15 – Mar 15 each year (submissions may be uploaded at any time but are only read during these windows)
details.red_flags: The three-month cooldown between submissions applies even if the prior work is still under review — this significantly limits how often a writer can submit. Scholarly critical writing is not handled through this portal; must be emailed separately.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 4,000 words (one story) or up to four flash pieces of 1,000 words each. Poetry: 3–5 poems per reading period.

minnesota review.index_line: Minnesota Review: open-aesthetic poetry and fiction/flash; 3-month wait required between submissions, even if still pending
minnesota review.name: Minnesota Review
minnesota review.summary: The Minnesota Review publishes poetry and short fiction (plus scholarly critical writing submitted separately by email), favoring no single stated aesthetic but welcoming all poetry forms. Fiction is capped at 4,000 words or four flash pieces (1,000 words each) per reading period; poetry at 3–5 poems. Writers must wait three months after any submission before submitting new work, even if the previous submission is still under review.

details.aesthetic: Prize-contest issue publishing poetry (3–5 poems), short fiction (600–8,000 words), and creative nonfiction/essays (600–8,000 words); English-language, human-generated work only.
details.multiple_submissions: Allowed; each additional entry requires a separate $16 fee
details.red_flags: Current or former USM employees/students ineligible; anyone with past or present affiliation with a staff member ineligible; no AI-generated work; no translations or work primarily in a language other than English; no previously published work; blind review so identifying info must be removed
details.response_time: Winners and finalists usually announced in March
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction and nonfiction: 600–8,000 words; Poetry: 3–5 poems totaling 10 pages or less

mississippi review.index_line: Mississippi Review: annual $16 contest for poetry/fiction/nonfiction, Aug 1–Jan 1; no AI or previously published work
mississippi review.name: Mississippi Review
mississippi review.summary: Mississippi Review runs annual prize contests in poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction, publishing winners and finalists in a dedicated summer contest issue. Each category has a $16 entry fee per submission, with fiction and nonfiction capped at 8,000 words and poetry at 3–5 poems/10 pages; the reading window is August 1–January 1. Watch out for broad ineligibility rules: no AI-assisted work, no translations or non-English-primary work, no previously published pieces, and anyone affiliated (past or present) with USM or a staff member is barred.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, and nonfiction of general interest; no literary criticism. Poetry published in features of 6–14 pages per poet (3 poets per issue). Fiction and essays: no stated thematic restrictions, but writers are encouraged to read previous issues. Also considers omnibus book reviews (3–6 books, 3,000–5,500 words) and interviews.
details.fee: none (contests have separate entry process; no fee mentioned for regular submissions)
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: AI usage in any portion of a submission must be disclosed in specific detail within the piece and in the cover letter; physical submissions without a SASE are recycled without response; do not mix genres in the same physical submission; no previously published material considered
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with notification required if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: No length restrictions stated for fiction or essays; poetry submissions should be 8–20 pages (no complete manuscripts); omnibus reviews 3,000–5,500 words

missouri review.index_line: Missouri Review: general-interest fiction, nonfiction, and poetry (6–14pg features); $25/page; strict AI-disclosure requirement
missouri review.name: Missouri Review
missouri review.summary: The Missouri Review publishes poetry (features of 6–14 pages per poet), fiction, and nonfiction of general interest—no literary criticism—seeking the best new voices across all three genres. Submissions are open year-round with no stated word limit for fiction/essays, response time is 10–12 weeks, and pay is $25 per printed page. Writers must disclose any AI usage in detail both within the piece and in the cover letter, and physical submissions without a SASE are recycled without response.

details.aesthetic: Experimental, critical, and contemporary Arab and SWANA writing and art; work that questions and expands forms and conceptual frameworks; supports diasporic, decolonial, and intersectional perspectives including Palestinian, Black, LGBTQIA+, disabled, and Indigenous liberation themes.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Submissions currently closed; check newsletter for next call
details.red_flags: Submissions are closed with no announced reopening date; no submission details (word limit, fees, response time, simultaneous submission policy) are available on the page — writers should subscribe to the newsletter and check back rather than preparing a submission now.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

mizna.index_line: Mizna: experimental, critical Arab/SWANA lit and art, decolonial and diasporic focus — closed; watch newsletter for next call
mizna.name: Mizna
mizna.summary: Mizna is a Whiting Award-winning biannual literary and art journal publishing experimental, critical Arab and SWANA (Southwest Asian and North African) voices in literature, art, and multidisciplinary forms. Submissions are currently closed with no stated word limit, fee, or response time. Writers should monitor the newsletter for the next open call, as no reading period dates are provided.

details.aesthetic: Motherhood-focused literary journal publishing poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, essays, craft writing, and hybrid forms. Work gravitates toward personal, emotional, and domestic experience as seen in titles like 'Everything Is Water,' 'The Presence of One Word,' and 'Singing from the Deep End.' Features art, interviews, and a 'Hybrids' special section, suggesting openness to experimental and cross-genre work.
details.fee: none (explicitly noted as 'no-fee' in the referenced blog post)
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: May 1 – July 15 (based on 'MER Submissions Open 5/1 – 7/15' notice)
details.red_flags: Reading window is narrow (roughly 10 weeks); the only deadline info comes from a sidebar notice, so writer should verify current-year dates on the submissions page before sending.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

mom egg review.index_line: Mom Egg Review — poetry, prose, hybrids on motherhood and domestic/emotional life; no fee; opens 5/1–7/15
mom egg review.name: Mom Egg Review
mom egg review.summary: Mom Egg Review (MER) is a literary journal centered on motherhood, publishing poetry, fiction, creative prose, essays, craft pieces, interviews, and book reviews with a strong focus on women's voices and experience. Recent online work includes poetry and essays with intimate, lyrical titles suggesting emotional and domestic themes. No submission fee; reading period appears to be May 1–July 15 based on a notice in the text.

details.aesthetic: Broad literary scope: fiction, flash fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, literary graphic narrative (fiction/nonfiction/poetry, B&W only), and translations of contemporary authors (permission required). No stated thematic or stylistic restrictions.
details.multiple_submissions: Genre-dependent: 1 story or 3 shorts (fiction/CNF); up to 3 flash pieces; up to 6 poems; up to 8 pages (graphic narrative)
details.red_flags: USPS submissions are neither read nor responded to; translators must provide proof of permission and the original text or risk rejection; summer response times are notably slower
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with prompt notification via Submittable upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction/CNF: up to 8,000 words (1 piece) or 3 shorts; flash: up to 1,000 words each (up to 3 pieces); poetry: up to 6 poems; graphic narrative: up to 8 pages

moon city.index_line: Moon City: fiction, flash, poetry, CNF, B&W graphic narrative, and permission-cleared translations; year-round, no fee, USPS ignored
moon city.name: Moon City
moon city.summary: Moon City Review publishes fiction, flash fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, graphic narrative (literary, black-and-white, up to 8 pages), and translations across a wide range of voices and forms. Submissions are year-round via Submittable only; fiction and CNF cap at 8,000 words, flash at 1,000 words per piece (up to 3), poetry at 6 poems, with genre-specific per-submission limits. Simultaneous submissions are allowed with prompt Submittable notification; USPS submissions are ignored entirely, and response times slow in summer.

details.aesthetic: Five distinct journals are described: A Cappella Zoo publishes magic realism fiction, poetry, drama, and art with altered realities and experimental sensibility (<3% acceptance). Sugar House Review is a print poetry journal out of Salt Lake City. The Moth is an Irish print journal publishing unusual, thought-provoking short fiction and poetry (<1% acceptance). The Baltimore Review publishes essays, narrative nonfiction, short stories, flash fiction, and poetry across electronic and print issues. The Found Poetry Review publishes only found/erasure poetry and text-incorporating forms (~20% acceptance).
details.multiple_submissions: Sugar House Review: packets of up to 5 poems. Others: unknown.
details.reading_period: As of February 2014: A Cappella Zoo closes February 28; others were reopening that month. Current periods unknown.
details.red_flags: This is a 2014 article — all details are likely outdated. A Cappella Zoo appears to no longer be active. Verify all policies directly with each journal before submitting.
details.response_time: A Cappella Zoo: ~6 weeks; Sugar House Review: ~6 months; The Moth: ~4 months; Baltimore Review: ~3 months; Found Poetry Review: unknown
details.simultaneous_submissions: Sugar House Review: allowed. Others: unknown.
details.word_limit: unknown

moth.index_line: Moth: Irish print journal, unusual/thought-provoking short fiction and poetry; <1% acceptance—brutally selective; ~4mo response
moth.name: Moth
moth.summary: This page is a 2014 roundup article from Authors Publish Magazine listing five literary journals reopening that February—not a single journal's own guidelines page. It covers A Cappella Zoo (magic realism), Sugar House Review (poetry only), The Moth (Ireland-based fiction/poetry), The Baltimore Review (multi-genre), and The Found Poetry Review (found/erasure poetry only). No unified submission guidelines apply; each journal has its own policies.

details.aesthetic: unknown
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: most of the year (exact dates unknown)
details.red_flags: Extremely sparse guidelines — no aesthetic focus, genre preferences, length limits, or response time given; writer would need to research the journal independently before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

mount hope.index_line: Mount Hope: no stated aesthetic, genre, or length limits — research before submitting; reads most of the year via Submittable
mount hope.name: Mount Hope
mount hope.summary: Mount Hope accepts electronic submissions via Submittable but provides almost no detail about aesthetic focus, word limits, or response times. The only practical information given is that submissions are accepted 'most of the year' and manuscripts must include the writer's name and email address.

details.aesthetic: Work that showcases, examines, or repurposes historical American culture across fiction, nonfiction, poetry, humor, art, and music; encourages weird, contradictory, or forgotten aspects of Americana; welcomes formally inventive work (e.g., poetry mixing Federalist Papers language with WWII propaganda); no misogyny, racism, ableism, homophobia, transphobia, classism, xenophobia, or bigotry.
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per genre per reading period only
details.reading_period: April, August, and December only (reviews, interviews, and American Songbook music accepted year-round)
details.red_flags: Submissions sent outside April, August, and December are deleted unread; no attachments accepted (prose must be pasted into email body); no payment for publication; previously published writers must wait for two new issues before resubmitting; art submissions must go through a web form, not email.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 3,000 words for prose; up to 1,500 words for humor; 3–5 poems or flash pieces per submission

museum of americana the.index_line: Museum of Americana: fiction/poetry/nonfiction/art reworking historical American culture; no bigotry; reads only Apr/Aug/Dec, unread submissions deleted
museum of americana the.name: *Museum of Americana, The
museum of americana the.summary: The Museum of Americana seeks fiction, poetry, nonfiction, humor, art, and music that examines or repurposes historical American culture, with a strong commitment to diversity and an explicit ban on bigotry of any kind. Prose is capped at 3,000 words and submissions are only read in April, August, and December (anything sent outside those months is deleted unread). Writers must use separate email addresses per genre, paste work into the email body (no attachments), and wait for two new issues to pass before resubmitting after publication.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, essays, criticism, translation, and poetry; strong emphasis on work by and about living authors; tone and style best inferred from reading the magazine itself.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Response is not guaranteed; art, illustration, and interview submissions are not accepted; no stated response timeline means writers may wait indefinitely with no confirmation.
details.response_time: unknown — they state they cannot always reply
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

n1.index_line: n+1: intellectually engaged fiction, essays, criticism, poetry, translation, focused on living authors; no fee; replies not guaranteed
n1.name: n+1
n1.summary: n+1 publishes fiction, essays, criticism, translation, and poetry with an emphasis on living authors, across a print magazine (3x/year) and an online section. No word limits, fees, or response time guarantees are stated. Writers should note that replies are not guaranteed, and art, illustration, and interview submissions are explicitly rejected.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, poetry, and nonfiction across all forms: short shorts, novels, novellas, personal essays, humor, memoirs, literary biographies, reportage, interviews, cartoons/graphic stories, photography. Emphasis on quality and originality of language; audience values storytelling and imaginative prose.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Machine-generated text explicitly not accepted. Full formatting, word-length, and payment policies are on a separate Submission Guidelines page not included here — writer should consult that page before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: All lengths accepted, from short short stories to complete book-length works

narrative magazine.index_line: Narrative Magazine: all lengths from flash to book-length serializations, all genres; quality storytelling and imaginative prose; no AI-generated work
narrative magazine.name: *Narrative Magazine
narrative magazine.summary: Narrative publishes fiction, poetry, and nonfiction of all lengths with a focus on quality storytelling and imaginative prose, including everything from flash to book-length serializations. They run named contests alongside general submissions and Story/Poem of the Week slots. Writers must note that machine-generated text is explicitly rejected.

details.aesthetic: Favors work that pushes against boundaries of genre, body, and expectation: fiction with tension and truth across lengths (micro to longer short stories), nonfiction essays unpacking the historical, political, and personal, poetry that surprises, plus translations, hybrid work, comics/graphic narrative excerpts, and striking visual art.
details.multiple_submissions: only one submission per genre per reading period
details.reading_period: Fiction, Poetry, Nonfiction, Translation read September/October and January/February; Art and Comics read year-round
details.red_flags: Caps submissions at 500 per section (sometimes fewer) and closes early if cap is reached before month ends; not currently accepting unsolicited reviews or interviews; no single-frame cartoons for comics; current/former Vanderbilt students and employees (within 5 years) are ineligible; email submissions not read (must use Submittable).
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with request to notify via Submittable if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction up to 7,000 words (flash up to 1,000, micro under 500); nonfiction up to 8,000 words; translation prose up to 8,000 words or up to 2 poems; poetry 1-3 poems/10 pages total

nashville review.index_line: Nashville Review: genre-bending fiction, essays, poetry, translation, comics; pays; Vanderbilt affiliates ineligible
nashville review.name: *Nashville Review
nashville review.summary: Nashville Review is Vanderbilt University's online literary journal, publishing boundary-pushing fiction, nonfiction, poetry, translation, comics, and visual art with an eye for tension, formal play, and genre-crossing hybrid work. It reads twice yearly for most genres (art/comics year-round), pays contributors, and caps submissions per section to keep response times reasonable.

details.aesthetic: Unpublished fiction up to ~3,000 words with personal, idiosyncratic voice; 'more poetry than cinema, more idiosyncrasy than generalization, more examination than explanation — writing that could only be made by a person.' New translations of fiction also welcome.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed; must wait a couple of months after receiving a response before resubmitting
details.red_flags: No reprints accepted. Translators must hold appropriate translation and publication rights and state so in cover letter. No fee or response time listed, so budget expectations accordingly.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; notify them if accepted elsewhere (implied standard practice)
details.word_limit: up to ~3,000 words

necessary fiction.index_line: Necessary Fiction: idiosyncratic, voice-driven short fiction & translations to ~3,000 words — "more poetry than cinema"; one submission at a time
necessary fiction.name: Necessary Fiction
necessary fiction.summary: Necessary Fiction seeks unpublished short fiction (and new translations) up to ~3,000 words with a distinctly personal, idiosyncratic voice — 'more poetry than cinema, more examination than explanation.' Simultaneous submissions are allowed but multiple submissions are not, and writers should wait a couple of months after a response before resubmitting. No reading period, fee, or response time is stated on the page.

details.aesthetic: Science fiction and fantasy magazine, open to both professional and amateur writers, favoring genre stories and SF/fantasy-themed poems; explicitly avoids horror and prefers not to impose rigid rules on form or content; also publishes original interior and cover art, mostly realistic in style.
details.multiple_submissions: each submission (including poems) must be sent separately, but multiple separate submissions appear allowed
details.reading_period: currently closed; next submission period not yet set
details.red_flags: Currently closed to submissions with no set reopening date; mailed submissions without a self-addressed stamped envelope or email address will be disposed of without reply; pays modestly (2.5 cents CAD/word, max $125) upon publication.
details.response_time: first stage up to 8 weeks; second stage may take longer; auto-reply within about a week of submission
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed
details.word_limit: stories more likely to be accepted under 6000 words; no strict cap stated

neoopsis.index_line: Neo-Opsis: Canadian SF/fantasy, unfussy accessible storytelling, no horror; under 6000 words; currently closed, no reopening date
neoopsis.name: Neo-Opsis
neoopsis.summary: Neo-opsis is a Canadian print science fiction and fantasy magazine that favors genre stories under 6000 words and SF/fantasy-themed poetry, with a preference for accessible, unfussy storytelling over horror or rule-bound experimentation; it pays on publication and is currently closed to submissions with no reopening date set.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction (short stories to novellas), poetry (long and short), nonfiction (personal/lyric essays, cultural criticism, travelogues, environmental writing), dramatic writing (short plays, monologues, screenplays), and translations. Prizes craft that is attentive but not showy, takes quiet or noisy risks, and is serious even when humorous. Committed to discovering debut and underrepresented voices.
details.fee: Small fee via Submittable; waived if subscription is purchased at time of submission; fee can be waived for financial hardship by emailing the editors; no fee for paper submissions
details.multiple_submissions: One submission at a time across all genres; exception: fiction pieces under 1,000 words (up to three); poetry up to six poems submitted as a single file
details.reading_period: March 1 – May 1 and September 1 – November 1 (may close early if submission cap is reached)
details.red_flags: Windows close early if volume cap is hit—submit at opening. No resubmissions of previously rejected work unless fully rewritten (fiction) or requested by editors. AI-generated work explicitly prohibited. Published NER contributors should wait ~1 year before submitting again.
details.response_time: Up to 12 weeks, but can take longer
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed in all genres; must withdraw immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction and nonfiction: up to 20,000 words (most published work under 10,000). Dramatic writing: up to 5,000 words. Poetry: up to 6 poems per submission. Staging Style essays: 900–2,000 words.

new england review.index_line: New England Review: risk-taking fiction, poetry, essays, drama, translation up to 20k words; Mar–May & Sep–Nov only, one sub at a time

Submissions are accepted only during two windows: March 1–May 1 and September 1–November 1, with windows potentially closing early; one submission at a time across all genres is enforced. There is a small Submittable fee (waived with a subscription purchase), AI-generated work is explicitly prohibited, and previously published writers must wait roughly a year before resubmitting.

details.aesthetic: Lively, fresh, vivid writing across all genres and subjects — fiction (traditional or graphic), nonfiction, poetry, chapbooks, novellas, book reviews, and visual art; open to critical discourse on writing, art, or culture; no rigid style or subject preferences.

Prose up to 5,000 words (novellas up to 30,000), poetry up to six poems, chapbooks up to 30 pages; one submission at a time via Submittable with a small fee (waived for subscribers). Writers should note the fee and that simultaneous submissions require immediate notification if accepted elsewhere.

details.aesthetic: Previously unpublished fiction and nonfiction (500–1500 words each), poetry (2–4 poems, with English translation required for non-English poems), and artwork (photography only: 1–3 high-res JPG or PNG files). No stated thematic or stylistic preferences beyond these categories.

Reading periods are Sep 15–Oct 15 and Feb 15–Apr 1; no submissions are currently open. Writers affiliated with New Mexico Highlands University must wait five full years after disaffiliation before submitting, and previous contributors must skip at least two issues.

new myths.name: New Myths
new myths.summary: NewMyths publishes balanced speculative fiction (SF and fantasy), poetry, and nonfiction across tones and lengths, favoring variety over a single style; fiction must be under 10,000 words, previously unpublished, and preferably PG-rated, submitted only during two narrow windows (Jan–Feb and Jun–Jul). Writers should note the strict AI-assistance ban (any AI involvement disqualifies a piece) and that submissions outside the reading periods are deleted unread.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, and nonfiction; no further description of voice, themes, or forms provided on this page.

new ohio review.name: New Ohio Review
new ohio review.summary: New Ohio Review publishes poetry, fiction, and nonfiction in two print and two online editions per year, favoring work submitted through Submittable during their defined windows. Submission periods are Aug 15–Nov 15 and Jan 15–Apr 15; contests carry a $21–$22 fee while regular submissions (when open) appear to be free. This fall, regular submissions are restricted—only membership and NORward contest entries are accepted—so writers should verify current access before submitting.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, nonfiction, and poetry from writers worldwide, with particular interest in marginalized voices including trans, non-binary, and gender non-conforming writers; also runs an ongoing column (Songs of the Sunbirds) for Palestinian writers and artists covering any subject, not limited to stories of suffering; book reviews of recent or neglected titles (500–1500 words).
details.fee: Fee applies (amount not stated); free submission periods for Black writers (February), writers with disabilities (March), AAPI writers (May), LGBTQIA2+ writers (June), Latinx writers (Sep 15–Oct 15), Indigenous writers (November); no fee for Songs of the Sunbirds column or book reviews
details.multiple_submissions: Only one piece at a time for flash fiction and flash nonfiction; up to 5 pages of poems (multiple poems allowed in one submission)
details.red_flags: Current Loyola University New Orleans students are ineligible for fiction, poetry, and nonfiction submissions; no previously published work accepted (online or in print); Songs of the Sunbirds column has a submission cap that may close periodically

details.word_limit: Up to 5,000 words for fiction and nonfiction; up to 5 pages for poetry; book reviews 500–1,500 words

new orleans review.index_line: New Orleans Review — fiction/nonfiction/poetry with a Palestinian-writers column (Songs of the Sunbirds); $300/$100 honoraria; fee applies, free windows for marginalized writers
new orleans review.name: *New Orleans Review
new orleans review.summary: New Orleans Review publishes fiction, nonfiction, and poetry year-round with a strong commitment to marginalized and diverse voices, including an ongoing column dedicated to Palestinian writers. Word limits are 5,000 words for prose and five pages for poetry; honoraria are $300 for prose and $100 for poetry. Writers should note that current Loyola University New Orleans students cannot submit fiction, poetry, or nonfiction, and there is a submission fee (amount not stated on page) with various free windows for specific communities.

details.aesthetic: Formally conscious Canadian literature across fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction; emphasis on style and narrative craft, writing that 'questions and challenges'; champions emerging writers alongside established Canadian authors.
details.multiple_submissions: One piece per author per genre per calendar year; per submission: max one fiction piece OR three poems OR three postscript stories.
details.reading_period: Fiction & Poetry: Feb 1–Apr 30 and Jul 1–Sep 30. Nonfiction: Jan 1–31 and Jun 1–30.
details.red_flags: Eligibility strictly limited to Canadian citizens, current Canadian residents, or First Nations/Inuit/Métis peoples — non-Canadians abroad cannot submit. Submission caps (150 fiction, 120 poetry, 50 nonfiction) can close the window early; submit in the first couple of months. Footnotes and Works Cited are not accepted.
details.response_time: 6–7 months from the opening of the submission period (approx. end of June for Feb window; end of January next year for July window; June for January nonfiction window; October for June nonfiction window).
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify TNQ immediately if accepted elsewhere.
details.word_limit: No hard limit stated, but typically 2,500–5,000 words; rarely publishes over 6,000 words.

new quarterly.index_line: New Quarterly — Canadians only: formally daring fiction, poetry, CNF that "questions and challenges"; no footnotes; caps fill fast, submit early
new quarterly.name: New Quarterly
new quarterly.summary: TNQ publishes Canadian writers only, seeking formally attentive fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction that 'questions and challenges,' with a strong focus on nurturing emerging voices alongside established ones. Fiction/poetry windows are Feb 1–Apr 30 and Jul 1–Sep 30; nonfiction windows are January and June only, with hard caps per cycle (150 fiction, 120 poetry, 50 nonfiction). Non-Canadian writers are categorically ineligible, submission caps fill fast so early submission is advised, and footnotes/Works Cited are explicitly forbidden.

details.aesthetic: High-quality work across all genres and forms with no regional requirement; prizes what is new, fresh, and different in poetry, fiction (including flash), and creative nonfiction/lyric essay.

Submissions are open September 1–March 31, with fiction and essays capped at 7,500 words, poetry at five poems, and response time of 3–6 months. The journal notes it is currently on hiatus, so writers should verify it is actively accepting work before submitting.

details.fee: none (no submission fees for 2026); contributors are paid $25–$100 upon publication (except fiction excerpts, which are unpaid)

details.red_flags: Fiction excerpts must be emailed directly (mary@theoffingmag.com) and are unpaid — do not submit excerpts through the portal. AI-assisted work requires explicit labeling and must critically engage with AI use or it will not be considered. No submissions accepted via email for all other departments.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; must withdraw promptly if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Wit Tea: up to 8 pages; Translation: Prose: up to 7,500 words; other departments: unknown

offing.index_line: Offing: humor, absurdity, translated prose, novel excerpts (email only, unpaid); no fee 2026; $25–100 pay otherwise
offing.name: *Offing
offing.summary: The Offing publishes humor, translated prose, fiction excerpts, and other genre work valuing strong voice, absurdity, vulnerability, and surprise; no submission fees for 2026, one submission per department at a time, with a six-month response target. AI-generated work is only considered if it explicitly engages with or critiques AI use and is clearly labeled. Fiction excerpts are handled via email (not the portal) and are unpaid, which is a notable exception to the general paid-contributor model.

details.aesthetic: Favors the weird, genre-bending, and slipstream; work that is funny and sad simultaneously; experimental, surreal, and magical realist sensibilities across flash fiction, micro batches, and poetry; explicitly avoids gratuitous sex, gore, violence, and bigotry, and seeks to amplify marginalized voices.
details.fee: none for regular submissions; optional paid Tip Jar and Expedited Response options available
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed - only one flash fiction/batch of micros or one poem per author per submission period; must wait for a response before submitting again
details.reading_period: Opens 1st of every month except December, closes early if submission cap is reached; reopens 1st of next month
details.red_flags: Strict caps mean regular submissions can close quickly each month; no flash nonfiction accepted; no anonymous work; no AI-generated writing; if rejected must wait 2 months to resubmit, if accepted must wait 1 year.
details.response_time: usually 2-3 months for regular submissions; 2 weeks for paid Expedited Response submissions
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed
details.word_limit: up to 1,200 words for flash fiction (single piece or batch of micros); poetry has no strict limit but they favor poems that fit on one page

okay donkey.index_line: Okay Donkey: flash fiction & poetry, weird/slipstream/funny-sad; one submission per month, $25/piece, weekly Friday posts
okay donkey.name: Okay Donkey
okay donkey.summary: Okay Donkey is an online literary magazine publishing flash fiction and poetry with a taste for the odd, off-kilter, funny-sad, experimental, surreal, magical realist, and slipstream; it posts one new piece every Friday, alternating genres. It pays a $25 honorarium per piece, caps monthly submissions, and offers optional paid expedited response.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction of any style or subject, 3,000–8,000 words; must stand alone and leave readers feeling satisfied. Translations accepted. No previously published work (North American or online); print publication outside North America is okay.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed; one story per writer per submission period
details.reading_period: Next period opens June 8, 2026; closes when submission cap is reached (spring 2026 cap already reached; fall 2026 reopening mentioned as interim)
details.red_flags: Strict no-AI policy at any stage; revisions of previously rejected stories automatically declined; stories published on blogs or personal websites considered previously published and ineligible; PDF via Submittable required (emailed submissions deleted unread)
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; must withdraw immediately upon acceptance elsewhere

one story.index_line: One Story: single standout literary story per issue, 3,000–8,000 words, any style—PDF only, opens June 8, 2026
one story.name: One Story
one story.summary: One Story publishes one literary short story per issue—any style or subject, as long as it stands alone and satisfies; stories must be 3,000–8,000 words and previously unpublished in North America or online. Submissions are capped per period (next opening June 8, 2026), one story per writer per period, via Submittable as a PDF only. Watch out for the strict no-AI policy, no revisions of rejected work, and the broad definition of 'previously published online' disqualifying blogs and personal websites.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction of any style or subject, 3,000–8,000 words; must feel satisfying and be strong enough to stand alone as a single issue. Translations accepted. No previously published work (online or North American print); print publication outside North America is okay.
details.multiple_submissions: One story per submission period only
details.reading_period: Opens June 8, 2026; closes when submission cap is reached (currently closed for spring 2026)
details.red_flags: No AI assistance at any stage (including ideation and revision); no revisions of previously rejected stories; stories published online in any form (blogs, personal sites, online magazines, forums) are ineligible; emailed submissions deleted unread; PDF strongly required
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must withdraw immediately if accepted elsewhere

one teen story.index_line: One Teen Story: sister zine of One Story, YA-facing, one standalone story per issue, 3,000–8,000 words; strict no-AI policy, PDF only, opens June 8, 2026
one teen story.name: One Teen Story
one teen story.summary: One Story publishes one literary short story per issue, seeking any style or subject as long as it stands alone and satisfies—strictly 3,000–8,000 words. Submissions are capped per period (next opens June 8, 2026), one story per writer per period, via Submittable as PDF only. Watch out for the strict no-AI policy, no revisions of rejected work, and the rule that stories previously published online in any form are ineligible.

details.aesthetic: Literary environmental/cultural nonfiction blending essay, memoir, reporting, science writing, criticism, and comics; digital pieces also include food writing, enumerations, conversations, graphic stories, and art portfolios. Values work that challenges or expands understanding of nature, culture, and place through thoughtful, lived experience rather than polemic or overly conceptual 'nature as metaphor' pieces. Visual art should have intuitive, literal connections to the physical world; not an 'art' magazine in the abstract sense.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed - prefer one story idea/pitch at a time
details.reading_period: Print: closed, check back for 2027 themes; Digital: opens twice yearly, Sept 1 and Feb 1, for two-week windows; no submissions accepted outside open windows
details.red_flags: Currently not accepting fiction, poetry, book reviews, op-eds, press releases, or AI-assisted work; feature submissions closed entirely (pitches only, periodically); very narrow, short windows (two weeks, twice a year) for digital pitches; requires close familiarity with past issues before submitting; strict formatting rules for visual art submissions (no email attachments).
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Pitches: up to 500 words (print), up to 400 words (digital); digital full drafts only if under 1000 words and unlikely to exceed 2,000; features typically 1,000-5,000 words (though feature submissions currently closed)

orion.index_line: Orion: literary environmental nonfiction (essay, memoir, reporting) on nature/place; pitch only, twice-yearly windows; no fiction/poetry
orion.name: Orion
orion.summary: Orion is a nonfiction-focused environmental and cultural magazine exploring nature, culture, and place through essay, memoir, reporting, science writing, criticism, and visual art (no poetry, fiction, book reviews, or AI-assisted work accepted). It works entirely by pitch rather than unsolicited manuscripts, opening briefly for themed print calls and twice yearly for digital pitches (Sept 1 and Feb 1), with a strong preference for concrete, specific stories over abstract concept art or straight environmental-catastrophe exposés.

details.aesthetic: Speculative fiction (sci-fi, fantasy, slipstream, horror, magic realism, surrealism, etc.) with significant genre elements—not token gestures. Poetry should be experimental and boundary-pushing, focused on emotion and experience rather than worldbuilding exposition. Reviews must offer analytical perspective, not plot overview.
details.multiple_submissions: Micro: up to 3 submissions per window (1 story each); Flash: up to 2 per window (1 story each); Poetry: only 1 submission per window (up to 5 poems); Reviews and Translations may be submitted in addition to a fiction/poetry genre
details.reading_period: Mar 1 – May 15 (Spring) and Sep 1 – Oct 31 (Autumn); currently closed until Sep 1, 2026 for stories and poems
details.red_flags: Story/poem submissions closed until September 1, 2026. Rejected stories cannot be resubmitted even if revised. Submitting in more than one fiction/poetry genre (flash, micro, poetry) means none will be read. Stories over 1000 words are auto-rejected. Art must be submitted by email, not Duosuma.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must withdraw via submission manager if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Micro fiction: up to 400 words; Flash fiction: 401–1000 words; Poetry: up to 5 poems, max 10 pages; Reviews: up to 1000 words

orions belt.index_line: Orion's Belt: speculative micro/flash/poetry/reviews, genre must be real not decorative; closed until Sep 1, 2026; no revised resubmissions
orions belt.name: Orion's Belt
orions belt.summary: Orion's Belt publishes speculative micro fiction (≤400w), flash fiction (401–1000w), poetry (experimental, emotion-focused), translations, reviews, and art, all requiring significant speculative elements. Two annual windows: March 1–May 15 and September 1–October 31; story and poetry submissions are currently closed until September 1, 2026. Writers must submit in only one fiction/poetry genre per window, rejected stories cannot be resubmitted even revised, and any story over 1000 words is auto-rejected.

details.aesthetic: Science fiction and fantasy short fiction, described by its editor as part of the 'polysymphonic wonder' of modern genre voices; historically associated with Orson Scott Card's sensibilities and one of the earlier professional online SFF magazines.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: The magazine ceased publication after its June/July 2019 issue, so it is defunct and no longer a viable submission target.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

orson scott cards intergalactic medicine.index_line: Card-associated online SFF magazine for genre short fiction — CLOSED since June/July 2019, not accepting submissions
orson scott cards intergalactic medicine.name: Orson Scott Card's Intergalactic Medicine Show
orson scott cards intergalactic medicine.summary: Orson Scott Card's Intergalactic Medicine Show was an online science fiction and fantasy magazine that published genre short fiction since the early days of digital SFF publishing, but it officially closed after its June/July 2019 issue and is no longer accepting submissions.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, poetry, and nonfiction 'tinged with the strange' — work from another dimension, weird/uncanny sensibility.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Submissions are currently closed; no reopening date given. Very few practical submission details (word limits, fees, sim-sub policy) are available on this page.
details.response_time: By September (implied September 2026 for Issue 10 submissions)
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

outlook springs.index_line: Outlook Springs — fiction/poetry/nonfiction 'tinged with the strange'; uncanny, otherworldly work; closed since May 2026, no reopening date given
outlook springs.name: Outlook Springs
outlook springs.summary: Outlook Springs publishes fiction, poetry, and nonfiction with a strange/weird/uncanny tilt. Submissions for Issue 10 closed May 15, 2026, with a response expected by September 2026. No other practical submission details are provided on this page.

details.aesthetic: Reported, narrative-driven journalism centering human impact and counter-narratives to mainstream coverage of the South; personal narrative considered but only as full drafts; visual art series (photography, film) also curated with a Southern lens; emphasis on specificity of place and 'stories neglected by national news media.'
details.fee: none for pitches or Eyes on the South submissions
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Work must engage with the American South or it will be rejected; no generative AI permitted at any stage (pitch, draft, editing); Dispatches submitted via pitch only, not full manuscripts.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Dispatches: 500-2,000 words; no stated limit for personal narrative drafts or Eyes on the South submissions

oxford american.index_line: Oxford American: pitch-only Dispatches (500-2,000 words, $300) on under-covered Southern stories; must engage the South; no AI
oxford american.name: Oxford American
oxford american.summary: Oxford American is a well-established Southern-focused magazine whose digital imprint publishes reported, narrative-driven Dispatches (500-2,000 words, $300 flat fee) on under-covered stories in Southern communities, plus an Eyes on the South series showcasing film, photography, and visual art ($100 honorarium). All work must substantively engage with the American South and generative AI is strictly prohibited.

details.aesthetic: Genre-bending prose, poetry, hybrid work, and art with experimental forms, unusual/bizarre premises, daring comparisons, strange points-of-view, and emotional ambiguity. Publishes fiction, CNF, poetry, and art/new media.
details.multiple_submissions: one submission per reading period only
details.reading_period: March 1 – April 20 (or until per-genre submission cap is met)
details.red_flags: Submission cap per genre can close the window before April 20 — submit early. No AI-generated work accepted; contact editors before submitting anything AI-assisted. No previously published work. No email submissions; Submittable only.
details.response_time: 8–10 weeks (may be longer; nudge editors at [email protected] if past window)
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must withdraw via Submittable immediately if accepted elsewhere; poetry submitters may note which poems are no longer available
details.word_limit: Fiction and CNF: up to 3500 words each; micro-work: up to 3 pieces within 3 pages; Poetry: up to 3 poems in one document

oxford magazine.index_line: Oxford Magazine: genre-bending prose/poetry/hybrid/art, bizarre premises, strange POVs, laugh-or-cry ambiguity; Mar 1–Apr 20, caps close early
oxford magazine.name: Oxford Magazine
oxford magazine.summary: Oxford Magazine seeks genre-bending prose, poetry, hybrid work, and art with experimental forms, bizarre premises, strange POVs, and emotional ambiguity (laugh-or-cry). Fiction and CNF cap at 3500 words, poetry at 3 poems, with a short reading window (March 1–April 20) and an 8–10 week response time. AI-generated work is not accepted, previously published work is not accepted, and submissions are capped per genre so the window may close early.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry (not light verse or traditional rhyme), visual art, and criticism/reviews; prioritizes work by Black and Brown, LGBTQ+, and disabled creators, and independently produced work without corporate promotion; seeks pieces that engage with what it means to be alive and amplify underrepresented voices.
details.multiple_submissions: one submission per genre category per window; submitting to both a regular and Emerging Voices category in the same genre is not allowed
details.red_flags: Strict AI ban—work found to use generative AI will be removed and publication rescinded; no reprints; duplicate or cross-category submissions within same window are declined; Emerging Voices Poetry does not accept translations
details.response_time: up to 6 months (wait 6 months before inquiring)
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 7,500 words; Emerging Voices Fiction: up to 5,000 words; CNF: up to 6,000 words; Poetry: up to 3 poems; Emerging Voices Poetry: up to 10 pages; Visual Art: 5–8 images or video under 10 minutes

oyster river pages.index_line: Oyster River Pages: fiction/CNF/poetry/art centering Black, Brown, LGBTQ+, disabled voices; strict no-AI policy; opens Jan 27, 2026
oyster river pages.name: *Oyster River Pages
oyster river pages.summary: Oyster River Pages publishes fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry, visual art, and criticism with a strong emphasis on marginalized and decentered voices; submissions are open January 27–May 15, 2026, with genre-specific word limits ranging from 5,000 to 7,500 words. Simultaneous submissions are allowed with immediate notification if accepted elsewhere, and response time can reach 6 months. Writers should note a strict ban on AI-generated work (published pieces can be removed), no reprints, and that submitting to both a regular and Emerging Voices category in the same genre will result in decline.

details.aesthetic: Traditional, straightforward narrative poetry and fiction with clear plot arcs and accessible language; avoids experimental, non-linear, or overly lyrical work. Focuses on emerging authors. Also publishes reprints at half pay.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No attachments accepted — work must be pasted into the email body or submission will be ignored. Website described as poorly organized. This page is a third-party review from 2013, so guidelines may be outdated.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Micro flash under 150 words; flash fiction up to 1,000 words; no stated limit for short stories or other forms

page and spine.index_line: Traditional, accessible poetry/fiction with clear narrative arcs, emerging authors; email body only, no attachments (2013 review, dated info)
page and spine.name: *Page & Spine
page and spine.summary: Page & Spine publishes traditional, straightforward poetry and fiction by emerging authors, favoring clear narrative arcs and accessible language over experimental or non-linear work. They accept poems, limericks, micro flash (under 150 words), flash fiction (up to 1,000 words), short stories, essays, and articles via email (pasted into body only), with a typical response time of one week. The website is noted as poorly organized, and payment details require a separate visit to their contact page.

details.aesthetic: Eclectic, genre- and school-agnostic; publishes poetry, fiction (including flash), essays, reviews, and creative nonfiction. Democratic multi-board editorial process across Philadelphia, New York, and Abu Dhabi.
details.multiple_submissions: Up to 3 flash pieces, 1 fiction piece, 1 prose piece, or up to 3 poems per submission; separate submissions per category implied
details.red_flags: $3 fee per submission and slow response times due to multi-board review; simultaneous submission policy not stated
details.response_time: unknown (editors note it may take a while due to democratic process)
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Fiction up to 5,000 words; flash fiction up to 1,000 words (up to 3 pieces totaling no more than 1,000 words); nonfiction/essays/reviews up to 3,000 words; creative nonfiction up to 5,000 words; poetry: no stated cap, up to 3 poems per submission

painted bride quarterly.index_line: Painted Bride Quarterly: eclectic poetry/fiction/nonfiction, no house style, three-board review; $3 fee, expect a long wait
painted bride quarterly.name: Painted Bride Quarterly
painted bride quarterly.summary: Painted Bride Quarterly publishes poetry, fiction, essays, and reviews with an eclectic, democratic aesthetic across three editorial boards (Philadelphia, New York, Abu Dhabi). Fiction up to 5,000 words, flash up to 1,000 words, nonfiction up to 3,000 words, poetry up to 3 poems per submission; reads year-round. There is a $3 submission fee per submission category, and the democratic multi-board review process means slower response times.

details.aesthetic: Strong point of view across fiction, poetry, nonfiction (with themed subgenres: food, education, health, science, family, politics), and comics/art; seeks remarkable narrators, argumentative essays, challenging poems, and visual work that complicates viewing; politically and socially engaged but edited for lasting quality.
details.fee: Required for fiction, poetry, and nonfiction (amount not specified); not required for By Prior Arrangement/art submissions authorized by an editor
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No AI-generated work accepted; do not send revisions after submitting; By Prior Arrangement category is strictly gated by editor authorization and will not be considered otherwise; payments via PayPal only, which may be an issue for some writers.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Nonfiction up to 3,500 words; fiction up to 5,000 words; poetry up to 3 poems; art up to 10 images per submission

pangyrus.index_line: Pangyrus: fiction/poetry/nonfiction/comics with strong POV—bold narrators, argumentative essays; themed nonfiction (food, health, politics); no AI work; $30/piece via PayPal
pangyrus.name: Pangyrus
pangyrus.summary: Pangyrus publishes fiction, poetry, nonfiction (including themed subgenres), and comics/art with a strong point of view—remarkable narrators, argumentative essays, challenging poems, work that connects ideas across genres and geographies. Two reading periods per year (Feb 15–May 15 and Sept 15–Nov 15); pays $30 per accepted piece via PayPal only; fiction capped at 5,000 words, nonfiction at 3,500, poetry up to 3 poems. AI-generated work is rejected outright, do not send revisions after submission, and the 'By Prior Arrangement' category requires explicit editor authorization or it will not be read.

details.aesthetic: unknown

details.aesthetic: Cross-genre fiction (sci-fi, horror, literary, bizarro, slipstream, noir, fantasy, and hybrids) that is energetic, gripping, and heartfelt—not boring, flowery, or instruction-manual-style. Also accepts music/movie/book reviews of recent releases, art/photos tied to quarterly prompts, and reprints. No poetry currently.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown

details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; notify them if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: under 7500 words (novellas considered as serials on request); reviews: under 1000 words

pantheon magazine.index_line: Pantheon Magazine: energetic, plot-driven cross-genre (sci-fi, horror, bizarro, noir, fantasy); ¼¢/word, PayPal only; no poetry
pantheon magazine.name: Pantheon Magazine
pantheon magazine.summary: Pantheon publishes cross-genre fiction (sci-fi, horror, literary, bizarro, noir, fantasy, and hybrids) that is energetic and plot-driven, plus reviews and art; poetry is not currently accepted. Fiction must be under 7500 words, reviews under 1000 words; simultaneous submissions are allowed with notification if accepted elsewhere; pay is ¼ cent per word via PayPal only. Writers should note that reprints earn no pay, accepted unpublished work becomes a reprint limiting future earnings, and the magazine plans to eventually request print rights from accepted contributors.

details.aesthetic: Jewish-interest fiction and poetry broadly conceived—including marginalized communities and writers in translation—aiming to expand what counts as the 'Jewish experience' while balancing scholarship with accessibility for Jewish and non-Jewish, lay and academic readers.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown

paper brigade.index_line: Paper Brigade: Jewish-interest fiction/poetry, broadly defined; Jan 16–Feb 16, 2026 only, $3 fee, 6mo+ response
paper brigade.name: Paper Brigade
paper brigade.summary: Paper Brigade (Jewish Book Council) publishes fiction and poetry with a Jewish-interest focus, broadly defined to include marginalized voices and work in translation, balancing scholarship with accessibility. The submission window is narrow: January 16–February 16, 2026, with a $3 reading fee and response times of six months or more. Writers should note the tight one-month window, the fee, and the expectation to have read prior JBC work before submitting.

details.aesthetic: Strong voices, compelling stories, emotional impact, and innovative narrative technique; welcomes fiction, poetry, nonfiction, flash, novel excerpts (if self-contained), and regular features; avoids poetry overtly about politics, nature, or religion.
details.multiple_submissions: Up to three flash pieces (in one document); poetry up to 10 pages; features one piece at a time; not explicitly stated for fiction/nonfiction
details.reading_period: unknown (page notes no currently open calls; past windows referenced but no fixed annual dates given)

details.response_time: Varies by editor; one editor responds near publication date, meaning potentially several months; no-reply equals rejection
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction/essays ~3,000 words or less; flash 1,000 words or less; features 1,500 words or less; poetry up to 10 pages

parhelion.index_line: Parhelion: fiction/poetry/flash wanting strong voices, emotional resonance; no pay; unpaid waits can stretch months, no-reply=rejection
parhelion.name: Parhelion
parhelion.summary: Parhelion seeks strong voices, emotional resonance, and innovative narrative technique across fiction, poetry, nonfiction, and flash; fiction/essays run ~3,000 words or less, poetry up to 10 pages, and flash up to 1,000 words. They publish three issues per year (February, July, October), with the Halloween issue limited to fiction/flash only; no compensation is offered. Response times vary widely by editor—one editor holds responses until just before publication—and no-reply means rejection.

details.aesthetic: Literary prose and poetry in English, previously unpublished; translations accepted with original copy. No unsolicited art.

details.reading_period: Mail: year-round. Submittable prose: February, June, October (until capacity). Submittable poetry: January, April, July, October (until capacity).

details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Prose: 40 pages maximum; Poetry: up to 6 poems per submission

paris review.index_line: Paris Review: top-tier literary prose/poetry, no fee; Submittable opens narrow rotating windows, mail year-round, 6-8mo wait
paris review.name: Paris Review
paris review.summary: The Paris Review publishes prose and poetry in English (previously unpublished, translations welcome) with a literary prestige focus. Mail submissions are accepted year-round; Submittable opens on a rotating monthly schedule by genre with capacity limits. Writers should note the 6–8 month response time and strict one-submission-per-period rule.

details.aesthetic: Experimental, genre-bending, risk-taking work across fiction, poetry, CNF, hybrids, short-shorts, and visual essays. Prizes strong voice, formal consciousness, and curiosity; welcomes speculative, lyric, and nontraditional forms. Fiction wants propulsive, character-driven stories (quiet or weird); poetry must know and break rules; nonfiction should be 'pathologically curious'; short-shorts favor density, mystery, and precision.
details.fee: Free tier available but monthly cap applies; fee charged for 'Rocket Fuel' category when free limit is hit (amount not specified)
details.multiple_submissions: Allowed across different genres simultaneously, but writers are asked to use judgment and avoid overloading editors
details.reading_period: Poetry, nonfiction/hybrids, short-shorts: Sept 1 – Apr 15; Fiction: Sept 1 – Oct 15 and Jan 1 – Feb 15
details.red_flags: Free submissions close mid-month when the monthly cap is hit — writers must wait until the 1st or pay the Rocket Fuel fee. Extensive color use in nonfiction or visual essays makes work less likely to be published in print. No contributor payment.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must withdraw immediately and notify Passages North if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: 1000–5000 words; Nonfiction/hybrids: up to 4500 words; Short-shorts: under 1000 words each (up to 3 per submission); Poetry: 1–3 poems per packet

passages north.index_line: Passages North: experimental, voice-driven fiction/poetry/CNF/hybrids; free subs cap monthly, then paid Rocket Fuel to submit
passages north.name: Passages North
passages north.summary: Passages North publishes fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, hybrids, short-shorts, and visual essays, favoring experimental, risk-taking, formally conscious work with strong voice. Fiction is capped at 1000–5000 words, nonfiction at 4500 words, poetry at 1–3 poems, short-shorts under 1000 words; reading periods are genre-specific and seasonal. Free submissions are monthly-capped and the site closes mid-month when the limit is hit, requiring either a wait or a paid 'Rocket Fuel' submission; extensive color use in nonfiction/visual work may hurt publishability.

details.aesthetic: Experimental, indie literary work; poetry-forward with visual arts; associated with small press and independent publishing culture.

Mixes proposals are restricted to previous Peach Mag contributors only. Writers looking to submit fiction, poetry, or essays have no viable path here right now.

details.aesthetic: Poetry-forward journal with a serious literary sensibility; editorial staff backgrounds suggest range from experimental (Arlene Ang, published in Diagram, Caketrain) to formal and war/trauma-inflected (Stefan Lovasik) to socially engaged (melissa christine goodrum, Zora Neale Hurston Award). Peer publications of editors include Ploughshares, Prairie Schooner, Georgia Review, Blackbird — suggesting mid-to-high literary register.
