pedestal magazine.index_line: CLOSED PERMANENTLY (Dec 2025) — poetry-forward, mid-to-high literary register spanning experimental to formal/trauma-focused work. Do not submit.
pedestal magazine.name: *Pedestal Magazine
pedestal magazine.summary: Pedestal Magazine was a long-running online literary journal focused primarily on poetry, edited by a team of accomplished poet-editors with ties to outlets like Ploughshares, Rattle, and NYQ Books. It published its final issue (Issue 97) in December 2025 marking its 25-year run, and is permanently closed to submissions.

details.aesthetic: Original, previously unpublished poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and book reviews; no specific thematic or stylistic focus stated beyond literary.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed until a response is received on the current submission
details.red_flags: Fee applies 8 of 8 open months; no email or paper submissions accepted; pays only in contributor copies
details.response_time: Mostly December and May; query after 4 months with no response
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify editor immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 7,500 words for standard fiction and creative nonfiction; up to 3 flash pieces per submission; up to 3 poems per submission

pembroke magazine.index_line: Pembroke Magazine — general literary poetry/fiction/CNF/reviews, no stated aesthetic; $3 fee 8 of 8 open months, pays in copies
pembroke magazine.name: Pembroke Magazine
pembroke magazine.summary: Pembroke Magazine publishes poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and book reviews with a traditional literary scope, accepting only previously unpublished work once per year. Submissions are open September 1–April 30 via Submittable only, with a $3 fee (waived in September) and a 7,500-word cap for prose. Writers must wait for a response before resubmitting, and simultaneous submissions are allowed but require immediate notification if accepted elsewhere.

details.aesthetic: unknown
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Submissions are closed at this time; writer should check back later
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

penn review.index_line: Penn Review — no stated aesthetic beyond closed-window notice; submissions currently closed, check back later
penn review.name: Penn Review
penn review.summary: The Penn Review is a literary journal associated with the University of Pennsylvania. No submissions are currently open, and the page reveals nothing about aesthetic, form preferences, or mechanics beyond the closed-window notice.

details.aesthetic: Clarity and genre-consciousness across fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and hybrid forms; values risk, experimentation, place-based writing, vulnerable or bizarre subject matter; welcomes speculative work, hermit crab essays, graphic/multimodal texts, flash and micro forms, and traditional poetry alongside experimental.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed — one submission at a time
details.red_flags: $5 fee per submission and a 6–9 month wait before even inquiring; no reading period listed so unclear if submissions are currently open.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 8,000 words for fiction, nonfiction, and hybrid; up to three flash pieces under 1,000 words each (fiction/nonfiction); up to five poems (poetry).

permafrost.index_line: Permafrost: clear, genre-aware fiction/nonfiction/poetry/hybrid embracing the vulnerable, bizarre, place-based, experimental; $5 fee, one submission at a time
permafrost.name: Permafrost
permafrost.summary: Permafrost seeks work with clarity, genre awareness, and willingness to engage the vulnerable, difficult, or bizarre — across fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and hybrid forms, with a soft spot for place-based and experimental writing. Submissions are capped at 8,000 words (fiction/nonfiction/hybrid), up to three flash pieces per submission, or up to five poems; there is a $5 online submission fee. Writers must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere, submit only one submission at a time, and allow 6–9 months before following up.

details.aesthetic: Short fiction, flash fiction, creative non-fiction, and poetry; no gratuitous violence, graphic horror or sex, religious intolerance, homophobia, racism, or YA/children's literature. Writers are asked to read an issue before submitting.
details.fee: Fee required; exact amount not stated on this page (link to external payment page)
details.multiple_submissions: Up to one short fiction, one CNF, one flash, and two poems may be submitted at the same time
details.reading_period: Currently closed; Winter 25 was Oct 4 – Nov 29; Summer 26 TBC (Flash Dash competition open May 30 – Jul 31)
details.red_flags: Fees are non-refundable even if work is withdrawn or exceeds word/line limits; acceptance rate ~5%; work exceeding limits will not be considered with no refund issued
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must notify The Phare immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Short fiction and creative non-fiction: up to 2000 words each; flash: up to 500 words; poetry: up to 2 poems, max 40 lines each

phare.index_line: *Phare: Fiction/CNF/flash/poetry, no violence/horror/sex/intolerance/YA; paid submissions, ~5% acceptance, closed until Summer 26
phare.name: *Phare
phare.summary: The Phare publishes short fiction, flash, creative non-fiction, and poetry, avoiding gratuitous violence, graphic sex, horror, religious intolerance, homophobia, racism, and YA/children's work. Submissions require a fee (amount on their site), are capped at 2000 words for fiction/CNF, 500 for flash, 40 lines per poem, with a 60-day response window. The journal is currently closed for general submissions (Winter 25 window was Oct 4–Nov 29; Summer 26 TBC), fees are non-refundable under any circumstance, and the acceptance rate is around 5%.

details.aesthetic: Experimental and conventional poetry, fiction, personal/lyric/journalistic essays, and visual art; prizes vigorous appeal to senses, intellect, and emotion; welcomes BIPOC, LGBTQ+, and international voices; visual art should illustrate narrative or convey emotion.
details.fee: $3 in all genres; fee waivers available by emailing phoebeliterature@gmail.com
details.multiple_submissions: allowed, but only one work per submission entry
details.reading_period: Aug 15 – Oct 15 (print issue); Jan 15 – Mar 15 (spring contest issue)
details.red_flags: No AI-generated text or artwork accepted; no previously published work or reprints; submissions only via Submittable (no email or postal mail); payment subject to U.S. sanctions laws, which may affect some international contributors
details.response_time: 30 days after submissions period closes; follow up if no response within 60 days
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; withdraw via Submittable immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: No strict word limit for prose; nonfiction over 4,000 words must be extraordinary

phoebe.index_line: Phoebe: experimental/conventional poetry, fiction, nonfiction, visual art; sensory-intellectual-emotional impact; $3 fee; Aug15-Oct15 & Jan15-Mar15
phoebe.name: Phoebe
phoebe.summary: Phoebe publishes experimental and conventional poetry, fiction, nonfiction, and visual art from emerging and established writers, prizing sensory, intellectual, and emotional impact across voices and forms. Print submissions run Aug 15–Oct 15 and Jan 15–Mar 15 (contest); there is a $3 fee in all genres, though fee waivers are available on request. No AI-generated content is accepted, and nonfiction over 4,000 words must be exceptional to be considered.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, poetry, essays, author interviews, book/film/music/zine reviews, and artwork (including photography, comics, short films, graphic novel excerpts, sculpture). Seeks originality and individual creative vision aimed at readers and writers; actively looking for humor writing; prefers content that resonates with writerly/artistic audiences. Avoids fan fiction, hate speech, lewd content, and overt political agendas.
details.multiple_submissions: Allowed for all genres, but each poem must be submitted as a separate individual submission
details.red_flags: Each poem must be its own separate submission — easy to miss. Previously published work is generally not accepted. Over-2,000-word prose submissions are strongly discouraged and likely to be rejected. Writers must review and agree to the Rights and Royalties policy before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; if accepted, 30-day exclusivity from publication date is required
details.word_limit: Under 2,000 words strongly preferred for fiction and essays; submissions over 2,000 words have a strong chance of rejection. No word limit stated for poetry.

pif magazine.index_line: PIF Magazine: fiction/essays under 2,000 words, poetry, humor, for a writerly audience; each poem submitted separately
pif magazine.name: *PIF magazine
pif magazine.summary: Pif Magazine publishes fiction, poetry, essays, reviews, and artwork for a writerly audience, strongly preferring original voices and individual creative vision over commercial sameness. The practical ceiling is under 2,000 words for prose, simultaneous submissions are allowed, and a response is promised within 90 days. Watch out for the strict aversion to fan fiction, hate/lewd content, and previously published work, and note the unusual requirement to submit each poem as a completely separate submission.

details.aesthetic: Cross-genre and nonconformist poetry, fiction, and essays that engage complexities and intersections of identity; work that challenges the status quo of form and content and explores experiences of underrepresented writers; welcoming to emerging writers and often a home for first publications.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Response times can be significantly delayed during summer and winter holiday periods due to following an academic calendar.
details.response_time: unknown, described as generally quick but delayed during summer and winter academic holidays
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

pinch.index_line: Pinch: Cross-genre, nonconformist poetry/fiction/essays on identity, form-bending "pinchy" work; welcomes emerging writers, year-round submissions
pinch.name: Pinch
pinch.summary: The Pinch publishes cross-genre, nonconformist poetry, fiction, and essays that engage with identity, challenge conventions of form and content, and often serve as a launching pad for emerging writers' first publications. The journal actively seeks work from underrepresented writers and encourages international submissions, valuing pieces that are thematically layered and formally adventurous—what its editors call 'pinchy.' Submissions are accepted year-round via Submittable, though response times slow during academic holiday breaks.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction, personal/memoir/lyric/flash/hybrid/experimental nonfiction (no critical essays), and prose poetry only (no lineated or traditional forms like sonnets, sestinas, villanelles). No genre fiction. Online monthly publication.
details.multiple_submissions: one submission at a time; wait for a decision before submitting again; if declined, wait one month before resubmitting
details.reading_period: year-round, but capped at 300 submissions/month; windows close early if cap is hit and reopen the 1st of the following month
details.red_flags: Strict formatting required (RTF/.doc/.docx only, double-spaced, 12pt font, author contact info on page 1, page numbers); no AI-generated work; no previously published work including blogs; Pithead may edit without notification; no payment to contributors
details.response_time: up to 2 months (query if no response after 2 months)
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: under 4,000 words

pithead chapel.index_line: Pithead Chapel — literary fiction/lyric nonfiction/prose poetry (no lineated verse, no genre fiction), under 4,000 words, unpaid, monthly cap of 300 subs
pithead chapel.name: *Pithead Chapel
pithead chapel.summary: Pithead Chapel publishes literary fiction, creative nonfiction (personal/lyric/experimental essays, no critical), and prose poetry only (no traditional/lineated forms) in a monthly online journal. Submissions are capped at 300/month across all genres and must be under 4,000 words, one piece at a time with a one-month wait after a rejection. Watch out for strict formatting requirements (RTF/.doc/.docx, double-spaced, 12pt font, contact info on first page), no AI-generated work, no genre fiction, no previously published work, and Pithead's right to edit without notification.

details.aesthetic: Hard sci-fi, soft sci-fi, speculative fiction, weird fiction, slipstream — broad genre remit with a campy, fun editorial personality; seeks diverse voices from writers worldwide; previously unpublished work only.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed — one submission per author per reading period
details.reading_period: Next period opens October 13, 2026; currently closed
details.red_flags: Submissions are currently closed until October 13, 2026; AI-generated content violates the author contract and will be rejected; story must not be pasted in email body and no images should be attached.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with prompt withdrawal if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: up to 5,000 words (single story or flash collection)

planet scrumm.index_line: Planet Scumm: pulpy, campy sci-fi/speculative/weird fiction, ≤5,000 words; closed until Oct 13, 2026
planet scrumm.name: Planet Scrumm
planet scrumm.summary: Planet Scumm publishes hard and soft sci-fi, speculative, weird fiction, and slipstream short stories with a pulpy, irreverent sensibility and a strong preference for diverse global voices. Submissions are capped at 5,000 words, sent via email as .doc/.docx, one story per reading period, with the next window opening October 13, 2026. AI-generated content is explicitly banned by contract, and the current reading period is closed.

details.aesthetic: Publishes poetry, fiction, nonfiction, and translations, plus reviews and author interviews; states a specific investment in reading and representing writers from historically marginalized communities; judges for its named prizes include literary figures like Kenan Orhan (fiction) and musician/poet Sadie Dupuis (poetry), suggesting an openness to writers with crossover reputations in music/pop culture as well as traditional literary credentials.
details.fee: None for general submissions; $20 per entry for Kinder/Crump Prize and Prufer Poetry Prize (fee waivers available on request)
details.multiple_submissions: Not more than one submission per genre per reading period for general submissions; for contests, multiple entries permitted but each requires a separate entry fee
details.reading_period: General submissions: June and December only; Kinder/Crump Fiction Prize: May 1-31; Prufer Poetry Prize: October 1-31
details.red_flags: Submissions outside the specific open windows are not considered and mailed/emailed general submissions are not accepted (except for incarcerated writers); contest entries require separate fee per submission and are only accepted via Duosuma.
details.response_time: 6-9 months for general submissions; do not inquire before 9 months
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed for general submissions, with request to withdraw via Duosuma if accepted elsewhere; unknown for contests
details.word_limit: Kinder/Crump Prize: up to 6,000 words for short fiction; general submissions word limit unknown (see genre-specific guidelines on Duosuma)

pleiades.index_line: Pleiades: poetry/fiction/nonfiction/translation with priority for marginalized voices; general reads June & December only, else contests only
pleiades.name: Pleiades
pleiades.summary: Pleiades: Literature in Context is a university-affiliated (University of Central Missouri) journal publishing poetry, fiction, nonfiction, translations, and reviews/interviews, with an explicit editorial interest in work from historically marginalized communities. It reads general submissions only during June and December, runs two annual contests (Kinder/Crump Prize for short fiction in May, Prufer Poetry Prize for poetry in October, each $1,000 and $20 entry fee), and has a fairly slow 6-9 month response time.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction, nonfiction, and poetry across standard and longform formats; guest-edited issues with a strong tradition of serious literary work.
details.fee: Fee appears to exist but exact amount is dynamic/subscription-dependent; shown as '$0.00' base with subscription pricing logic
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — only one submission per reading period
details.reading_period: June 1 – November 15 (regular); Emerging Writers' Contest: February 1 – March 31
details.red_flags: Manuscripts must have all identifying information removed before upload (anonymous review); fee charges appear on statements as 'EMERSON' not Ploughshares, which may cause confusion; fee amount is unclear from static page content.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Fiction/Nonfiction: up to 6,500 words; Longform Fiction/Nonfiction: up to 15,000 words; Poetry: 3–5 pages; Longform Poetry: 6–10 pages

ploughshares.index_line: Ploughshares — top-tier literary fiction, nonfiction, poetry; anonymous review; one submission per period, June–Nov; fee dynamic/unclear at checkout
ploughshares.name: Ploughshares
ploughshares.summary: Ploughshares publishes fiction, poetry, and nonfiction with an established literary reputation; standard submissions are limited to once per reading period with word limits up to 6,500 words (or up to 15,000 for longform). Writers must remove all identifying information for anonymous review, and the fee structure is unclear from the page—the cost appears dynamic and subscription-dependent.

details.aesthetic: Fantasy in all its subgenres (magical realism, urban fantasy, slipstream, high fantasy, and everything between), chosen specifically for audio performance—strong pacing, well-defined characters, engaging dialogue, clear action, and prose that remains beautiful when read aloud; humor encouraged; fantastical elements must be meaningful to the story; actively seeking settings outside America and characters from a range of backgrounds/ethnicities; selkie stories are a noted 'hard sell' due to overrepresentation.
details.multiple_submissions: up to one original and one reprint under consideration at the same time (max two stories total)
details.red_flags: Currently closed to submissions with no set reopening date; stories over 6,000 words submitted without prior query will likely be rejected unread; AI-generated or AI-assisted stories are banned and grounds for permanent ban; selkie stories are a known hard sell.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with disclosure in cover letter; exception—do not simultaneously submit to sister EA podcasts (Escape Pod, PseudoPod, Cast of Wonders, CatsCast)
details.word_limit: up to 6,000 words for originals (sweet spot 3,000-4,000); reprints may go up to 17,000 words with prior query for anything over 6,000

podcastle.index_line: PodCastle — audio fantasy podcast, all subgenres, written for reading aloud; pro rates; currently closed, no reopening date set
podcastle.name: PodCastle
podcastle.summary: PodCastle is an audio fantasy fiction podcast/magazine publishing all fantasy subgenres from high fantasy to magical realism to urban fantasy and slipstream, with a strong preference for stories that read well aloud: tight pacing, clear action, vivid characters, engaging dialogue, and humor welcome. It pays professional rates for original fiction and accepts reprints (including translations and previously-podcasted work), but is currently closed to general submissions with no announced reopening date.

details.aesthetic: Philosophical, essayistic, earnest, and intellectually pluralist—no single political line. Favors essays rooted in personal confusion or lived problems that draw on philosophy, literature, or cultural criticism to reach genuine insight. Discourages mocking or condescending tones; values enthusiasm and reverence alongside rigorous criticism. Publishes on culture, ethics, everyday life (food, love, work, grief, social media, therapy, effective altruism). Essay is central; also publishes symposia and reviews. Fiction and poetry are not the focus.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This is primarily an essay/ideas magazine, not a fiction or poetry venue—writers submitting literary fiction or poetry should verify whether those forms are accepted at all before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

point the.index_line: Point, The: Philosophical essays on everyday life—Instagram, grief, dating—earnest and rigorous, not ironic; essays/symposia/reviews only, no fiction or poetry
point the.name: Point, The
point the.summary: The Point is a print/digital magazine of philosophical writing about everyday life and culture, publishing essays, symposia, and reviews that treat cultural phenomena—Instagram, therapy, grief, online dating—with earnest generosity rather than ironic detachment or political agenda. Its signature mode is the essay as self-understanding: a writer faces a lived problem, draws on thinkers or artists, and works toward new ground through the writing itself. Published three times a year; submission mechanics are not detailed in this text.

details.aesthetic: Professional and reflective work in creative arts therapies (art, drama, dance movement, music therapy): feature articles on programs/projects, practice papers, case reflections, theory, interviews, podcasts, book reviews, artwork, and poetry—all must have a sound conceptual or evidence base in therapeutic arts practice.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This is a specialist journal for creative arts therapists and allied professionals—not a general literary journal. All contributions must relate to arts therapies practice, research, or theory. Open-access publication (no payment to authors). Page content cuts off mid-sentence in the Practice Paper section, so full guidelines may not be shown.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Articles/reflections/interviews/practice papers: up to 2000 words; book reviews: up to 1000 words; artwork statements: up to 500 words; feature article abstracts: up to 100 words

polyphony.index_line: Polyphony: practice papers, case reflections, art & poetry by creative arts therapists only, not general literary fiction
polyphony.name: Polyphony
polyphony.summary: Polyphony publishes academic and reflective work by creative arts therapists (art, dance, drama, music therapy) including feature articles, practice papers, poetry, artwork, interviews, and book reviews, with a strong professional/clinical focus rather than literary fiction. Word limits are tight: 2000 words for articles, 1000 for reviews, 500 for artwork statements. This is a specialist professional journal for IACAT members and allied practitioners—general creative writers without a creative arts therapy context are not the target contributor.

details.aesthetic: Fiction: emotionally affecting, haunting, bizarre, strong storytelling mechanics. Nonfiction: discovery-driven, mutual construction via literary dialogue—essays, memoir, reportage. Poetry: reinvigorated everyday language or novel/rarefied text, inventive forms. Flash: full narrative arc in 1,000 words or less. Reviews: voice-driven and incisive, book-focused but open to music/film/TV/comics. Field Notes (craft blog): personal-essay intimacy exploring the writing life, especially for marginalized writers.
details.fee: $3 for regular submissions; no fee for Reviews or Field Notes
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Currently open for Editors' Prize Contest and Field Notes blog; broader reading period otherwise unknown
details.red_flags: Current Texas State University students, faculty, and staff cannot submit; alumni must wait 3+ years post-graduation. Reviews are currently unpaid. Submittable only—no paper or email submissions accepted.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must immediately withdraw if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction and nonfiction: up to 5,000 words; flash: up to 1,000 words per piece (max 3 pieces); poetry: up to 5 poems; reviews: up to 2,000 words; Field Notes: ~2,500 words preferred, no strict limit

porter house review.index_line: Porter House Review: emotionally affecting/haunting fiction, discovery-driven nonfiction, inventive poetry, voice-driven reviews; $3 fee; Texas State affiliates barred
porter house review.name: *Porter House Review
porter house review.summary: Porter House Review publishes emotionally affecting fiction, discovery-driven nonfiction, inventive poetry, and voice-driven reviews, all previously unpublished. Fiction and nonfiction cap at 5,000 words, poetry at five poems, flash at 1,000 words per piece; a $3 fee applies to regular submissions (not Reviews or Field Notes). Current Texas State students, faculty, and staff cannot submit, and alumni must wait three or more years post-graduation.

details.aesthetic: Publishes emerging and established writers; values work by marginalized voices (people of color, women, disabled people, LGBTQIA+, intersectional identities); no further genre/form specifics stated on this page.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Not currently accepting visual art. No previously published material accepted. Online publication only (no print since 2020).
details.response_time: up to 6 months; do not query before then
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must withdraw immediately via Submittable if accepted elsewhere; partial withdrawal of a poetry/image collection allowed via message
details.word_limit: unknown

portland review.index_line: Portland Review: fiction/poetry centering marginalized voices (LGBTQIA+, POC, disabled, women); online-only, no visual art currently; 6-month response
portland review.name: *Portland Review
portland review.summary: Portland Review publishes emerging and established writers with an explicit commitment to marginalized voices, including LGBTQIA+, POC, disabled, and women writers, across fiction, poetry, and visual art (no visual art currently). Submissions are online-only via Submittable with a six-month response window and no stated word limit. No previously published work is accepted, and writers must withdraw immediately if accepted elsewhere.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and theater — no further aesthetic detail provided
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No word limits, pay rates, or response times stated; submitters should check the main website for fuller guidelines
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but writer must notify Post Road immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

post road.index_line: Post Road: fiction, nonfiction, poetry, theater; no stated aesthetic — open until Mar 15, 2026; check site for guidelines
post road.name: Post Road
post road.summary: Post Road publishes fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and theater, with no stated aesthetic specifics. Submissions open until March 15, 2026; simultaneous submissions allowed with immediate notification required upon acceptance elsewhere. No word limits, response times, or fees are mentioned.

details.aesthetic: Literary poetry, short fiction, personal essays, creative nonfiction, meditations, and hybrid forms; currently themed around Water (rivers, oceans, drought, memory, migration, transformation); no academic essays.
details.multiple_submissions: One submission at a time per reading period
details.red_flags: Montgomery College affiliates (staff, faculty, students) are ineligible; AI-generated work not accepted; previously published work not accepted
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere and withdraw via Submittable
details.word_limit: Up to ~7,500 words for fiction and nonfiction; up to 5 poems per poetry submission

potomac review.index_line: Potomac Review: poetry/fiction/nonfiction/hybrid, currently themed on Water; no Montgomery College affiliates, no AI-generated work
potomac review.name: Potomac Review
potomac review.summary: Potomac Review publishes poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and hybrid literary work; their current special themed issue (#80) focuses on Water. Fiction and nonfiction run up to ~7,500 words; poetry allows up to 5 poems per submission; two reading windows per year (Jan 1–Apr 1 and Jul 1–Oct 1). Watch out for the blanket ban on submissions from anyone affiliated with Montgomery College (staff, faculty, students) and on AI-generated or previously published work.

details.aesthetic: Literary (not commercial) writing in poetry, fiction, and creative non-fiction; actively encourages submissions from BIPOC, LGBTQ+, and disabled writers; does not publish sexist, racist, homophobic, transphobic, ableist, hate-speech, or AI-generated work.
details.fee: none (for general submissions; contest fees apply for contests)
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per category (Poetry, Fiction, Creative Non-Fiction) per 12-month period for general submissions; separate allowance for special calls and contests
details.red_flags: No revisions, replacements, or substitutions once submitted; must wait 12 months before resubmitting to the same general category; Submittable closed over summer, reopens September 2nd
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

prairie fire.index_line: Prairie Fire: literary poetry/fiction/CNF centering BIPOC, LGBTQ+, disabled voices; opens Sep 2, one submission/category per year, no revisions after
prairie fire.name: Prairie Fire
prairie fire.summary: Prairie Fire publishes literary (not commercial) writing across poetry, fiction, and creative non-fiction, with an emphasis on underrepresented voices including BIPOC, LGBTQ+, and disabled writers. General submissions open September 2, 2025 via Submittable (snail mail/email also accepted), with a 3–6 month response time. Writers must wait 12 months between general submissions per category, and no revisions or substitutions are permitted once submitted.

details.aesthetic: Short story collections or mixed novella-plus-stories manuscripts (no novels, no single novellas, no novella collections); poetry collections. Writing in English from any living writer worldwide. No stated thematic or stylistic preference beyond genre eligibility.
details.multiple_submissions: Writers may enter both the fiction and poetry contests
details.red_flags: Previously published manuscripts (including self-published) are disqualified; novels, single novellas, and novella collections are not considered; UNL employees, faculty, and students are ineligible; hard copy submissions require a stamped self-addressed envelope and postcard for receipt confirmation — manuscripts are not returned.
details.response_time: Results announced on or before August 15 of each year
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction manuscripts at least 150 pages; poetry manuscripts at least 50 pages. No upper limit stated.

prairie schooner.index_line: Prairie Schooner Book Prize: story collections (150+ pp) or poetry (50+ pp), no novels/novellas; $25 fee, Jan 15–Mar 15 only, $3,000 + UNP publication
prairie schooner.name: Prairie Schooner
prairie schooner.summary: Prairie Schooner's Book Prize accepts poetry (50+ pages) and short fiction collections (150+ pages) in English from any living writer, awarding $3,000 and publication through University of Nebraska Press. Submissions are accepted only January 15–March 15 annually, with a $25 entry fee per manuscript. Writers should note that previously published manuscripts (including self-published) are ineligible, novels and single novellas are not considered, and UNL faculty/students/staff are excluded.

details.aesthetic: Distinctive poetry, short fiction, and flash nonfiction; any theme, form, or style welcomed; both emerging and established writers considered.
details.multiple_submissions: one piece per category per submission period
details.reading_period: Jan–Feb, May–Jun, Sept–Oct only (first two months of each quadrimester); closes early once submission cap is reached
details.red_flags: Social media posts (Facebook etc.) and self-published work count as previously published and are ineligible; email submissions are ignored; payment is a copy of the guest editor's book only for US/UK/Australia residents — writers elsewhere receive only publication credit.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but writer must withdraw immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

prime number.index_line: Prime Number: poetry, fiction, flash nonfiction, any style; capped submission windows Jan–Feb/May–Jun/Sept–Oct; no email subs
prime number.name: *Prime Number
prime number.summary: Prime Number Magazine publishes distinctive poetry, short fiction, and (as of Jan 2025) flash nonfiction in any theme, form, or style, appearing three times a year online. Submissions open only during the first two months of each quadrimester (Jan–Feb, May–Jun, Sept–Oct) and are capped at 199 per period for poetry/fiction and 101 for flash nonfiction. Social media posts count as prior publication, and email submissions are flatly rejected.

details.aesthetic: Original literary fiction, creative non-fiction, literary essays, comics, hybrid works, and cross-genre/interdisciplinary poetry; no rhetorical, academic, or strictly journalistic non-fiction; welcomes translations into English and work from Indigenous, BIPOC, disabled, 2SLGBTQIA+, and other marginalized writers.
details.fee: $3 CAD per submission (Inclusive Access/fee-waiver option available on Submittable; no fee for incarcerated writers)
details.multiple_submissions: Prose: one piece at a time (except flash, up to 3 pieces); must wait for response before resubmitting. Poetry: up to 4 poems per submission.
details.red_flags: UBC School of Creative Writing current/incoming students and faculty are ineligible; alumni cannot have taken a UBC SCW course in the past two years; same writer cannot be published twice in one publication year; no email or mail submissions accepted (except incarcerated writers); 6–12 month response time with no status inquiries answered.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; withdraw or notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere

prism international.index_line: PRISM International: fiction, CNF, poetry, comics, hybrid & translation, prose under 4,000 words; UBC SCW writers ineligible; $3 fee
prism international.name: PRISM International
prism international.summary: PRISM international publishes original literary fiction, creative non-fiction, poetry (including cross-genre and interdisciplinary work), comics, hybrid works, and translations from writers worldwide, with a preference for prose under 4,000 words. Submissions are open until June 14th for issue 65.1, cost $3 CAD per submission via Submittable only, and response times run 6–12 months. Key watch-outs: UBC School of Creative Writing students/faculty/recent alumni are ineligible, the same writer cannot appear twice in one publication year, and prose submitters must wait for a response before resubmitting.

details.aesthetic: Regional arts magazine covering artists and writers connected to Cape Cod and the Outer Cape; publishes original articles, interviews, book reviews, scholarly articles, poetry, and fiction; values magazine journalism and art writing experience but does not require it.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Full fiction prize guidelines only posted in July — check the website then before submitting. Proposals are strongly preferred over unsolicited article manuscripts. Poetry selection is entirely at guest editor's discretion each issue.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Up to 20,000 words for fiction prize manuscripts; up to 3 poems for poetry; article length not specified

provincetown arts.index_line: Provincetown Arts: Cape Cod-connected art/writing coverage plus poetry and fiction; reads Aug–Jan; fiction prize guidelines post in July
provincetown arts.name: Provincetown Arts
provincetown arts.summary: Provincetown Arts is a regional arts magazine focused on artists and writers connected to Cape Cod, publishing articles, poetry, fiction, book reviews, and scholarly pieces. Proposals and submissions are accepted August–January; fiction prize manuscripts up to 20,000 words; poetry up to three poems per submission. Poetry is selected by a guest editor per issue, and full fiction prize guidelines are only posted in July, so writers should check the site before submitting.

details.aesthetic: Inventive, fresh, authentic prose, poetry, hybrid work, reviews, criticism, and artwork; no standardized aesthetic—prizes sincerity and respect; both emerging and established writers welcome.
details.fee: None for general submissions; $15 for poetry and prose contests
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — only one submission per year
details.reading_period: General: Sept. 1 – May 1 (currently closed until further notice); Poetry Contest: March 15 – Sept. 1, 2025; Prose Contest: March 15 – Sept. 1, 2026
details.red_flags: General prose and poetry submissions are currently closed indefinitely due to high volume; previously published work or excerpts not considered; NMSU students/faculty from last 5 years and judges' close friends/former students ineligible for contests.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must notify promptly if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Prose contest: under 25 pages; poetry contest: up to 3 poems; general submissions: unknown

puerto del sol.index_line: Puerto del Sol: inventive, no-formula prose/poetry/hybrid/art; general subs closed indefinitely; $15 contests only
puerto del sol.name: Puerto del Sol
puerto del sol.summary: Puerto del Sol publishes inventive, authentic prose, poetry, hybrid work, reviews, criticism, and artwork with no fixed aesthetic—favoring sincerity over formula across emerging and established voices. General submissions run Sept. 1–May 1 (with possible summer openings), capped at one submission per year, with response times up to 6–8 months; paid contests ($15 fee) for poetry and prose run March 15–Sept. 1, 2025/2026 respectively. Critical watch-out: general prose and poetry submissions are currently closed indefinitely due to high volume, and NMSU-affiliated writers/judges' associates are ineligible for contests.

details.aesthetic: Short, sweet, and sassy flash fiction with a hidden sting — concise, punchy stories up to 750 words; previously unpublished only.
details.fee: $25 entry fee ($15 earlybird before 15 January 2027); optional $50 editorial critique; fees include a 1-year digital subscription
details.multiple_submissions: allowed — multiple stories can be paid for together by adjusting cart quantities
details.red_flags: Contest capped at 300 total entries and may be cancelled (with refunds) if fewer than 25 qualifying entries are received; no AI-generated work accepted; no simultaneous submissions.
details.simultaneous_submissions: not allowed
details.word_limit: up to 750 words

pulp literature.index_line: Pulp Literature — Bumblebee Flash Fiction Contest: sharp, sassy flash to 750 words with a sting; $25 fee, cap 300 entries, no AI work
pulp literature.name: Pulp Literature
pulp literature.summary: Pulp Literature publishes short, sweet, and sassy flash fiction (up to 750 words) with a hidden sting, judged by flash fiction master Bob Thurber, for the Bumblebee Flash Fiction Contest. Entry fee is $25 (earlybird $15 before 15 January), with an optional $50 editorial critique; total entries capped at 300. No simultaneous submissions allowed, AI-generated work is rejected outright, and the contest may be cancelled if fewer than 25 qualifying entries are received.

details.aesthetic: Innovative writing in any genre; open to new and established writers.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown

details.word_limit: unknown

quarter after eight.index_line: Quarter After Eight: innovative, boundary-pushing writing in any genre; Oct 15–Apr 15; details on Submittable, withdrawals via Submittable only
quarter after eight.name: Quarter After Eight
quarter after eight.summary: Quarter After Eight publishes innovative writing across all genres from both new and established writers. Reading period runs October 15–April 15; full submission details live on their Submittable page. Writers must use Submittable's withdraw/note functions for withdrawals—no email contact about this.

details.aesthetic: Exciting, challenging, risky, unpredictable writing across poetry and prose; welcomes hybrid genres, non-linear forms, and work that defies convention. Publishes special themed features (e.g. Queer Time & Space, Extreme Environments).
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed; one entry per genre per submission period; additional submissions declined unread
details.reading_period: March 1 – April 1 (or until 500-submission-per-genre cap is reached)
details.red_flags: Former contributors must wait at least one year after publication before submitting. Print manuscripts sent for online submission are recycled even with SASE. Hard cap of 500 submissions per genre may close the window well before April 1.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; must withdraw promptly via Submittable if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

quarterly west.index_line: Quarterly West: hybrid, non-linear, convention-defying poetry/prose; Mar 1–Apr 1, capped at 500/genre, fills fast
quarterly west.name: *Quarterly West
quarterly west.summary: Quarterly West seeks formally adventurous, hybrid, and risk-taking poetry and prose that defies easy categorization. Submissions are open March 1–April 1 with a 500-submission-per-genre cap; one entry per genre per period, no previously published work. Former contributors must wait a full year before resubmitting, and print manuscripts sent for online submission will be recycled unread.

details.aesthetic: Any topic offering a novel angle on the contemporary world; prizes singularity of voice, accessibility of ideas, and relevance to shared concerns. Publishes essays, short stories, poetry, photography, and 'anything else that's interesting.'
details.multiple_submissions: up to 6 poems or 2 stories (or equivalent) per submission
details.red_flags: Non-Canadian writers face a hard publication cap under Canadian federal content guidelines. Submission must be MSWord, not PDF. Cover letters explaining ideology or listing publication credits are explicitly unwelcome.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but previously published work is not accepted
details.word_limit: ~3,000 words for prose; up to 6 poems or 2 stories per submission

queens quarterly.index_line: Queen's Quarterly: essays, fiction, poetry, photography with a distinct voice on contemporary life; 9% acceptance, quota caps non-Canadian writers
queens quarterly.name: Queen’s Quarterly
queens quarterly.summary: Queen's Quarterly seeks singularity of voice and accessibility of ideas across fiction, essays, poetry, and photography on topics relevant to contemporary life, with a premium on work that can spark national conversation. Prose is capped at ~3,000 words, up to six poems or two stories per submission, and all submissions must be emailed as MSWord documents. Non-Canadian writers face publication limits under Canadian federal content guidelines, and the 9% acceptance rate is worth noting.

No information about any single journal's submission mechanics can be reliably extracted from this aggregator post.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, creative non-fiction, and drama; also accepts art (1–5 pieces). Refer to their Statement of Purpose and recent issues for specific aesthetic direction—not detailed on this page.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown

quiddity.index_line: Quiddity — poetry, fiction, CNF, drama, art; no stated aesthetic; strict no-AI policy, blind submissions (no contact info in file)
quiddity.name: *Quiddity
quiddity.summary: Quiddity is Arcadia University's undergraduate-edited online journal publishing poetry, fiction, creative non-fiction, and drama twice yearly; submissions cap at 7,500 words (prose/drama) or 1–5 poems up to 7 pages, with no previously published work accepted anywhere in North America. Simultaneous submissions are allowed with immediate notification upon acceptance elsewhere. Writers should note the strict no-AI policy and that contact info must appear only in the email body, not the attached file.

details.aesthetic: Daring, pulse-raising fiction; knowledge-bringing essays; moving and thrilling poetry. Prizes secretive stories, unwitnessed moments, fresh perspectives. Focus on West of Ireland and Irish writers, plus international voices. Also accepts cover art.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown

ragaire.index_line: Ragaire (Galway): daring, secretive-feeling fiction/essays/poetry, West of Ireland focus; free; closes July 15, 2025; check site for full guidelines
ragaire.name: Ragaire
ragaire.summary: Ragaire is a Galway-based journal championing emerging West of Ireland and international writers, seeking daring, emotionally resonant poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction. Prose up to 3,000 words; up to 3 poems totalling no more than 40 lines; current window closes July 15, 2025. This is a news post announcing the deadline rather than a full guidelines page, so several practical details are absent.

details.aesthetic: Nature-focused work only — poetry, short fiction, art, and photography inspired by the natural world; established and emerging writers welcome; current theme is 'Paths' for Winter–Spring 2026.

ragged lion.index_line: Ragged Lion (Tiny Seed) — nature-inspired poetry, 300-word max; poems only through Nov 1, no humans in photos, fee charged
ragged lion.name: Ragged Lion
ragged lion.summary: Tiny Seed is a nature-focused online journal publishing poetry, short fiction, art, and photography inspired by the natural world, with a strict 300-word maximum for prose and poetry. Submissions open Oct 1–Nov 1, 2025, via Google Forms only; currently only poems (2–3 per submission) are accepted for this window. Writers should note there is a submission fee (amount unstated, though fee waivers are available on request), and previously published work is explicitly welcome.

details.aesthetic: Experimental and traditional fiction, micro/flash fiction, creative nonfiction, interviews, book reviews, and comic/graphic narratives centered on non-heteronormative, marginalized parenthood and family; strong literary voice, non-academic; 2026 themes include Online/IRL, Adoption Truths, Beyond Borders, Writing Midlife, Girlhood, and a Hurricane Katrina 20th anniversary call.

details.red_flags: Non-exclusive online archiving rights held in perpetuity; first electronic rights exclusive for 6 months post-publication; eBook, print, and audiobook first rights reserved; multiple submissions locked behind paid membership; previously published work not accepted; AI-generated work auto-rejected; submitted draft considered final.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed — notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

raising mothers.index_line: Raising Mothers: fiction, flash, CNF, interviews, graphic narratives by BIPOC/LGBTQIA+/disabled/marginalized mothers & parents, plus adoptee voices; free to submit
raising mothers.name: *Raising Mothers
raising mothers.summary: Raising Mothers publishes experimental and traditional fiction, flash, creative nonfiction, interviews, book reviews, and graphic narratives exclusively from self-identified mothers/parents who are BIPOC, LGBTQIA+, disabled, gender-marginalized, or living at intersections of those identities, plus un-mothered/adoptee voices. No word limit stated; response time is 3–6 months; fee is entirely voluntary; no AI-generated work accepted. Multiple submissions are restricted to paying members only (via Substack or Patreon), and Raising Mothers retains non-exclusive online rights to archive work in perpetuity.

No single journal is being described here; the page is a directory tool for writers.

details.aesthetic: Creative writing and art about environmental justice; fiction, nonfiction, poetry, essays, novellas, translations, reviews, reprints, and art; prioritizes voices of Indigenous, racialized, queer, trans, disabled, and globally marginalized people; no ecofascism, no prejudiced work of any kind.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown

details.word_limit: unknown

reckoning.name: Reckoning
reckoning.summary: Reckoning publishes creative writing and art focused on environmental justice, actively seeking work from Indigenous, racialized, queer, trans, disabled, and globally marginalized writers. No fees; submissions open now through August 31, 2026; response time 1–6 months (slowest Oct–Jan). Writers must not use any LLM or AI-assisted tools (including Grammarly), with permanent ban as penalty for violations.

details.aesthetic: New and under-published voices; fresh, off-beat, inventive work that challenges genre boundaries; emotional truth, complex characters, everyday subjects examined obliquely; welcomes genre fiction only with strong prose (hard sci-fi, high fantasy, tawdry romance discouraged); also publishes cultural critique (casual or academic), memoir/personal essay, and experimental/hybrid blurred-genre work.
details.multiple_submissions: Varies by category: poetry up to 5 poems as one submission; flash fiction up to 3 pieces per submission; fiction, memoir/essay, and cultural critique are one piece per submission; cover art one submission of up to 6 images
details.reading_period: Blurred Genre summer issue: May 1 – June 1; reading period for other categories unknown
details.red_flags: No AI-generated content in any form; accepted authors must wait 2 years before submitting again; plagiarism results in permanent blacklisting; submissions endorsing prejudice/racism/sexism etc. are rejected outright and the author banned from future submissions; must use Submittable only (no email or USPS).
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed (no withdrawal condition stated)
details.word_limit: Flash fiction: up to 1,200 words; Fiction: 1,200–6,000 words; Memoir & Personal Essay: up to 6,000 words; Cultural Critique: up to 8,000 words; Blurred Genre: up to 3,000 words (or 10 pages graphic media); Poetry: up to 5 poems, 10 pages

redivider.index_line: Redivider: fresh, off-beat fiction/poetry/nonfiction and hybrid work from under-published voices; oblique takes on everyday life; no AI-written work
redivider.name: *Redivider
redivider.summary: Redivider seeks fresh, off-beat, inventive literary work across fiction, flash, nonfiction, poetry, cultural critique, and hybrid forms, favoring under-published voices with emotional truth and unconventional angles. Word limits range from 1,200 words (flash) up to 8,000 words (cultural critique), with category-specific caps; poetry is capped at 5 poems/10 pages. Watch out for the strict AI-writing ban, the 2-year resubmission wait after acceptance, and hard rejections for prejudice-endorsing content or plagiarism.

details.aesthetic: Fiction: experimental and literary short stories (no novel chapters). Nonfiction: creative nonfiction—personal essays and narratives, not scholarly papers or reviews (no excerpts). Poetry: eclectic, all forms, styles, and dictions. Art: imagery that 'reverberates beyond the page'; variety of media including photography.
details.fee: Free for general submissions; paid contest option exists (amounts not stated on this page)
details.multiple_submissions: Maximum 2 free-category submissions per person per reading period; no limit on paid contest entries
details.reading_period: May 1 – Oct 1 (fiction, nonfiction, poetry); May 1 – Nov 1 (art and Emerging Voices)
details.red_flags: AI policy statement is cut off mid-sentence—writer should seek clarification before submitting AI-assisted work. Previously published art from other literary journals (print or online) is rejected outright. Cover letter must include personal details but those details must be excluded from the work itself—easy to accidentally violate blind-review requirement.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed for visual art (with immediate withdrawal required if accepted elsewhere); unknown for prose and poetry
details.word_limit: Up to 5,000 words (fiction and nonfiction); up to 5 poems (poetry); up to 5 pieces (art)

reed magazine.index_line: Reed Magazine: eclectic, craft-focused fiction/nonfiction/poetry/art; May 1–Oct 1 reading period; blind review, watch cover letter details
reed magazine.name: Reed Magazine
reed magazine.summary: Reed Magazine publishes fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and art (including photography) with an eclectic, craft-focused aesthetic open to experimental and literary work; prose is capped at 5,000 words, poetry at 5 poems, and art at 5 pieces, with a May 1–October 1 reading period for prose/poetry and May 1–November 1 for art. Free-category submissions are capped at 2 per person per reading period; paid contest entries have no cap. Writers should note that previously published art from other literary journals is not accepted, and the page cuts off mid-sentence on AI policy, so that policy is unknown.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction, creative nonfiction (exploratory essays with emotional arc, not memoirs or devotionals), poetry with authentic spiritual/emotional/social engagement and strong musicality, and short graphic narrative—all through the lens of art and faith; prizes artistic excellence above all.
details.fee: yes, charged via Submittable (exact amount not stated)
details.multiple_submissions: Up to 3 fiction stories or 3 CNF essays per reading period (each as separate file in one submission); up to 5 poems per submission; only one submission per genre at a time—wait for a decision before submitting again in that genre
details.red_flags: Submission fee required; blind review so no identifying info in document; must wait for decision before re-submitting in same genre; previous one-year wait for past contributors has been lifted.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must withdraw immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 8,000 words (shorter preferred, flash encouraged); Creative nonfiction: up to 5,000 words (shorter preferred); Poetry: up to 1,000 words

relief a journal of art and faith.index_line: Relief: fiction, CNF, poetry, graphic narrative exploring art and faith; artistic excellence over devotional writing; fee via Submittable
relief a journal of art and faith.name: Relief: A Journal of Art & Faith
relief a journal of art and faith.summary: Relief publishes literary fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry, and graphic narrative through the lens of art and faith, favoring shorter, artistically excellent work with authentic spiritual, emotional, and social engagement. Reading period runs September 1–February 1; fiction up to 8,000 words, CNF up to 5,000, poetry up to 1,000, with multiple pieces per submission allowed but only one submission per genre at a time. There is a submission fee charged via Submittable, and writers must withdraw immediately if accepted elsewhere.

details.aesthetic: Publishes poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and art; no further detail about voice, themes, or sensibility is available from this source

details.aesthetic: High-literary, craft-serious poetry, fiction, essays, and criticism with a strong critical-intellectual sensibility. Contributor list spans celebrated mid-career and major poets (Kay Ryan, Brenda Hillman, A.E. Stallings, Terrance Hayes) alongside fiction writers like Joy Williams and Charles Baxter and essayists/critics. Suggests a journal that values formal intelligence, lyric ambition, and serious critical thought over experimental or pop-cultural work.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown

revel.index_line: Revel: high-literary poetry, fiction, essays, criticism (Ryan, Williams, Hayes); Revel 5 open only to debut authors, Submittable only
revel.name: Revel
revel.summary: Revel is a twice-yearly print literary journal edited by poet-critic Peter Campion, publishing poetry, fiction, literary essays, criticism, and art at a high literary register—contributors include Kay Ryan, Joy Williams, William H. Gass, Terrance Hayes, A.E. Stallings, and Christian Wiman. The aesthetic skews toward serious, craft-conscious writing with strong critical intelligence alongside creative work. Submissions are open only during announced limited periods via Submittable; Revel 5 (early 2026) is currently open specifically for debut authors.

details.aesthetic: Fiction (micro through short story), nonfiction essays, poetry, graphic stories/poems, interviews, and visual/multimedia art; print editions are built around an announced theme (open to unexpected interpretations); online edition is general/unthemed.

Portal closes when capacity is reached with no set calendar date, so a writer must check the Submittable portal and the magazine's website to confirm it is open before submitting. Payment is via PayPal or Venmo only; no checks or ACH.
details.response_time: Up to 5 months; longer for long-form work. Do not query before 5 months.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere.
details.word_limit: Nonfiction: up to 5000 words. Fiction: stories over 1500 words submitted singly; stories 1500 words or fewer in groups of up to three. Poetry: up to five poems per submission. Graphic stories: no set page limit.

river styx.index_line: River Styx: fiction, poetry, nonfiction, and graphic work; print issues built around an announced theme—check site for open/closed status

river styx.summary: River Styx publishes fiction, poetry, nonfiction, and visual/multimedia work in themed print editions (twice yearly) and a general online edition; prose is capped at 5000 words for nonfiction and one story per submission for fiction, with poetry up to five poems. Response time is up to five months; do not query before then. Print submissions must address an announced theme, and the portal closes when capacity is reached, so checking the website directly is essential.

roanoke review.index_line: Roanoke Review: multi-genre, experimental-friendly, underrepresented voices; unpaid, can pull work post-acceptance, cap 1/category/year

roanoke review.summary: Roanoke Review publishes poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, flash, photographic essay, graphic narrative, and visual poetry in both traditional and experimental modes, with a stated commitment to diverse and underrepresented voices. Submissions are open September 1–December 1 (with monthly caps that reset on the 1st), capped at 5,000 words for fiction/nonfiction, 1,000 for flash, and five poems max. Writers should note the journal reserves the right to pull accepted work at any time and for any reason, pays nothing, and asks for indefinite electronic archival rights alongside first serial rights.

Writers should note the mandatory $1 fee for prose, the requirement for a physical SASE, and that the page appears dated (© 2014), so guidelines may be outdated.

Overall sensibility is contemporary, socially engaged, and voice-driven, with attention to identity, women's interiority, and pop culture.

It maintains a brisk publishing pace with new pieces nearly every day, suggesting an active, high-volume outlet rather than a quarterly.

Submissions up to 12,000 words (prose) or five to six poems, sent by postal mail only, with a response time of up to one year; no response means rejection. The reading period is currently closed with no reopen date given, and writers should subscribe to the magazine before submitting.

details.aesthetic: Literary poetry, fiction, and nonfiction that pushes genre boundaries, blending fiction/poetry techniques into true stories; wants memories, arguments, meditations, philosophical rants—not articles or reports. Fiction is capped at 30 pages; poetry at five poems per submission; nonfiction and art are accepted year-round while fiction and poetry have two narrow windows (December–January and July–August). No payment is offered, and writers may only submit once per genre per reading period.
