smokelong quarterly.name: *SmokeLong Quarterly
smokelong quarterly.summary: SmokeLong publishes flash narratives up to 1000 words, seeking work that is surprising, singular, and built to withstand rereading—23 years of archives are free to browse as a guide. One piece at a time is standard (free, up to 4-week response), or up to three pieces bundled in one document via a paid multiple-submission option with a 3-day turnaround. Writers should note that general submissions close Feb 16–May 14 during the Award competition, that free windows exist but are time-limited and announced only on social media, and that payment via PayPal/Zelle may carry fees the writer absorbs.

details.aesthetic: All forms, genres, styles, and approaches welcomed—poetry (up to 4 poems), short fiction, traditional and creative nonfiction, memoir, and visual art/photography. Encourages both innovation and tradition; especially invites senior writers.
details.multiple_submissions: Poetry: max 4 poems; Prose: max 1 fiction and 1 nonfiction per issue; dual poetry+art submissions considered if each piece stands alone
details.reading_period: Feb 1 – Jun 15 (Fall/Winter issue); Aug 1 – Dec 15 (Spring/Summer issue)
details.red_flags: Withdrawing a submission still counts as your sole submission for that period—no replacement allowed. Exceeding piece limits results in discards with no refund. No AI-generated or AI-assisted work accepted. No revisions of previously submitted work, accepted or not. No individual feedback provided.
details.response_time: Up to 2 months after each deadline (i.e., by ~Aug 15 and ~Feb 15)
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must notify promptly and withdraw if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 5,000 words (prose); poetry limited to 4 poems per issue

smoky blue literary and arts magazine.index_line: Smoky Blue Literary and Arts Magazine — all genres/forms, "make it new" ethos, welcomes senior writers; one submission per window, no withdrawals replaced
smoky blue literary and arts magazine.name: Smoky Blue Literary and Arts Magazine
smoky blue literary and arts magazine.summary: SBLAAM publishes poetry, fiction, and nonfiction across all forms and genres, with a noted focus on senior writers and a 'make it new' creative ethos. There is a $3 fee, a 5,000-word prose cap, and two annual submission windows (Feb 1–Jun 15 and Aug 1–Dec 15). Key watch-outs: withdrawing a submission still counts as your one allowed submission per period, no AI-assisted work, no revisions accepted, and excess submissions are discarded without refund.

details.aesthetic: Diverse and established or new voices; values dialogue and unity; no specific genres, forms, or themes stated beyond broad literary openness.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — one piece at a time only
details.reading_period: Currently closed; open period dates unknown
details.red_flags: Submissions are currently closed with no reopen date given. Bio must be copied onto the first page of the submission or it cannot be processed — easy to overlook. No payment for published work.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must immediately notify submissions@solsticelitmag.org if accepted elsewhere, including the piece's title
details.word_limit: unknown

solstice a magazine of diverse voices.index_line: Solstice: no stated aesthetic beyond diverse voices; unpaid, closed now; one submission at a time, bio required on page one
solstice a magazine of diverse voices.name: *Solstice: a Magazine of Diverse Voices
solstice a magazine of diverse voices.summary: Solstice seeks diverse voices across experience levels, aiming for dialogue and unity, though aesthetic specifics (forms, themes, genres) are vague. No multiple submissions; one piece at a time only, with a 4–6 month response window and no payment. Submissions are currently closed, and the bio-on-first-page formatting requirement is strict and will block processing if missed.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and prose poems — no specific thematic or stylistic focus stated beyond these genres
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Year-round, but does not read during summer
details.red_flags: Submissions sent during summer will not be read; manuscripts must be typed and double-spaced; physical SASE required (postal submission process)
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed — no specific withdrawal condition stated
details.word_limit: up to 10,000 words (fiction/nonfiction); up to 5 poems (poetry)

sonora review.index_line: Sonora Review — fiction, nonfiction, poetry, prose poems; no stated aesthetic; skip summer, no online reading
sonora review.name: Sonora Review
sonora review.summary: Sonora Review (University of Arizona) publishes fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and prose poems across two issues per year. Word limit is 10,000 words for prose; up to five poems for poetry submissions; simultaneous submissions are accepted with a 3–4 month response time. Writers should note the journal does not read during summer, so timing submissions to avoid that window is important.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction; quality-focused, student-edited journal with 50+ year history.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No open calls for submissions currently; writer should check back before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must be labeled as such and journal notified immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

soundings east.index_line: Soundings East — poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, no stated aesthetic beyond quality; currently closed, no open calls
soundings east.name: Soundings East
soundings east.summary: Soundings East publishes quality poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction with a student-edited focus at Salem State University. Reading period runs September 1 to February 1, with a target response time of three months. No open calls at this time—submissions are currently closed.

details.aesthetic: High-quality poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and children's/YA writing; values accessibility and depth — work should create an immediate connection and reward rereading. Poetry should be moving with vivid, breathless endings. No hate literature, 'isms', pornography, or gratuitous violence.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — must wait for response before submitting again
details.reading_period: Sep 1 – Dec 1 and Mar 1 – Jun 1 (currently closed)
details.red_flags: Submission fee of $3; no multiple submissions allowed; acquires first North American serial rights plus one-time anthology reprint rights without additional payment
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; withdraw promptly if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Prose: rarely accepts over 5,000 words; sweet spot 3,000–4,000 words or under 1,000 words. Poetry: under 40 lines preferred, up to 3 poems per submission.

soundings review.index_line: Soundings Review: accessible, resonant poetry/fiction/CNF/kidlit-YA, no dark themes; $3 fee, closed now
soundings review.name: Soundings Review
soundings review.summary: Soundings Review publishes poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and children's/YA writing that balances accessibility with depth — no hate literature, stereotyping, pornography, or gratuitous violence. Prose is rarely accepted over 5,000 words; poetry should be under 40 lines with up to three poems per submission; there is a $3 submission fee. The journal is currently closed, and writers must wait for a response before submitting again (no multiple submissions).

south carolina review.index_line: South Carolina Review: no aesthetic details found in source; check journal's own submissions page directly
south carolina review.name: South Carolina Review
south carolina review.summary: This page does not contain useful submission guidelines for a specific literary journal. It is a general Writer's Digest article from 2011 about how to write a cover letter for literary journal submissions, using a fictitious example to illustrate common mistakes. There is no information about a specific journal's aesthetic focus, word count limits, reading periods, or submission restrictions. A writer looking for guidelines for a particular journal should visit that journal's official submissions page directly.

details.aesthetic: Cultural diversity, American West, American Indian writers, 'New West' complexities, landscape/place/eco-criticism in surprising and innovative ways; fiction, poetry, and essay/memoir.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: The submission instructions on the page are for LitRagger, a third-party site that republishes previously printed work — not a submission portal for new work to South Dakota Review. Writer should find South Dakota Review's own submission guidelines directly.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

south dakota review.index_line: South Dakota Review: American West/Native voices, landscape & eco-criticism — but this page is a reprint site, not their real submission portal
south dakota review.name: South Dakota Review
south dakota review.summary: South Dakota Review publishes work committed to cultural diversity, the American West, American Indian writers, and themes of landscape, place, and eco-criticism in innovative forms. Reading period is rolling with no word limit or response time stated. Note: the submission page shown is for a third-party site (LitRagger) republishing previously printed work online, not for submitting new work to South Dakota Review itself.

details.aesthetic: Voice-driven writing that takes risks with structure and content; short stories, novel excerpts, flash fiction, creative nonfiction, memoir, personal essay, traditional essay, poetry, fine art, photography, illustration, and graphic/comic work. Encourages unpublished authors.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed — one submission per reading period only
details.reading_period: Fiction & Nonfiction: Feb 7 – Mar 15 2026; Poetry: Mar 6 – Mar 15 2026
details.red_flags: Very narrow reading windows (as short as 10 days for poetry); no pay for TSR Online publication; current or recent (within 3 years) SUNY/CUNY students or employees cannot be paid; no email submissions accepted
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: 5,000 words max for fiction and nonfiction; 5 poems max per submission; 10 images max for art

southampton review.index_line: Southampton Review: voice-driven, risk-taking fiction/nonfiction/poetry/art, welcomes unpublished writers; $3 fee, narrow Feb–Mar windows, SUNY/CUNY affiliates unpaid
southampton review.name: Southampton Review
southampton review.summary: TSR publishes voice-driven, risk-taking fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and visual art, with a strong interest in unpublished authors. Reading periods are narrow (Feb 7–Mar 15 for prose/nonfiction, Mar 6–Mar 15 for poetry) and there is a $3 submission fee. Writers affiliated with SUNY or CUNY institutions within the past three years cannot be paid, and TSR Online contributors are also unpaid.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, literary fiction, creative nonfiction, and art; open to memoir, travel writing, personal essay; innovative black-and-white cover art; no academic/research writing, no novellas (novel excerpts only if standalone); rarely publishes short-shorts outside their dedicated contest.
details.fee: $3 (waived for BIPOC writers and currently/formerly incarcerated writers)
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed; must wait for a reply before submitting a new piece
details.reading_period: Fall and spring (exact dates not specified)
details.red_flags: No AI-generated work accepted; no previously published work; FSU current students, recent graduates (within 5 years), contest judges, and masthead members are ineligible; art and book review submissions only open at certain times—query editors first.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must withdraw via Submittable immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 7500 words; Nonfiction: up to 5000 words; Poetry: up to 5 poems, 15 pages total; Book reviews: 800–1200 words

southeast review.index_line: Southeast Review: broad-aesthetic fiction/nonfiction/poetry/art, $3 fee (waived BIPOC/incarcerated), no simultaneous new subs until reply, FSU affiliates ineligible
southeast review.name: Southeast Review
southeast review.summary: Southeast Review publishes poetry, literary fiction, creative nonfiction, and art with a broad aesthetic, favoring emerging alongside established writers across biannual print and online formats. Fiction runs up to 7500 words, nonfiction up to 5000, poetry up to 5 poems/15 pages; a $3 reading fee applies (waived for BIPOC and incarcerated writers). No AI-generated work, no previously published work, and writers must wait for a reply before submitting again—simultaneous submissions are allowed but require prompt withdrawal.

details.aesthetic: Work that enriches the mind and stirs the heart; fiction, creative nonfiction (memoirs, lyric essays, literary journalism, travelogues, flash, research-based), and poetry from all human communities and perspectives; also scholarly essays directed at a general humanities audience (no specialized jargon). Not regionally restricted despite Southern location.
details.fee: $3 reading fee for print submissions; 100 free submissions per genre per reading period available; fee can be applied as discount toward subscription or latest issue
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed until a response is received on the current submission; poetry: up to 3 poems per submission; fiction and nonfiction: one piece per submission
details.red_flags: Strict genre caps (250 poetry, 300 fiction) may close submissions early; no AI/LLM-assisted work accepted; mail and email submissions are discarded without consideration; must wait for response before resubmitting, which combined with a 6-month response window means long turnaround between attempts
details.response_time: At least 6 months (query only after 6 months)
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction (print): up to 8,000 words; Nonfiction (print): generally no more than 12,000 words; Online fiction features: 500–2,000 words; Poetry: up to 3 poems per submission

southern humanities review.index_line: Southern Humanities Review: fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and general-audience scholarly essays; $3 fee; strict genre caps close reading early
southern humanities review.name: Southern Humanities Review
southern humanities review.summary: Southern Humanities Review publishes fiction, nonfiction, and poetry that is 'thoughtfully conceived to enrich the mind and stir the heart,' welcoming diverse geographic and career-stage perspectives including scholarly essays for a general humanities audience. Submissions are open fall (Aug 1–Nov 1) and spring (Feb 15–May 15) via Submittable only, with fiction capped at 8,000 words, nonfiction generally under 12,000, online fiction features 500–2,000 words, and a $3 reading fee (waivable via 100 free slots per genre per period). No AI/LLM use is permitted, genre caps apply (250 poetry, 300 fiction), and writers must wait for a response before resubmitting—query only after 6 months.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction (flash, short stories, stand-alone novel excerpts), creative nonfiction (personal, critical, historical, nostalgic essays, profiles, interviews), and poetry in any form or subject. Eclectic but literary in orientation.
details.fee: $4 upload fee for regular (non-contest) submissions via Submittable
details.multiple_submissions: One piece of fiction or nonfiction, or up to five poems per submission; must wait for a response before sending more work
details.red_flags: Accepted writers must wait one year before submitting again; $4 fee applies to all regular submissions; stories over 10,000 words strongly discouraged
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but writer must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: No stated limit, but stories over 10,000 words are noted as particularly difficult to publish

southern indiana review.index_line: Southern Indiana Review: eclectic literary fiction, nonfiction, and poetry, any form; $4 fee; stories over 10,000 words a tough sell
southern indiana review.name: Southern Indiana Review
southern indiana review.summary: Southern Indiana Review publishes literary fiction (including flash and novel excerpts), creative nonfiction (personal, critical, historical, profile), and poetry in any form or subject. Submissions are limited to one prose piece or up to five poems per round, with a $4 upload fee via Submittable; stories over 10,000 words are a tough sell. Writers accepted for publication must wait one year before submitting again, and should notify immediately if a simultaneous submission is accepted elsewhere.

details.aesthetic: unknown
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No previously published work considered; editors will not provide feedback or comments on submissions
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

southwest review.index_line: Southwest Review — no stated aesthetic; general literary quarterly; pays + 5 copies; closed, opens Dec 1
southwest review.name: Southwest Review
southwest review.summary: Southwest Review is a quarterly literary journal currently closed to submissions, typically opening December 1st. No word limits or response times are stated, but authors receive nominal payment plus five contributor copies. Submissions are currently closed — check social media for reopening announcements.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction; prioritizes writers from marginalized communities (Black diaspora, indigenous, Asian, Latinx, neurodivergent, disabled, LGBTQIA+); seeks fiction that transcends the everyday, haunts, and feels fresh.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Closed at time of page; reopen date listed as 'September' with no year specified.
details.red_flags: Submissions are currently closed with no confirmed reopen date; no practical submission details (word limits, fees, response times, simultaneous submission policy) are provided on these pages.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

souwester.index_line: Sou'wester: poetry, fiction, nonfiction wanting fresh, haunting work, prioritizing marginalized voices; closed, reopens September (year unstated)
souwester.name: Sou’wester
souwester.summary: Sou'wester publishes poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction with a stated commitment to diverse and marginalized voices, seeking fiction that is fresh, haunting, and awe-inspiring. Submissions are currently closed, with a note to check back in September for an update. No word limits, fees, or response times are specified on these pages.

details.aesthetic: Genre-blending speculative fiction and poetry with strong voice, atmosphere, and imaginative risk—strange, lyrical, mythic, futuristic, haunted, or experimental work that resists easy classification; issues are themed monthly (e.g. 'Prepare to Advance,' 'Shadows Mean Light,' 'Sharpen Your Tools'); historically published Jonathan Maberry, Aliette de Bodard, Jack Ketchum, Norman Spinrad, and others.
details.fee: none to submit; pays $10 flat (0.01/word) for fiction and $5 per poem, via PayPal, plus a digital contributor copy
details.multiple_submissions: One poem per submission; fiction submission limits not specified
details.reading_period: Themed submission windows open the first of each month for one week only
details.red_flags: Very narrow one-week monthly submission windows tied to specific themes; low pay rate; PayPal required for payment, with only limited alternatives for countries without PayPal access.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with prompt withdrawal via Duosuma if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Flash fiction up to 1,000 words; poetry up to 35 lines

space and time magazine.index_line: Space & Time: monthly-themed flash SF/horror/fantasy (to 1,000 words) & poetry; one-week windows only, $10 flat/$5 poem
space and time magazine.name: Space and Time Magazine
space and time magazine.summary: Space & Time is a legendary speculative fiction magazine founded in 1966, publishing themed monthly issues of speculative flash fiction and poetry that blend horror, science fiction, fantasy, and the unclassifiable. Themed calls open only for one week each month, work must be short (flash fiction to 1,000 words, poetry to 35 lines), and pays a small fee for first print/electronic rights that revert after publication. Also accepts translated submissions from Portuguese, Spanish, French, and Italian.

details.aesthetic: Humorous, thought-provoking, unconventional short fiction; also accepts comics and video. No alien rape stories; no AI-assisted work.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Submitters are automatically added to the mailing list; opt-out requires sending a blank email manually. Failing to disclose a reprint or excerpt can result in a permanent ban. Sloppy formatting (non-Shunn) risks rejection without reading.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: up to 5000 words (longer pieces may be considered if writer justifies in comments)

space squid.index_line: Space Squid: humorous, unconventional fiction/comics/video to 5000 words; free; no alien rape or AI-assisted work; strict Shunn format
space squid.name: Space Squid
space squid.summary: Space Squid publishes funny but thought-provoking, unconventional fiction (and accepts comics/video), capped at 5000 words with Shunn modern manuscript format required. No fee; reprints accepted only if disclosed upfront. Writers should note the automatic mailing-list subscription on submission, the ban on AI-assisted work and alien rape stories, and that sloppy formatting can trigger rejection without reading.

details.aesthetic: Work engages with the idea that perception is never neutral—'lenses matter, they focus, distort, clarify, conceal'—and the journal foregrounds pairings between text and original visual art; strong commitment to under-represented voices (BIPOC, women, LGBTQIA+, disabled writers).
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: September-October for general submissions (main magazine); THE REVUE reads year-round
details.red_flags: Full current guidelines are only on their Submittable page, not detailed here; do not email to withdraw or partially withdraw submissions—must be done via a note in Submittable.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

spectacle.index_line: Spectacle: Poetry/fiction/nonfiction paired with visual art; prioritizes BIPOC, women, LGBTQIA+, disabled writers; general reads Sept-Oct only
spectacle.name: *Spectacle
spectacle.summary: The Spectacle is a biannual literary magazine run by graduate students at Washington University in St. Louis, publishing poetry, fiction, and nonfiction paired with original visual art from contributing artists, plus a year-round companion, THE REVUE, for flash prose, short poems, and interviews. It emphasizes the interplay between literary and visual art and prioritizes under-represented voices, including BIPOC, women, LGBTQIA+, and disabled writers. General submissions open only in a narrow September-October window each year.

details.aesthetic: Literary memoir, flash fiction, poetry (one poem only), literary/mainstream/experimental fiction (no genre fiction), book reviews/author interviews, and art. Favors work that illuminates the human condition; seeks voices from marginalized groups and has a dedicated free-submission track for Black writers. Art should feel grounded, pop-surreal, hyperreal, or abstract with a humanist edge.
details.fee: Free in odd months (Jan, Mar, May, Sep, Nov); fee amount unspecified for tip-jar months (even months); $5 for expedited 2-week review. Fee waivers available on request.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — one submission per writer at a time across all genres
details.reading_period: Open most of the year; closed July 1–Aug 15 and Dec 15–31. Free subs: Jan, Mar, May, Sep, Nov. Fee-based subs: Feb, Apr, Jun, Aug, Oct, first half of Dec.
details.red_flags: Free submission periods can close early due to volume — submit early. Work must be unpublished everywhere, including personal blogs/websites. AI use must be disclosed or submission is non-compliant. Interviews/reviews must be submitted via a separate link, not Submittable. Art submissions only open during free submission periods. Post-submission edits require full withdrawal and resubmission.
details.response_time: Up to 6 months; or 2 weeks with $5 expedited fee
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but must withdraw immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: Flash: under 1000 words; Memoir: under 2000 words; Fiction: 1000–3000 words; Poetry: 1 poem; no word limit stated for reviews/interviews

split lip.index_line: Split Lip: humanist memoir/flash/poetry/fiction; free odd months only, one sub at a time, Black-writer initiative
split lip.name: Split Lip
split lip.summary: Split Lip publishes literary memoir, flash, poetry, fiction, and art with a humanist, accessible sensibility—favoring fresh voices and work from marginalized groups, with a particular initiative for Black writers. Word limits vary by genre (poetry: 1 poem; flash: under 1000w; memoir: under 2000w; fiction: 1000–3000w); submissions are free in odd months and fee-based in even months, with a closure July 1–Aug 15 and Dec 15–31. Only one submission at a time is allowed, no previously published work (including personal blogs), AI use must be disclosed, and free submission periods can close early without warning.

details.aesthetic: Short fiction, novel extracts (standalone chapter/section), non-fiction, poetry, graphic fiction/non-fiction, and prose/poetry in translation; Irish and international writers; strong emphasis on new/emerging voices, the short story form, diversity and inclusivity, and Irish-language writing (Comhchealg section).
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — writers may submit under only one category per submission period
details.reading_period: Periodic open rounds only; May 2026 round just closed; next round dates TBA; Featured Poet submissions accepted in November each year; Irish Writers Centre Prize: June 16 – June 30, 2026.
details.red_flags: Submissions only accepted during announced open rounds (currently closed; next dates TBA), so timing is critical. The one-category-per-period rule is easy to overlook. The Irish Writers Centre Prize is restricted to Ireland-based writers who have not previously published fiction with the magazine.
details.response_time: Within 4 months of the closing date
details.simultaneous_submissions: Not allowed — work must not be under consideration elsewhere
details.word_limit: Short fiction/non-fiction: 'just as long as it needs to be' (no explicit cap stated); flash fiction implied at 1–2 pages; Irish Writers Centre New Writing Prize stories must be under 3000 words; poetry: up to 3 poems per general submission; Featured Poet: 8 poems.

stinging fly.index_line: Stinging Fly: Irish short fiction, novel extracts, poetry; new voices favored; closed now, rounds TBA; one category per submission only
stinging fly.name: Stinging Fly
stinging fly.summary: The Stinging Fly publishes short fiction, novel extracts, non-fiction, and poetry (including Irish-language work and translations) with a strong interest in new writers and the short story form. Submissions are open in periodic rounds only (not year-round), accepted via Submittable, with no fee; response time is within four months of the closing date. Writers should note the strict 'one category per submission period' rule, that work must not be under consideration elsewhere, and that the current round (May 2026) is already closed—next round dates TBA.

details.aesthetic: Arts and ideas rooted in Upstate New York; publishes fiction, nonfiction, poetry, drama, and visual art from emerging and established creators; content must be family-appropriate per YMCA standards; work need not be about New York but the author must have an Upstate NY connection.
details.multiple_submissions: No more than two categories per year
details.reading_period: April 1 – July/September (varies by genre: Fiction July 15, Nonfiction July 22, Drama July 29, Poetry Aug 18, Visual Art Sept 15)
details.red_flags: Strict Upstate NY residency requirement (current or former) — no exceptions without prior email confirmation; no previously published work including online; YMCA family-oriented content standards exclude profanity, sexual content, and gratuitous violence; Bea Gonzalez Poetry Prize may be cancelled if funding unavailable
details.response_time: By mid-November; if no response by December 15, contact the editors
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but must withdraw immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Genre-specific; poetry up to 5 poems; visual art up to 5 images; prose/drama word limits listed within individual genre guidelines (not fully detailed on this page)

stone canoe.index_line: Stone Canoe: All genres, family-friendly YMCA standard; open only to current/former Upstate NY residents (excl. NYC/Long Island)
stone canoe.name: Stone Canoe
stone canoe.summary: Stone Canoe publishes fiction, nonfiction, poetry, drama, and visual art from current or former residents of Upstate New York (excluding NYC and Long Island), with a family-friendly YMCA content standard. Submissions open April 1 with genre-specific deadlines ranging from July 15 (fiction) to September 15 (visual art); responses aim for mid-November. Writers outside Upstate NY are categorically excluded, and pieces with excessive profanity, sexual content, or views contrary to an antiracist, equitable community will not be considered.

details.aesthetic: Publishes short fiction across a range of lengths (flash, short story, long story), described by the editors as engaging and unforgettable; past contributors include award-winning writers Carolyn Ferrell and Crystal Wilkinson, suggesting a literary, prize-caliber standard.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown, but do not mix genres (flash, short story, long story) within the same submission
details.red_flags: Payment is per printed page ($10), so pay depends on how the piece is typeset rather than a flat fee; previously unpublished material only.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with notification required if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

story magazine.index_line: Story Magazine: prize-caliber short fiction, flash to long story; pays $10/printed page; year-round, one form per submission
story magazine.name: Story Magazine
story magazine.summary: Story is a print literary magazine publishing short fiction across flash, short story, and long story lengths, paying $10 per printed page, with a legacy tied to prize-winning authors like Carolyn Ferrell and Crystal Wilkinson.

details.aesthetic: Previously unpublished literary fiction (short stories, short shorts, novel excerpts) and creative nonfiction; judged on style, craft, freshness, and vision.
details.fee: none (pays $25 honorarium; annual fiction contest has separate entry window)
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Fiction: Aug 17 – Nov 24, 2024; Nonfiction: Aug 17 – Dec 1, 2024; Fiction contest: Nov 30, 2024 – Mar 23, 2025 (for Issue 57)
details.red_flags: Submission windows are short and seasonal; missing them means waiting until the next issue cycle. Contest entries are separate from general submissions.
details.response_time: 4–6 months, potentially longer for promising submissions during backlogs
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but writer must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: up to 6,250 words

storyquarterly.index_line: StoryQuarterly: literary fiction/nonfiction to 6,250 words, novel excerpts welcome; narrow seasonal windows, no fee, $25 honorarium
storyquarterly.name: StoryQuarterly
storyquarterly.summary: StoryQuarterly publishes literary fiction (short stories, flash, novel excerpts) and creative nonfiction, selected for style, craft, freshness, and vision. Submissions are capped at 6,250 words with specific seasonal windows and a 4–6 month response time. Writers should check Submittable for open/closed status, as windows are narrow and backlogs can extend waits for promising work.

details.aesthetic: Literary speculative fiction and poetry with an emphasis on voice-driven, often elegiac or lyrical prose, body horror and grief (e.g. 'Scarcely Gone'), mythic/theological imagery ('The Deicide'), climate and ecological anxiety, queer and diasporic perspectives, and formally experimental poetry (fragmented lines, non-English scripts). Strong parallel identity as a criticism venue: reviews, podcasts (Critical Friends), and non-fiction essays on SFF craft and theory (e.g. lycanthropy metaphors, fungal anxieties, worldbuilding critique). Explicitly engages contemporary genre discourse, including AI-generated writing and awards culture.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: none noted
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

strange horizons.index_line: Strange Horizons: literary spec-fic/poetry, queer & diasporic voices, body horror, myth, climate grief; robust review/criticism wing too
strange horizons.name: Strange Horizons
strange horizons.summary: Strange Horizons is a long-running weekly online speculative fiction magazine publishing fiction, poetry, nonfiction/criticism, reviews, and podcasts with a strong literary, socially engaged, and often queer/politically aware sensibility. It publishes prolifically (near-weekly issues) and pairs original work with an active review and critical-essay wing, including a stated policy on AI-generated submissions. This page is a table of contents / submissions landing page rather than a full guidelines document, so specific mechanics like word limits and fees are not given here.

details.aesthetic: Original fiction, poetry (theme issues only for unsolicited), creative nonfiction, and social/cultural commentary; encourages unique and unusual interpretations of themes; publishes three times a year.
details.fee: $3 for electronic submissions via Submittable; none for mailed submissions
details.multiple_submissions: Allowed with caps: max 3 fiction pieces, max 5 poems, max 2 CNF articles, max 2 commentary pieces per issue
details.reading_period: No open calls currently; unknown when next period opens
details.red_flags: No open calls at time of this page; unsolicited poetry rejected except for theme issues; art and photography only accepted if solicited; no email submissions accepted.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 3,000 words; Creative Nonfiction: up to 4,000 words; Commentary: up to 4,000 words

subterrain.index_line: subTerrain: theme-driven fiction/CNF/commentary rewarding unusual angles; no open calls currently; unsolicited poetry only for themes
subterrain.name: subTerrain
subterrain.summary: subTerrain publishes fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, and commentary three times a year around themes, rewarding unusual interpretations; fiction tops out at 3,000 words and CNF/commentary at 4,000, with per-genre caps per issue. Electronic submissions via Submittable carry a $3 fee, while mailed submissions are free; allow 6 months for a response. Unsolicited poetry is only accepted for theme issues, and there are no open calls at the time of this page.

details.aesthetic: Best literary fiction (short shorts to novellas, self-contained novel excerpts), essays of any length, and poetry; work in translation welcomed; republishes out-of-print classics occasionally; skeptical of second-person fiction but open to persuasion.
details.multiple_submissions: One story, essay, or group of poems at a time; must wait for a response before resubmitting, then wait at least one additional month; only one submission per reading period total
details.reading_period: Prose: Jan 19–21, 2026 only; Poetry: not open this spring
details.red_flags: Prose reading window is only 3 days (Jan 19–21, 2026); poetry closed this spring; poets in the last two issues cannot submit; subsequent submissions after a response in the same period are rejected outright; no personal replies given
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; must notify if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Any length for fiction and essays; up to 4 poems per submission

subtropics.index_line: Subtropics: fiction/essays/poetry, wary of 2nd-person; prose window Jan 19-21, 2026 only, $3 fee, poetry closed this spring
subtropics.name: Subtropics
subtropics.summary: Subtropics publishes literary fiction (any length, including novellas and excerpts), essays, and poetry, with appreciation for translation and work skeptical of second-person voice. Prose reading window is very narrow (Jan 19–21, 2026 only); poetry submissions are not open this spring. There is a $3 fee per submission, a strict one-submission-per-reading-period rule, and poets who appeared in the last two issues must sit out.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction and nonfiction; poetry. Online-first publication. Encourages reading the journal to understand their tastes; editor interview available for deeper insight into aesthetic. Excerpts considered if self-contained; reprints only if work is forthcoming in a collection and not yet published elsewhere.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — must wait for a response before submitting more work; also, contributors must wait two years from date of publication before submitting again
details.red_flags: Two-year embargo on resubmitting after publication. Microsoft-based email clients (Hotmail, Outlook, MSN) frequently block their responses — writers using these should check spam carefully.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed — encouraged
details.word_limit: Up to 8,000 words (prose); up to 5 poems (poetry)

summerset review.index_line: Summerset Review: online literary fiction/nonfiction/poetry, standalone work; free, sim-subs OK; 2-year wait after publishing before resubmitting
summerset review.name: *Summerset Review
summerset review.summary: The Summerset Review publishes literary fiction, nonfiction, and poetry in an online-first format, favoring work that stands alone on its own merits. Prose up to 8,000 words; up to five poems; submissions by email only (Word or plain text, no PDF); responds within four months year-round. Note the two-year cooldown before resubmitting after publication, and Microsoft-based email systems (Hotmail, Outlook, MSN) are known to block their replies.

details.aesthetic: Personal essays, short stories, poetry, and black-and-white photography; narrative and evocative work mapping the human landscape — vulnerability, difficult truths, joy and darkness; welcomes first-timers and established authors; especially seeks marginalized voices.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This page does not contain the detailed submission guidelines — word limits, response times, simultaneous submission policy, and compensation rates are stated to exist on a separate page not included here; writer must locate that page before submitting.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

sun the.index_line: Sun, The — Vulnerable personal essays, fiction, poetry, B&W photos on hard human truths; seeks marginalized voices; full guidelines on separate page
sun the.name: Sun, The
sun the.summary: The Sun publishes vulnerable, truth-driven personal essays, fiction, poetry, and black-and-white photography that explore the full human experience, with particular interest in marginalized voices. Detailed word limits, response times, and compensation are referenced but not included on this page. The page is a high-level overview and news/deadlines hub — full practical guidelines require navigating to a separate submissions page.

details.aesthetic: High-quality poetry (traditional or experimental, formal or free verse), fiction with a quick start and strong narrative arc, and all forms of creative nonfiction (personal narrative, lyric essay, immersive journalism). Especially interested in work addressing contemporary North American concerns: environment, race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, and class.
details.fee: $3 (via Submittable; mailed submissions require a check or are discarded)
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed for general genre submissions until a response is received on the first; multiple contest submissions are allowed
details.reading_period: Varies by genre and prize; generally follows UNI academic year with closures during university breaks. General Fiction: Nov 2–May 1; General Nonfiction: Apr 2–Nov 30; General Poetry: Jan 15–May 1; Visual Art and Book Reviews: year-round
details.red_flags: Current University of Northern Iowa students are ineligible; no AI-generated writing or art accepted; no previously published work or work in press elsewhere; no email submissions; no entire novels, collections, or books; $3 fee applies even to mailed hard copies
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must withdraw via Submittable if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction: up to 10,000 words (one story) or flash up to 1,500 words each (two pieces); Nonfiction: up to 10,000 words (one essay) or flash up to 1,500 words each (two pieces); Poetry: up to five poems; Book reviews: up to 1,200 words

superstition review.index_line: North American Review: fiction, nonfiction, poetry on race/gender/class/environment; $3 fee; no AI-generated work; UNI students ineligible
superstition review.name: *Superstition Review
superstition review.summary: North American Review (est. 1815) seeks high-quality poetry, fiction, and nonfiction with a strong interest in contemporary North American concerns—environment, race, gender, class—favoring strong narrative arcs, passionate imagery, and creative nonfiction that moves beyond the personal. Limits are up to 10,000 words for fiction/nonfiction, up to five poems, with a $3 submission fee via Submittable; reading periods vary by genre and follow the University of Northern Iowa academic calendar. Writers should note the strict no-AI policy, that current UNI students are ineligible, that multiple general-genre submissions are not allowed until a response is received, and that mailed submissions without a fee check are discarded.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction (any shape: letter, list, memoir, ekphrasis, flash, long-form); poetry should leap from the first line, inhabit a distinct world, and avoid over-explaining; strong interest in writers from marginalized and underrepresented communities at all career levels.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Closed roughly half the year (Jan and June–Aug); 12–16 week response time is on the longer side.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed for all genres; no withdrawal condition stated
details.word_limit: Prose up to 7,500 words; flash fiction up to 1,500 words (up to 3 pieces in one document); poetry 3–6 poems per submission

swamp pink formerly crazyhorse.index_line: swamp pink: fiction/poetry/CNF favoring marginalized voices; poems that leap fast, no over-explaining; free, no fee, $200 top pay
swamp pink formerly crazyhorse.name: *swamp pink (formerly Crazyhorse)
swamp pink formerly crazyhorse.summary: Swamp Pink (formerly Crazyhorse) publishes fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction with a particular commitment to marginalized and underrepresented voices, seeking work that is exceptional and resonant across all career stages. Prose submissions cap at 7,500 words (flash at 1,500), poetry at 3–6 poems, with two reading windows: Sept 1–Dec 31 and Feb 1–May 31; response time is 12–16 weeks and pay tops out at $200. The word limit is soft—they've published longer work—but writers should not count on exceptions.

details.aesthetic: Fiction with imaginative premises, unusual/marginalized characters, high stakes, complex motivations, and experimental work; brave, polished nonfiction including lyrical, experimental, and narrative essays; poetry and translations; graphic narratives up to 10 pages. No misogynistic or bigoted content; no children's/YA, plays, screenplays, reviews, or novel excerpts.
details.fee: $4 for poetry, translations, graphic narratives, and flash; $5 for longer prose; free complimentary tier for writers from historically marginalized groups (capped each period)
details.multiple_submissions: One submission per writer per reading period, across all genres
details.reading_period: Aug 15 – Oct 31 (Spring 2027 issue); critiques available year-round
details.red_flags: Previously published material not accepted (including personal blogs); previous TLR contributors must skip one full reading period before resubmitting; free marginalized-group submissions are capped and may close early; fees apply even if rejected
details.response_time: Up to 12 weeks (standard); 2 weeks for $3 expedited fee
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed — must notify via Submittable Withdraw or Message feature if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Flash up to 1,100 words; longer prose 1,101–6,000 words; graphic narratives up to 10 pages; poetry up to 6 poems per submission

tahoma literary review.index_line: Tahoma Literary Review: imaginative, experimental fiction/nonfiction, poetry, graphic narratives; one submission per period; $4–5 fee applies even if rejected
tahoma literary review.name: Tahoma Literary Review
tahoma literary review.summary: Tahoma Literary Review seeks fiction and nonfiction with imaginative premises, unusual characters, and experimental forms, plus poetry, flash, graphic narratives, and translations. Prose runs 1,101–6,000 words; flash up to 1,100 words; poetry up to six poems per submission; one submission per writer per reading period across all genres. Writers should note the per-submission fees ($4–$5), the cap on free marginalized-group submissions (submit early), and that novel excerpts, plays, reviews, and YA/children's lit are not accepted.

details.aesthetic: Personal essays, first-person journalism, flash nonfiction/hybrid work, short fiction, flash fiction, poetry, and visual art/comics — all favoring clear provocative arguments, strong first-person voice, non-academic tone, and connection to reading/writing culture; themed issue essays and meta/literary comics also welcomed; no political cartoons or single-book reviews.
details.fee: $3 via Submittable for most submissions; queries are free; visual art and comics submissions are free
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Year-round for most categories; poetry and general fiction accepted only during specific (unstated) reading periods — check Editorial Calendar
details.red_flags: No payment to writers or artists; poetry and fiction reading periods not specified on this page (must check elsewhere); work should be previously unpublished
details.response_time: As quickly as possible; delays expected during summer hiatus and around holidays
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must disclose in cover message and notify if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Varies by category: Theme Essays 800–1,200 words; Features 800–1,500 words; Poetry up to 5 pages (3–5 poems); Short fiction up to 8,000 words; Flash fiction up to 1,000 words (max 3 stories); Flash Nonfiction/Hybrid 500–1,500 words; 'Why I Write' essays 800–1,200 words; Interviews 800–2,500 words; general preference for under 1,200 words

talking writing.index_line: Talking Writing: personal essays, flash CNF, short fiction, poetry on reading/writing life; non-academic voice; $3 fee; poetry/fiction windows limited, unpaid
talking writing.name: *Talking Writing
talking writing.summary: Talking Writing seeks personal essays, first-person journalism, flash nonfiction, short fiction, and poetry with clear arguments, strong hooks, and a non-academic voice, all tied loosely to reading and writing life. Word limits vary by category (500–8,000 words), with a stated preference for pieces under 1,200 words for online readability; a $3 Submittable fee applies to most submissions (visual art excepted). Poetry and general fiction are accepted only during specific, unstated reading periods, so writers should check the Editorial Calendar before submitting.

details.aesthetic: A university-affiliated journal with a broad, quality-driven sensibility across poetry, fiction, nonfiction, cross-genre, essay, and visual art. Named prizes (Danahy Fiction Prize, Richard Mathews Poetry Prize) signal investment in both emerging and established voices. No single dominant aesthetic stated, but the institutional and faculty-edited context suggests craft-oriented, serious literary work rather than experimental-only or genre fiction.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Submittable only; AI usage must be disclosed in the manuscript per COPE Guidelines; prize entries are separate categories from general submissions. International authors receive digital copies only, not print.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

tampa review.index_line: Tampa Review: craft-oriented poetry, fiction, nonfiction, cross-genre, visual art; $10/page; Sept–Dec only, Submittable fee applies
tampa review.name: *Tampa Review
tampa review.summary: Tampa Review is the faculty-edited literary journal of the University of Tampa, publishing two print issues per year plus online content, with a broad range of poetry, fiction, nonfiction, cross-genre, and visual art. The journal maintains high standards (the essay on the site notes Blackbird rejects 96% of submissions, signaling the general caliber expected in the field) and pays $10 per published page. Submissions are accepted only September 1–December 31 via Submittable, with a small fee; AI-assisted work requires disclosure.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, short fiction, and 'other words' published seasonally online; no specific thematic or formal preferences stated beyond that.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Closed in June, September, December, and March; open other months — but currently on hiatus with no open calls.
details.red_flags: Magazine is currently on hiatus — no submissions are being accepted. No payment offered. Previously published work (including blog posts) is not accepted.
details.response_time: A few days to a few weeks; never longer than 8 weeks. Query at tendrilmag@gmail.com if no response within 8 weeks.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

tendril.index_line: Tendril: seasonal online poetry, fiction, and other words; no aesthetic stated; unpaid; currently on hiatus, not accepting submissions
tendril.name: Tendril
tendril.summary: Tendril publishes poetry, short fiction, and other writing seasonally online; submissions are closed in June, September, December, and March, with a max response time of eight weeks. No payment is offered, and previously published work (including blog posts) is not accepted. The magazine is currently on hiatus, so no calls are open.

details.aesthetic: Near-future speculative fiction grounded in tech, science, and contemporary digital/internet culture; favors sharp, zeitgeist-driven premises (AI chatbots, climate dystopia) over far-future space opera; open to unconventional forms like social media posts from the future, fictive data dumps, and experimental graphic narratives.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed - limit one story per submission
details.reading_period: year-round (submissions open to the public on a rolling basis)
details.red_flags: Does not consider previously published work; no personal response if not accepted; do not email the Motherboard editor inbox with Terraform queries.
details.response_time: up to 4 months; if no response by then, assume rejection
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: 2,000 words or fewer

terraform.index_line: Terraform: near-future tech/internet-culture SF, 2,000 words max, any form incl. experimental; pays $0.20/word
terraform.name: Terraform
terraform.summary: Terraform, VICE Motherboard's speculative fiction imprint, publishes very short (2,000 words or fewer) near-future science fiction focused on tech, science, and internet-age culture — think sentient chatbots and climate dystopias rather than space opera — in any form including experimental and graphic narratives, running one new story per week.

details.aesthetic: Place-based work across poetry, creative nonfiction (personal/lyric essays, memoir, literary journalism), fiction, articles, artwork, and video; themes of climate, environment, and social/justice; seeks work that yields new insights; especially welcomes Indigenous, Native, Black, Brown, LGBTQ+, women, and other underrepresented voices.
details.fee: General and ARTerrain/Letter to America: none (pays $50 per published piece). Contests: $20/entry. Sowell Prize: $25/entry.
details.multiple_submissions: General submissions: no more than once every six months unless invited. Contests: one entry per submission form (multiple poems up to 5 per entry allowed in poetry).
details.reading_period: General nonfiction/fiction: Jan 1–Apr 30. Poetry general: suspended in 2026. Annual contests: May 1–Sep 1, 2026 (deadline Sep 7, 2026). Sowell Emerging Writers Prize: Sep 15–Nov 15, 2026. ARTerrain and Letter to America: year-round.
details.red_flags: No AI-generated or AI-assisted submissions accepted. Poetry general submissions entirely suspended in 2026. Contest entries must have author name removed from document. Six-month cooldown between general submissions.
details.response_time: General submissions: within 6 months. Letter to America and ARTerrain: within 6 weeks.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed for contests; notify via Submittable if withdrawing. Not stated for general submissions.
details.word_limit: Contest: up to 5,000 words per story or essay; flash up to 1,000 words each (2 allowed); poetry up to 5 poems/7 pages per entry. General submissions: unknown.

terrainorg.index_line: Terrain.org: place/climate/justice-focused poetry, essays, fiction, art; $50 pay; poetry closed 2026; no AI submissions
terrainorg.name: *Terrain.org
terrainorg.summary: Terrain.org is a place-based journal publishing poetry, essays, fiction, artwork, and more focused on place, climate, and justice, with particular interest in marginalized voices. General nonfiction/fiction submissions are open Jan 1–Apr 30 (free, pays $50); poetry general submissions are suspended in 2026; annual contests run May 1–Sep 1 ($20/entry); ARTerrain and Letter to America are year-round. Writers should note the AI-submission ban, the six-month cooldown between regular submissions, and that poetry general submissions are not accepted in 2026.

details.aesthetic: Works of literature, illustration, music, and other art that are about maps and their paradoxes, are themselves maps of a territory, or respond ekphrastically to an existing map; multi-media and cross-disciplinary work encouraged; strong preference for pieces written specifically to the stated theme.
details.multiple_submissions: Only one manuscript per year per submitter
details.red_flags: This is the journal's thirteenth and final issue — no future publishing opportunities here; submitting non-theme-specific work is discouraged; if responding to a map not on their preview pages, a hi-res image and full rights/citation info must accompany the submission or it will likely be rejected.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but journal prefers work written specifically to theme
details.word_limit: Up to 7,500 words for prose; poetry/shorter forms: 4–6 pieces, no more than 1,000 words each

territory.index_line: Territory: cartography-themed lit/art/music/multimedia; FINAL issue (Cursed), theme-specific work strongly preferred, closes Mar 15 2021
territory.name: Territory
territory.summary: Territory publishes literature, visual art, music, and multimedia centered on maps, cartography, and the paradoxes of representation — work that is about, responds to, or itself constitutes a map. Submissions for their thirteenth and final issue (Cursed) are capped at 7,500 words for prose or 4–6 pieces up to 1,000 words each for poetry, accepted only via Submittable from January 1–March 15, 2021. Writers should note this is the journal's final issue, simultaneous submissions are allowed but theme-specific work is strongly preferred, and each submitter is limited to one manuscript per year.

details.aesthetic: Thoughtful, deliberate, and authentic work that is concrete and direct and can justify its own existence; poetry in the vein of Williams, Sexton, Giovanni; essays like Orwell; flash fiction like Barthelme, Paz, Borges; black-and-white photography only.
details.multiple_submissions: One essay or one flash fiction piece at a time; up to 5 poems in one document; up to 5 photos in one PDF
details.red_flags: Poetry must be unpublished in any form (not just print); $3 fee applies to all submissions; photographs must be black-and-white and in portrait (not landscape) orientation
details.response_time: 12 weeks minimum before querying; final decisions for Spring by February 1st, Fall by August 1st
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; withdraw immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Essays up to 2,000 words; flash fiction up to 1,000 words (two pieces under 500 words each may be submitted together); up to 5 poems per submission

texas review.index_line: Concrete, direct poetry/flash/essays in the vein of Williams, Sexton, Borges, Orwell; B&W photos only; $3 fee, unpublished work required
texas review.name: Texas Review
texas review.summary: West Texas Literary Review seeks concrete, direct, authentic poetry, flash fiction, essays, and black-and-white photography in the tradition of Williams, Sexton, Orwell, and Borges, published in semi-annual print issues. Limits are 5 poems, essays up to 2,000 words, flash fiction up to 1,000 words, and up to 5 photos; submissions via Submittable only with a $3 fee. Work must be unpublished in any form, and writers should wait 12 weeks before querying status.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction spanning experimental, formal, flash, prose poetry, memoir, narrative nonfiction, and nature writing; editors favor succinct, attention-grabbing work.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Extremely short reading windows totaling ~10 weeks per year; paper and email submissions will not be read—online submission manager only.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed
details.word_limit: unknown

the boiler.index_line: The Boiler: succinct, attention-grabbing poetry/fiction/CNF, no fee; reads only May 15–Jul 15 & Nov 15–Dec 15, online submissions only
the boiler.name: *The Boiler
the boiler.summary: The Boiler publishes poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction across experimental, formal, flash, and narrative subgenres, preferring succinct, attention-grabbing writing. Two short reading windows per year (May 15–Jul 15 and Nov 15–Dec 15), no fee, simultaneous submissions allowed, response time 3–6 months. Writers should submit only via the online manager—paper and email submissions are ignored.

details.aesthetic: Experimental, form-pushing work across CNF (essays, memoir), fiction (strange, surreal, sincere, genre-bending), poetry (weird, hybrid, multilingual, any form), multimedia (comics, photo/video essays, audio), and visual art; prioritizes historically underrepresented and marginalized voices.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Variable — check current open period on Submittable
details.red_flags: No email submissions accepted; no hard-copy submissions accepted; do not contact editors via personal email or social media; previously published work not considered; poetry submissions that borrow heavily from other artists must disclose this in the cover letter or risk rejection.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Nonfiction: up to 5000 words (ideal ~3500); Fiction: up to 5000 words; Poetry: up to 5 poems per submission; Multimedia/Art: not specified

the normal school.index_line: The Normal School: experimental, surreal/hybrid CNF, fiction, and multilingual poetry; centers marginalized voices; Submittable only, variable reading period
the normal school.name: *The Normal School
the normal school.summary: The Normal School publishes experimental, form-conscious creative nonfiction (essays/memoir up to 5000 words), strange/surreal fiction (up to 5000 words), hybrid/multilingual poetry (up to 5 poems), multimedia, and visual art, with a strong commitment to historically marginalized voices. Submissions are via Submittable only (no email, no hard copy); reading period is variable and must be checked on Submittable. Writers must notify immediately upon acceptance elsewhere, and poetry inspired by other artists requires a cover letter disclosure.

details.aesthetic: unknown
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This is not a journal. The page is a Writer's Digest craft article, not a submission guidelines page for any publishable journal. No submission target can be identified from this content.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

the white review.index_line: The White Review — mislabeled: this source is a Writer's Digest cover-letter guide, not journal guidelines; no aesthetic info available
the white review.name: *The White Review
the white review.summary: This is not a literary journal — it is a Writer's Digest instructional article about how to write cover letters for literary journal submissions. It contains no information about any specific journal's aesthetics, submission guidelines, or policies.

details.aesthetic: Not explicitly described beyond genre categories: literary fiction, nonfiction, poetry, drama (10-min and one-act plays), interviews, and book reviews with a noted interest in small-press titles.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed — one manuscript at a time (exception: up to 3 flash fiction pieces submitted together, and up to 5 poems submitted as one document count as one submission)
details.reading_period: Oct. 1–31 (general submissions); Jan. 1–Feb. 15 (fiction/poetry contest and drama/nonfiction general submissions)
details.red_flags: WMU current students and recent alumni (graduated within 4 years) are ineligible; no payment for publications; do not query until at least one year has passed; email and postal submissions are discarded
details.response_time: At least 1 year before querying; book reviews within 6 months
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; no withdrawal condition stated beyond notifying via Submittable message
details.word_limit: Fiction up to 7,500 words; nonfiction up to 7,000 words; poetry up to 5 poems/15 pages; drama up to 20 pages; interviews 750–2,000 words

third coast.index_line: Third Coast — fiction, nonfiction, poetry, drama, interviews; no stated aesthetic; unpaid; Oct-only general submissions; 1-yr query wait
third coast.name: Third Coast
third coast.summary: Third Coast publishes fiction (up to 7,500 words), nonfiction (up to 7,000 words), poetry (up to 5 poems/15 pages), drama (10-min or one-act plays up to 20 pages), book reviews, and interviews, with no clear stated aesthetic beyond a preference for small-press books in reviews. General submissions open Oct. 1–31 and drama/nonfiction Jan. 1–Feb. 15; simultaneous submissions allowed but only one manuscript at a time (except flash fiction bundles and poetry sets). Current WMU students and alumni who graduated within the last 4 years are ineligible, no payment is offered, and the do-not-query window is at least one year.

details.aesthetic: Themed speculative fiction anthologies; also accepts short humor pieces ('Grins and Gurgles'). Work must be original, unpublished, and not AI-generated.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed; if rejected, one more submission permitted per reading period (limit 2 total per period)
details.reading_period: Currently closed; themes announced on main page
details.red_flags: Currently closed to submissions; no reprints accepted; AI-written work explicitly banned; simultaneous and multiple submissions both prohibited
details.simultaneous_submissions: Not allowed
details.word_limit: 1,500–3,000 words for stories; 600–1,000 words for flash humor

third flatiron publishing.index_line: Third Flatiron Publishing — Themed SF/speculative anthologies, 8¢/word; currently closed, watch site for themes; no reprints, no AI, one sub only
third flatiron publishing.name: Third Flatiron Publishing
third flatiron publishing.summary: Third Flatiron publishes themed SF/speculative anthologies, paying SFWA pro rate (8¢/word) for original, unpublished, non-AI work of 1,500–3,000 words (flash humor 600–1,000 words). The market is currently closed; writers should watch the main page for upcoming theme announcements before submitting. No simultaneous or multiple submissions are allowed, and AI-assisted work is explicitly prohibited.

details.aesthetic: Student-produced work spanning literature, visual art, and music from a high school community; no further detail on voice or themes is available from this text.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: ongoing; published bi-annually in February and June
details.red_flags: This is a high school literary magazine (Newton North High School); submissions are almost certainly restricted to current students, making it irrelevant for most adult writers.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

thoughtprints.index_line: Thoughtprints — Newton North High School's lit/art/music magazine; students only, not for adult writers
thoughtprints.name: Thoughtprints
thoughtprints.summary: Thoughtprints is a student-produced literary, art, and music magazine from Newton North High School, published twice yearly in February and June. It publishes a mix of literature, visual art, and music, with a student contributor base. This is a high school publication, which almost certainly limits submissions to current students.

details.aesthetic: Hybrid works between prose poetry and flash fiction; original, previously unpublished prose, poetry, fiction, nonfiction, and hybrid text that resists classification. No mixed-media or multimedia projects.
details.multiple_submissions: Up to 5 short pieces per submission
details.reading_period: Currently on hiatus; not accepting submissions
details.red_flags: Journal is on hiatus — submitting now would be a wasted effort; check back for reopening announcement
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed; must notify/wait for response before resubmitting
details.word_limit: Fewer than 1000 words preferred; longer work considered

threadcount.index_line: Threadcount: hybrid prose poetry/flash under 1000 words, genre-resistant work — CLOSED, on hiatus, do not submit
threadcount.name: *Threadcount
threadcount.summary: Threadcount focuses on hybrid work between prose poetry and flash fiction, preferring writing that resists genre classification under 1000 words. Submissions are sent via email with up to 5 pieces at a time; simultaneous submissions are allowed but no resubmitting until you hear back. The journal is currently on hiatus and not accepting submissions.

details.aesthetic: Original, unpublished speculative fiction across horror, dark fantasy, and SF, including fluid genre mixtures. Wants emotionally resonant, narratively driven voices from literary to pulpy—unique but not too experimental. Values diverse characters and perspectives; encourages BIPOC and LGBTQIA2S+ voices. No Cthulhu pastiches, extreme gore, erotica, fan fiction, poetry, or non-fiction.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed; one submission per reading window
details.reading_period: Jan 1–15, May 1–15, Sep 1–15 (Pacific Time); currently closed

The reading period is narrow (January 1–April 14 only), and emailed submissions are permanently discarded unread.

Recurring themes: colonialism and its aftermath, racial hierarchy, African sovereignty, cultural memory, and resistance. Work is politically engaged but intellectually layered—pieces on dancehall as spiritual practice, museum collections as colonial denial, genocide in Sudan. Contributors include major figures (Bernardine Evaristo, will.i.am, Delroy Lindo) alongside emerging voices.

Explicitly rejects grimdark, torture porn, erotica, revenge fantasies, and stories concluding humanity is terrible.

Submissions are capped at 5,000 words, open two one-month windows per year (Mar 15–Apr 15 and Sep 15–Oct 15), with responses by ~6 weeks after close. No simultaneous submissions, no reprints (including self-published/website posts), no AI-generated content, and only one submission per writer per window.

Reading windows are cap-based (500 submissions) opening September and April for most genres, year-round for video essays and craft pieces, with ~6-month response times. Current Northwestern MA/MFA students, recent graduates (within 5 years), and program faculty are ineligible, and only one submission per open call is allowed.
