details.reading_period: Issue Two is closed; no current open period stated
details.red_flags: Issue Two is currently closed — no active submissions window. Reprints not accepted if the work is still available anywhere online or in print regardless of publication date.
details.response_time: As soon as possible; if no response after 3 months, writer may enquire
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but writer must send withdrawal requests to other outlets if accepted
details.word_limit: Micro fiction to 3000 words preferred; will consider up to 5000 words; nothing above 5000 words accepted

visions.index_line: Visions: literary/reflective sci-fi & speculative on humanity themes, no fantasy — CLOSED (Issue Two), pays ~6¢/word
visions.name: Visions
visions.summary: Visions publishes literary, reflective science fiction and speculative fiction (not fantasy/paranormal) on a themed basis — Issue Two's theme was humanity, covering AI, DNA, death, society, and more. Stories run up to 3000 words preferred, hard cap at 5000; multiple micro/flash submissions allowed if combined under 3000 words, one piece only for longer work. Issue Two is now closed, so there is no active reading period; writers should watch for the reprint restriction (nothing still available online or in print) and a required withdrawal notice if accepted elsewhere.

details.aesthetic: Innovative, challenging, experimentally-inclined poetry, fiction, hybrids, and visual art; feminist ethos; eclectic in style but always aesthetically cohesive; not aligned with any particular poetic movement; subtlety valued alongside innovation.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: No payment to contributors; Submittable only — email submissions explicitly not accepted.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

volt.index_line: Volt (Posit): Experimental, feminist-leaning poetry, fiction, hybrids & visual art, cohesive over trendy; Submittable only, no pay, Sep–May
volt.name: Volt
volt.summary: Posit publishes innovative, experimentally-inclined poetry, fiction, hybrids, and visual art with an emphasis on aesthetic cohesion and fine craftsmanship, operating as a feminist, all-inclusive journal. Submissions are open September 1–May 31 via Submittable only, with no fee and no payment to contributors. Writers should note there is no payment, and email submissions are explicitly rejected.

details.aesthetic: War, literature, and the arts across a growing range of creative genres — fiction, poetry, essays, and visual art exploring conflict, culture, and war's 'jagged and fragmented horrors' alongside its 'provocative and captivating narratives.'
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Submissions sent outside the two reading periods will not be processed — staff explicitly unavailable. No other submission details (word limits, fees, response times) are provided on this page.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

war literature and the arts.index_line: War, Literature and The Arts: fiction, poetry, essays, and visual art on conflict and culture; reads Feb–May and Aug–Dec only, strictly enforced
war literature and the arts.name: War, Literature and The Arts
war literature and the arts.summary: WLA publishes work across creative genres exploring the nexus of war, culture, and conflict, with past contributors including Brian Turner, Sara Nović, and Dunya Mikhail. They have two reading windows per year: Feb 1–May 31 and Aug 15–Dec 1. Submissions sent outside these periods will not be processed.

details.aesthetic: A university-affiliated literary journal publishing fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry, and translations; runs a New Voices Award for poetry; emphasizes previously unpublished, polished literary work typical of MFA-program-adjacent journals rather than genre or experimental niches.
details.multiple_submissions: not allowed - one story or nonfiction piece per submission period
details.reading_period: Currently open for fiction, nonfiction, and translation for Spring 2027/Issue 57, until September 15, 2026; poetry reading via New Voices Award
details.red_flags: No monetary payment for publication (contributors receive two copies, half-price additional copies, and a one-year subscription); current NYU students and recent NYU MFA graduates/affiliates (within 3 years) are ineligible to submit; submissions accepted only via Submittable during specified windows, not by mail or email.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, with request to notify promptly if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Fiction and nonfiction up to 5,000 words; poetry up to 5 poems per submission

washington square review.index_line: Washington Square Review — general literary fiction, nonfiction, poetry, translation; NYU students/recent MFA grads ineligible; pays in copies only
washington square review.name: Washington Square Review
washington square review.summary: Washington Square Review is NYU's award-winning literary journal publishing fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and translations, with a general-interest literary sensibility drawn from an MFA program context. It reads in defined windows tied to specific print issues rather than year-round, and pays contributors in copies and a subscription rather than money.

details.aesthetic: Fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction; known for concision, elegance, and rigorous curation; publishes established and emerging voices across a range of themes.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Closed; typically opens around October 1 for one month, but suspended for 2025; anticipated reopening fall 2026 for Volume 29.
details.red_flags: Submissions are fully closed with no open window in 2025; the journal is in a fundraising/restructuring hiatus and does not expect to reopen until fall 2026 at the earliest.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

waterstone review.index_line: Water-Stone Review: elegant, tightly curated fiction/poetry/CNF - closed until fall 2026 for Vol. 29, skip for now
waterstone review.name: Water-Stone Review
waterstone review.summary: Water~Stone Review is a literary annual (fiction, poetry, CNF) from Hamline University known for elegant, rigorously curated work. Submissions are currently closed with no open period for 2025, and they hope to reopen for Volume 29 by fall 2026. Writers should not submit now and should monitor for a future fundraising-linked reopening.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, non-fiction, and visual arts; open to all writers and visual artists. No stated thematic or stylistic preferences beyond genre acceptance.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: unknown (2014/2015 cycle had an October 1st deadline; current status unknown)
details.red_flags: This is a 2014 third-party blog post, not the journal's official guidelines page; information is almost certainly outdated and incomplete. Writers must visit ubalt.edu directly for current submission details.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

welter.index_line: Welter (UBalt): poetry, fiction, nonfiction, visual art—no stated aesthetic; verify current guidelines at ubalt.edu, this listing is a stale 2014 secondhand post
welter.name: Welter
welter.summary: This is a brief blog post on 'Cija's Quips' announcing that Welter Literary Journal (University of Baltimore) was open for submissions for its 2014/2015 issue, accepting poetry, fiction, non-fiction, and visual arts with an October 1st deadline. Almost no practical submission details are provided, and the content links out to the journal's own site for actual guidelines. This is a years-old secondary announcement, not the journal's own submission page—writers should go directly to the UBalt Welter site for current guidelines.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and translation; original unpublished work only; acquaintance with the magazine strongly encouraged before submitting.
details.multiple_submissions: Maximum 2 submissions per contributor per reading period; submission manager only allows 1 piece under consideration at a time.
details.red_flags: The system enforces the 2-submission cap and auto-rejects excess submissions; pen name variations still count toward the limit. Only one piece can be under consideration at a time, so a second submission cannot be made until the first is decided.
details.response_time: 10 weeks or less typically; query after 4 months.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but must be clearly marked in the comments section; writer must withdraw immediately if accepted elsewhere.
details.word_limit: Up to 30 pages for a single prose piece; up to 6 poems; up to 3 flash/short-short pieces totaling under 15 pages.

west branch.index_line: West Branch: poetry/fiction/nonfiction rewarding close reading; pays; max 2 submissions/period, one active at a time (Aug 1–Apr 1)
west branch.name: West Branch
west branch.summary: West Branch publishes poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and translation, with payment ($100/poetry submission, $0.10/word prose up to $200) and a preference for work that rewards close reading. Submissions are limited to 6 poems or 30 prose pages, with a hard cap of 2 submissions per contributor per reading period (Aug 1–Apr 1). Writers should note the submission manager only allows one piece under consideration at a time, and exceeding the 2-submission limit results in automatic rejection of additional pieces.

details.aesthetic: Inferred from editor biography and context: queer and neurodivergent perspectives, literary fiction and poetry, themed issues. The editor's own publishing credits span horror, dark fiction, and literary venues, suggesting range across genre-adjacent and literary work.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This page is a blog post advising writers on submission strategy generally, not In Her Space Journal's own submission guidelines. No mechanics for submitting to this journal are given here.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

west review.index_line: In Her Space Journal: queer, neurodivergent-informed themed issues, fiction and poetry — verify submission details, page mainly offers general submitting advice
west review.name: *West Review
west review.summary: In Her Space Journal is a literary journal run by a queer, autistic editor with a sensibility toward themed, identity-informed writing; the page text is primarily a how-to guide on finding and organizing submissions rather than the journal's own guidelines. No concrete submission mechanics for In Her Space Journal itself are provided here, so specifics should be verified before submitting.

details.aesthetic: Contemporary poetry, fiction, nonfiction, hybrid, audio/visual work, essays, and reviews; seeks dynamic writing that 'engages, surprises, and moves'—work with strong voice and emotional force. Notable contributors include Brian Evenson, Vi Khi Nao, and Cris Mazza, suggesting appetite for experimental and literary work.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: 9+ month response time with an explicit inability to answer status queries; accepts only ~2% of submissions; pays contributor copies only, no cash; Submittable only—no email or postal submissions accepted.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but must withdraw immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

western humanities review.index_line: Western Humanities Review: experimental, voice-driven lit across all forms (Evenson, Vi Khi Nao); copies only, 9+ month wait, no status checks
western humanities review.name: Western Humanities Review
western humanities review.summary: WHR publishes poetry, fiction, nonfiction, hybrid, audio/visual, essays, and reviews with a taste for dynamic, surprising, emotionally charged writing across all forms. They read year-round via Submittable only, with no word limit stated, and pay two contributor copies with no cash payment. The critical watch-out is a severe backlog—9 months or more for a response—and they explicitly cannot respond to status queries.

details.aesthetic: Original poetry, fiction, and creative essays; no further thematic or stylistic criteria stated
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed
details.red_flags: No multiple submissions and no previously published work; submissions are currently closed
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must be identified as such in cover letter
details.word_limit: Up to 6000 words (fiction); unknown for poetry and essays

whiskey island.index_line: Whiskey Island: poetry, fiction, essays, no stated aesthetic beyond originality; fiction to 6000 words; one submission only; no multiple subs
whiskey island.name: Whiskey Island
whiskey island.summary: Whiskey Island publishes original poetry, fiction, and creative essays with no stated aesthetic beyond originality. Fiction is capped at 6000 words; two reading periods run Aug 15–Nov 15 and Jan 15–Apr 15. No multiple submissions and no previously published work are the key restrictions to watch.

details.aesthetic: Flash fiction and micro fiction only; no stated thematic or formal restrictions beyond brevity.
details.multiple_submissions: 1–2 stories per submission in one document; up to 5 micros; must wait for response before submitting again
details.reading_period: Final 7 days of August, September, October, January, February, March; Nov 8–14 only; closed December
details.red_flags: Submissions may close early if Submittable cap is hit; no query responses about status; de-platforming policy for hate speech/bigotry
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, no conditions stated
details.word_limit: Under 1000 words per story; micros under 250 words each (up to five micros per submission)

wigleaf very short fiction.index_line: Wigleaf: flash/micro only (under 1000 words, micros under 250); free; brief windows within select months, closed December
wigleaf very short fiction.name: *Wigleaf: (very) short fiction
wigleaf very short fiction.summary: Wigleaf publishes flash fiction under 1000 words (up to five micros under 250 words each), with a narrow rolling reading window of the final seven days of select academic months. Writers submit one or two stories in a single document and must wait for a response before resubmitting. Note the early-close cap on Submittable and the de-platforming policy for hate speech.

details.aesthetic: Excellence in literature and the arts broadly construed: poetry (any length, any form), fiction (very short to novelette), nonfiction with 'interesting footnotes,' positive book reviews, and 2D-reproducible visual art (minimum 6 pieces) with bio and statement. Published works accepted with attribution.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed for fiction: one fiction submission per author per issue; additional stories may not be reviewed. Poetry and other genres not explicitly addressed.
details.reading_period: Quarterly deadlines: March 1 (Spring), June 1 (Summer), September 1 (Autumn), December 1 (Winter)
details.red_flags: No PDF submissions accepted. No payment. Non-exclusive license grants them right to publish in any form, including print. Book reviews must be positive in tone. Submitting multiple fiction pieces risks all but the first being ignored.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: Fiction: under 500 (very short), under 1000 (short), or under 3000 (standard); longer fiction occasionally accepted. Nonfiction: well under 5000 words. Poetry: any length.

wilderness house literary review.index_line: Wilderness House Literary Review — poetry/fiction/nonfiction/art, no pay; fiction capped at 3000 words, one per issue; book reviews must stay positive
wilderness house literary review.name: Wilderness House Literary Review
wilderness house literary review.summary: Wilderness House Literary Review publishes poetry, fiction, nonfiction, book reviews, and visual art with a broad literary mission tied to the Bagel Bards community; fiction is capped at 3000 words (with occasional longer exceptions) and nonfiction well under 5000 words, with quarterly submission deadlines. No payment is offered, but authors retain all copyrights under a non-exclusive license. Writers should note that PDFs are explicitly rejected, only one fiction piece per issue is allowed, and book reviews must be positive unless the subject is a 'well-known blowhard.'

details.aesthetic: Poetry, fiction, and non-fiction in most styles, forms, or genres; no single aesthetic imposed, but reading past issues is strongly recommended.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Rolling basis; currently reading for Autumn 2026
details.red_flags: No payment offered; grants electronic archival rights in perpetuity and requires wildness to be credited in any subsequent publication; no OneDrive or Google Docs accepted
details.response_time: Within 1 month; writers should query if longer
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but must be disclosed in the email; notify immediately if accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Up to 1,000 words for fiction and non-fiction; up to 5 poems for poetry

wildness.index_line: Wildness: eclectic poetry/fiction/nonfiction, no fixed aesthetic; unpaid, 1,000-word cap, claims perpetual archival rights
wildness.name: *Wildness
wildness.summary: Wildness publishes poetry, fiction, and non-fiction in most styles and forms, with a strong recommendation to read past issues for aesthetic context. Hard limits are 5 poems or 1,000 words for prose, with submissions by email only as a .docx or PDF. No payment is offered, and the journal claims electronic archival rights in perpetuity, requiring credit if the work is later republished.

details.aesthetic: Legal scholarship and public policy on a wide range of issues; online supplement also accepts essays on timely legal topics, responses to print publications, book reviews, and dialogues.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.reading_period: Print: until volume is full (academic year cycle); Online: year-round on a rolling basis
details.red_flags: Current law students who are not members of the journal are explicitly excluded. Emailed submissions are not accepted — must use Scholastica. Expedited review requests are not guaranteed.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

william and mary review.index_line: Legal scholarship and public policy essays; Scholastica only, non-member law students excluded, no emailed submissions
william and mary review.name: William and Mary Review
william and mary review.summary: William & Mary Law Review publishes legal scholarship and public policy essays across a print journal (6 issues/year) and a rolling online supplement; submissions go through Scholastica only, with no word limit or response time stated. Current law students outside the journal's own membership are explicitly excluded, and emailed submissions are rejected outright.

details.aesthetic: General literary journal publishing fiction, poetry, and nonfiction; short prose pieces under 1,000 words are welcomed alongside longer works, and translations are accepted with author permission. No further stylistic specifics given, but the pay-per-piece structure and high submission volume (4,000/year) suggest a broad, competitive, mainstream literary scope.
details.multiple_submissions: wait for a response before submitting again; up to 3 short stories or 5 poems can be included per submission
details.reading_period: Fiction and poetry: Sept 1 - May 31; Nonfiction: year-round
details.red_flags: Reading fee required for all submissions; high volume (4,000+ submissions/year) suggests long odds and possible slow responses; no AI-generated or AI-assisted work accepted; work must be previously unpublished.
details.response_time: usually within 6 months, follow up only after 12 months
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed
details.word_limit: unknown for long-form; short prose must be under 1,000 words (up to three per submission)

willow springs.index_line: Willow Springs: general literary fiction, poetry, nonfiction, pays contributors; $3 fee, 4,000+ subs/year, no AI-generated work
willow springs.name: Willow Springs
willow springs.summary: Willow Springs is a biannual literary magazine out of Eastern Washington University publishing fiction, poetry, nonfiction, and translations, paying contributors for accepted work and accepting up to several thousand submissions a year. It reads fiction and poetry September through May, nonfiction year-round, and charges a $3 reading fee per submission.

details.aesthetic: Poetry, prose, and visual art engaging authentically with identity, oppression, and liberation; values the poet's positionality; welcomes multilingual work and language-subverting pieces; excludes erotica, graphic violence, and bigoted work.
details.multiple_submissions: Multiple pieces allowed but must be combined into one document per category (e.g., all poems in one file, all prose in another)
details.reading_period: Currently on extended hiatus — not open to submissions
details.red_flags: Journal is on extended hiatus and closed to all submissions; automatic rejection if any identifying information appears on the uploaded document; artist statement on first page of submission is required or submission may be non-compliant.
details.response_time: Up to 8+ months; do not request status updates unless 8+ months have passed
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed, but must notify via Submittable immediately upon acceptance elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

winter tangerine.index_line: Winter Tangerine — poetry/prose/art on identity, oppression, liberation, positionality; $50 flat pay; CLOSED (extended hiatus)
winter tangerine.name: Winter Tangerine
winter tangerine.summary: Winter Tangerine publishes poetry, prose, and visual art with a strong focus on positionality, identity, and genuine engagement with oppression and liberation narratives—not married to a single aesthetic but attentive to who is speaking and why. Submissions go through Submittable with no identifying info on the document, an artist statement required, and a flat $50 payment; no word limit is stated. The journal is currently on extended hiatus and not open to submissions, and automatic rejection applies if identifying info appears on the uploaded document.

details.aesthetic: Issue-oriented literary magazine interested in innovative, boundary-pushing work that engages oppression and transcendence, prejudice and compassion, fear and raw honesty; actively amplifies historically marginalized voices, trans writers, and international perspectives; mixes emerging and established authors; themed Spring print issue vs. unthemed Fall/Winter online issue.
details.fee: Suggested $3 reading fee for general submissions
details.multiple_submissions: Only one (1) submission per genre allowed; poetry may include up to 5 poems and flash fiction up to 3 pieces within that single submission
details.reading_period: Opens September (Spring themed print issue and Witness Literary Awards) and February (Fall/Winter online, unthemed); dates may vary and windows can close early if submission volume is high
details.red_flags: No previously published work accepted, including anything posted online or on personal blogs; previously published authors must wait two years before resubmitting; UNLV/BMI affiliates (students, faculty, staff, past readers) must wait two years post-graduation/employment before submitting.
details.response_time: Poetry ~4 months; fiction/nonfiction ~6 months or longer; inquire after 10 months
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, but withdraw promptly if accepted elsewhere; notify genre editor if one piece from a poetry/flash set is accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: Prose 7,000 words or less; flash fiction pieces 1,200 words or less each (up to 3); poetry up to 5 poems per submission

witness.index_line: Witness: issue-oriented fiction/nonfiction/poetry bearing witness to oppression and compassion; prioritizes marginalized, trans, and global voices; pays
witness.name: Witness
witness.summary: Witness, published out of UNLV's Black Mountain Institute, blends literary and issue-oriented sensibilities, seeking innovative, unapologetic fiction, nonfiction, and poetry that bears witness to the present moment, with explicit commitment to marginalized and global voices, including trans writers. It publishes a themed Spring print issue and an unthemed Fall/Winter online issue, pays contributors, and charges a modest suggested reading fee.

details.aesthetic: Publishes poetry and fiction; no explicit thematic or stylistic mission stated beyond genre categories, though its institutional, annual-volume structure and regional name suggest a traditional literary-journal sensibility rather than experimental or niche focus.
details.fee: $3 per submission via Submittable; fee waived for BIPOC writers, and waivable on request to editor for financial hardship
details.multiple_submissions: only one submission per genre per volume; additional submissions declined unread
details.reading_period: 2025 reading period currently open for Volume 46
details.red_flags: Previously published work not considered; work must not appear elsewhere before Fall 2026; past contributors must wait one year after publication before submitting again; do not withdraw and resubmit to fix errors, use Submittable messages instead.
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, and encouraged; withdraw promptly if piece is accepted elsewhere
details.word_limit: unknown

worcester review.index_line: Worcester Review — poetry and fiction, no stated aesthetic beyond genre; one submission per genre; $3 fee, waived for BIPOC writers
worcester review.name: Worcester Review
worcester review.summary: The Worcester Review is a print literary journal publishing poetry and fiction, organized around annual volumes with a defined publication timeline (Volume 46 due Fall 2026), suggesting an editorial process rooted in a specific literary community (Worcester, Massachusetts) rather than rapid-fire online publishing.

details.aesthetic: Translated contemporary international literature organized into monthly themed issues by region or country; publishes short fiction, poetry, fiction serials, and book reviews; strongly oriented toward non-Anglophone voices and cross-cultural conversation.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: This text is a third-party educational summary, not the journal's own guidelines page; no submission information is present. Writer should go directly to wordswithoutborders.org for submission mechanics.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

words without borders.index_line: Words Without Borders: translated international lit in monthly regional/country-themed issues—fiction, poetry, nonfiction; check site for submissions
words without borders.name: *Words without Borders
words without borders.summary: Words Without Borders is a monthly online journal publishing contemporary international literature in English translation, organized around thematic issues that spotlight specific countries or regions (e.g., Macau, Estonia, the Caribbean) alongside poetry, fiction, and nonfiction from other world literatures. The sensibility is cosmopolitan and curatorial, foregrounding cultural multiplicity and cross-regional dialogue. No submission mechanics are visible in this text, which appears to be a third-party educational catalog entry rather than the journal's own guidelines page.

wrathbearing tree.index_line: Wrath-Bearing Tree: essays, reviews, fiction, poetry on military/social violence from lived experience; no guidelines here, check site directly
wrathbearing tree.name: The Wrath-Bearing Tree
wrathbearing tree.summary: This page does not contain useful submission guidelines for writers. It is primarily a blog post announcing an interview with the Middle West Press editor-publisher, along with background on The Wrath-Bearing Tree journal and brief descriptions of Middle West Press anthology projects. While it mentions that The Wrath-Bearing Tree publishes essays, reviews, fiction, and poetry focused on military and social violence from those with lived experience of it, no specific submission guidelines, word count limits, reading periods, or response times are provided. A writer seeking to submit to either outlet should visit those publications' websites directly for current guidelines.

details.aesthetic: Literary fiction, memoir/personal essay, poetry, visual art, and comics; no literary criticism or translations; no previously published work.
details.fee: Small fee charged; fee waiver available by emailing writersfoundryreview@gmail.com with 'Fee Waiver 2022' in subject line.
details.multiple_submissions: Not allowed; submit only once during the period.
details.red_flags: Reading period appears to be closed (ended Jan 3, 2023); guidelines are for a specific second issue only, so current applicability is uncertain.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must note in cover letter and notify promptly if accepted elsewhere.
details.word_limit: Up to 4,500 words for prose; up to 3 flash pieces totaling no more than 4,500 words; up to 3 poems or visual art pieces; comics limited to one page.

writers foundry review.index_line: Fiction, memoir, poetry, art, comics; $500 prizes; guidelines tied to a past issue, status unclear—verify before submitting
writers foundry review.name: Writer’s Foundry Review
writers foundry review.summary: WFR publishes fiction, memoir/personal essay, poetry, visual art, and comics, with prize opportunities ($500) for fiction and poetry judged by named authors. Prose is capped at 4,500 words, up to 3 poems or art pieces, one-page comics; the reading period ran Nov 1, 2022–Jan 3, 2023 with one submission allowed per period. A small submission fee applies (fee waiver available by email), and no literary criticism or translations are accepted.

details.aesthetic: Literary prose that is uncomfortable, entertaining, and revealing — fiction, flash, micros, and creative nonfiction; genre fiction discouraged; CNF editors want writing that moves, surprises, and exposes inner life.
details.multiple_submissions: One piece per submission for flash, short stories, and CNF; micros allow 1–3 pieces in one document; must wait for response before submitting again
details.reading_period: Opens 1st of each month per category (micros open 21st); closes when monthly cap is reached
details.red_flags: Monthly cap is variable and unstated — submissions can close quickly after the 1st; every other month short story submissions are restricted to writers who have never submitted short stories to them before, potentially locking out repeat submitters.
details.response_time: 1–8 weeks overall; flash 4–8 weeks; short stories 4–6 weeks; CNF 4–6 weeks; micros 1–4 weeks
details.simultaneous_submissions: allowed, no conditions stated
details.word_limit: Short stories 2,000–7,500 words; CNF 300–7,500 words; flash fiction 300–2,000 words; micros up to 300 words

xray.index_line: *X-R-A-Y: uncomfortable, entertaining literary prose (fiction, flash, micros, CNF), no genre; opens monthly, closes at variable cap—move fast
xray.name: *X-R-A-Y
xray.summary: X-R-A-Y publishes uncomfortable, entertaining literary prose (short fiction, flash, micros, CNF) that cuts beneath the surface — no poetry, and genre fiction is gently discouraged. Submissions open on the 1st of each month per category (micros on the 21st) and close when a variable cap is hit, so timing matters. Writers must wait for a response before resubmitting, and every other month short story slots are reserved for first-time submitters to the magazine.

details.aesthetic: Criticism (review essays with strong arguments, not straight single-work reviews), critical essays blending reportage/argument/personal reflection, fiction, and poetry; seeks sharp original voices, unexpected juxtapositions, formal play, and committed argument across literature, art, history, politics, film, music, and internet subcultures.
details.fee: $3 per poetry submission via Submittable; fee waivers available on request; no fee mentioned for nonfiction or pitches.
details.multiple_submissions: One piece/pitch at a time only (explicitly stated for both nonfiction and pitches).
details.reading_period: Poetry: opens August 26, 2026 (response by end of May 2027); Nonfiction: opens August 26, 2026; Fiction: closed, check back 2027.
details.red_flags: Fiction closed until at least 2027; AI-generated drafts not accepted; nonfiction submissions not following exact formatting instructions (Word attachment, specific subject line, cover letter) will be ignored; no mailed submissions read; interviews not being accepted for pitches.
details.response_time: Poetry: responses by end of May 2027; Nonfiction and pitches: assume rejection if no reply within 4 weeks.
details.simultaneous_submissions: Allowed; must notify promptly if accepted elsewhere.
details.word_limit: Pitches/essays typically 2,000–5,000 words, occasionally longer; no stated limit for poetry or fiction.

yale review.index_line: Yale Review: argument-driven criticism, essays, and poetry with sharp voice; fiction closed until 2027
yale review.name: Yale Review
yale review.summary: The Yale Review publishes criticism, essays, fiction, and poetry that prioritize sharp argument, strong voice, and intellectual adventurousness across literature, art, politics, and culture, with pieces typically 2,000–5,000 words. Poetry opens August 26, 2026 via Submittable with a $3 fee (waivers available); nonfiction opens August 26, 2026 by email; fiction is closed until at least 2027. Writers should note that fiction is currently suspended, AI-generated drafts are not accepted, and strict formatting rules apply to nonfiction submissions or they will be ignored.

details.aesthetic: Literary short fiction, one-act plays, and film-related essays; polished, prize-caliber work by internationally acclaimed and literary-celebrity contributors; strong crossover with visual art and film culture, each issue designed by a guest artist/filmmaker.
details.multiple_submissions: unknown
details.red_flags: Currently closed to general submissions with no stated reopening date; not accepting intern or volunteer reader applications either.
details.simultaneous_submissions: unknown
details.word_limit: unknown

zoetrope allstory.index_line: Coppola's Zoetrope: All-Story - Murakami/Atwood/Ferrante-caliber literary fiction, one-act plays, film essays - CLOSED to submissions, no reopening date
zoetrope allstory.name: Zoetrope: All-Story
zoetrope allstory.summary: Zoetrope: All-Story is a prestigious quarterly print magazine of short fiction, one-act plays, and essays on film, founded by Francis Ford Coppola, with a roster of contributors including Murakami, Atwood, Ferrante, and Adichie, and each issue art-directed by a different guest artist or filmmaker (David Lynch, Bowie, Almodóvar, etc.). It is a top-tier, highly selective venue known for polished, award-winning literary fiction; however, it is currently closed to general submissions with no reopening date given.

details.aesthetic: Contemporary literary poetry, fiction, and nonfiction with a strong lyric and confessional bent; recurring concerns include family and intergenerational relationships, interlingual/immigrant experience, illness and mortality, and place. Poems range from formal etudes to ghazals to free verse; nonfiction includes personal essay; fiction favors close, interior narration. Also features visual art (e.g., silkscreen painting) alongside each issue.

zone 3.index_line: Zone 3: image-driven lyric poetry, essays, and fiction on family, migration, illness, and memory; free verse, ghazals, close interior narration
zone 3.name: Zone 3
zone 3.summary: Zone 3 is a university-affiliated literary journal (housed at Austin Peay State University) publishing poetry, fiction, and nonfiction that favors intimate, image-driven lyricism—family, migration, language, illness, memory—alongside a companion small press running book contests (currently on hiatus). Work leans toward emotionally direct free-verse poems and quietly observed personal essays and short fiction, often centered on domestic, immigrant, or bodily experience.

zzyzzyva.index_line: ZYZZYVA — West Coast/California-leaning fiction, nonfiction, poetry; prose closed until late 2026, poetry open now
zzyzzyva.name: ZZYZZYVA
zzyzzyva.summary: ZYZZYVA publishes fiction, creative nonfiction, and poetry with a West Coast/California focus, welcoming writers from anywhere. Prose submissions are currently closed; poetry is open, with the next prose window announced in late 2026. Writers submitting prose now would be wasting their time.
